At these low levels, staining of clothing or skin is minimal to none but you should always test your finished product against white cloth or paper.

missing.title: Ylanganate
missing.description: Ylanganate glows with solar white flowers. Ylang, orange blossom and tuberose all shine through, bright and creamy, over a fresh green edge and a soft grape-like fruitiness. It smells radiant and natural. A small amount rounds and brightens ylang, orange blossom, neroli and tuberose, pushing them toward a fresher, more natural radiance. It also lends a dewy, creamy roundness to gardenia and softens synthetic-smelling florals. Pair it with vanillin and coumarin to add a solar top to a gourmand, or with ylang and neroli to amplify a classic white bouquet. Keep the dose small; its lift is generous.

missing.title: Ysamber® K
missing.description: Ysamber K opens with an exceptionally pure, luminous woody character that immediately distinguishes itself from heavier amber materials. It delivers remarkable diffusion without the aggressive metallic edge often found in super-ambers. Its exceptional substantivity anchors volatile notes whilst maintaining a luminous, unobtrusive quality. Ysamber K radiates with extraordinary diffusion yet never flattens a composition. You'll find this material indispensable when building contemporary woody structures that demand both power and refinement. Use it at 1-2% to add radiant lift and tenacity to citrus top notes, or dose it generously at 5-10% as your primary woody pillar. The material excels at harmonising aggressive molecules like Ambrocenide or Norlimbanol, smoothing their sharp edges whilst maintaining their incredible performance. Transform your woody accords by pairing Ysamber K with sandalwood molecules like Ebanol or Javanol for enhanced depth and creaminess. When combined with soft musks and transparent florals, it provides an elegant foundation that never overwhelms delicate nuances. Exercise caution with citral-containing materials—this combination can veer towards functional freshness if not carefully balanced.

missing.title: Z11™ 10 MIP
missing.description: Z11 (Ambraketal) was initially sold only as part of Firmenich's Fixobois base and so it found early use in fragrances like Chanel No 19 . In time the material itself became available as a 10% dilution in IPM owing to its high strength. That is Z11 10 MIP (sometimes simply called Z11 MIP). In recent years a new product emerged which is the so called HD or "high definition" version which is sold as both an 8.5% dilution (Z11 8.5 HD) and pure. It is in that pure crystalline form that it found its way in to the popular fragrance One Million by Paco Rabanne. The two products are very similar but the classic Z11 retains its supremacy in terms of sheer beauty and Firmenich keep the pure form captive. To compare the two in furniture making terms, Z11 8.5 HD is like a steel nail holding a door together — intense and penetrating, while Z11 10 MIP is like a wooden peg or a dovetail joint in an antique armoire. They both do the same job (holding two pieces of timber together) but the second has heritage, prestige and elegance. Z11 10 MIP is the Fraterworks choice for this material as it is simply the most beautiful and far better suited to quality fragrances that rely on purest radiant elegance over intensity and short-lived dazzle. Z11 10 MIP is ambery, woody and dry and has an astonishing trigeminal effect which causes intense psychological pleasure in those who smell it. Firmenich states that Z11 10 MIP diluted further by another 10% can double the power of Ambrox. In other words: 5 Ambrox® Super 5 Z11 10 MIP 10% is equal to 10 Ambrox® Super

missing.title: Z11™ HD 8.5 MIP
missing.description: First, it is worth noting that MIP is simply the French version of IPM so this is an 8.5% dilution of high purity Amberketal in IPM. Z11™ HD delivers extraordinary woody-amber power with remarkable iris elegance. This sophisticated synthetic creates a multifaceted foundation with exceptional tenacity and projection. Perfumers value its dual nature as the cornerstone in prestigious compositions where powerful woody character and refined powdery nuances define modern luxury. While our personal preference is for the softer form of this chemical ( Z11™ 10 MIP ) this more recently released HD (high definition) version is extremely popular and if you are looking for a more pronounced amber, this is the material to get. While it is already diluted to 8.5% by Firmenich, it is version powerful and you should still use Z11™ HD 8.5 MIP at 0.1-1.5% concentration in woody-amber accords. This material pairs beautifully with ionones, orris materials, and woody notes while adding sophisticated depth to floral and oriental compositions. Apply judiciously in fine fragrances where its distinctive radiant character provides exceptional longevity and seamlessly bridges base and heart notes.

missing.title: Zenolide
missing.description: Zenolide opens with a clean, airy muskiness threaded with a distinctive red berry sweetness you won't find in most other musks. The waxy, skin-like quality is immediate and inviting. As it develops, a gentle animalic warmth emerges beneath the softness, giving it real depth without any harshness. This macrocyclic musk excels at adding volume and lasting power to compositions that need a polished base. It sits beautifully behind floral and fruity accords, lifting them with transparent warmth rather than weighing them down. Pair it with ethylene brassylate for a layered musk foundation, or use it to soften woody notes in modern masculine and unisex builds. Zenolide works across fine fragrance, soaps, shampoos, and home care with excellent stability. Note that it can solidify below 18°C—warm it gently until fully liquid before weighing to avoid crystallisation issues. At typical usage levels of under one percent, it provides a quiet musky glow; push it higher for unmistakable soft-musk presence.

missing_other.title: 1872 Men Type Formula
missing_other.description: This is our exclusive deluxe formula for the surprisingly complex Clive Christian fragrance from master perfumer Geza Schoen (of Escentric Molecules fame). It was released in 2001. Clive Christian has a great reputation for quality and unlike some brands (Amouage and Tom Ford for example) the high price the brand commands really is often justified by the complexity and richesse of their scents. Top Notes: Petitgrain, Lime, Bergamot, Rosemary, Lavender, Galbanum, Pepper, Peach, Pineapple, Mandarin and Nutmeg Heart Notes: Clary Sage, Cyclamen, Marigold, Jasmine and Freesia Base Notes: Virginia Cedar, Musk, Patchouli, Amber, Olibanum and Labdanum Total Lines: 58 Naturals: 19 Bases: 4

missing_other.title: Absolute Ambergris™
missing_other.description: Absolute Ambergris™ is a painstaking reconstruction of 25 year aged Ambergris resin. Use it one for one in vintage formulas to replace 3% ambergris tincture, or as a magnificent and rich animalic ambergris note. This is an essential item for all perfumers as there is nothing on the market that comes close to the elegance and blending power of Absolute Ambergris . Not only do you get the full scent of rich aged ambergris, but also all of the qualities of fixation, blending, and exaltation that natural ambergris gives. This has an indistinguishable scent from natural aged white ambergris tincture but we do not use alcohol in its manufacture. Unlimited use allowed for IFRA 49 and up to 8.3% for IFRA 51 and IFRA 52.

missing_other.title: Aerolide®
missing_other.description: This is the only white musk accord you will ever need. Aerolide® combines the essential high volume musks with the most modern radiant ones in a perfectly blended base. In complete equilibrium and dosed to get the optimum power and nuance that each included musk has to offer, Aerolide® can be used in traces to megadose (over 20%). Aerolide® gives your fragrance vitality, diffusion, radiance and longevity. Aerolide® blends exceptionally well with other musks, particularly Helvetolide ®.

missing_other.title: Aetoxylon “White Oud” Oil
missing_other.description: A large fruiting tree endemic to West Borneo Aetoxylon (also known as Gaharu Buaya or Black Eaglewood) that is becoming extremely desirable as a new wood note in perfume that is particularly synergistic with agarwood and consequently being used in high amounts in Middle Eastern luxury fragrances where it is easier to obtain. Imagine Oud without the intense animalic quality and you have Aetoxylon. More versatile and appealing even to those who don't normally like Oud. Dress it up for a full Agarwood impression, or use it as it for a lovely complex and little-known wood note. To ensure the highest possible quality on the market, we supply the finest quality from MANE in Grasse. Origin: West Borneo Part: Wood

missing_other.title: Agarwood Boya Oil
tags: locale:heat needed for pure. Diluted is still thick.
missing_other.description: Agarwood Boya Oil is the waxy extract of the aquilaria tree taken from uninfected wood (oud oil is distilled exclusively from disease-infected wood). The oil (which presents as a solid wax like orris butter), is gentler and creamier than oud oil but still retains all the characteriistic animal power, with fruity facets. This material is absolutely convincing as the much higher cost oud oil in fragrances and if we are honest, it is probably what makes up the bulk of the oud note in premium oud fragrances these days. It is also known to be used to adulterate real oud to attract higher profits. If you are not an expert, it is wise to stick with the oud extracts from prestige houses like Firmenich which supplies our marvellous Bangladeshi Oud Assam oil , and LMR (maker of this Boya oil) which has an intense but fruitier Vietnamese Oud oil . In fact, this boya oil comes from the same source wood as the LMR Vietnamese oud. Note: This is a creamy, semi-solid wax at room temperature, not a free-flowing liquid, so it needs gentle warming to work with. We offer this perfumery marvel at 10% in a Superessence. To achieve this, we dilute the pure oil in a blend of Benzyl Benzoate (approximately 20%) and IPM (approximately 70%) resulting in a clear and easy to use liquid. Agarwood Boya is true Aquilaria, fully CITES-documented and so for commercial re-selling a re-export certificate may be required by your country. For personal use no certificates are needed. We can assist you with the re-export certificate should you require it, at a cost.

missing_other.title: Akigala Extreme
missing_other.description: Akigalawood is all the rage at Givaudan right now. It is a captive molecule derived from the upcycling of waste from patchouli manufacturing and it has a profile which is peppery and woody and, as is to be expected given the starting material, distinctly patchouli like. It stars in such fragrances as Dark Rebel (2015) by Rodrigo Flores-Roux for Varvatos where it contributes both patchouli and pepper notes. It is also used in Tom Ford's Fougère d'Argent (2018) where it blends with lavender and tonka and features in Quentin Bisch's Purpose (2023) and Guidance (2023) both for Amouage. Akigala Extreme is our interpretation of the Akigalawood captive in the form of a base built around an extraordinary quality (and amount) of molecular distilled patchouli with accents of pepper and dank woods. Use Akigala Extreme in place of patchouli or as an entirely novel new earthy wood note.

missing_other.title: Aldalia
missing_other.description: Aldalia is a beautiful woody aldehydic lily of the valley base used in large quantities in such fragrances as 1000 by Jean Patou and La Rose Jacqueminot by Coty—his first commercial success. It was copied by Roure in the form of Aldehone which was used by Jean Carles in Ma Griffe . At its core is a beautiful rich lily of the valley with accents of rose and cistus. The whole is topped with a big dose of sparkling aldehydes. There is no better way to floralise and enhance a fragrance. Use it in place of a single lily chemical or as part of a more complex heart. Fraterworks Aldalia is a restoration of the original formula, being modified only to comply with EU regulations banning the use of musk ambrette. It is otherwise completely IFRA compliant up to 18.78% of the finished product.

missing_other.title: Aldehone Extra
missing_other.description: Aldehone Extra is Jean Carles' (when working at Roure) artistic replica of Aldalia from Chuit Naef & Cie which we also stock. Aldehone Extra combines aldehydes with a fond of delightful floral and wood materials. Beautifully decorated with citrus and luxurious oriental resins, this is a marvel to behold and despite its historic age, is an astonishingly modern base with great potential for a revival today. Use our demonstration formula of Nuit de Paris (based loosely on the ideas contained in Soir de Paris) to understand the power of Aldehone Extra or use it as a one for replacer in our formula for 1,000 by Patou for a variation on that same theme.

missing_other.title: Amarante
missing_other.description: Amarante is a beautifully balanced floral base that melds muguet, lilac, jasmin and rose notes with a soft woody dry down. Originally created by Marius Reboul for Givaudan in 1924, Amarante was popularised in the 1920s by Henri Almeras who loved it so much he used it in doses well beyond 30% in multiple fragrances for Jean Patou. Its presence can be felt profoundly in Amour Amour (1925). This base is perfect as a core blender around which a distinctive character can be built with nuancers and high impact materials. Usable at up to 10% when seeking IFRA 51 compliance, this is a very versatile base. Amarante is the epitome of classic French elegance.

missing_other.title: Amaretto Saronno
missing_other.description: Amaretto is an Italian liqueur flavoured with the almond-scented kernels of apricots. The drink dates back to the town of Saronno in the 16th century and its true origin is unknown. In addition to apricot kernels, some recipes also add bitter almonds and peach kernels. Most importantly the drink is rounded off with a burnt sugar giving rise to its name ("amara" means bitter in Italian). Our Amaretto Saronno base is a wonderfully boozy top note interpretation of the esteemed drink containing all its nuances and character. It can be used as an alternative almond / benzaldehyde note in a scent and we highly recommend blending it with Coconut Dream and Raspberry Ripple for a “wow” gourmand accord. It also blends incredibly well with Wild Cherry.

missing_other.title: Amazonia™
missing_other.description: Amazonia™ is unspoiled nature distilled. It is the scent of rushing water, wild jungles, untrodden earth and fresh air. It is a boat ride down the Amazon river. If Werner Herzog's masterpiece Fitzcarraldo had a scent, this would be it. Constructed around a combination of radiant and ultra-modern molecules (including Firmenich's Cascalone®), there is nothing old school about Amazonia™; this is pure modernism. Use it as a completed scent with just a touch of musk added, or embellish it with woody molecules and a touch of floralisation as seen in our demonstration formula, Waterfall, below. Amazonia™ blends extraordinarily well with Jasmolactone® Delta , Jasmin Fleurs , Aetoxylon Oil , Orcanox ™ and Gardenia J. Ellis . Demonstration Formula Details Waterfall , a short demonstration formula, combines a simplified Grojsman accord with Cedramber ® for a sheer wood effect, while Helional ® extends and enhances the freshness of an overdose of Amazonia™. A light touch of Gardenia and Champaca Red Absolute adds an exotic floral nuance while MANE's Orcanox adds radiance and longevity and an incredibly modern ambergris note.

missing_other.title: Amber Crave
missing_other.description: AMBER CRAVE® is a profoundly evocative neo-gourmand fragrance base masterfully created by esteemed perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour , exclusively for Fraterworks. Inspired by the relentless allure of indulgence, AMBER CRAVE® transforms the amber accord into an intensely desirable scent experience—an olfactory narrative of insatiable hunger, comfort, and sweet obsession. Top notes: Honey, Liquorice, Davana Heart Notes: Beeswax, Lily of the Valley, Rose, Peach Base notes: Myrrh, Patchouli, Tonka Bean, Benzoin, Vanilla, Ambergris Scent Profile AMBER CRAVE® unfurls with a luscious, irresistible blend of golden honey and sensuous liquorice, enriched by davana’s uniquely fruity, aromatic touch. At its sumptuous heart, beeswax imparts a warm, enveloping texture, harmoniously paired with delicate lily of the valley, romantic rose, and the ripe sweetness of peach. Anchored in a decadent base, AMBER CRAVE® rests on a bed of resinous myrrh, smoky patchouli, rich benzoin, creamy vanilla, luxurious tonka bean, and the subtle allure of ambergris, crafting a scent that embodies the moment when urgency turns into necessity. Perfumery Usage AMBER CRAVE® is expertly crafted to deliver remarkable intensity, warmth, and complexity, making it perfect as an enticing standalone fragrance base or as a sophisticated note within diverse fragrance compositions. Its rich, yet universally appealing gourmand character is designed to blend seamlessly with oriental ambers, luscious fruit accords, and luxurious florals, allowing perfumers to create unforgettable signature scents embraced by all consumers. Process AMBER CRAVE® is crafted through meticulous blending of premium natural essences and advanced aroma molecules. This carefully constructed formula exemplifies Fraterworks’ commitment to excellence in perfumery, realised through the artistic collaboration between Creative Director Jamie Frater and master perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour. Background AMBER CRAVE® forms a crucial part of the Gluttony Tr

missing_other.title: Amber Flux
missing_other.description: AMBER FLUX® is a daringly innovative neo-gourmand fragrance base expertly envisioned by esteemed perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour , exclusively for Fraterworks. Infused with contemporary dynamism and a luxurious oriental amber foundation, AMBER FLUX® reinvents the amber genre with electrifying intensity and a distinctly futuristic edge—where indulgent excess becomes sublime perfection. Top Notes: Cedrat, Toffee, Star Anise Heart Notes: Hibiscus, Magnolia, Metallic Notes Base Notes: Super Amber, Patchouli, Tolu Balsam, Vanilla Bean Scent Profile AMBER FLUX® bursts forth with an exhilarating opening of sparkling cedrat infused with molten toffee, enlivened by star anise's captivating warmth. At its vibrant heart, lush hibiscus and radiant magnolia blend masterfully with innovative metallic notes, imparting a luminous, forward-thinking allure. A luxurious base of super amber harmonises seamlessly with velvety patchouli, rich tolu balsam, and creamy vanilla bean, crafting an opulent, futuristic gourmand fragrance that pulses with vibrant energy and sophisticated indulgence. Perfumery Usage Formulated to deliver outstanding projection, longevity, and complexity, AMBER FLUX® excels as a luxurious standalone neo-gourmand fragrance base or as a dynamic enhancer in contemporary compositions. Its uniquely modern profile blends flawlessly with vibrant citrus accords, sophisticated floral materials, experimental metallic nuances, and avant-garde synthetic ambers—allowing perfumers to innovate boldly at the cutting edge of fragrance design. Process AMBER FLUX® is meticulously crafted from an expertly selected blend of premium natural extracts and state-of-the-art aroma molecules. This sophisticated formulation reflects Fraterworks’ unwavering dedication to quality and innovation, developed through the visionary collaboration of Creative Director Jamie Frater and master perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour. Background AMBER FLUX® completes the Gluttony Triptych, a groundbreaking collection o

missing_other.title: Amber Genesis
missing_other.description: AMBER GENESIS® i s a luxurious neo-gourmand fragrance base masterfully composed by renowned perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour , exclusively for Fraterworks. Inspired by the timeless allure of classical amber bases reimagined through a contemporary lens, this fragrance invites you into a decadent world where temptation becomes tangible. Rich labdanum, velvety vanilla, and opulent rum intertwine elegantly, offering a modern interpretation of the globally coveted amber profile—an olfactory overture to refined indulgence. Top notes: Rum, Caramel, Red Fruit Heart notes: Lily of the Valley, Egyptian Geranium Base notes: Vanilla Bean, Vetiver, Patchouli, Tonka Bean, Labdanum Scent Profile AMBER GENESIS® opens with a provocative introduction of lush dark rum, splashed upon ripe red fruits draped in silken caramel. At its heart, the soft purity of lily of the valley elegantly complements Egyptian geranium, delivering refined floral clarity. Gradually, the fragrance transitions into a sumptuous base, harmonising sweet vanilla bean, deep vetiver, earthy patchouli, comforting tonka bean, and resinous labdanum. The result is a fragrance of captivating warmth, embodying an irresistible, sophisticated temptation. Perfumery Usage AMBER GENESIS® is meticulously formulated to deliver exceptional longevity, depth, and complexity, ideal both as a foundational base and as a sophisticated enhancer within modern fragrance compositions. Its versatile neo-gourmand character blends effortlessly with complementary gourmand ingredients, luxurious resins, aromatic woods, and rich vanillas—providing perfumers expansive creative possibilities. Process AMBER GENESIS® is expertly crafted from a carefully curated palette of premium natural extracts and specialised aroma molecules. This sophisticated blend exemplifies Fraterworks’ unwavering commitment to quality and scent artistry, realised through the visionary collaboration between Creative Director Jamie Frater and master perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour.

missing_other.title: Ambergris Intense™
missing_other.description: The heart of our Absolute Ambergris ™ , we are now making available the pure resin for those who need to go a step further into intensely animalic territory. This product is strong. Incredibly so. It is the most intense ambergris product we sell and the one most like classic aged pure ambergris resin - you would treat this as you would a resinoid made from pure ambergris. Dilute it as you would civet absolute in terms of power for making tinctures, or dose it as is in a fragrance that is bold enough to handle it. Animalic this may be, but it is also one of the most strangely beautiful odours you will ever smell.

missing_other.title: Ambergris Tincture 2%
missing_other.description: It seems almost too good to be true but it isn't! This is a deluxe natural grey ambergris tincture that goes against the norm by being a mainstay of our specialist supplier's catalogue. Through a very long relationship with local ambergris gatherers in New Caledonia, this is a readily available material. Ambergris tincture is marine and animalic with fecal qualities. It's ability to fix (to make something last longer) a perfume is historically renowned and despite its origins as a pathological metabolite of sperm whales which are considered endangered, this is not restricted in perfumery (though some countries do have restrictions on importing the product). While no hard and fast rule ever existed to determine the right amount of tincture to use in a perfume, we recommend around 1% – 3% of the total weight in alcohol. so 100 grams (or mls or drops) of alcohol will have 1–3 grams (or ml or drops) of Ambergris Tincture 2% added. Bear in mind that you can add significantly more tincture if you wish, particularly if you wish to have the ambergris easily perceptible in odour rather than simply as a fixative. If you are seeking a vegan alternative to Ambergris tincture we recommend our acclaimed Ambergris Intense or Absolute Ambergris ™ products.

missing_other.title: Ambra Velvet
missing_other.description: Ambra Velvet captures that precious velvety quality of fine aged ambergris—smooth, warm, and unmistakably luxurious. The amber character sits at the heart, rich without being cloying. Subtle animalic undertones provide the complexity that separates true ambergris effects from simple synthetic alternatives. This classic base has anchors fine fragrances, filling the void left by increasingly scarce and prohibitively expensive natural ambergris. The composition brings together natural animal musks with key ambergris molecules including ambrox, providing radiance and woody warmth—together creating a complete ambergris impression that rounds out fragrances in a way that purely synthetic ambergris replacers can't. Use Ambra Velvet as the foundation for oriental compositions or as a sophisticated fixative in florals and woody blends. It works beautifully from the smallest traces, adding depth and tenacity without overwhelming. The velvety smoothness makes it particularly valuable when you need ambergris warmth without harsh edges.

missing_other.title: Ambranum
missing_other.description: A rich, complex amber compound offering exquisite depth and radiance in perfumery applications. This sophisticated specialty base combines vanillin's sweet warmth with Peru balsam's resinous character, creating a full-bodied amber that enhances compositions with its remarkable persistence and dimension. Ambranum provides the perfect foundation for oriental, woody and amber fragrances, adding both complexity and longevity. Its balanced profile works beautifully with labdanum, vanilla, and woody notes, making it an exceptional building block for distinctive signature scents while ensuring excellent performance in fine fragrance applications. If you like this product you'll love our own Ambre Royal which is extremely similar in profile but enriched with luxurious natural oils and absolutes. Ambranum makes a great foundation material and works very well with the following: Ginger Oil , Vetikolacetat , Rose Oxide Laevo , Ylang Ylang Extra , Veticoeur and many more.

missing_other.title: Ambre Aegyptus
missing_other.description: Ambre Aegyptus is the scent of Ancient Egypt. Weave a magical tale of Ancient Egypt into the fabric of your fragrances with this beautiful modern amber base. Constructed around a heart of intensely sweet vanilla tempered with exotic mandarin and crowned with rare herbs and precious oriental resins, this amber is a fragrant treasure. Dazzling white musks meld with the latest radiant wood molecules in perfect balance with luscious Mysore sandalwood, sweet patchouli and aged cedarwood. Jasmine absolute from the grand Nile Delta recalls the anointing of the king-gods as they were laid to rest in the gilded tombs of the ancient city of the dead: Abydos. Use Ambre Aegyptus alone in overdose as a more beautiful and interesting version of Ambre Sultan by Serge Lutens, or use it as the foundation of a magnificent modern oriental fragrance needing little more than a tweak in a novel direction. Usable at a whopping 25.37% of your finished product. “The only lamp of this lone hour Is glimmering in Zuleika's tower. Yes! there is light in that lone chamber, And o'er her silken Ottoman Are thrown the fragrant beads of amber, O'er which her fairy fingers ran; Near these, with emerald rays beset, (How could she thus that gem forget?) Her mother's sainted amulet, Whereon engraved the Koorsee text, Could smooth this life, and win the next;” — The Bride of Abydos, by Lord Byron, 1813.

missing_other.title: Ambre Doux
missing_other.description: A delicate liquid amber base first created by Roure in the 1930s and used in Tabu. This is a light and airy amber based on labdanum and vanilla notes without the characteristic dominance of citrus making it a wonderful fixative and enricher of those more common ambers such as Ambreine Samuelson and Opoponax Doux . The sheer nature of this amber makes it decidedly modern and it can most certainly be used easily in that context. Pair with Ambre Royale in overdose with sweet notes of ethyl hydrocinnamate, phenyl propyl alcohol and ethyl safranate .

missing_other.title: Ambre Royal
missing_other.description: Supremely beautiful, Ambre Royal is a modern amber base built around vanilla, citrus, resins and woods. It can be used in small amounts to impart a wonderfully sweet dry down or in overdose for a novel new take on an oriental scent. Ambre Royal contains radiant modern musks and luxurious aged naturals woods and floral absolutes. This base is essential for all perfumers — it is a fragrance unto itself. Safe at up to 100% of the finished product!

missing_other.title: Ambre Solide (Ambre 83)
missing_other.description: Ambre Solide is a classical amber fixative base built around resins and vanilla with an intensely floral note dominated by floral absolutes, including jasmine and rose, and civet. Depending on environmental conditions, Ambre Solide is a solid paste or highly viscous liquid. It can be added directly to your formulas or diluted — we recommend 50% in DEP. This is the original Ambre 83 Solide of De Laire which was used in Chanel No 5 in combination with Ambreol , a balsamic vanilla base. It was also used by Ernest Beaux in Bois des Îles and by Jean Carles in Miss Dior . Due to the high content of the permitted purified musk ketone, this product can be used at up to 7% of your finished product in Europe and 40% in other countries for compliance with IFRA. NOTE: This product contains no musk xylene or other prohibited materials.

missing_other.title: Ambreine Biolandes
missing_other.description: A thick, honeyed amber opens with warm balsamic sweetness before revealing a smoky leather undertone and faint olibanum dryness. The overall impression is of something ancient and precious — amber that glows rather than shouts. Viscous and deeply comforting on the blotter. Where labdanum absolute can overwhelm a formula, this extract channels the same raw material into a more refined, focused amber impression. Oriental accords take on a darker, more sensual foundation. Your leather and incense compositions gain a complexity from this extract that sets it apart from standard labdanum absolute. Low doses in a chypre or fougere furnish amber warmth without tipping the balance. Go full oriental by stacking it with benzoin resinoid, vanilla absolute, frankincense and myrrh for a sacred resin effect. The smoky-sweet facet also grounds oud compositions that need a softer anchor. Owing to its thickness we sell this pure and diluted to 50% in natural TEC, making it easier to use when working in natural perfumery. NOTE: This is a specialty extract of labdanum by Biolandes and should not be confused with Ambreine Samuelson (and the natural variant of the same) which is a historic base of citrus, resins and vanilla.

missing_other.title: Ambreine Natural
missing_other.description: 100% Natural and ISO 9235 compliant. The famed Ambreine Samuelson base back from the golden age to add beauty and opulence to your perfumes — but now all natural! Fraterworks Ambreine is loaded with Mysore sandalwood, resins and pure oils and absolutes. Ambreine type bases are rich base notes built on a harmony of citrus oils, vanilla, resins and woods. Ambreine Natural by Fraterworks in traces, adds a balsamic warmth to a scent's dry down and in overdose it imparts a wonderful ambery quality felt through the whole life of the fragrance. This is a perfume unto itself. Beloved by Messrs Coty and Guerlain, it can now be part of your creative toolkit. This version is 100% natural, being composed entirely of luxurious essential oils, absolutes and certified natural isolates. Just floralise and add unadulterated ethanol to have a complete 100% natural fragrance! For the standard version, go here . NOTE: This product is a base composed of multiple materials. It is not related to ambergris.

missing_other.title: Ambreine Rustica
missing_other.description: This is the marvelous agrestical ambreine base used at over 40% of the total formula of Coty's last perfume La Fougeraie au Crépuscule (formula below named Twilight Fern ). Whilst most ambers focus solely on the resinous and vanilla qualities, this base places a stronger emphasis on the herbal notes. This is the closest thing you will get to a top note ambreine base. This base is loaded with Mysore sandalwood, natural tonka bean and many other absolutes and oils. If you're not sure which amber base or bases you need, take a look at our handy guide to understanding ambers . NOTE : This product is a base composed of multiple materials. It is not related to ambergris .

missing_other.title: Ambreine Samuelson
missing_other.description: The famed Ambreine Samuelson base back from the past to add beauty and opulence to your perfumes! Fraterworks Ambreine Sameulson (formerly known simply as "Ambreine") is loaded with Mysore sandalwood and pure oils and absolutes. Ambreine type bases are rich base notes built on a harmony of citrus oils, vanilla, resins and woods. In traces Ambreine adds a balsamic warmth to a scent's dry down and in overdose it imparts a wonderful ambery quality felt through the whole life of the fragrance. Ambreine by Fraterworks is a perfume unto itself. Beloved by Messrs Coty and Guerlain, it can now be part of your creative toolkit. This base is also similar to the other great ambreine type base Coralys . This product is a base composed of multiple materials. It is not related to ambergris. We also have a 100% natural and vegan version of this base which is available here . NOTE : This product may partially crystallise at low temperatures. Gently heat prior to use.

missing_other.title: Ambreol
missing_other.description: Ambreol was a classical vanilla base, similar to Ambreine Samuelson (our Ambreine ) and Opoponax Doux but with a pronounced vanilla note. In overdose and balanced with Sephora (our Sophira base), it was the key of Tabac Blond and was a vital component of both Bois des Iles and Chanel No 5. Fraterworks' restored Ambreol is rich with mysore sandalwood, natural vanilla, tonka bean absolute and many resins and essential oils. IFRA safe at up to 17.7% of the finished product.

missing_other.title: Ambrette Seed Oil
missing_other.description: The seeds of this hibiscus-like flowering plant contain one of the treasures of the perfumery world: ambrettolide — one of the few natural non-animal musks. With a delicate raspberry nuance, this rich oil adds softness, muskiness, and radiance to every blend. A trace can completely remove the chemical sharpness from alcohol making it a wonderful alternative to Ambergris. Our Ambrette Seed Oil is manufactured in France by LMR, one of the finest makers and suppliers of precious essential oils and absolutes. There is no denying that you'll need a swooning couch when you see the price tag on this beauty! Therefore, we also offer it at 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate, keeping it ISO 9235 compliant and making it more cost effective. Origin: France Part: Seeds Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Ambrette Seed Tincture 20%
missing_other.description: Being one of the few natural plant musks, ambrette seed is absolutely essential for perfumers and those seeking all natural or vegan musks. But it comes at a very hefty price tag. In classical perfumery another option existed, one very often overlooked today: tincture of ambrette seed. For a significantly lower cost you get all the smoothing and fixing power of ambrette seeds. Ambrette Seed Tincture 20% is pale yellow in colour and very light in scent, but don't be fooled, its magic is not in its smell, but in the fact it contains natural ambrettolide, one of the most diffusive and powerful musks in modern perfumery. As with all our tinctures, this is made with 100% pure and natural alcohol produced with glacial waters from the Southern Alps. The absence of denaturants allow this to be used in natural perfumery, both EU and US standards.

missing_other.title: Ambrexol™
missing_other.description: Ambrexol features the addictive and subtly animalic sweetness of long aged wild ambergris. Once you smell this amazing product, you'll want to add it to everything. Ambrexol™ is an alternative to the old Fixateur® 404 product of Firmenich® which was temporarily replaced by a dilution of racemic Cetalox® under the new code name of Fixateur 505 . Ambrexol is softer and less animalic (though it does still maintain a soft animal warmth). Fraterworks Ambrexol™ pairs the nearest equivalent of ambrox classique with traces of supporting materials to honour the power and magical effect of Fixateur with a more rounded scent of ambergris. Just a touch is all that's needed to turn any blend into a perfume.

missing_other.title: Amyris “Signature” Oil, Haiti
missing_other.description: Amyris wood oil (often colloquially referred to as West Indian Sandalwood and historically as santal citron) is a soft creamy wood oil which frequently finds itself at the heart of Sandalwood recreations alongside Guaiacwood oil and cedarwood oil. But it should not be seen as a replacer oil because in its own right it has a beautiful rich complexity which blends with all the usual modern wood chemicals like Orbitone , Iso E Super and the ambers and super ambers. Our Amyris is particularly elegant and smooth, coming from a single origin harvest in Haiti by Payan Bertrand a company we hold in the highest esteem when it comes to naturals. Note: Owing to scarcity of supply, the cost of Amyris oil has recently increased significantly.

missing_other.title: Angel
missing_other.description: Compound Angel is our internal formula for the original 1992 Angel by Thierry Mugler – not the later reformulations. Created by Olivier Cresp and Yves de Chiris at Quest International, this is the fragrance that invented the modern gourmand: an amber vanilla built on an unprecedented overdose of patchouli against caramel, praline and chocolate. This compound reproduces the original composition as it was launched, before successive reformulations thinned the patchouli and flattened the sweetness. The base is dense and earthy, wrapped in vanilla, tonka bean, caramel and chocolate, with the maltol lift that made the original so instantly recognisable. The top notes of bergamot, mandarin, cassis and cotton candy open with an almost edible sugar rush, while a heart of honey, red berries, blackberry, plum, peach and apricot sits over jasmine, rose and lily-of-the-valley. The result is a monumental, unapologetically divisive fragrance with enormous projection and legendary longevity – exactly as it smelled in 1992. This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Because it contains Lilial, it is not EU compliant. Top Notes: Bergamot, Mandarin Orange, Cassis, Melon, Coconut, Cotton Candy, Jasmine Heart Notes: Honey, Red Berries, Blackberry, Plum, Apricot, Peach, Nutmeg, Caraway, Rose, Lily-of-the-Valley, Orchid Base Notes: Patchouli, Vanilla, Tonka Bean, Caramel, Chocolate, Praline, Amber, Musk

missing_other.title: Angelica Glauca Oil
missing_other.description: Angelica glauca oil takes the familiar angelica character and pushes it somewhere darker and wilder. The earthy, rooty depth is far more pronounced, with an ancient, almost subterranean quality. Subtle celery-lovage sweetness emerges alongside warm spice, but the dominant impression is brooding, untouched earth. This oil brings a dark, almost archaeological earthiness to orientals and chypres. Pair it with oakmoss and patchouli for a damp, forested accord, or blend it into your amber bases where its ancient rootiness adds extraordinary dimension. Its fixative power is remarkable. Use angelica glauca to ground floral compositions with earthy darkness. A trace transforms rose accords into something enigmatic and deep. It fills a similar role to lovage and costus root but with a quality all its own — brooding, ancient, and endlessly tenacious on the blotter. If you know Angelica archangelica root oil — musky, peppery, amber-like — you will recognise glauca as family, but a wilder branch. The earthy depth is far more pronounced, the musk gives way to something darker and more ancient, and the tenacity is even greater. Fraterworks carries both, and they complement each other beautifully. Visual Differences Angelica glauca and Angelica archangelica are easily distinguished in the field. The European species, A. archangelica , is the larger and bolder of the two — a tall, robust biennial reaching up to 2.5 metres, with bright yellow-green leaves, thick fleshy stems, and large globular umbels of greenish-white flowers. A. glauca , the Himalayan species, is a more refined perennial growing to around 1–2 metres, and takes its name from the distinctive bluish-grey, waxy bloom on the undersides of its broader, oval leaflets — a feature entirely absent in its European cousin. Its flowers also set it apart, ranging from white through yellow to purple, whereas A. archangelica flowers are consistently greenish-white to pale yellow. In short, if A. archangelica is the big, bright, a

missing_other.title: Angelica Root Oil
missing_other.description: Angelica root oil opens with a distinctive peppery-green freshness that quickly reveals a rich, musky-amber heart unlike anything else in perfumery. The scent carries an unmistakable earthy quality — damp forest floor mingled with warm spice. Naturally occurring musk compounds shared with ambrette seed give this oil its remarkable tenacity. This is one of perfumery's great fixatives, capable of anchoring compositions while adding mysterious depth. It excels in chypres alongside oakmoss and patchouli, where it contributes an earthy-musky foundation. Fougères gain complexity from its herbal-amber character, and oriental bases benefit from its warm, almost animalic undertones. Use angelica root oil sparingly — its power sneaks up on you and can dominate a blend over time. Pair with vetiver for earthy richness or with clary sage for herbaceous sophistication. In citrus colognes, a trace adds unexpected depth and lasting power without announcing itself. Angelica Root Oil vs Angelica Seed Oil Both oils come from Angelica archangelica but deliver very different results. The root oil is dark, earthy, and distinctly musky thanks to naturally occurring musk compounds shared with ambrette seed — it is one of perfumery's great natural fixatives. The seed oil is lighter, fresher, and more peppery with a sweet anisic undertone — a top-to-heart note that adds herbal spark rather than musky depth. Where the root oil anchors, the seed oil lifts. Blending the two gives you the complete angelica spectrum from bright peppery top to musky earthy base.

missing_other.title: Angelica Seed Oil
missing_other.description: Angelica seed oil opens with a strong, fresh, peppery-green burst that feels almost bracing at full strength. Beneath that initial rush sits a sweet, almost anisic undertone — the signature that makes it immediately recognisable. The impression is bright, herbal, and surprisingly clean. Use it to add peppery-green spark to chypres, fougères, and citrus colognes — accords where you need herbal lift without heaviness. It sits in the top-to-heart transition, providing aromatic freshness that complements oakmoss, clary sage, and bergamot. Pair it with the root oil for a complete angelica signature. Both angelica oils are among the rarest essential oils in commerce — world production of each has historically been under a ton annually. Evaluate at 10% dilution; the peppery top overwhelms at full strength. The seed and root come from the same plant but deliver entirely different effects. Angelica Seed Oil vs Angelica Root Oil Both oils come from Angelica archangelica but deliver very different results. The seed oil is light, fresh, and peppery with a sweet anisic undertone — a top-to-heart note that adds herbal spark. The root oil is darker, earthier, and distinctly musky thanks to naturally occurring musk compounds shared with ambrette seed. Where the seed oil lifts, the root oil anchors — it is one of perfumery's great natural fixatives. Blending the two gives you the complete angelica spectrum from bright peppery top to musky earthy base.

missing_other.title: Animalia™ CMP
missing_other.description: Animalia CMP is the Fraterworks restoration of the magnificent original Animalis base of the 20th century. Featured in such fragrances as Cabochard , Men's Club , Obsession, Opium and Bourjois's Mais Oui. Use it as a one for one replacer for Animalis to get a more luxurious and elegant result. Loaded with natural woods and precious spices, Animalia can enhance any fragrance. See the demo formula for an Aramis -like gentleman's scent. Once you've smelled this base you will never reach for the Animalis Hypo 27 or Animalis 1745-3 again. Use up to 1.65% of your finished product for IFRA 51. Animalia CMP contains no animal products.

missing_other.title: Animusk™ Extra
missing_other.description: Animusk Extra is our restoration of Chevral, the incredible base by Bernard Chant which he used in numerous fragrances. Animusk contains natural animal musks and is IFRA and EU compliant. This base is, in our opinion, the finest animalic musk ever created, far surpassing Animalis (our Animalia™ CMP ). In small amounts this base imparts a wonderfully elegant and smooth animalic note, far gentler and kinder than pure animal musk but decidedly more interesting than synthetic musk. It was used in the great Aramis, Van Cleef and Arpels for Men, Drakaar Noir, Kouros and many others.

missing_other.title: Apple Supreme
missing_other.description: Every bit of crunchy apple that you need. This base is an instant "apple shampoo" note for me, taking me right back to stingy eyes in the bath as a child. This can be used in overdose — up to 100% in perfumes in fact, or as a nice top note modifier when something more interesting than Verdox is wanted. This is one you will find yourself opening just to take a guilty-pleasure sniff from time to time.

missing_other.title: Armoise Heart
missing_other.description: Armoise Heart is cool, sharp and camphoraceous, with a minty bite and the bitter, green freshness of wormwood. Underneath runs a dry, resinous pine note. It hits the nose with real force, clean and bracing rather than dusty or muddy. A little brings instant freshness and green lift to aromatic structures. Use it to sharpen fougères and chypres, to give colognes a herbal snap, and to add a cool, wild edge to lavender and rosemary. It works best in traces, where its diffusive power reads as energy rather than bitterness.

missing_other.title: Armoise Oil, Morocco
missing_other.description: From the same family as Tarragon and common wormwood, Armoise (mugwort or artemesia) oil is wonderfully thujonic (the characteristic odour of Absinthe which is made from Artemsia absinthium). Armoise features in such wonderful masculines as Polo (1978) and Safari for Men (1992), Kouros (1981), Paco Rabanne Pour Homme (1973), Azzaro Pour Homme (1978), Aramis (1966), Drakkar Noir (1982) and many many more. Blends well with tarragon , galbanum , lavender , vanilla notes , cardamom , clovebud , oakmoss . Origin: Morocco Part: Leaves Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Artemal™
missing_other.description: Artemal™ is our reconstruction of an original IFF internal masterpiece named Amaro, a base of fresh forest notes with herbs, spices and masculine florals. It is one of the finest green type bases we know and provides the key olfactory character to Polo Green. On its own this base is practically an entire fragrance and would be especially suited to forest fresh fragrances. Add a percent or two to a body wash, shampoo or conditioner base and you have a luxurious fresh product ready to go.

missing_other.title: Asparagus Twigs Absolute
missing_other.description: Asparagus Twigs Absolute (produced from the foliage and twigs of the plant, not the green spears we eat) opens with astonishing complexity—dry tobacco leaves mingle with bitter cocoa dust. This isn't the sulfurous vegetable you'd expect. Instead, woody stems yield cigar-box richness with earthy undertones reminiscent of aged oakmoss, creating immediate intrigue and sophistication. This absolute bridges disparate olfactory families with remarkable finesse. Deploy it to connect tobacco accords with gourmand bases, adding mysterious depth without sweetness. The subtle animalic-valerian facet makes it invaluable for modern oud compositions where its sour tang enhances natural wood complexities without dominating. Work with this material at 0.1-1% to exploit its fixative properties and unique character. It excels when paired with tobacco absolute for ultra-realistic cigar accords, or combine with cocoa and labdanum for avant-garde leather-gourmands. The absolute's unexpected profile rewards experimental perfumers seeking distinctive signatures. This absolute transforms traditional tobacco compositions by eliminating fruity damascone characters, instead delivering dry, masculine cigar-box woodiness. You achieve remarkable oud synergies by exploiting its unique sour valerian aspect, which harmonises beautifully with acidic Assam oud oils. Layer it with vetiver and patchouli to amplify its oakmoss-like structural properties in IFRA-compliant chypre bases.

missing_other.title: Attar Base N.18
missing_other.description: Attar Base N.18 is a one-for-one drop-in replacement for Dioctyl Phthalate — a now-prohibited chemical formerly used in very large quantities as an odourless direct replacer for sandalwood oil due to cost. For some time, DOP was the go-to carrier for attars and other blends, but with its prohibition, perfumers have had to look at alternatives such as DPG overdoses (note: in most cases these are being used instead of alcohol in non-alcohol perfumes — hence their use at up to 80% in some cases). However, DPG on its own is not the best carrier, as it lacks a silken hand-feel and cosmetic appeal. Attar Base N.18 gives you that hand-feel and longevity on the skin, while also supporting your formula with a touch of natural antioxidant and an antibacterial blend to combat the negative effects of using a dipper which touches the skin and then goes back into the bottle of perfume. Fraterworks Attar Bases Once upon a time, an attar was a co-distillation of precious botanical matter, traditionally done using two stills. Nowadays the term has broadened considerably to include blends of plant extracts and aroma chemicals diluted in sandalwood as a carrier oil. Cost and rarity make pure sandalwood difficult to justify, so alternatives are needed. Fraterworks Attar Bases are designed to be used as ingredients in precious mukhallats (the Arabian term for a blend of naturals and aroma chemicals — in other words, a perfume base) and other fragrance forms. Each Attar Base has different nuances, but the core objective remains: compliance with IFRA and EU regulations at concentrations up to at least 80%.

missing_other.title: Attar Base N.27
missing_other.description: Attar Base N.27 is a sandalwood/oud-character carrier — not a neutral replacement like Attar Base N.18, but an active participant in your composition. Where N.18 is designed to disappear, N.27 is designed to evoke the creamy, woody warmth of traditional sandalwood oil at a fraction of the cost. The result is a carrier that behaves like sandalwood oil on the skin: the slow, radiant diffusion, the creamy warmth, the way it lifts and supports everything blended into it. If you've ever used genuine Mysore sandalwood as a carrier and mourned the cost, N.27 is what you've been waiting for. Use N.27 wherever your formula calls for sandalwood oil as a carrier or diluent — in attars, mukhallats, and oil-based perfumery of all kinds. It gives you the character of sandalwood without the extraordinary price tag, while also supporting your formula with a touch of natural antioxidant and an antibacterial blend to combat the negative effects of using a dipper which touches the skin and then goes back into the bottle of perfume. To use, simply add 20% (or more!) of your favourite Mukhallat blend (or oud oil, attars, etc) to 80% of Attar Base N.27. Alternatively use it as an incredibly cost effective sandalwood alternative that will cause any oriental blend to bloom. This can also be used in an alcohol perfume in the same way Sandalwood oil is used. Fraterworks Attar Bases Once upon a time, an attar was a co-distillation of precious botanical matter, traditionally done using two stills. Nowadays the term has broadened considerably to include blends of plant extracts and aroma chemicals diluted in sandalwood as a carrier oil. Cost and rarity make pure sandalwood difficult to justify, so alternatives are needed. Fraterworks Attar Bases are designed to be used as ingredients in precious mukhallats (the Arabian term for a blend of naturals and aroma chemicals — in other words, a perfume base) and other fragrance forms. Each Attar Base has different nuances, but the core objective remain

missing_other.title: Baume Ambré
missing_other.description: Baume Ambré is a co-distillation — benzoin resin distilled directly onto gurjun balsam, producing aromatic compounds that neither material creates alone. This is not a blend. When two botanicals are distilled together, heat and steam generate new molecules at the interface, yielding a material with qualities impossible to achieve by simply mixing the finished oils. The result here is benzoin transformed: still sweet, still vanillic, but carrying the memory of hot stone and burning paper. The classic benzoin sweetness is immediately recognisable, but the gurjun co-distillation pushes it somewhere strange and nostalgic. A faint plastic edge adds tension to the sweetness. As the top notes vaporise, a cinnamic warmth emerges underneath — tying Baume Ambré back to the ancient balsamic family while keeping it unpredictable. The smoke quality is not birch or cade but papier d'Arménie: delicate, sweet, devotional. Use it as a base anchor in orientals where standard benzoin feels too simple. It bridges the gap between clean vanillic sweetness and the darker, more complex resinous territory that modern niche compositions demand. Layer it beneath florals to give them warmth without heaviness. Note that in colder climes, Baume Ambré may have some separation. It is simply the heavier benzoic acid from the benzoin fraction. Gentle warmth will homogenise the material.

missing_other.title: Bay Oil, Dominica
missing_other.description: Bay oil from Dominica hits the nose with a bold, sweet-spicy warmth built on rich eugenol. Beneath the clove-like character you find a fresh, almost lemony lift, balanced by sweet-balsamic undertones. The effect is immediately recognisable—warm, rounded, and distinctly Caribbean. This oil defines the classic bay rum accord that has anchored masculine grooming since the 19th century. It excels in aftershaves and hair tonics, but sells itself short if confined there alone. Blend it with lavender or lavandin for a traditional Rondeletia-type accord, or pair with citrus oils, petitgrain, and ylang-ylang for sophisticated colognes with real backbone. Push bay oil into modern territory by combining it with oakmoss and patchouli in spicy chypres. A few drops transform oriental bases, adding lived-in warmth without heaviness. Don't confuse your bays This West Indian bay oil ( Pimenta racemosa , Myrtaceae family) is an entirely different material from bay laurel ( Laurus nobilis , Lauraceae family), the culinary herb with a sharp, medicinal, cineole-heavy profile. It is also distinct from pimento berry oil ( Pimenta dioica )—commonly called allspice—which shares the same botanical family but produces a rounder, warmer, more cinnamon-clove spice character from its berries rather than leaves.

missing_other.title: Beeswax Absolute, Glacé
missing_other.description: Beeswax is a wonderful animalic product for perfumery. It contributes a softness and natural rounding of scents as well as being a long lasting fixative. The biggest annoyance with Beeswax Absolute is the difficult in dissolving it and the fact that it is mostly insoluble waxes that must ultimately be chilled and filtered from your fragrance. But not so with our incredible Beeswax Absolute Glacé from LMR. In a special process LMR processes this absolute with a technique they call glazing. That process involves freezing the beeswax absolute and removing insoluble matter so what you are left with is pure beeswax odour with guaranteed solubility. Discarding nearly 75% of the non-useful material does come at a price: this absolute is an incredibly expensive product. But oh what a product it is. We love it, we use it and we heartily recommend it. In fact, this is the only Beeswax absolute we use at Fraterworks and Frater Perfumes; nothing else comes close in quality and usability. Splurge: your fragrances are worth it. “Their musk encroaches, circle after circle, A well of scents almost too dense to breathe in." — Sylvia Plath, The Beekeeper's Daughter Origin: France Part: Beeswax Process: Solvent extraction followed by speciality freeze filtering

missing_other.title: Beginner's Journey Kit
missing_other.description: The first of the Fraterworks' Journey Kits gives you a broad overview of our most essential bases, naturals and aroma chemicals. Each kit contains forty-six products including ten of our best selling bases, ten prestige naturals, and twenty-six aroma chemicals, including the most common crystallines. All liquids come in our high quality German-made glass bottles with naturals weighing 4g and aroma chemicals and bases weighing 5g each. Each Beginner's Journey Kit comes with 40 high quality single-use transfer pipettes and, when new stock arrives, 100 mouillettes (scent strips)

missing_other.title: Benzoin Siam Resinoid 50% TEC
missing_other.description: This is a wonderfully sweet and fine benzoin resinoid made from only Grade A tears (the highest quality). Furthermore, to maintain its natural certifiability it is diluted to 50% in natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless diluent isolated from citrus oil). Many Benzoin products have chemical side odours (or perhaps worse, no odour at all) because they are produced in a relatively careless way owing to their use more as a fixative than a note in itself, but this Benzoin from V. MANE Fils pays homage to the raw material — being made with as much dignity and care as it would receive if it were the finest rose extract. Origin: Laos Variety: Styrax Tonkinensis Part: Exudate Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Benzoin Siam “Signature” Tincture 20%
missing_other.description: Fraterworks manufactures this superior tincture using completely cold alcohol and highest quality wild-harvested benzoin Siam gum. The drug (raw gum) is the highest grade and our tincturing process uses the finest odourless food grade alcohol only. Absolutely no synthetic plasticisers, denaturants or diluents are used, resulting in a totally natural product by ISO 9235 standards. This is the gold standard of benzoin extracts and every care has been taken to ensure consistent excellence in every drop. In addition to being a perfumery material, Benzoin Siam Tincture was a starting material for Friar's Balsam , a medicinal compound invented in the 1760s by Dr Johua Ward who combined it with smaller amounts of styrax resin and the bitter aloe ferox (a plant related to aloe vera). Fraterworks' Benzoin Siam Tincture is not produced in a food safe or pharmaceutical environment and as such is not be taken internally . This is not a medicine and is not made according to the USP standards. Combining this tincture in a ratio of 1:10 up to 1:50 with distilled water will give you Lac Virginis (virgin's milk), an olden days cosmetic to brighten a young lady's complexion. The tincture may louche upon blending with water. Origin: Siam (Thailand) Variety: Styrax tonkinensis Part: Gum Method: Cold ethanol tincture

missing_other.title: Benzoin Sumatra Resinoid 50% TEC
missing_other.description: Benzoin Sumatra resinoid has a warm, balsamic aroma with a distinctive blend of sweet vanilla, smoky undertones, and a spicy edge, largely due to its content of cinnamic acid alongside benzoic acid. This cinnamic acid contributes a subtle cinnamon-like sharpness that sets it apart from the more common Siamese variety, giving Benzoin Sumatra a rugged, slightly resinous depth with a hint of smokiness In comparison to Benzoin Siam, Sumatra's thicker, darker consistency and reddish hue further reflect its robust character, appealing to perfumers seeking a bold, anchoring base note. Benzoin Sumatra is ideal for grounding spicy, oriental, or woody perfume compositions. Due to its thickness, we offer it at 50% in natural TEC making it ISO 2935 compliant.

missing_other.title: Bergamot Oil FCF, Côte d'Ivoire
missing_other.description: Forget everything you know about bergamot. Côte d'Ivoire bergamot grows under equatorial sun in West Africa, and it shows. The oil opens with recognisable bergamot brightness but quickly reveals a warmer, rounder, more honeyed character than any Italian oil you have smelled. The sharp green-terpenic edge of Calabrian bergamot is absent here. This is an LMR captive — a material specially offered to us and unavailable to independent perfumers through normal channels. The terroir shifts the entire balance of the oil toward tropical-fruity warmth. Where Italian bergamot leads with crisp aldehydic freshness, this leads with sun-ripened sweetness and a soft floral undertone that sits comfortably in the heart, not just the top. It lasts noticeably longer on a strip than its European counterpart. Use it when you want bergamot's signature without bergamot's sharpness. It excels in oriental-citrus fusions, amber accords that need a golden top note, and any composition where a conventional bergamot feels too cold or too brief. This is a genuine rarity — treat it as one.

missing_other.title: Bergamot Oil FCF, Organic
missing_other.description: This is bergamot for people who already know what bergamot smells like and want more of it. The organic cultivation produces a fuller, more three-dimensional oil — the familiar bright citrus top is there, but underneath it you find a richer floral-sweet body and a smoother, less terpenic drydown than conventional FCF. Compare it directly to our CAPUA 1880 Bergamot "Superior" Oil FCF — both are excellent, but the organic takes a different path. The linalyl acetate heart is broader and more expressive. The green-peppery facets soften into something almost tea-like. This is the bergamot you choose when the formula is simple enough that every ingredient has to justify its presence. Use it wherever you would use standard bergamot FCF and want the quality to show. It earns its place in stripped-back soliflores, transparent colognes, and any composition where the citrus top note IS the story. Furocoumarin-free and skin-safe without compromise.

missing_other.title: Bergamot Oil FCF, Terpeneless
missing_other.description: Despite appearing in, arguably, the most famous perfume in the world ( Chanel No 5 ), Terpeneless Bergamot is virtually unknown today. It has the characteristic delicate Earl Grey tea quality that we all love in a quality Bergamot oil, but in a concentrated form, without the sharp fresh notes. When would you consider using terpeneless bergamot over regular? When you have a perfume that needs an elegant and refined bergamot note more for its scent than its top note lightness. Fragrances designed for very high parfum or extrait concentrations (such as No 5's original 38% strength) tend to have a different ratio of notes, with top notes being reduced in favour of heart and base. That is where bergamot terpeneless shines and it is the logic behind Ernest Beaux's decision to use it. This Bergamot oil is free of furocoumarins, making it safe for use in large quantities. Origin: Calabria, Italy Variety: Citrus sinensis Part: Peel Method: Cold pressed at source and molecule distilled

missing_other.title: Bergamot Oil Melito
missing_other.description: In Melito di Porto Salvo (25km from Reggio) there can be found two treasures — the first is the holy image of the Madonna of Porto Salvo, and the second the locals call "Green Gold"… Bergamot Melito. The finest bergamot in the world grows in the Calabrian region of Italy and Melito di Porto Salvo is home to the most revered crops. For that reason we present it here in its purest form. This is not bergaptene or furocoumarin free. This is 100% pure and natural green bergamot oil and you will never find better. Hand selected by Fraterworks, this is the very same quality bergamot used by master perfumers such as Jean Carles, Ernest Beaux, Edmond Roudnitska, the heads of the House of Guerlain and many others. Fortunately, while IFRA restricts the amount you can use of this oil, it is still perfectly permissable up to 0.4% of your finished fragrance. Max it out and then top up with our superior Bergamot Oil FCF Calabria which is, in itself, a masterpiece of modern citrus meets molecular science. Origin: Melito, Calabria (Italy) Part: Peel Method: Cold pressed at source

missing_other.title: Bergamot Oil Spugna, Calabria
missing_other.description: Spugnato bergamot oil is richer, rounder, and more floral than any machine-pressed bergamot you have smelled. The hand-sponging preserves delicate jasmine-like sweetness and an oily-herbaceous depth that industrial extraction destroys. The drydown is warm, tobacco-balsamic, and remarkably persistent for a citrus oil. Spugnato means 'sponged' — the rind is pressed by hand against a natural sea sponge, with no machines, no metal, no heat. Traditionally the sfumatori worked through the night, protecting the delicate essence from the Calabrian sun. Before machines arrived in 1840, this was the only way bergamot oil existed. Fraterworks is currently the only supplier on earth stocking spugnato bergamot oil. Ongoing supply is not guaranteed — treat this as a rare, one-off treasure. Once it is gone, there is no certainty it will return. Dior used oil extracted with this method in a one-off limited supply of their Sauvage fragrance (not Eau Sauvage) and commissioned CAPUA 1880 to produce the oil. The process was so time consuming that even CAPUA will no longer make this oil on demand and Dior now utilised the same highest quality FCF Bergamot that we stock.

missing_other.title: Bergamot Reggio
missing_other.description: Bergamot Reggio is a reconstruction of Calabrian bergamot pure and natural. As an alternative to bergaptene free oil this base is vastly superior, offering more personality and vibrance than the chemically degraded natural. Surpassing all other bergamot bases in quality, this is a one for one replacement for the natural oil that can be used with virtually no restrictions as it is IFRA compliant up to 88% of the finished product!

missing_other.title: Bergamot “Superior” Oil, FCF
missing_other.description: CAPUA 1880's Calabrian bergamot oil FCF (furocoumarin* free) is produced using a highly specialised cold extraction process that removes restricted furocoumarins (including bergapten) without any damage to the oil. Because of the process used, this bergamot oil remains 100% natural. There is no doubt this is one of the highest quality FCF bergamot oils on the market and the closest to the classic pure and natural oil. It is so good it even retains some of its true colour! Most furocoumarin free bergamot from other suppliers is modified with a chemical process involving caustic soda; as a result the oil is often damaged to a point that while it may still smell of bergamot, it lacks much of the beauty of pure bergamot oil. Furthermore, caustic treated oil may often not be considered natural. You will not find a finer and more true to the classic Italian green bergamot oil than Fraterworks' bergaptene free Bergamot “Superior” Oil. Our oil can't be beaten, and neither can our price! * Furocoumarins (or furanocoumarins) are a type of molecule that react with human DNA in the skin, causing changes which makes the skin extremely sensitive to sun damage. Some common furocoumarins are bergapten, bergamottin, psoralen, and xanthotoxin.

missing_other.title: Bigaflower™
missing_other.description: Bigaflower opens with the bittersweet glow of fresh orange blossom, all dewy white petals and sunlit neroli. A crisp green petitgrain note cuts across the top, sharp and leafy. Underneath, a soft creamy sweetness rounds everything into a smooth floral whole. This is a truly beautiful complete orange blossom heart in a single bottle, built on a generous dose of MANE captive Bigarane™ for that green petitgrain freshness. Use it to brighten citrus colognes and add a natural, just-picked lift. It also smooths and fills out heavier white florals. Push Bigaflower into fruity accords and it lends a creamy, marshmallow-like softness that tames sharp edges. Small amounts ground a cologne in believable neroli; larger ones turn a fragrance fully into orange blossom. Let its green side carry your topnote and the floral warmth linger below.

missing_other.title: Bigaradier Heart
missing_other.description: This is petitgrain bigarade stripped down to its most beautiful fractions — the floral, the woody, the delicate. What you smell is orange flower water in concentrated form: cosmetic, slightly green, with a subtle violet-like quality from its ionone content. The harsh herbal top notes of whole petitgrain are gone. Use it wherever you want a neroli-like florality without neroli's price. It furnishes a sparkling top that lifts citrus-floral-woods structures and adds unexpected contrast to amber bases. In eau de colognes, it sits between bergamot and lavender, supplying the orange blossom character that makes classic formulas glow. The refined character means it blends without dominating — a trait the whole oil rarely achieves. Try it in chypres where the green-floral facet bridges oakmoss and citrus. In rose compositions, it introduces a clean, soapy freshness. Pair with neroli oil for a richer orange blossom effect, or with linalool and petitgrain for a modern cologne heart.

missing_other.title: Birch Tar Oil, Purified
missing_other.description: Warm smoke and charred wood, then a sweet, oily leather note emerges underneath — unmistakably Russian leather. This purified grade has had the harsh medicinal bite stripped away. What remains is the heart of birch tar: pure, smooth cuir with extraordinary diffusion. Fraterworks carries three grades of birch tar oil. Rectified is the standard perfumery grade — smoky and leathery but with a rough, medicinal edge. Clear is the same oil decolourised; purified goes furthest, stripping out the harshest notes to leave only the smooth leather heart. Pair birch tar with castoreum and isobutyl quinoline for a full Russian leather accord, or with styrax and labdanum for a smoother amber-leather effect. It bridges beautifully into oud and tobacco compositions. Work from a dilution — the diffusion is extraordinary.

missing_other.title: Birch Tar Oil, Rectified
missing_other.description: Just because Birch Tar is mostly used in very small amounts doesn't mean we can't find the most beautiful example of the material. Far too often perfumers seek the lowest cost birch tar but at Fraterworks we consider that every material must be truly exquisite to be used in our fragrances and bases and sold to our clients and customers. And so we present this marvellous product from Payan Bertrand. Payan Bertrand's rectified Birch Tar from Finland is a model of good behaviour. It sits smoothly in a blend with absolutely no unwanted meaty or fishy notes that so often mar lower-quality versions of this natural. Because of the strength and cost of this birch tar we also offer it at 10% dilution in natural triethyl citrate which means it is still compatible with natural perfumery. Even at 10% dilution this oil is still very strong, so we suggest diluting further to 1% where its effect is still noticeable (as evidenced in our Aventus demonstration formula below). If you prefer something a little easier to dose and historically interesting, you might like our wonderful recreation of classic birch tar oil from the 19th century Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 . We are also offering our signature Birch Tar Clear oil which is IFRA compliant, low colour and more refined. Origin: Finland Part: Bark Process: Distillation followed by rectification

missing_other.title: Birch Tar “Signature” Oil, Clear
missing_other.description: Payan Bertrand is the master of Birch Tar and so we stock their wonderful rectified product — IFRA safe and not fishy. But we are now offering another of their marvels: Birch Tar Clear. While rectified Birch is the scent of camp fires and outdoor winterly adventures, Birch Tar Clear is the scent of pipe ash, cigars and warm hearths — and it's IFRA compliant too! This clear oil is also about 50% lighter in colour than standard rectified oil. Clear Birch has a more refined and complete scent and has hints of boozy liquor and vanilla. This oil also has less top note impact making it more useful when a smoky dry down is wanted without the dirty top notes that can sometimes be apparent in other birch oils. Because of the strength and cost of this clear birch tar we also offer it at 10% dilution in natural triethyl citrate which means it is still compatible with natural perfumery. Even at 10% dilution this oil is still very strong, so we suggest diluting further to 1% where its effect is still noticeable (as evidenced in our Aventus demonstration formula below). If you prefer something a little more historically interesting, you might like our wonderful recreation of classic birch tar oil from the 19th century Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 . Origin: Finland Part: Bark Process: Distillation followed by rectification for IFRA compliance and decolourisation

missing_other.title: Bitter Orange Oil
missing_other.description: Bitter orange oil is more complex and, in our opinion, more interesting than sweet orange oil. It is, however, quite restricted by IFRA with an allowance of up to 3% of your finished product. Bitter orange (also known as bigarade or Seville orange) is the fruit from which the original Marmalade was made. The finest qualities come from Europe where adulteration is unlikely. According to Steffan Arctander: "The odor is very peculiar, fresh and yet "bitter" in the sense of "dry", but with a rich and lasting, sweet undertone. There are notes which remind of bergamot, grapefruit and sweet orange, but overall, the odour is distinctly different from that of other citrus oils. It is a different ype of freshness, a peculiar floral undertone which occasionally shows indolic notes, and a comparatively good tenacity." It is interesting to note that cold pressed citrus oils are not technically essential oils as they do not undergo distillation. Origin: Calabria, Italy Part: Peel Method: Cold pressed at source

missing_other.title: Black Agar Givco® 215/2
missing_other.description: Black Agar Givco is one of (if not THE) most popular replacer bases for agarwood (oud). It is a rather bright (and rather loose) interpretation of the natural oil and has very elegant nuances of olibanum and amber which makes it a particularly good blender. Black Agar Givco is built around a hefty dose (around 9%) of Amber Formate (Oxyoctaline Formate) accented with naturals such as patchouli oil, amyris wood, cedar, labdanum, frankincense and guaiacwood. This is what Givaudan has to say of the material: “Odor: Woody, Ambery, Olibanum. Use: Agarwood is a classical material used in perfumery. When this wood is infected by fungi, it develops dark streaks charged with an odouriferous oleoresin. The darkest grade, black or true agar, resembles black stone because of the intense impregnation of oil. This resin is highly valuable due to its rich, complex, powerful, woody-ambery scent. It is however an extremely expensive material that is difficult to find.” Black Agar Givco is a new base reflecting the typical odour of the black resin of agarwoood. This complex, powerful formulation with a resinous character brings together olibanum and balsamic/oriental notes.”

missing_other.title: Black Currant Bud Abs MD 37% TEC
missing_other.description: This is a very special Black Currant bud absolute from LMR. It is molecular distilled absolute which amplifies the fruity quality of the material while downplaying the sulphurous and unpleasant side-notes. It is a rare material and LMR doesn't typically advertise its existence, reserving it for special uses and clients (such as Hermès). The most notable feature of this absolute is just how clean and refined it is. The balance is almost hard to believe for a natural extract of this type. It is also decolourised making it very useful for modern perfumery. Use it as a one for one replacer for Black Currant Bud 50% as the refined nature of this product gives it more top note presence. Once you try this black Currant bud absolute you will be a convert for life. Regulatory Please note that Black Currant Bud absolute is unrestricted by IFRA and can, as such, be used at any level in a finished perfume. However, LMR performs its own Human Repeated Insult Patch Test (HRIPT) and have an internal company limit of 1.1% of the finished fragrance. The IFRA certificate we offer below is a Fraterworks issued certificate under IFRA 51 and is the necessary legal limit. The LMR certificate based on a combination of IFRA 51 AND HRIPT can be downloaded here . Origin: Burgundy, France Part: Buds Method: Solvent extraction and molecular distillation

missing_other.title: Black Datura
missing_other.description: BLACK DATURA® is a powerful fragrance base developed by Master Perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour for Fraterworks. Inspired by the enigmatic Datura flower—renowned for its intoxicating beauty and hallucinogenic potency—this base explores the intersection of seduction and danger. Sweet, creamy floralcy is laced with soft spice and a narcotic depth that expands on skin like a velvet shadow. Perfumery Usage BLACK DATURA® offers bold character and long-lasting diffusion, ideal for adding richness and mystery to florals, orientals, and modern chypres. It blends especially well with Tuberose, Cumin, Suederal®, and dark ambers. Use sparingly to add tension, or in full bloom as a central floral theme. Process This complex base is composed of layered synthetic florals, trace spice notes, and select naturals, carefully balanced to reflect Datura’s rich scent and symbolic weight. The composition pushes the boundary between the hypnotic and the forbidden, staying true to the flower’s role in folklore and ritual. Background Datura’s infamy in medicine, mythology, and magic is matched only by the beauty of its flower. BLACK DATURA® brings this contradiction to perfumery: it is lush yet unsettling, refined yet raw. It offers perfumers a tool to express the darker side of floral storytelling. BLACK DATURA® is the Poison Bloom of The Night Garden —beautiful, narcotic, and not to be trusted. Creative Director: Jamie Frater Master Perfumer: Bertrand Duchaufour Fragrance Composition House: Fraterworks®

missing_other.title: Black Opoponax
missing_other.description: Opoponax bases are a subset of amber (or ambreine) type bases; both are loaded up on citrus, animalics, resins and sweet crystallines (vanillin and coumarin in very high doses usually).
