While Ambreine bases are usually erogenous and very vanilla-oriented, Opoponax bases are drier, more agrestic and often featuring lower (but still significant) amounts of crystallines. A classic base, Black Opoponax was used by Jacques Cavallier in the classic men's oriental fragrance Opium Pour Homme (1995) at around 5%. This base is extremely versatile and fits just as nicely into a post-modern fragrance as it did into the '90s YSL hit. Absolutely IFRA compliant and built entirely without the use of any musks (nitro or otherwise), this base is an excellent fixative. With judicious amounts of luxurious oriental resins, natural Mysore sandalwood and patchouli Aceh oil, Black Opoponax is a fragrance in its own right.

missing_other.title: Black Pepper Absolute
missing_other.description: Black Pepper Absolute is nothing like the essential oil. Where the distilled oil gives you bright, terpenic freshness, the absolute delivers the deep warmth of freshly crushed peppercorns — leathery, smoky, almost tar-like, with an animalic dirtiness hiding in the base. Solvent extraction captures heavy, non-volatile fractions that steam distillation misses — the eugenol warmth, the tobacco and old-leather facets, the barnyard undertones. This makes it indispensable for leather accords and oriental bases where a lighter pepper note would vanish. Pair with oud, labdanum, or birch tar for seriously dark territory. The absolute also works beautifully in rose compositions — the warmth rounds and deepens the floral character without overpowering it. Try it alongside castoreum and vetiver for a smoky-leather backbone. Dose carefully: this is thick, concentrated material with real potency. This is extracted in a two step purification process using propylene glycol which is suitable for perfumery but most often seen in the flavours industry.

missing_other.title: Black Pepper Oil
missing_other.description: Black pepper oil is a surprisingly versatile spice which blends very well with the salicylates, other spice oils and earthy naturals like Vetiver. For a novel use of black pepper try using it with a sweet rose to add texture and warmth or make a spice blend that departs from the beloved clove, cinnamon and cardamom combo. Out Black Pepper Oil is produced by Floral Concept a company with an exceptional understanding of the subtle nuances of spice oils. It is rounded, balanced and very well behaved. This is now the only black pepper oil we use.

missing_other.title: Black Tea Supreme
missing_other.description: This beautiful Fraterworks base represents fine black China tea of the variety used by Sir Joseph Banks who invented Earl Grey Tea (later named for Banks' friend the second Earl Grey, prime minister of England). It is a full bodied robust tea base built around many rich and luxurious naturals. It will impart a top to bottom tea note and can be used in very small amounts to overdose though we recommend something in the vicinity of 0.5 – 1%. Add Bergamot for a distinct Earl Grey note, or a touch of Fir Needle Oil and our signature rectified Birch Tar to mimic Lapsang Souchong tea.

missing_other.title: Black Tea “Signature” Resinoid
missing_other.description: A very refined and distinctive black tea note that has absolutely no off notes and is considered a signature speciality of Payan Bertrand. It is really one of the finest specimens of tea that we have experienced and we are thrilled to offer it alongside our Black Tea base . The natural resinoid is found in such fragrances as L'Ombre Des Merveilles (2020) by Hermès, Kilian's Imperial Tea (2014) and Gucci Pour Homme II (2007). Make a lovely Earl Grey tea note by combining this product with Neobergamate Forte and our marvelous Bergamot Reggio base. This material is very stiff when cold so heat should be used to liquify it.

missing_other.title: Blackcurrant Bud Absolute
missing_other.description: Blackcurrant bud absolute has a powerful, tangy fruit note with a very characteristic ammoniac "cat pee" nuance, alongside spicy-woody and green minty-sulfurous facets. This variant from LMR is the very best classic extract of pure Burgundy blackcurrant buds. We also offer a very special molecular distilled version also from LMR. Use this material as a powerful modifier in trace amounts (often This material functions as an "exalting agent," brightening compositions with effervescent quality whilst providing remarkable longevity that bridges top through base phases. Its multifaceted profile allows strategic use as a connector between different olfactory families - green facets link to herbaceous notes, fruity aspects harmonise with citrus, woody undertones connect to sandalwood bases. Apply sparingly in citrus colognes to add sparkling freshness. Combine with galbanum or violet leaf to enhance green facets. Use traces in rose or jasmine bases for surprising naturalness.

missing_other.title: Blonde Amber Type Formula
missing_other.description: In 2022 Clive Christian really hit its stride with this fragrance which I dare say may be the best in its lineup. Formulated by Vincent Ricord who should probably be more well-known than he is, it combines my personal favourite sandalwood accord of Sandalore®, Polysantol® and Javanol® with sweet natural woods and luxurious florals. Clive Christian has a great reputation for quality and unlike some brands (Amouage and Tom Ford for example) the high price the brand commands really is often justified by the complexity and richesse of their scents. Top Notes: Petitgrain, Rum, Rock Rose, Bitter Orange, Cardamom, Pink Pepper, Ginger, Bergamot and Grapefruit Heart Notes: Dried Fruits, Tobacco, Sandalwood, Tuberose, Saffron, Osmanthus, Orris and Jasmine Base Notes: Tonka Bean, Myrrh, Vanilla, Labdanum, Patchouli, Cedar, Musk and Vetiver Total Lines: 52 Naturals: 16

missing_other.title: Blood Orange Oil
missing_other.description: Blood orange oil opens with the bright, zesty freshness you expect from orange peel, then immediately reveals something more. A distinctive tart, berry-like sweetness sits beneath the citrus, giving this oil a richness and depth that standard sweet orange completely lacks. The overall impression is of a fuller, more luxurious orange. Use blood orange to add premium citrus character to your top notes. It lifts gourmand compositions with a sparkling tartness, bridges citrus and fruity-floral accords naturally, and brings modern complexity to colognes where plain sweet orange would feel ordinary. Slightly better tenacity than standard orange too. Pair blood orange with black pepper and cardamom for a vibrant spicy-citrus opening. Try it alongside bergamot and neroli for a sophisticated Sicilian hesperidic accord. Blend with elemol, frankincense or sandalwood to extend its fruity warmth deeper into the heart of your composition. Three orange oils, three distinct characters. Sweet orange is bright, simple, and cheerfully familiar — the classic citrus top note. Blood orange keeps that freshness but adds tart berry sweetness and a fuller body. Bitter orange is drier and sharper, with a sophisticated floral edge closer to bergamot. Sweet lifts, blood enriches, bitter refines.

missing_other.title: Blue Cypress Oil
missing_other.description: Blue Cypress Oil delivers an extraordinary aromatic signature unlike any other woody material. The thick blue-green liquid exudes powerful woody depth with wonderfully sweet undertones. This rare Australian oil is treasured for its exceptional fixative properties and remarkable tenacity. This extraordinary material commands attention in woody-oriental blends. Apply at 0.5-2% concentration for optimal results in base accords. Pair with sandalwood, vetiver, or citrus notes to enhance its multi-faceted character. Use sparingly to ground floral compositions without overwhelming delicate notes. Blue Cypress blends exceptionally well in combination with Ambergris Intense ™, Paradisamide ®, and Madranol .

missing_other.title: Blue Hemlock Abs, Decolourised
missing_other.description: Blue hemlock absolute opens with a burst of sweet, juicy forest berries and blackcurrant that immediately set it apart from other conifer materials. A rich caramelised sugar quality reminiscent of warm berry jam underpins the fruitiness. Resinous woody depth and subtle smokiness emerge gradually, grounding those unusual fruity facets. This is almost like liquid fir balsam. Add this to pine accords for multidimensional forest depth that no synthetic can replicate. In fruity florals the natural berry sweetness reads as genuinely real, not candy-like. Even trace amounts lend unexpected juiciness to citrus compositions and woody orientals. Build autumn-inspired gourmands by pairing blue hemlock with davana and patchouli for a berry-woods foundation. Use it to add naturalistic depth to forest fantasy accords where synthetic berries fall flat. The decolourised version (which has an orange tone) gives you all this character without staining your blends. This is extracted onto 80% IPM making it a fully mobile liquid.

missing_other.title: Blue Tansy Oil
missing_other.description: Blue Tansy Oil pours out a deep ink-blue and smells nothing like the sharp common tansy. The scent is sweet and fruity, like ripe apple and warm honey, softened by a gentle herby-floral haze. A faint camphor coolness keeps it lively. Use Blue Tansy to bring a natural, chamomile-like sweetness to florals and to soften the green bite of aromatic and fougère accords. It rounds sharp herbs and lends a sun-warmed, fruity glow underneath top notes. A little goes a long way, since its colour and odour both take over fast. Think of it as a sweetener for herbal and apple-fruity effects rather than a loud feature. Trace amounts lift a chamomile or clary sage heart; a touch more pushes a blend toward jammy, wine-like richness. Its blue tint also tells you instantly how much you have added.

missing_other.title: Bois de Cendres
missing_other.description: The nostalgic scent of a campfire that radiates with cedarwood and resinous nuances and a powerful smoke note. This is a base with a split personality: it is smoky intensity with extreme radiance from power ambers and some of the longest-lasting wood chemicals in the industry. Use Bois de Cendres (wood of ashes) at less than 1% as an alternative to birch tar or cade when wanting to represent glowing embers, cinders and floating sparks from a crackling fire. But at 2% IFRA compliance in a finished product, this can also be overdosed to give Tauer's Lonestar Memories a run for its money! Synergies: Frankincense and resins in all forms but especially Fumencens HTC, Hydrocarboresine , and Olibanum Vulcain .

missing_other.title: Bois de Violette
missing_other.description: Bois de Violette is a beautiful and very stylish violet base which gives the simplest, cleanest and most elegant form of a violet note to fragrances. While our Violette Bleue focuses on the modern green molecules found in violet leaves, Bois de Violette conveys the wild flowers in their entirety. This is the violet smell that floats on the air and surprises you on a walk through a cottage garden. If you pick just one violet, this is the one we recommend. In small amounts it can add a purple nuance while in overdose, as is, it contributes the finest violet note possible for a modern fragrance. This violet is built with rare ionone molecules so it really does add a special quality to a fragrance impossible to get otherwise. This base is classical in its conception but absolutely fits into a modern context perfectly. This is not an old fashioned violet, this is simply “violet”. Blends beautifully with Iso E Super , Isoraldeine Cetone Alpha , Iraldeine Delta , Epice FW , Dianthine Extra , Cyclamen des Alpes and, of course, Violet leaf absolute .

missing_other.title: Bois Noir Type Formula
missing_other.description: This is our exclusive deluxe formula for Chanel's Bois Noir (1987) the first public release of what was to become Égoïste just a few years later. When first released Bois Noir didn't sell well so Chanel removed it from the shelves. It eventually found its way back to the public with a few fairly minor tweaks for simplicity. Bottles of Bois Noir are so rare they currently sell in the $2,000 range when they come up on eBay. When comparing this to the Égoïste Cologne Concentrée the Bois Noir has a softer and more velvet dry down most likely coming from the broader range of musks which were removed in favour of just 0.5% Musk Ambrette in the Égoïste family. This demonstration formula was derived some inside knowledge and multiple GCMS analyses of a pristine bottle owned by Fraterworks. Comparisons were also made with Égoïste Cologne Concentrée and vintage Ëgoïste. Top Notes: Bergamot, Rosewood, Green Mandarin, Grapefruit, Lemon, Plum, Anise, Cinnamon Heart Notes: Lavender, Coriander, Ylang Ylang, Carnation, Geranium Bourbon, Thyme, Tagetes Minuta Base Notes: Sandalwood Mysore, Amber, Leather, Musk, Labdanum, Myrrh, Tobacco, Castoreum Total Lines: 50 Bases: 5

missing_other.title: Boronia Supreme TruAbs
missing_other.description: With Boronia absolute at an eye watering price there is a real need for an incredibly high quality completely natural replacer base. This is it. With all the complexity of the natural absolute, this base is magic. It adds floralcy, nuance and luxury to all fragrances. Boronia absolute was a key floral addition to Diorissimo by Edmond Roudnitska. Boronia is one of those few flowers rich in ionones (along with violet, mimosa and cassie). In the Southern hemisphere it's brief appearance marks the start of summer as it stains the air with its profoundly beautiful scent. Like our amazing Rose de Mai Supreme , this base is created scientifically for Fraterworks in Grasse and is so good it is practically impossible to differentiate it from pure and natural Boronia absolute. Due to the high cost of this replica, we sell it at 10% dilution in odourless natural triethyl citrate — just make your selection above. We can supply an unlimited quantity of Boronia Supreme TruAbs®, just contact us for pricing. This product may contain traces of nicotine:

missing_other.title: Bouleau Pyrogene 1840
missing_other.description: In days past, birch tar ( le bouleau pyrogéné ) was used in its crude form. Modern safety requirements mean that it must now be rectified via distillation to be used in cosmetics and fragrances. This rectification process removes unwelcome molecules but it also destroys a large number of safe and decidedly beautiful ones. This results in a piercing "smoke essence" far stronger than the original and lacking much of its character. Classic birch tar was more than just smoke: it was sweet, it was woody and it was evocative. Using a sample of a well-preserved batch of crude birch tar from 1840 as a guide, we were able to reconstruct this treasured oil in the form of a base. Centred around a heart of IFRA compliant rectified birch tar, Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 includes many natural materials and highly specialised aroma chemicals that allow us to offer a product that not only smells just like the real thing, but is also balanced when used in bold doses; indeed you may use this up to 1.81% of your finished product though we suggest far less. The base opens with an appealing hint of herbal medicaments making it an ideal companion to intense florals such as Tuberose Absolute and Ylang-ylang , especially the Extra Superior quality. Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 is animalic, smokey and woody with accents of florals, fruit and wild honey. This is the true birch tar profile so beloved of perfumers like Ernest Beaux who used it liberally in Bouquet De Catherine (later Rallet Le No 1 — formula below), an early iteration of his great masterpiece Chanel No 5 . Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 can be used as a one for one replacer of Birch Tar in classical formulas or in lesser amounts for modern fragrances. Combine it with Ambergris Intense , Thujopsene , Iraldeine Delta and marine synthetics to conjure images of wooden sailing ships and tar soaked ropes, or create a Guy Fawkesian delight by adding touches to flinty Karanal, Frankincense oil and Iso E Super for a gunpowder meets bonfire night accord.

missing_other.title: Bouvardia DL
missing_other.description: Bouvardia was an iconic 20th century De Laire base of citrus with orange flower and jasmine nuances. Beloved by Francois Coty and used skillfully in L'Origan (at 0.8%), it is now available to the market for the first time in decades. It hints at the highly scented notes of both flowers and due to its somewhat ambiguous nature blends beautifully with many other floral materials. It is a wonderful nuancer for top notes based on bergamot and it is beautifully at home in oriental types. This early De Laire base is more of a citrus top note base than a heart base, making it a rather unique product.

missing_other.title: Boxtree Absolute 50% TEC
missing_other.description: Known to most of us as trimmed and shaped hedges à la Edward Scissorhands , living Boxtree (buxus) has a characteristic grimalkin scent not dissimilar to an odour exhibited by some black currant extractions. MANE's boxtree absolute does not have that urinous note, instead being primarily woody with complex moss and iodine nuances. It also has a very unique fruity character in the opening which hints at the scent of cooked ripe bananas. Boxtree absolute is an interesting material to use when considering one's options for replacing highly restricted oakmoss and tree moss absolutes. It is intensely green and in its normal form a solid mass similar to very high quality pure castoreum absolute. For that reason we supply it at 50% dilution in natural triethyl citrate, making it possible to use it in all natural perfumes. Origin: France Part: Twigs

missing_other.title: Bran Absolute
missing_other.description: Bran absolute opens with a rich, buttery warmth — toasted wheat grain, the honeyed sweetness of a just-baked biscuit. Dried apricot and hay facets emerge quickly, giving it a sun-dried pastoral quality that sits somewhere between bakery and field. The drydown settles into soft pecan nuttiness with a whisper of chocolate. This is a textural material. It fills the gap between sharp gourmand synthetics and the lived-in warmth of real food. Drop it into a tobacco accord and watch the harshness smooth out. Use it beneath tuberose or jasmine and the florals gain a honeyed, skin-warm quality that feels expensive. It pairs particularly well with dried fruit notes, tea accords, and anything amber-adjacent where you want golden warmth without cloying vanilla. Bran absolute has solubility quirks — its waxy nature means it can cloud in high-alcohol solutions. Pre-dissolve in a warm carrier or blend it into your base notes first. It fixes beautifully and extends the life of lighter materials around it. Think of it as liquid cashmere: invisible structure that makes everything above it feel richer.

missing_other.title: Buchu “Extra” Oil
missing_other.description: Buchu Betulina is a flowering shrub from South Africa (which should not be confused with Korean Buchu AKA garlic chives or Allium tuberosum ) with a strong and distinctive odour of blackcurrant (particularly its cat-pee quality) and peppermint. It is not for no good reason that one of the most sulphurous and intense aroma chemicals in perfumery is named after it: Buchu Mercaptan (T hiomenthone). It has still to find its place as an overdose material though it does make up a distinct part of Tom Ford's Azure Lime (2010), Calvin Klein's CK Free (2009) where it is blended with Juniper , tobacco , coffee and Armoise and Calice Becker's Killing Me Slowly (2014) for Kilian where it combines with Black Currant and Lychee. Use Buchu Oil to add interesting and natural fruit notes to synthetics or to bring out certain aspects of other naturals. This Extra oil from Payan Bertrand is superbly extracted, with a particularly refined and almost tamed top note making it far more versatile than those of other manufacturers. Owing to its high strength and cost, we are also offering this in a 10% solution with natural triethyl citrate (an odourless natural extract from citrus).

missing_other.title: Buddhawood “Mulacro” Oil
missing_other.description: Buddhawood oil (AKA “Mulacro” oil) is the steam distilled extraction from the Buddha Wood shrub (Eremophila mitchellii), a native Australian plant that is also known as false sandalwood or desert rosewood. Dark brown in colour, this viscous essential oil has a wonderfully soft woody smell with subtle traces of smoke and spice. It is effective in doses under 1% (though it could potentially be used in overdose) and it is a superb naturaliser and enhancer of all members of the Iso E Super family and amber materials. Blends of cinnamon leaf oil , muscade absolute and theaspirane are sublime and the oil works wonderfully with grapefruit and rhubarb notes. This is a highly deceptive material, seeming to be mild or ineffective but its ability to add velvety naturalness and luxury to wood synthetics is unparalleled. Great skill is required to use this oil to its fullest potential.

missing_other.title: Butter “Signature” CO2
missing_other.description: This Butter CO2 is a wonderful non-vegan natural which can be used in traces to add naturalness and richness to a scent or in larger doses to add character go a gourmand as in our demonstration formula for Sora Dora's Jany (see below). This comes in a solid waxy form but gentle warmth will bring it to a liquid state. As natural animalics become more scarce we highly recommend this product as it is a much needed filler for a gap in the market. The scent of Butter CO2 is characteristic of fresh butter (this is used in the flavour industry also) with a mildly butyric acidity in the top. It is very useful for adding creamy notes to florals and woods (especially sandalwood) and it blends beautifully with the likes of Acetoin and Sulfurol.

missing_other.title: Cabreuva Wood Oil
missing_other.description: Sweet, woody and floral with a metallic hint of tinsel, Cabreuva oil is a wonderful material for adding natural richness and complexity to orange blossom and neroli type fragrances and, owing to its very high nerolidol content, many other florals that need naturalising or lift. Cabreuva is an excellent blender for wood materials (especially Cedarwood) and has great longevity so it can be used as an interesting fixative alongside the more common synthetics.

missing_other.title: Cadamba Attar
missing_other.description: The cadamba tree produces golden globe-shaped blossoms during the Indian monsoon season — round, spiky, and intensely fragrant. These are gathered at dawn and distilled into sandalwood oil over about fifteen days, with fresh flowers added daily. The yield is vanishingly small, making cadamba one of the rarest of the classical Indian attars. The scent opens with a surprising cool, almost minty flash, then settles into thick, honeyed, powdery sweetness unlike any other flower. It touches on champaca, neroli, and orange blossom without precisely duplicating any of them. Arctander described its staying power as "almost incredible" — flowers wrapped in a damp cloth held their fragrance for over a week. That tenacity carries through to the finished attar. Use cadamba as a honeyed floral heart in orientals, or alongside champaca for a lush, narcotic Indian floral accord. It pairs well with ylang-ylang, neroli, and jasmine. Cadamba rewards careful blending — let it support florals rather than lead, and its deep sweetness adds extraordinary persistence to everything around it. We have an excellent article on Cadamba by Christopher McMahon of White Lotus Aromatics fame that you can read.

missing_other.title: Cade Oil, Rectified
missing_other.description: Cade oil is the most common alternative to Birch Tar oil but it shouldn't be seen as the poor cousin. In fact Cade Oil (also known as Juniper Tar Oil) has qualities that, to our mind, can make it a superior option. While Birch Tar oil can have an oily quality (and some low class versions - from other suppliers - a decidedly fishy aroma), Cade Tar Oil is drier and bears a stronger resemblance to a freshly extinguished camp fire, ash and all. It is certainly different enough from Birch oil that interesting and novel accords might be come to by blending the two. For IFRA compliance this oil is rectified which is a distillation process that removes potential allergens and harmful chemicals from the naturally produced tar oil. If you prefer something a little different, you might like our wonderful recreation of classic birch tar oil from the 19th century Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 or our exquisite Birch Tar Oil, also from Payan Bertrand. Origin: Spain Part: Twigs and branches Process: Burning, followed by distillation and rectification

missing_other.title: Calamus Oil
missing_other.description: Calamus root essential oil, also known as "Sweet Flag", is a pale yellow liquid displaying a smooth, warm, woody-earthy-spicy bouquet with a milky, sweet undertone of very good tenacity. You have never smelled anything quite like this lovely rare oil. Our calamus oil is wonderful for adding complex and interesting notes to a scent. It's gentle spice is vaguely reminiscent of the scent of cinnamon bark floating on the air while its earthy tones are well rounded and subtle. Calamus oil can contain around 70% asarones which are highly restricted by IFRA in natural oils to 0.01% of a finished product, however this Payan Bertrand speciality still allows for a maximum use of 0.47% in your finished product. Despite the restrictions this is still a wonderful material to have in the perfumer's palette and is most certainly still useable in commercial scents. Origin: Korea Part: Rhizomes Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Cananga Oil
missing_other.description: Cananga oil is not ylang-ylang. They share the same species but come from different varieties, different islands, and different distillation methods. Where ylang-ylang from the Comoros is bright, sparkling, and overtly floral, Javanese cananga is heavy, woody-leathery, and balsamic. The great perfume writer (and spy) Arctander was emphatic: they are not interchangeable in character or in function. Ylang-ylang is fractionally distilled into grades — Extra, I, II, III — letting you choose brightness or depth. Cananga is a single complete distillation: the whole flower in one oil, from the lightest floral top to the heaviest balsamic base. That gives it a roundness and tenacity that no single ylang-ylang fraction matches. It also survives alkaline conditions, making it far more reliable in soap formulations where ylang-ylang's bright topnotes simply fall apart. Use cananga oil in leather accords alongside castoreum, labdanum, and birch tar — this is one of its classic roles. It anchors fougères with balsamic warmth and lends lasting power to oriental bases. Think of it as the dark, serious side of the ylang family: less pretty, more powerful, and built to last.

missing_other.title: Caraway Seed “Superior” Oil
missing_other.description: Caraway seed (actually a fruit not a seed) is often confused with cumin seed due to the similarity in appearance (both are from the Apiaceae family). The main visible difference is that Caraway seeds are crescent shaped with raised ridges while cumin seeds have smoother ridges and are not curved. The main odiferous component of caraway is carvone giving it a herbal minty quality while cumin has a more animal or skin like scent owing to the cuminaldehyde dominance. Caraway seed features in Le Male by Francis Kurkdjian for Gaultier (1995), Declaration by Cartier, Tom Ford's Santal Blush (2011), and the beautiful Hypnotic Poison (1998) by Dior. Our oil hails from the Netherlands, long the preferred source of Caraway seed oil to the top luxury fragrance houses. Origin: Netherlands Part: Seeds Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Cardamom Absolute
missing_other.description: Cardamom Absolute is a rich and long lasting extraction from green cardamom pods harvested in Guatemala. It has a similar profile to the essential oil but is much more intense. Despite being an absolute, it has a rather interesting and vibrant top note presence with a clear ginger nuance making it very useful from top to bottom as a replacer or booster for the oil. Owing to the high cost we offer this pure and diluted to 10% in natural triethyl citrate, an odourless extract from citrus. Interpreting Arctander: “Cardamom Oil has been used in perfumery for centuries, first written about in 1540 by Valerius Cordus. The oil is pale yellow to light brown and darkens in sunlight. Its scent starts strong and fresh, like eucalyptus, but softens into a warm, spicy, and woody aroma with a sweet floral touch. It is long-lasting and adds depth to any fragrance. In perfumes, cardamom oil brings a warm sweetness and spicy richness. It works well in floral bases like rose and lily of the valley. It also adds warmth to Oriental fragrances, chypres, and powdery scents. Cardamom blends beautifully with oils like bergamot, ylang-ylang, and labdanum. Coriander oil is its perfect partner, making the scent more complex and refined. For perfumers, it is a versatile and essential ingredient.” We also offer the finest steam distilled essential oil of cardamom and Cardamom CO2 .

missing_other.title: Cardamom CO2
missing_other.description: Cardamom CO₂ is a luxurious extraction that captures the true soul of cardamom with unmatched depth and purity. Unlike traditional methods, this gentle technique preserves the full aromatic spectrum, unveiling a vibrant, spicy warmth interwoven with hints of sweet resin and fresh citrus undertones. Its exceptional clarity and aromatic potency make it indispensable for perfumers crafting refined fragrances where authenticity and complexity are paramount. Used at just 0.2–0.5%, Cardamom CO₂ adds a captivating spicy elegance without overshadowing delicate accords. Its versatile nature makes it a harmonious partner for bright citrus oils, sophisticated woods, and rich balsamic notes, enhancing depth and dimensionality in compositions. A subtle touch in the top notes brings an alluring, spicy sparkle that instantly elevates any fragrance, making Cardamom CO₂ an essential ingredient in the palette of the discerning perfumer.

missing_other.title: Cardamom “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: Green cardamom (the queen of spices) is a radiant gem in perfumery. While most suppliers sell oil from Ceylon and India, the supreme variety comes from the lush volcanic nation of beautiful Guatemala. In its native land of India, the spice is held in such high esteem that it forms a vital part of the festival dish payasam , a sweet and highly fragrant rice pudding. Our cardamom oil comes from the highest grade of green cardamom pods and is the ultimate extraction of the spice. So much so that we call it our signature oil. Interpreting Arctander: “Cardamom Oil has been used in perfumery for centuries, first written about in 1540 by Valerius Cordus. The oil is pale yellow to light brown and darkens in sunlight. Its scent starts strong and fresh, like eucalyptus, but softens into a warm, spicy, and woody aroma with a sweet floral touch. It is long-lasting and adds depth to any fragrance. In perfumes, cardamom oil brings a warm sweetness and spicy richness. It works well in floral bases like rose and lily of the valley. It also adds warmth to Oriental fragrances, chypres, and powdery scents. Cardamom blends beautifully with oils like bergamot, ylang-ylang, and labdanum. Coriander oil is its perfect partner, making the scent more complex and refined. For perfumers, it is a versatile and essential ingredient.”

missing_other.title: Caress Musk
missing_other.description: Caress Musk is a soft but powerful white musk blend blend that contributes elegance, richness and depth to a scent without dominating. Its blends with vanilla odourants are supreme but it also works wonders in floral compositions. Use it in an overdose like you would the Grojsman accord or in small amounts to add complexity and interest to your fragrance while benefiting from its extraordinary fixative power. Caress Musk is beautiful in its own right and can be worn as a complete fragrance. Blends with Cashmeran, Grojsman Accord, Ambreine Samuelson, Vanillin “Signature”, Ethyl Vanillin, Vanilla Supreme, Solafleur™ and Celestafleur™.

missing_other.title: Carnation “Signature” Absolute
missing_other.description: Carnation absolute is as rare as hen's teeth and getting rarer by the day. We have searched high and low to bring you the very finest carnation extract. We found that perfect extract in LMR one of the few large scale companies that produce this absolute. With LMR comes the guarantee of compliance with set standards meaning you don't have to worry that the next batch will vary wildly as is the case with the small batch makers. In the words of LMR: “ A warm powdery floral note that has a spicy clove-like body, gives a green olive impression, and has a herbaceous fruity background with honey undertones.”

missing_other.title: Carrot Heart MD
missing_other.description: Carrot heart from LMR is a revelation! Starting with a luxurious extraction of seeds from finest French carrots, a molecular distillation process gives us the purest heart. This unique product from one of France's most esteemed luxury oil producer is rich with notes of apricot skins in the opening and fresh earth and classic powder in the dry down. In the words of LMR: “We source our carrot seeds from France in July, mainly from the South of France, but also from Anjou and Normandy.⁣ To create this extract, our sourcing experts have carefully selected the highest quality of carrot seeds that were destined to be discarded. [This is] a classic perfumery ingredient with a sustainable twist.⁣” Origin: France Part: Seeds Method: Steam distillation at source followed by molecular distillation

missing_other.title: Carrot Seed Oil, Vaucluse
missing_other.description: While cheap and cheerful carrot seed oil from India is widely available, the very precious Vaucluse carrot seed oil is not so. The French take their carrots very seriously and unlike we étrangers who like our vegetables crisp and cold, French gastronomes know that carrots are best after aging; limp and warm is the name of the game en France . Vaucluse is renowned for its carrots and, indeed, the seeds of the same. Vaucluse carrot seed oil is a wonderful blender for iris materials, adding naturalisation to synthetics and nuance to naturals. It has a slightly tangy quality with accents of earth after gentle rains, musky cumin seeds and sweet apricots. Comparing this oil to the Indian, we find the French to be vibrant and transparent with a very discreet carrot nuance, while the Indian oil has a decidedly muddy aspect which can stifle the delicate odour. The Vaucluse oil practically dances. Origin: Vaucluse, France Variety: daucus carota Part: Seeds Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Cascarilla Bark Oil
missing_other.description: Cascarilla bark oil is a wonderful spicy oil extracted from the bark of the croton eluteria tree. Most production of the oil takes place in the Bahamas. Our cascarilla is a delight to the senses with an odour profile that walks the line between nutmeg, black pepper and ginger. The bark, dried and processed to remove sapwood and heartwood, yields a pale yellow to amber liquid with a spicy-aromatic, warm-woody, and slightly peppery scent reminiscent of nutmeg, myrtle, and hyssop. Its top note may not appeal initially, but its diffusiveness and strength make it a valued "trace" component in perfumes. Renowned for its complex spiciness and warm, woody undertone, Cascarilla Oil has intrigued perfumers, finding use in chypre bases, Oriental fragrances, men’s colognes, and fantasy scents. It pairs harmoniously with materials like nutmeg, pimento berry oil, oakmoss, and coumarin, offering depth and intrigue to high-class perfumes. Though often underestimated, its versatility and power make it a key asset in sophisticated fragrance design. Deceptively powerful, cascarilla is perceptible at less than 1% of a fragrance. Cascarilla is part of the secret formula for Campari , the wonderful Italian liquor, and featured in the classic Coty fragrance, L'Origan .

missing_other.title: Cassie Absolute, Egypt
missing_other.description: Cassie and mimosa are both members of the Acacia family. Mimosa is sweeter and more refined, while cassie is fuller bodied and complex. Both are essential naturals for perfumers, with mimosa often appearing as a rich floral note in fine fragrances and cassie being used to create masterful floral bases or add a je ne sais quoi . Cassie is a wonderful naturalizer and can round out and enrich fragrances at mere traces in much the same way as violet leaves do. For clarification, we offer the following: Mimosa (Acacia dealbata or decurrens): Natural Absolute , or Mimosa de Provence [base] Cassie (Acacia farnesiana): Natural Absolute [this product], or Fleur de Cassie [base] Pink Acacia : Unrelated to the acacia plant family this is faux acacia or Black Locust. Cassie absolute blends exceptionally well with the aforementioned bases as well as Violet Leaf “Signature” Absolute , Violette Bleue and the classic synthetics of this family Isoraldeine™ Cetone Alpha (Givaudan), Iralia ® (Firmenich), Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur (IFF) and Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra (IFF). Because of the high cost of this material, we are also offering it at 10% in natural odourless triethyl citrate.

missing_other.title: Castoreum Firbest®
missing_other.description: Castoreum Firbest opens with a warm, leathery-animalic character—smoky, phenolic (somewhat akin to calamine lotion), and unmistakably reminiscent of traditional castoreum. There are birch-tar facets and a sweet, resinous undertone that softens the smoke. As it develops, a musky sensuality emerges with hints of fruitiness in the drydown. This is Firmenich's Firbest reconstruction of castoreum, created without any animal-derived ingredients. The Firbest technology combines natural and synthetic materials to replicate the olfactory profile of traditional castoreum absolute—the warm, animalic, leather-like sweetness that made natural castoreum essential in classic chypres, fougères, and leather perfumes. Use it wherever you need that distinctive smoky-phenolic warmth and animalic depth. Castoreum Firbest is clearer in colour than traditional natural extracts, making it suitable for a wider range of applications.

missing_other.title: Castoreum Hyperessence 50% TEC
missing_other.description: Robertet's Castoreum Hyperessence 50% TEC is a particularly clean castoreum absolute. Formerly under the Charabot brand (now owned by Robertet), Castoreum Hyperessence tones down the rough edges of the material and enhances the sweet raspberry facets, making for a castoreum absolute of the finest quality and a product much easier to use than most. Castoreum Hyperessence is solid when pure so we offer it here at a 50% dilution in completely natural Triethyl Citrate, an odourless isolate from citrus. Use Castoreum Hyperessence anywhere you would normally use Castoreum absolute. We also offer an intense Castoreum “Signature” Absolute from Floral Concept which has more of a wild character and the elegant and 3% Siberian Castoreum Tincture , the softest of the group.

missing_other.title: Castoreum Synth 184004D
missing_other.description: Castoreum Synth hits with immediate smoky-phenolic intensity — warm leather, birch-tar depth, and a dark animalic presence that commands attention. Beneath the smoke sits a surprising dried-fruit sweetness, almost plum-like. The overall effect is richer and darker than most castoreum reconstructions. This Firmenich creation functions as both a standalone castoreum note and a powerful fixative — it smooths transitions between top, heart, and base while adding depth. Use it in leather accords, chypres, tobacco bases, and oud compositions. Even trace amounts transform a blend's character. Pair with isobutyl quinoline for a green-leather chypre, or bridge into balsamic amber with labdanum and benzoin. At eighty hours on a smelling strip, Castoreum Synth anchors your base notes with extraordinary persistence. Dose carefully — its odour impact is immense. Castoreum Synth and Castoreum Firbest are both Firmenich castoreum bases, but they differ in construction and character. Firbest achieves its animalic note through natural sources (non-animal) and reads clearer and more phenolic. Synth uses captive synthetic molecules to deliver a darker, richer profile with distinctive dried-fruit depth that Firbest lacks.

missing_other.title: Castoreum Tincture 10%
missing_other.description: This replaces our previous Canadian castoreum tincture (9 years aged) which is now sold out. This new product is one of great refinement owing to the extremely high quality wild castors we have used to produce this special tincture. In comparison to our Siberian tincture, this is less smoky and more typical of the scent most people associate with classic castoreum. ‘Castoreum [tincture's] warm, animal, leather-like sweet odour makes it an interesting item in “men's perfumes”, fougeres, chypres, Oriental bases, leather notes, Tabac bases, etc. [It blends] particularly well with ambra notes, calamus, cananga, cedarwood Atlas, chamomile moroccan, creosol, labdanum products , isoeugenol , oakmoss products , sandalwood oil , […] etc.’ — S. Arctander. Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin, Carol Stream: Allured Publishing Corporation, 2008, pp. 136–137. French Name: Infusion de Castoréum

missing_other.title: Castoreum “Signature” Absolute 50%
missing_other.description: Floral Concept is an expert when it comes to animalics and this Castoreum Absolute is proof indeed. Intensely leathery, this black solid material lacks all of the off-notes characteristic of most other products on the market. At room temperature Castoreum Absolute is a solid mass requiring heat to make mobile, therefore we are making it available in a 50% dilution in natural benzyl benzoate. NOTE: our most recent batch was made with 50% castoreum and 50% Triethyl Citrate. We are now using natural Benzyl Benzoate as it gives a much better and more easily controlled solution. Origin: Canada Variety: Castor canadensis Part: Castor Sacs Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Cedarome
missing_other.description: Cedarome is a rich and mysterious woody base loaded with vetiver, Mysore sandalwood, rose, cedar and more. It has a very long heritage, being first used in L'Origan in 1905. This magnificent piece of perfume history can be used as a complete fragrance, or in small amounts as you would use sandalwood or cedarwood in a luscious dry down accord. Absolutely IFRA compatible up to an enorrmous 16.7% of the finished product. NOTE: Cedarome may crystallise at low temperatures. Warm gentley if necessary. * Cedarome by Firmenich (formerly CNC) and Sophira (AKA Sophora by Roure) were very similar bases, with Sophira being an artistic copy made by the great Marius Reboul.

missing_other.title: Cedarwood Oil Rect, Texas
missing_other.description: _*]:min-w-0 gap-3"> Cedarwood Oil Rectified Texas opens with clean, sweet woody character—that unmistakable pencil-shavings aroma everyone recognises. Balsamic-smoky depth adds complexity, while dry powdery facets prevent heaviness. The rectification process removes the darker, tarry notes of crude oil, leaving a refined woody profile that works across fine fragrance and functional applications alike. The cedrol-rich composition provides excellent fixative properties, anchoring more volatile materials. Blend with vetiver, patchouli, sandalwood, and leather notes for classic masculine accords. It works beautifully in fougères alongside lavender and coumarin, and adds dry woody depth to amber and oriental compositions. Cedarwood Texas vs Virginia vs Atlas vs Alaska The three major perfumery cedarwoods each offer distinct character. Texas (Juniperus mexicana) is the sweetest and most pencil-like, with pronounced balsamic-smoky depth and excellent tenacity. Virginia (Juniperus virginiana) is drier and more austere, with a sharper, less sweet profile. Atlas (Cedrus atlantica)—a true cedar—is the most refined, with cleaner, brighter woody character and subtle camphoraceous lift. Alaska (Chamaecyparis nootkatensis) is the most complex and unusual, with fresh sparkling grapefruit-citrus top notes, spicy cumin-like facets, and leathery-herbal undertones alongside its woody base. Use Texas for warm, sweet woody effects; Virginia for dry, austere woodiness; Atlas when you want elegant cedar brightness; Alaska when you need fresh, spicy complexity with citrus sparkle.

missing_other.title: Cedarwood Oil, Alaska
missing_other.description: Owing to a very high natural content of nootkatene and nootkatone, this treasure from Firmenich has a definite grapefruit character. A fascinating and unique wood oil, Alaskan Cedar is produced entirely from the sustainable offcuts of the forestry industry. This is also a replacer for the now discontinued Wood 49 of Robertet and is sometimes referred to as Nootka Tree Oil. In Firmenich's words: “ Not as camphoraceous and smoky as a cedarwood but stronger, longer-lasting and very linear.”

missing_other.title: Cedarwood “Superior” Oil, Virginia
missing_other.description: Virginian Cedarwood oil (from the cypress family) is the most versatile and important of the various so-called cedarwood oils (the others being Texas, Himalayan and Atlas, the latter two being members of the pine family and not the cypress family). It is an excellent extender to Sandalwood oil, Guaiacwood and Oud and owing to its refined and low-key odour it can be used as a wonderful canvas material upon which to build an entire fragrance. This Payan Bertrand quality is of a particularly fine character, with only the nicest aspects of the oil presenting.

missing_other.title: Cedrat Heart
missing_other.description: Cedrat Heart captures the most compelling fractions of citron peel oil — the bright, mouthwatering zest and the elegant bitterness — while discarding the unstable monoterpenes that make whole citrus oils so fleeting. What remains is sparkling, sweet-bitter, and surprisingly tenacious. A candied quality sets it apart from lemon or bergamot. This concentrated citrus is equivalent to a terpeneless oil, so you use it at roughly one-tenth the rate of whole cedrat. That concentration means citrus character reaches deep into the heart of a composition rather than flashing and vanishing in the first minutes. Classic Guerlain-style colognes depend on exactly this kind of persistent citrus backbone. The sweet-bitter balance invites creative use beyond pure cologne work. It sharpens vetiver and woody compositions with a zesty edge. In gourmand accords, the candied facet bridges citrus and vanilla. Try it alongside bergamot and neroli for a full hesperidic heart, or with lavender and coumarin for a citrus fougere with real sparkle.

missing_other.title: Cedrat Oil, Italy
missing_other.description: Cedrat, AKA Citron, is one of the oldest citrus fruit — indeed it is one of the varieties from which most other citrus has developed from. Cedrat has a wonderfully gourmand quality which makes it a wonderful oil to use in modern food-related formulas. Reminder: this is an essential oil for manufacturing and it is not a food. Do not consume this product. Origin: Italy Part: Peel Method: Cold pressed at source

missing_other.title: Celery Seed Oil
missing_other.description: Celery seed bears little resemblance to the scent of its more well-known celery plant, having really just a faint nuance of green celery. Mostly this material has a warm quality that is not entirely dissimilar to the scent of Cis Jasmone. Unsurprisingly, then, celery seed oil is a wonderworker when it comes to adding naturalness to heady florals; in particularly it adds space and lightness to intense tuberose accords. Despite its light aroma, celery seed is deceptively powerful and can overtake a blend quite easily, so careful dosing is required. Origin: India Part: Seeds Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Celestafleur™
missing_other.description: Forget Lyral ® and Lilial replacers; now is the time for the ascent of true alternatives that offer beauty and elegance and the benefit of what modern lily and green chemicals have to offer us as perfumers. Celestafleur ™ is radiant and long lasting but it has a quality that really sets it apart from the classic muguet chemicals: it is effervescent. Celestafleur ™ sparkles like stars in the firmament and it is from that characteristic that it derives its name. Usable at a massive 9%, this can be a one for one replacer for Lyral ® and Lilial but it can also be overdosed as the foundation of a highly modern monolithic lily scent. Celestafleur ™ makes for a perfect general floraliser upon which to layer other luscious flowers, as in the case of Chanel's Gabrielle (2017) for which we present a demonstration formula further down this page. Celestafleur ™ blends incredibly well with citrus oils and has a synergy with green, ozonic and watery chemicals such as Calone® Plus , Cis 3 Hexenol (and its esters), Florhydral , Floralozone , and Helional . Bases such as Amazonia ™ are elevated when combined with Celestafleur ™, and herbal bases such as Suralette™ Extra and Artemal ™ are wonderful with it.

missing_other.title: Chocovan
missing_other.description: With the very high cost of cocoa related materials, Chocovan from Givaudan is a God-send. It has a powerful powdered chocolate profile which, despite its clearly gourmand characteristics, is surprisingly versatile. Traces add a natural powderiness to orris accords, and it blends beautifully with resins for a modern take on the classic oriental form. It pairs beautifully with coffee notes, hazelnut materials like Filbertone , and lactones for creamy dessert accords. While we sell it pure, it is highly recommended that you keep a 10% dilution handy as it really is much stronger than it appears to be upon first sniff, and it has a tendency to overwhelm. The base saves you significant formulation time when chocolate is your target.

missing_other.title: Choya Loban
missing_other.description: Think about the difference between holding a lump of frankincense resin to your nose and placing it on a glowing coal. Conventional frankincense oil preserves the bright, citrusy, piney top of the raw resin. Choya loban preserves the smoke — it captures what frankincense actually smells like when it burns. The result is sweet, balsamic, deeply warm, and comforting. Indian frankincense resin is roasted in a sealed clay pot at high temperature, and the aromatic smoke is captured by distillation. The natural balsamic sweetness of the resin survives the charring process, softening the smokiness into something rounded and approachable. Of the three traditional choya materials — raal, nakh, and loban — this is the most immediately familiar to Western noses. Use choya loban wherever you want the smell of frankincense incense rather than frankincense oil. It excels in dark amber accords, ecclesiastical compositions, and resinous bases where conventional olibanum feels too clean or too bright. Pair it with labdanum, benzoin, and opoponax for a complete temple-incense foundation, or with styrax for added depth.

missing_other.title: Choya Nakh
missing_other.description: This is one of the strangest materials in all of perfumery. Choya nakh is made by dry-roasting the hard, nail-like trapdoor discs from certain sea snails in a sealed clay pot, then distilling the smoke into sandalwood oil. These same shell pieces appear in the Book of Exodus as an ingredient in sacred temple incense, and they have been used across India, Japan, and the Middle East for centuries. There is smoke here, certainly, but beneath it lies something oceanic and mineral — a briny, mossy depth with faint animalic warmth that no synthetic marine note can touch. In aged choya nakh, the harsher smoke recedes and the amber-marine character deepens beautifully. It is a natural route to smoky-marine effects that feel organic and alive rather than clean and manufactured. Use choya nakh with extreme restraint — a single extra drop changes everything. In heavy dilution it reveals extraordinary nuance: salt, dry moss, warm mineral amber. Pair it with oud and labdanum for dark orientals, or use traces in marine accords for a living, salty depth. Best appreciated well diluted before blending.

missing_other.title: Choya Raal
missing_other.description: Choya raal is made by roasting the resin of the sal tree (Shorea robusta) inside a sealed clay pot until it chars, then capturing the smoke. The sal is one of India's great native hardwoods — sacred in both Hinduism and Buddhism, with tradition holding that Buddha was born and died beneath one. The result of the distillation smells of dry, mineral smoke with a sweet resinous undertow — imagine standing downwind of a controlled resin fire on a warm night. This is one of the few genuinely natural leather notes available. The dry, mineral smokiness creates a leather effect that synthetic approaches struggle to replicate. In traditional Indian perfumery, choya raal provides the smoky backbone of complex attars like shamama and hina — the dark foundation that everything else is built upon. If you know cade oil or birch tar, choya raal occupies similar smoky-leathery territory — but it is noticeably warmer and sweeter because it starts from a balsamic resin rather than wood or bark. Cade and birch tar hit harder, more phenolic, more purely tarry. Choya raal keeps an amber sweetness underneath the smoke that they lack, making it softer and more versatile. Use it wherever you want natural smokiness and leather without harshness, or try it as a warmer alternative to birch tar in leather accords. Pair it with labdanum and cypriol for a complete smoky foundation, or with patchouli for earthy darkness. Caution: do not confuse the sal tree with the cannonball tree (Couroupita guianensis), a showy South American species widely misidentified as the sal at temples across South Asia since the 1880s. They are completely unrelated.

missing_other.title: Cinnamon Bark Ceylon “Supreme” Oil
missing_other.description: In the golden age of perfumery one type of cinnamon was king: cinnamon bark oil Ceylon with 60% cinnamaldehyde. Our “Supreme” oil is exactly that. No competing product comes close to the exquisite complexity imparted by our precious cinnamon bark oil. Any cinnamon with less than 60% cinnamaldehyde content is an inferior product. Featured in such masterpieces as YSL Opium (1977), Dior's Poison (1985), and the treasure of the golden age, Jicky (1889) by Guerlain (along with many other Guerlain classics). This is the smoothest and most complete cinnamon bark. It's fullness and subtle nuances even surpass that of modern CO2 extractions! One whiff will transport you to the wild jungles of faraway Ceylon. This is the gold standard of cinnamon extracts. Blends beautifully with sticky fruit notes (particularly plum), resins and balsams. Origin: Ceylon (Sri Lanka) Part: Bark only Method of production: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Cinnamon Ceylon Tincture 25%
missing_other.description: In days past, even though cinnamon bark and leaves had long given up their precious oils to the steam distillers of the 19th century, tincture of cinnamon bark was still a thing and was prized for its softer and more rounded scent profile. Fragrances such as the original Jicky (formula below) capitalised on this by using the tincture to modify essential oil of cinnamon . This Fraterworks Tincture is made according to the oldest traditions of French infusion manufacture with purest glacial food grade alcohol. It makes for a wonderful alternative to cinnamon oil and SFE products. Origin: Ceylon (Sri Lanka) Variety: Cinnamomum verum Part: Dried bark Method: Cold ethanol tincture

missing_other.title: Cinnamon Leaf Oil, Low BAP
missing_other.description: Cinnamon leaf oil is the unsung hero of the cinnamon family. While the bark oil sits at the head of the table as patriarch, cinnamon leaf is usually relegated to the role of little brother. But ourcinnamon leaf oil is not just a cheap soap oil; it brings a brighter top note spice to fragrances and accents the richer deeper bark oil as well as standing on its own. Our cinnamon leaf oil from Ceylon has been hand picked from the offerings of numerous suppliers. We are very proud of this Ceylon origin oil which presents with all usual characteristics of leaf oil but with a more intensely rich body and dry down. Like cinnamon bark, the leaf oil blends beautifully with sticky fruit notes (particularly plum). It is also a wonderful companion to rose in fragrances and works extremely well alongside the classic oriental resins. Origin: Ceylon (Sri Lanka) Variety: Cinnamomum zeylanicum Part: Foliage Method of production: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Cinnamon “Gold” Absolute
missing_other.description: We stock several cinnamon materials — Ceylon bark oil , leaf oil , the tincture — and each has its place. But nothing we have ever carried smells like this. Cinnamon "Gold" Absolute is an extraction of the whole bark that captures everything steam distillation leaves behind: the sweet, baked, buttery facets that make cinnamon one of the most universally beloved spices on earth. Where cinnamon bark oil hits you with a sharp, aldehydic top note that can overwhelm a formula at even modest levels, this absolute is smooth from the first moment. It smells the way cinnamon tastes — warm, rounded, confectionery, with a Red Hots candy sweetness that is immediately recognisable and immediately appealing. The colour is a deep olive green, slightly viscous but readily pourable at room temperature. We also offer it at 20% in TEC for easy weighing and incorporation. In perfumery, this changes what cinnamon can do. An amber base of labdanum , benzoin, and vanillin — materials that already lean warm and sweet — becomes something extraordinary with the addition of this absolute. The cinnamon warmth integrates seamlessly instead of sitting on top as an aggressive spike. Gourmand compositions that would normally require careful balancing to tame a bark oil can use this absolute more freely, because there is nothing to tame. It also works brilliantly in contexts where you want cinnamon warmth without the spice-rack cliché: woody-amber accords, soft orientals, tobacco bases, even certain floral compositions where a thread of baked spice adds intrigue without disrupting the balance. Pair it with our Coffee Espresso SFE, Tonka Bean “Luxe” Absolute , and Vanilla Supreme for something that smells like the best café in the world.

missing_other.title: Cistus Creticus Resin Absolute, 50% ETH
missing_other.description: This is a speciality Fraterworks product. Starting from wild cistus gum gathered by hand in Crete using the ancient l adanisterion tool, we cold extract the pure labdanum heart and then remove 50% of the alcohol leaving us with a classic “Resin Absolute of Cistus Creticus, 50% ETH”. Cretan cistus (also known as Cretan Rock Rose or Rockrose) is very similar to the more well-known cistus ladanifer, the source of cistus essential oil , labdanum resinoid and labdanum absolute but it differs in having a richer complex of accent notes. A more radiant resin, cistus creticus has distinct nuances of fine styrax resin , frankincense and herbs. We use pure food grade ethanol produced with water from glacial lakes and the lowest temperature possible to extract the resin absolute from the raw gum. This maintains the integrity of the product and respects the heritage and labour of the men of Crete who collect this material in the same way as their ancient forebears. Crude Exudate → Steam Distillation → Essential Oil Crude Exudate → Non-Ethanol Solvent Extraction → Resinoid Crude Exudate → Ethanol Extraction → Resin Absolute of Exudate, 𝓷 % [evaporated to 𝓃 %] Crude Exudate → Ethanol Extraction → Resin Absolute [vacuum distilled to 100%] While a resin absolute is often wrongly referred to simply as an "absolute", the correct use of that term within the balsams category is for an alcohol extraction of a previously extracted resinoid (usually produced with hexane or other non-alcohol solvent). Resinoid → Alcohol Extraction → Absolute Origin: Crete Variety: Cistus Creticus Part: Raw exudate from foliage Harvest Method: Traditional harvesting with a Ladanisterion

missing_other.title: Cistus Green Absolute
missing_other.description: Cistus green is all about terroir and artisanship. It is extracted from the young foliage of cistus plants growing wild in the Moroccan Atlas Mountains. It has more of the green leaf volatiles of the plant and less of the dark animalic growl of labdanum absolute (which is why it was used in perfumes like Ralph Lauren's Polo Green and Coco by Chanel). And because of the special conditions of the area in which it grows, it even has some trace elements that are unique to its type. Use it for a more modern approach to cistus. Accords with Cistus essential oil and Labdanum Light absolute are extremely special and new, and this finds itself perfectly suited to aquatics and ozonics in a way that the richer labdanum products normally don't. It loves to be with herbal notes (not surprisingly) so you must try it with Artemal , and the very nature of its colour cries out for blending with green mandarin (à la Coco ). Because cistus absolute is highly viscous, we offer it pure and diluted to 50% in triethyl citrate , a completely natural, odorless plant extract. Perfect for perfumers who maintain an all-natural ingredient philosophy.

missing_other.title: Cistus Oil “Rock Rose”
missing_other.description: As featured in the luxurious fragrance Rock Rose (2016) by Clive Christian, cistus oil is the essential oil of the plant more commonly known for labdanum resinoids and absolutes. Cistus is supremely elegant, offering a wonderfully bright top note. It blends extremely well with other resinoids (particularly those of its own family) and is synergistic with aldehydes. The extraction we sell has been selected from the offerings of all the top global suppliers. It is particularly vibrant and has the clearest and most warming scent of luxurious labdanum. Due to it's high cost and power, we are offering this pure and at 10% dilution in natural odourless triethyl citrate.

missing_other.title: Citroasis
missing_other.description: Citroasis revolutionises citrus perfumery by solving volatility issues inherent to natural citrus oils. This pre-engineered specialty base delivers authentic citrus character with unprecedented 3-4 day longevity on smelling strips. Contains stabilised citral acetals that slowly release freshness over extended periods. Use at 1-2% to boost natural citruses or up to 10% as foundational core structure. The aldehydic sparkle combined with neroli heart creates an instantly recognisable cologne signature that performs exceptionally in modern fresh fragrances. Blend this material with Paradise Molecule ® for enhanced diffusion, Dihydromyrcenol for masculine freshness, or Ambroxan for contemporary amber-citrus contrasts. The built-in grapefruit sulphur notes pair beautifully with Elemi or Frankincense for naturalistic bridges. Always work from 10% dilution due to extreme potency and consider IFRA limits of 4.3% maximum in fine fragrance applications.

missing_other.title: Citronella Oil
missing_other.description: Citronella oil is fresh, sweet, and lemony-rosy — a clean, bright, green-grass character with a surprisingly warm woody drydown. It bridges citrus and floral families in a single natural oil. The sweetness is genuine and complex, not the harsh chemical note you might expect from the name. Citronella oil appeared in two of the twentieth century's greatest perfumes — Tabu and Ma Griffe — where it contributed fresh, rosy-green sparkle to compositions that redefined their categories. It fell from favour because cheap citronella became synonymous with insect-repelling candles. That association is deeply unfair to the real oil. Citronella deserves a comeback. Use it in green chypres, citrus colognes, and rosy-fresh compositions — it adds a naturalistic sparkle that isolated materials cannot replicate. Pair it with geranium, bergamot, cedarwood, and oakmoss for the kind of bright, green freshness that defined mid-century perfumery.

missing_other.title: Civet “Supreme” Absolute
missing_other.description: Ethiopia (historically Abyssinia) is the classic source of civet materials for perfumery. Our highest quality "supreme" absolute (obtained within the CITES guidelines from Ranched animals) is intensely fecal and, to most people, extremely obnoxious in scent. However, in dilution (typically from 1–10%) the material becomes far more appealing and begins to show the qualities for which is has earned its long-standing position as the peak of perfection in legally traded perfume animalics. Civet absolute is easier to use than raw paste as you simply dilute it to your needs and use it immediately; on the other hand the unprocessed secretion must be tinctured and rested for many months (or even years) to be fully usable. Civet is a CITES appendix II product. In most countries this can be lawfully traded without extra paperwork if purchased for personal use. We recommend checking in advance with your own regulatory bodies. If you are purchasing for commercial reasons you may need a CITES re-export or origin certificate to accompany your purchase. You should check with your national authorities. We charge $60 USD for this certificate and it takes approximately ten days for us to apply and provide it. Simply contact us for help. We will endeavour to make the process as seamless and speedy as possible. NOTE: We ship civet and other very high-odour products in sealed foil bags to prevent cross-contamination in the event of leaks or parcel damage. We are also now selling this at 10% in natural TEC to make it more affordable and easier to dose. Origin: Abyssinia (Ethiopia) Part: Glandular secretion Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Civette Synth 039648
missing_other.description: Civet whether natural or synthetic is a marvelous naturaliser. In florals it is indispensible as evidenced by the masterwork of François Coty, 1917 Chypre. Use it one for one anywhere natural civet is used for a vegan alternative to one of the famous, and perhaps most controversial animal musks. For those needing the natural article, we also sell Civet “Supreme” Absolute .

missing_other.title: Clary Sage Absolute
missing_other.description: Clary Sage Absolute is a solvent extraction from Russian clary sage with the most wonderful herbal pipe tobacco quality. This is a solid and requires heating to liquify. It can be added pure to your formula as it will dissolve in the other materials. Average Constituents Linalyl Acetate 66.5% ( cf. French Oil: 49–73.6%) Linalool 8.9% ( cf. French Oil: 9–16.0%) Geramacrene D 9.4% ( cf. French Oil: 1.6–2%) Sclareol 2.4% β-Caryophyllene 1.9% ( cf. French Oil: 1.4–1.6%) α-Copaene 1.1% Bicyclogermacrene 1.1% * R. Tisserand * R. Young. Essential Oil Safety. Churchill Livingstone Elsevier, 2014. pp 1084–1085. Synergies and Blending Clary sage absolute is an excellent fixative and extender for Clary Sage Oil, France. Blends well with Bergamot Oil, FCF and other citrus oils , Cardamom , Cinnamon , Cedarwood Virginia, Olibanum and Frankincense , Geranium Bourbon , Genet , Hay (Flouve) , Jasmine Absolute , Juniper Oil Rectified , Lavender ( oil and absolute ), Lavandin , Patchouli , Rose Absolute , Sandalwood Mysore Oil , and Ylang-ylang . Complimentary Base pairings: Fleur de Tabac , Suralette™ Extra , Verdantol , Artemal ™, Jasmin Russe , Foin Coupé de Laire . Origin: Russia Part: Leaves and flowering tops Method: Solvent extracted absolute

missing_other.title: Clary Sage Oil
missing_other.description: Our clary sage oil from Provence opens with complex notes of herbs and flowers. It is by far the most floral and luxurious clary sage we have experienced which is what led us to select it for our exclusive offering. Traditionally manufactured and steam distilled onsite, this oil is the finest example of a truly versatile and loved top note oil. Clary sage blends perfectly with bergamot , lavender and other fresh notes, adding complexity and interest. Touches were used to great effect in Moment Supreme where it modifies the beautiful aldehydic lavender opening and helps unite the central floral notes of the fragrance with the sweet labdanum in the dry down. Origin: France Part: Leaves and flowering tops Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Clematis
missing_other.description: Clematis flowers have no odour and so historically (like classic orchid bases,) they are fantasy creations. This Fraterworks base is a restoration of the wonderous Roure Clematis base of the 1930s which was used by Jean Carles in combination with his Fleur de Tabac base to construct Shocking for Schiaparelli in 1937, a wild perfume built around a heat of pink florals. It is from this fashion house and fragrance that the colour “shocking pink” was born. Wonderfully floral, rich and aldehydic, this clematis base would find a home in a modern fragrance as easily as it did the classics of yesteryear.

missing_other.title: Clove Bud “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: Clove bud oil is perhaps the most versatile of all the spices. It adds naturalness and warmth to rose bases, delightful spiced notes to gourmands and interesting medicinal notes to more exotic blends. This clove bud oil is a speciality of Payan Bertrand and is superior to all others. We hand selected it from the myriad options on the market today. Having a sweeter and more vanilla nuance, this Madagascan clove is extremely close to the near-mythical Zanzibar clove bud oil of the past.

missing_other.title: Clovebud Zanzibar Tincture 25%
missing_other.description: In the golden age of perfumery the most sought after clovebuds were those of Zanzibar, hand plucked in the beating African sun on plantations owned by the Sultan. The sultan is now exiled and the global demand is mostly met by Madagascar. But many Zanzibar families still make a living harvesting the buds of wild trees by hand. Fraterworks imports these superior cloves from Zanzibar and tinctures them with care using the classical cold alcohol method. Our tincturing process uses the finest odourless food grade alcohol only. Absolutely no synthetic plasticisers, denaturants or diluents are used, resulting in a totally natural product by ISO 9235 standards. This is the gold standard of clove extracts and every care has been taken to ensure consistent excellence in every drop. Tincture of cloves has a smoother and sweeter fragrance than the essential oil now commonly found. It also has the power to soften the oil when used in combination with it. Origin: Zanzibar Variety: Syzygium aromaticum (L.) Merr. & L.M. Perry Part: Unopened flower buds Method: Cold ethanol tincture

missing_other.title: Cocoa Absolute 5% IPM
tags: locale:new! do not confuse with 20% resinoid from MANE
missing_other.description: Cocoa absolute opens with immediate dark chocolate richness reminiscent of melted couverture. Its roasted character evokes freshly ground cacao beans whilst creamy liqueur facets add indulgence. The subtle bitter edge provides sophisticated balance preventing cloying sweetness. You'll find this absolute essential for authentic chocolate notes in gourmand compositions where synthetic alternatives disappoint. It excels at adding sensuality to amber bases and unexpected depth to white florals. Use it sparingly—its intense concentration means tiny amounts create lasting chocolate impressions without dominating delicate accords. Blend cocoa absolute with vanilla and tonka for complete gourmand indulgence or combine with benzoin for balsamic chocolate warmth. Pair with coffee absolute to enhance roasted facets. This material bridges fruity top notes with amber bases beautifully, particularly with cherry and citrus accords. This comes pre-diluted to 5% in IPM by LMR so it is not suitable for all natural perfumers. Resinoid vs Absolute Cocoa Resinoid from V. MANE Fils presents a slightly bitter dark chocolate profile ideal for fine and functional applications. LMR's Cocoa Absolute offers superior aromatic refinement with an even truer-to-life chocolate character. Where MANE's resinoid provides robust chocolate with practical advantages, LMR's absolute delivers concentrated luxury with deeper complexity and smoother integration into sophisticated compositions.

missing_other.title: Cocoa Resinoid 20% TEC
missing_other.description: Imagine the smell of smashed chunks of chocolate slowly warming in your hands and releasing their enticing aroma; white chocolate, dark chocolate, milk chocolate and every variety in between. From V. MANE Fils comes a truly wonderful cocoa resinoid extracted with ethanol rather than harsh chemicals and made practical with the addition of natural odourless triethyl citrate — our own personal favourite when it comes to natural diluents and dilutants. Cocoa resinoids and absolutes are famously difficult to work with and all suppliers tend to offer the virtually impossible pure product which all need diluting not just to render them usable but also because cocoa is a very strong material (deceptively so). This beautiful resinoid is clean, powder, richly chocolate and wonderfully clean. There are no off notes and no surprises. It's just good chocolate. Some of our favourite combos are Wild Cherry and Cocoa Absolute with a touch of Rum P. Jungle Essence for a crazily good Cherry Chocolate Liqueur accord or blend it with all the rich orris materials to enhance and enrich their powdery side, just as master perfumer Olivier Polge did in the now near-mythical 2005 original Dior Homme Intense. This Cocoa Resinoid has

missing_other.title: Coconut CO2, P. Jungle Essence
tags: locale:heat to melt and use bottles not pots
missing_other.description: This extract smells exactly like cracking open a fresh coconut. Warm, creamy richness fills the air alongside waxy-nutty facets and gentle toasted sweetness. MANE's low-temperature CO2 process captures the full aromatic picture from bright fruity top through rich, buttery base. You can add this to white floral hearts without creating an overtly tropical effect. Instead it plumps up petal notes and renders the fleshy quality of flowers through textural creaminess. It also forms the backbone of convincing beach-inspired accords where synthetic coconut reads hollow. Try it with vanilla and tonka for rich gourmand indulgence. Blend with jasmine and ylang-ylang for an unexpected tropical floral that avoids cliche. Massoia bark CO2 makes an excellent partner, layering complementary coconut facets for deep, convincing richness. To power it up for a bold coconut note we recommend Coconut Delight, our complex coconut base, or Gamma Octalactone, the single best coconut lactone. And for a beautifully tropical perfume, try it with Gardenia J. Ellis , Rum CO2 , and Dark Ginger CO2 P. Jungle Essence. Pure, this is solid. So we offer it in a 10% solution with IPM. Natural perfumers should purchase the undiluted material as IPM ( Isopropyl Myristate / MIP) is a synthetic diluent.

missing_other.title: Coconut Delight
missing_other.description: In perfume history coconut is often supplied as a simple touch of Nonalactone Gamma (Aldehyde C-18 so-called) with occasional accents added by other lactones that vary in intensity and nuance. Coconut Delight, on the other hand, gives you the full coconut experience. A delicious oily opening leads to a sweeter and more interesting dry down. This can be used as a replacer for nonalactone and is far easier to dose. We recommend starting at around 0.5% and working up to doses of 5% though you can certainly use more if you wish. Coconut Delight blends beautifully with our boozy Amaretto Saronno base and Raspberry Ripple .

missing_other.title: Coffee Arabica CO2
missing_other.description: Foggy headed you rise from your slumber and drift to the kitchen to imbibe your first coffee for the day. The rich scent of freshly roasted beans awakens your senses as warm sunlight streams through the windows; all is good with the world and your day now begins. Coffee Arabic Pure Jungle Essence from V. MANE Fils manages to encapsulate that very moment when the colour rushes back to the world and the fuzz of sleep departs. It is the scent of hot coffee, freshly poured. It is the scent of optimism and the scent of anticipation. This is such a rich and luxurious coffee extract that nothing at all compares to it; no other supplier comes close to capturing this most beloved material. This is practically begging to be part of a gourmand fragrance. Pair it with the caramel notes of Opoponax Resinoid , the chocolate nuance of Orris Resinoid , or the fresh pasty delight of Tonka Bean resinoid; and don't forget luscious Bourbon Vanilla Absolute . MANE states that this product is soluble in 10% Oil, TEC, DPG and IPM. For full solubility in alcohol it should be diluted with 50/50 ethanol and IPM.

missing_other.title: Coffee Espresso SFE
missing_other.description: Our Coffee Arabica CO2 from MANE is the gentle morning cup — warm sunlight, the colour rushing back to the world. It is refined, rounded, optimistic. This is not that coffee. This is 11pm in Naples. A tiny cup, almost too hot to hold, from a machine that has been running all day. The barista doesn't smile. He doesn't need to. The espresso speaks for itself: dark, intense, slightly burnt, impossibly concentrated. You bury your face in the grounds and breathe in. That is what this smells like. Firmenich's Coffee Espresso SFE captures a roast level and an intensity that the MANE extract deliberately avoids. Where the Arabica CO2 paints a nuanced portrait — chocolatey, nutty, sophisticated — this one fills the room with a single, uncompromising statement: coffee, at full volume. The slightly charred edge lifts woody-smoky undertones that make it feel less gourmand and more animalic. Less pastry shop, more leather armchair. Both are supercritical CO2 extracts. Both are extraordinary. But they are as different as a light-roast Ethiopian pour-over and a ristretto from a Neapolitan bar — the word "coffee" and precious little else in common. You definitely want both. The Espresso SFE cuts through sweetness rather than adding to it. Pair it with tobacco, leather, labdanum, or dark woods for compositions where a softer coffee note would simply vanish. With birch tar and castoreum, it produces a coffee-leather accord that is devastatingly good.

missing_other.title: Cognac Oil, Green
missing_other.description: Green Cognac Oil opens with a distinctly panary note with a recognisable dry-winey character—tart, herbaceous, and immediately evocative of crisp white wine. Green apple facets dominate the top, while fatty-oily undertones add naturalistic depth. The herbaceous-grassy dryness recalls late summer hayfields, and the overall effect is of sparkling, boozy freshness that transforms any composition it touches.
