The initial baked-bread note makes this very an excellent oil to temper the saccharine intensity of sweeter gourmands. This essential oil comes from wine lees—the yeasty sediment left at the bottom of oak barrels after Cognac fermentation. Copper still distillation creates the distinctive emerald-green colour through oxidation, a traditional French method now increasingly rare. The result is an intensely diffusive oil with remarkable 200-hour substantivity. Work with it heavily diluted (5–10%) to tame its raw power before blending. Use Cognac Oil Green in trace amounts—one or two drops can lift an entire composition. It excels in colognes, fougères, and aftershave fragrances where its sparkling freshness adds sophistication. Blend with bergamot, lavender, clary sage, and ylang-ylang for classic effects. Pair with methyl anthranilate for authentic grape-wine accords or the rarer allyl anthranilate if you seek more power. The tart green apple character makes it valuable in fruit compositions seeking naturalistic depth rather than synthetic sweetness. Cognac Oil Green vs Cognac Oil White These two Cognac oils share the same botanical source (Vitis vinifera lees) but differ meaningfully in character. Green Cognac, distilled in traditional copper stills, is bolder, more boozy, with pronounced herbaceous-grassy notes, green apple tartness, and an almost harsh bready intensity that demands careful dosing. White Cognac, distilled in stainless steel, is smoother and more refined—less boozy, with rounder fruity-floral qualities and a champagne-like elegance that's easier to b

missing_other.title: Cognac Oil, White
missing_other.description: White Cognac Oil greets you with rounded, fruity-winey warmth — muscatel grape tartness and a champagne-like sparkle that immediately distinguishes it from its harsher green sibling. Delicate floral nuances thread through the dry-wine character. The overall impression is of polished, boozy elegance without any fatty heaviness. Use White Cognac Oil where you need boozy sparkle without overwhelming power. It lifts floral accords — jasmine, rose, and neroli all respond beautifully — and adds sophisticated winey warmth to orientals. Work in dilution; even at five percent this oil transforms a composition's top notes. Blend with methyl anthranilate for an authentic grape-wine accord, or pair with vanilla and Benzoin Oiffac for brandy-amber warmth. Stainless steel distillation gives White Cognac its cleaner, more refined character versus the copper-distilled green type. Use this version for feminine florals and orientals. Cognac Oil Green vs Cognac Oil White These two Cognac oils share the same botanical source (Vitis vinifera lees) but differ meaningfully in character. Green Cognac, distilled in traditional copper stills, is bolder, more boozy, with pronounced herbaceous-grassy notes, green apple tartness, and an almost harsh bready intensity that demands careful dosing. White Cognac, distilled in stainless steel, is smoother and more refined—less boozy, with rounder fruity-floral qualities and a champagne-like elegance that's easier to blend. Use Green Cognac when you want powerful boozy lift in heavier compositions, forest themes, or masculine fougères; reach for White Cognac when you need delicate fruity-floral effects in oriental and feminine compositions. Both require trace amounts—their intensity easily overwhelms at higher concentrations.

missing_other.title: Cologne Imperiale 1853
missing_other.description: Use it just like perfumer's alcohol. This is the original 1853 eau de cologne that launched the Guerlain brand. It is a ready-to-wear 5% strength cologne as was the norm for distilled fragrances such as these. According to the house: “[c]reated in 1853 by Pierre-François-Pascal Guerlain, Eau de Cologne Imperiale is the first cologne Guerlain specially composed for the Empress Eugenie, wife of Napoleon III, earning its creator the title of ‘Her Majesty's patented Perfumer’.” This cologne was used as the base for the first version of Jicky which was decidedly different from the construction style of later versions. Below is a formula for a Jicky-style fragrance that illustrates how this was done as well as a formula for an Eau Sauvage type to demonstrate a modern use of the style. This is a wonderful technique never seen today but is certainly due a renaissance. And now with Fraterworks Cologne Imperiale 1853 , it is possible to experience this treasured perfumery style. Fraterworks distills this cologne in a classic copper still (as pictured) just as the original was. A truly unique product. Top notes: Bergamot, Lemon, Orange, Rosemary Heart Notes: Neroli, Lavender, Verbena Base Notes: Cedarwood, Tonka bean, Benzoin, Ambergris

missing_other.title: Compound 33
missing_other.description: Compound 33 is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Santal 33 from Le Labo. Launched in 2011, this is a modern woody fragrance built around Australian sandalwood and cedarwood with a distinctive violet-iris accord that gives it its characteristic dry, slightly pickle-like opening. This compound features sandalwood lactones and cedarwood derivatives creating a dry, pencil-shaving effect, enhanced with Iso E Super for diffusion and Ambrox for depth. The addition of cardamom, papyrus, and leather accord creates a minimalist yet complex composition that has become one of the most recognisable fragrances of the 2010s. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Violet Leaf, Australian Sandalwood, Cardamom Heart Notes: Iris, Papyrus, Ambrox Base Notes: Cedarwood, Leather Accord, Musk

missing_other.title: Compound Afternoon
missing_other.description: Compound Afternoon is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Afternoon Swim from Louis Vuitton. Launched in 2019, this is a bright citrus-aquatic fragrance built around mandarin and orange with a distinctive ginger note and clean ambroxan base. This compound features high levels of mandarin and orange oils combined with fresh ginger and a transparent aquatic accord. The base of ambroxan provides the characteristic clean, skin-like drydown while maintaining the citrus brightness throughout wear. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Mandarin, Orange, Bergamot Heart Notes: Ginger, Aquatic Accord Base Notes: Ambergris

missing_other.title: Compound Aramis
missing_other.description: Aramis, launched in 1966 and created by the great Bernard Chant, was an icon of classic masculinity, is to be discontinued. It was a derivative of Gris' Cabochard (by the same perfumer) but replacing the floral notes with green aromatic ones. This compound is for a scent in the style of the original with authentic oakmoss levels, musk ambrette, and animalic notes that modern reformulations have stripped away. The opening is sharp and challenging: sparkling aldehydes cut through herbal artemisia and bergamot, lifted by thyme and clover. The heart reveals a complex spiced floral accord of patchouli, sage, jasmine and cardamom, grounded by powdery orris root. The base is where Aramis earns its reputation – rich leather, dense oakmoss, warm sandalwood, vetiver and amber create a foundation of unmistakable masculinity. The result is a fragrance of commanding presence with exceptional longevity and projection – not for the faint-hearted. To evaluate properly, dilute to 14% and use a smelling strip. Do not put on the skin. Note: This compound is based on the original 1966 formula and is not IFRA compliant. It is intended for educational use only and not for commercial resale or cosmetic use. Top Notes: Aldehydes, Bergamot, Artemisia, Thyme, Clover, Myrtle Heart Notes: Patchouli, Sage, Jasmine, Cardamom, Orris Root Base Notes: Leather, Oakmoss, Musk, Vetiver, Sandalwood, Amber

missing_other.title: Compound Armenie
missing_other.description: Compound Armenie is our faithful reconstruction of a scent in the style of Bois d'Arménie by Guerlain, based off meticulous GCMS analyses and research. Launched in 2006 as part of the L'Art & La Matière collection, this is a smoky oriental woody fragrance inspired by the tradition of burning benzoin-infused Armenian paper as incense. Tragically discontinued in 2024, this compound is as close as you can possibly get to the original formula which we have painstakingly restored. his fragrance costs upwards of $1,000 per bottle on the secondary market today. This compound features a rich resinous heart of benzoin and guaiac wood that evokes smouldering incense. The top notes of frankincense, iris and pink pepper provide a powdery, spiced opening with immediate smoky depth, while coriander adds an aromatic lift to the heart. The base delivers copaiba balsam alongside earthy patchouli and soft white musk for a warm, lingering finish. The result is a contemplative, incense-laden fragrance with excellent longevity and close-to-skin projection – refined, meditative and quietly distinctive. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Incense, Iris, Pink Pepper Heart Notes: Benzoin, Guaiac Wood, Coriander Base Notes: Copaiba Balsam, Patchouli, White Musk

missing_other.title: Compound Balade™
missing_other.description: In French, Balade means "ride" and it is a term used in the popular French film "La Balade Sauvage" (The Wild Ride). It is also the name of a marvellous Dior fragrance created by François Demachy and launched in 2018 in their Collection Privée. Alas it has been discontinued from 2024. Balade Sauvage is a light cologne that has perhaps the most wearable representation of a fig note. The scent is hugely popular, garnering 4.3 stars out of 5 on Fragrantica and it contains no EU or IFRA prohibited materials so the discontinuation seems rather odd. Fraterworks now presents this intricate and luxurious scent in the style of the original in compound form for perfumers to understand and appreciate the odour of a masterpiece prior to dilution and mass distribution. The price is very good — in fact it is commercially viable at the 1kg point. Top Notes: Ozone, Bergamot, Petitgrain Heart Notes: Fig Tree, Fig, Sunlight, Seaside, Peach, Orange Blossom, Hedione, Rose Base Notes: Pebbles, Amberwood, Labdanum, Vanilla Allergens: Citral, Geraniol, Citronellol, Eugenol, Limonene, Linalool, Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, Farnesol, Coumarin, BHT.

missing_other.title: Compound Black®
missing_other.description: Due to high demand we are now selling a complete compound of our private label formula for a scent in the style of Aventus, a popular Creed men's fragrance launched in 2010. Because of the recent European ban on some raw materials we stock two versions of Compound Black® . The original version is the unaltered original fragrance and the (EC) No 1223/2009 version is as close as we can get while complying with EU requirements. Both compounds are IFRA compliant because the original Aventus was. If you prefer a smokier version of this fragrance add a trace of our Birch Tar Rectified (dilute it to 1% first). And to boost the fruit, try a little of our highly popular Pineapple Supreme. Did you know? : just 50g of Compound Black® and 200g of Deluxe Perfumer's Alcohol gives you everything you need to fill two 100ml (or four 50ml) bottles at extrait strength.

missing_other.title: Compound Blue®
missing_other.description: Due to high demand we are now selling a complete compound of a scent in the style of Bleu by Chanel as launched in 2010 and created by Jacques Polge. This remains, to this day, the definitive blue scent. Because of the recent European ban on some raw materials this can not be combined with alcohol and sold as a finished perfume in Europe but it can be purchased for personal use and evaluation and is IFRA compliant. If you would like to purchase a European safe version, we can supply that with a minimum order quantity of 1 kilogram. Allergens: Citral, Geraniol, Citronellol, Eugenol, Limonene, Linalool, Coumarin, Butylphenyl Methylpropional.

missing_other.title: Compound Brut™
missing_other.description: “There's something about Brut, that's nice to be close to.” So said the commercials way back in 1964 when perfumer Karl Mann created what could arguably be considered the most iconic men's scent in history. With a massive overdose of Musk Ambrette (an astonishing 13%) it is not surprising this fragrance was practically destroyed by legislative banning of raw materials and what is on the shelf in drug stores and department stores today is a mere shadow of what once was. Until now. Compound Brut is our internal version of a scent in the style of the unchanged original fragrance. There is no EU compliant or IFRA compliant version of this compound - it just isn't possible. Instead what you get is a compound that will allow you to study the profile and qualities of one of the most popular perfumes for gents without having to imagine what it was like. Freshly made with the finest materials (as with all Fraterworks products) you will be astonished by how good this product is. This is not a "perfume for grandpa" or an old man's scent. This is class to the extreme. With high quality Mysore sandalwood (a lot!), patchouli, green oakmoss and vetiver you realise just how much care went in to scents in the past - even those that are now deemed to be nasty cheapies. Originally diluted to 10% it was Brut. Diluted to 5% (with some distilled water in the alcohol blend) it was Brut 33. Make it both ways to further your perfumery education. WARNING: This is not compliant with any fragrance laws in any countries and should not be worn on the skin. It is sold in an undiluted form for educational purposes only. Luca Turin, the esteemed perfume writer, recently reviewed this product and said: “ It definitely is Brut[. …] Compound Brut™ made a happy man feel very old.” Go here to read Luca Turin's review of Compound Brut™. Top Notes: Bergamot, Orange, Lavender, Tarragon Heart Notes: Geranium, Jasmine, Ylang Ylang, Anise Base Notes: Sandalwood, Oakmoss, Vetiver, Musk, Patchouli, Vanilla, Ton

missing_other.title: Compound Celsius™
missing_other.description: Due to high demand we are now selling a complete compound of a scent in the style of the original Dior masterpiece from 1988: Fahrenheit. The fragrance was created by Jean-Louis Sieuzac, Michel Almairac, and Maurice Roger and was the first to exploit a high dose of Methyl Heptine Carbonate. Because of the recent European ban on some raw materials this can not be combined with alcohol and sold as a finished perfume in Europe but it can be purchased for personal use and evaluation and is IFRA compliant to 5%. If you would like to purchase a European safe version, we can supply that with a minimum order quantity of 1 kilogram and IFRA/EU Compliant to 20%. Allergens : Citral, Citronellol, Geraniol, Linalool, Benzyl Benzoate, Coumarin, Eugenol, Benzyl Alcohol, Benzyl Cinnamate, Cinnamyl Alcohol, Cinnamal, Limonene, Isoeugenol, Hydroxyisohexyl 3-Cyclohexene Carboxaldehyde, Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, Methyl 2-Octynoate, Butylphenyl Methylpropional.

missing_other.title: Compound Cool
missing_other.description: Compound Cool is our internal formula for a perfume in the style of Cool Water from Davidoff. Launched in 1988, this is the fragrance that defined the aquatic genre — a bold marine fougère built on dihydromyrcenol's cool transparency, layered with aromatic herbs and a warm musky base. This compound balances crisp mint and lavender against a powerful calone-driven sea breeze accord, with rosemary and neroli adding aromatic complexity in the heart. The drydown settles into a clean sandalwood and musk foundation with subtle tobacco warmth, giving the fragrance its distinctive masculine signature. This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. However, it is not EU compliant as it contains Lyral. We can produce special order versions that are EU compliant on request with a minimum order quantity of 1kg. Top Notes: Mint, Green Notes, Lavender Heart Notes: Sea Air, Rosemary, Neroli, Geranium Base Notes: Sandalwood, Musk, Tobacco, Cedarwood

missing_other.title: Compound Correspondence
missing_other.description: Compound Correspondence is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Correspondence by Henry Jacques. Launched in 2016 as part of the Les Classiques de HJ collection, this is a floral oriental fragrance built around two varieties of rose and precious oud, with powdery and fruity facets. This compound features an exceptional rose accord combining bright damask rose with the honeyed richness of rose de mai. The top notes of damask rose, iris and hyacinth provide a powdery, almost soapy elegance, while the heart adds soft apricot – reading more as the bitter kernel than the flesh – alongside earthy patchouli. The base delivers a refined natural oud deepened with ambergris and smoothed by vanilla. The result is a dark, mesmerising rose oud with outstanding longevity and moderate sillage – opulent without shouting. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Recommended concentration: 40% extrait. Top Notes: Damask Rose, Iris, Hyacinth Heart Notes: Rose de Mai, Apricot, Patchouli Base Notes: Ambergris, Oud, Vanilla

missing_other.title: Compound Drakkar
missing_other.description: That famous metallic freshness hits first — dihydromyrcenol at full 1982 strength, backed by lavender, bergamot, and a cooling herbal rush of rosemary, basil, and mint. Nothing in the modern version comes close to this opening. It reads as clean, sharp, and almost industrially powerful. The heart thickens with spicy carnation, coriander, and cinnamon, lifted by juniper. The spice sits on a dark animalic foundation the reformulated versions stripped away entirely. Our compound preserves all the great historic bases that gave the original its depth. Underneath everything lies the real Drakkar Noir — patchouli, oakmoss, leather, and vetiver at full strength. The 1989 reformulation gutted the patchouli; subsequent versions removed the animalic and mossy fixatives too. This compound is for a scent in the style of the original. This formula contains IFRA compliant oakmoss and Lyral so while it is IFRA compliant (to 1.75%) it is not EU compliant. We are able to craft an IFRA and EU compliant variant that is safe to a higher level. Contact us for details. An MOQ of 1kg applies on custom modifications.

missing_other.title: Compound Elixir
missing_other.description: Compound Elixir is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Le Male Elixir by Jean Paul Gaultier. Launched in 2023 and created by Givaudan's Quentin Bisch, this is an amber fougère fragrance that amplifies the DNA of the iconic 1995 original into something richer, sweeter and more intense. This compound features a bold lavender accord lifted by cool mint in the opening, transitioning quickly into a creamy, resinous heart of vanilla and benzoin. The base delivers warm honey, nutty tonka bean and a subtle tobacco note that adds depth without heaviness. The result is a sweet, gourmand-leaning masculine with outstanding projection and longevity of eight to ten hours – confident and unapologetically warm. As with most of Bisch's fragrances, the original contains a number of Givaudan captives. Our captive replacer bases are arguably equal to the products they substitute, and paired with our exceptionally high-quality raw materials library, the result is a compound we believe surpasses the original. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Lavender, Mint Heart Notes: Vanilla, Benzoin Base Notes: Honey, Tonka Bean, Tobacco

missing_other.title: Compound Feminité
missing_other.description: When Feminité du Bois was unveiled by Shiseido in 1992, it marked a watershed moment in perfumery that would reshape how we think about gendered fragrance. Created by the masterful duo of Christopher Sheldrake and Pierre Bourdon under the artistic direction of Serge Lutens, this scent dared to centre massive doses of cedarwood—traditionally masculine territory—in a composition explicitly celebrating femininity. The timing was audacious. The early '90s fragrance market was dominated by aquatic freshness (L'Eau d'Issey had just launched) and clean, ozonic scents. Into this landscape came Feminité du Bois with its unapologetic 60% woods concentration, wrapped in dried fruits and spices like something from a Moroccan souk. Sheldrake's genius was in softening the cedar's astringency with an innovative plum accord—not fresh plum, but rather dried, honeyed, almost wine-like—creating a push-pull between austere wood and sensual fruit that had never been attempted at this scale. This wasn't just a pretty wood scent; it was architectural, almost brutalist in its commitment to cedar, yet somehow intimate and skin-like. The composition became the template for Lutens' entire wood series (Cèdre, Santal Blanc, Chêne) and influenced everything from Hermès Terre d'Hermès to contemporary niche brands. It proved that women would embrace—even crave—compositions beyond the floral-oriental safety zone. This compound is our internal formula for a scent in the style of the original. Top Notes: Ginger, Cinnamon, Plum Heart Notes: Cedarwood, Turkish Rose, Peach, Ylang-Ylang, Cardamom, Clove Base Notes: Benzoin, Vanilla, Musk, Sandalwood, Patchouli

missing_other.title: Compound Five™
missing_other.description: Compound Five is a raw compound of our scent in the style of Chanel No 5 by Ernest Beaux! Because the original perfume contained Musk Ambrette which is prohibited from perfume use, we are offering this as an archival compound only. It must not be used or sold as a perfume and must not be applied to skin. We recommend pairing this with our Deluxe Perfumer's Alcohol which contains Solgard® (to minimise the destructive properties of the sun), a 15ml Luxury Glass Bottle and a set of 100 mouillettes so you can display this piece of history in your own home and allow friends and family to enjoy its scent safely through the use of smelling strips. Compound Five contains more than 25% pure jasmine absolute , rare Iris absolute, Ylang-ylang , finest Bourbon vanilla absolute , and many many more naturals and isolates which were cutting edge in 1921 when Mr Beaux crafted this masterpiece. The original perfume was sold as a 38% dilution. All you need to fill a 15ml bottle is 5 grams of Compound five blended with with 10 grams of alcohol.

missing_other.title: Compound Green™
missing_other.description: Polo Green was a masterpiece in refined perfuming from IFF perfumer Carlos Benaim in 1978. Benaim (born in Tangiers) is behind some of the most popular scents of the modern era, scents such as Flowerbomb, Armani's My Way, Calvin Klein Eternity for Men, Quorum, and Elizabeth Taylor White Diamonds. The prohibition on large quantities of tree moss and the restriction of chemically modified IFRA "safe" tree moss all but destroyed the scent and so Polo Green faded from popularity and in some cases can be virtually impossible to find on a department store shelf (even in its now thin reformulation). Compound Green fixes that. All perfumers should have a chance to smell and experience the original Polo — to understand what Benaim intended and why it was such a smash hit. Compound Green is our internal formula reconstructing the smell of the original. WARNING: This product contains non-IFRA compliant oakmoss and tree moss as well as other materials prohibited under IFRA 51 (including but not necessarily limited to Musk Ambrette). You should check with your local regulations prior to use. Compound Green is sold in an undiluted form for educational and industrial purposes only. Dilute to 10% or 15% in alcohol and rest for a month at least. After that time sample it by spraying it onto a perfume card. Allergens: Linalool, Benzyl Alcohol, Benzyl Benzoate, Benzyl Salicylate, Eugenol, Farnesol, Geraniol, Isoeugenol, Hydroxycitronellal, Citral, Citronellol, Limonene, Coumarin, Benzyl Cinnamate, Hexyl Cinnamal, Hydroxyisohexyl 3-Cyclohexene Carboxaldehyde, Amyl Cinnamal, Evernia Furfuracea Extract, Evernia Prunastri Extract.

missing_other.title: Compound Gris™
missing_other.description: Iris Gris (1946) from Jacques Fath is perhaps the most famous of all perfumes (amongst aficionados) and certainly the greatest Iris scent. It is now so rare to find a bottle that the cost currently runs over $10,000 US for one ounce of parfum! It was created by master perfumer Vincent Roubert who worked for Coty and produced Knize Ten in collaboration with him as well as number of other great scents like L'Aimant (1927) and A Suma (1934). Fraterworks now presents this intricate and luxurious scent in the style of the original for perfumers to understand and appreciate the odour of a masterpiece prior to dilution and mass distribution. This is loaded with Jasmin absolute and Rose de Mai from Grasse and, of course, an overdose of natural iris. Because the compound contains IFRA prohibited Musk Xylene, this compound must not be sold as a commercial fragrance and is for educational purposes only. Sampling should be done by smelling strip and this should not be applied to the skin. Notes: Iris, Peach, Musk, Violet, Cedar, Vetiver, Lilac, Heliotrope, Carnation, Rose de Mai, Sandalwood, Lily of the Valley, Tuberose, Jasmin de Grasse. Allergens: Citral, Farnesol, Geraniol, Linalool, Citronellol, Limonene, Eugenol, Benzyl Benzoate, Hydroxycitronellal, Benzyl Alcohol, Amyl Cinnamal, Benzyl Salicylate, Cinnamyl Alcohol, Isoeugenol, Coumarin, Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, Methyl 2-Octynoate, Cinnamal.

missing_other.title: Compound Homme™
missing_other.description: Homme 2005 was a masterpiece of perfumery precision and is, at least in our opinion, one of the finest men's fragrances ever crafted. The classic Dior scent had the distinction of being one of the few modern fragrances to use a hefty dose of genuine Orris Absolute which it combined masterfully with other treasured naturals of cocoa, myrrh, incense, and much more. Our compound is an internal formula in the style of the original, based on GCMS. We have not skimped and we have not made substitutions. Top Notes: Lavender, Bergamot, Sage, Incense Heart Notes: Iris, Cocoa, Cardamom, Amber Base Notes: Leather, Myrrh, Vetiver, Patchouli Allergens: Linalool, Citral, Geraniol, Citronellol, Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, Coumarin, Butylphenyl Methylpropional, Eugenol.

missing_other.title: Compound Imagination
missing_other.description: Compound Imagination is our internal formulation for a scent in the style of Imagination by Louis Vuitton. Launched in 2021, Imagination is a modern synthetic fragrance built around a massive dose of Ambroxan with black tea and citrus notes, creating a clean, radiant, and futuristic scent. This compound features an exceptionally high concentration of Ambroxan (approaching 20%), paired with synthetic citrus molecules and a unique black tea accord. The result is a polarising but distinctive fragrance that embraces its synthetic nature rather than mimicking natural materials. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Sicilian Lemon, Calabrian Bergamot, Orange Heart Notes: Black Tea Accord, Nigerian Ginger, Cinnamon Bark Base Notes: Ambroxan, Guaiac Wood, White Musks

missing_other.title: Compound Insensé
missing_other.description: This is probably the most demanded perfume compound from Fraterworks customers. Considered by many to be the greatest men's scent, it is a work of art. Alternating with the original Drakkar Noir, this is the fragrance I wear the most. I recommend 18% dilution for personal wear but IFRA compliance requires a lesser amount for sale. Compound Insense opens with shimmering aldehydes, deep green fir, and bright citrus — luminous, almost crystalline. An extraordinary lily of the valley blooms at the heart, cool and radiant, threaded with sharp green basil. Powdery iris and creamy magnolia support the florals as conifer notes rise from the base. This is a scent in the style of Givenchy's legendary 1993 masculine — awarded five stars by Luca Turin. The original was discontinued twice, leaving one of the finest men's fragrances ever created nearly impossible to find. Our compound preserves the original's character with the key materials that made it great. This compound is IFRA (but not EU) compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Aldehydes, Blackcurrant Bud, Lavender, Basil, Bergamot, Mandarin, Lemon Heart Notes: Lily of the Valley, Magnolia, Iris Base Notes: Fir Balsam, Vetiver, Cedar, Amber

missing_other.title: Compound Male
missing_other.description: Compound Le Male is our internal formula for a scent in the style of the original Le Male from Jean Paul Gaultier. Launched in 1995, this is a classic fougère with an unconventional twist—featuring prominent vanilla and sweet notes alongside traditional barbershop lavender and mint. This compound features a distinctive sweet-spicy profile with high levels of vanilla and coumarin, balanced with lavender, mint, artemisia, cardamom and cinnamon. The result is a powerful masculine fragrance that helped redefine men's perfumery by proving that sweetness and strength could coexist. This compound is IFRA compliant (at a huge 25%) and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Please note that as this is the original formula it contains Lilial and is therefore not EU compliant. We may produce an EU compliant edition if there is sufficient demand. Top Notes: Mint, Lavender, Bergamot, Artemisia Heart Notes: Cinnamon, Cumin, Orange Blossom, Cardamom Base Notes: Vanilla, Tonka Bean, Sandalwood, Cedar, Amber

missing_other.title: Compound Nile
missing_other.description: Compound Nile is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Un Jardin sur le Nil by Hermès. Launched in 2005 as part of the Jardins collection, this is a fresh green floral fragrance built around tart green mango and aquatic lotus with vegetal and woody facets. This compound features a distinctive green mango accord brightened with grapefruit and unusual vegetable notes of tomato leaf and carrot. The top notes of sparkling grapefruit and unripe mango provide a crisp, tangy opening, while the heart reveals delicate lotus and earthy bulrush evoking the riverbank. The base delivers soft musk, subtle incense and woody sycamore for a clean, airy finish. The result is a refreshing, transparent fragrance with moderate longevity and gentle sillage – natural and unforced. This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Grapefruit, Green Mango, Tomato Leaf, Carrot Heart Notes: Lotus, Bulrush, Peony, Hyacinth Base Notes: Musk, Incense, Sycamore Wood, Labdanum

missing_other.title: Compound Nomade
missing_other.description: Compound Nomade is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Ombre Nomade from Louis Vuitton. Launched in 2018, this is an intense oud-centric fragrance featuring a dark, smoky oud accord balanced with rose and raspberry. This compound features a high concentration of oud accord combined with incense, benzoin, and amberwood. The addition of raspberry gives a subtle fruity facet to the composition while Damascus rose adds depth. The result is a powerful, long-lasting Middle Eastern-inspired fragrance with exceptional projection. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Incense Heart Notes: Rose, Raspberry Base Notes: Oud, Benzoin, Amberwood

missing_other.title: Compound Oscar
missing_other.description: When Oscar de la Renta launched his first fragrance, simply called Oscar, in 1977, it was a significant moment in the perfume world for several reasons. At the time, the fragrance industry was buzzing with bold, statement-making scents, and Oscar stood out by blending elegance with a fresh, modern twist that reflected the designer's fashion ethos. Created by perfumer Jean-Louis Sieuzac, Oscar wasn’t just a pretty floral—it had depth, with aromatic herbs like basil and rosemary cutting through the sweetness, and a powdery, musky base that gave it staying power. This made it a bridge between the floral classics of earlier decades (think Guerlain’s L’Heure Bleue) and the bolder scents that would dominate the '80s. People noticed its versatility—it could be worn by a socialite at a gala or a professional woman in the office, which broadened its appeal. This is our internal compound of a scent in the style of the original. Top Notes: Basil, Coriander, Orange Blossom, Peach Heart Notes: Tuberose, Ylang-Ylang, Jasmine, Rose, Orchid, Lavender Base Notes: Sandalwood, Patchouli, Musk, Amber, Vetiver, Cloves, Opoponax

missing_other.title: Compound Oud Wood
missing_other.description: Compound Oud Wood is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Oud Wood by Tom Ford. Launched in 2007 as part of the original Private Blend collection, this is a refined woody amber fragrance built around smoky oud and creamy sandalwood with warm spices and resinous depth. This compound features a smooth, accessible oud accord softened by rich sandalwood and earthy vetiver. The top notes of Brazilian rosewood, cardamom and Sichuan pepper provide an exotic yet approachable spiced opening, while the heart reveals precious oud notes balanced by creamy woods. The base delivers tonka bean, vanilla and amber for lasting warmth. The result is an elegant, quietly confident fragrance with moderate longevity and intimate sillage – sophisticated rather than challenging. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Notes: Brazilian Rosewood, Cardamom, Sichuan Pepper, Oud, Sandalwood, Vetiver, Tonka Bean, Vanilla, Amber

missing_other.title: Compound Outlands
missing_other.description: Compound Outlands is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Outlands by Amouage. Launched in 2024 as part of the prestigious Essences collection, this is a sophisticated oriental woody fragrance built around frankincense and patchouli with a striking contrast between bright citrus opening and deep resinous base. This compound features a complex incense-forward heart enhanced with earthy patchouli and warm spices including saffron and cumin. The top notes of lemon, bergamot, and cardamom provide an unexpectedly bright and invigorating opening, while elemi and Sichuan pepper add aromatic lift. The base delivers a rich amber accord layered with vanilla, benzoin, and labdanum, grounded by subtle oud and birch. The result is a dry, resinous fragrance with excellent projection and exceptional longevity – sophisticated and uncompromising. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Lemon, Bergamot, Cardamom, Elemi, Frankincense, Sichuan Pepper Heart Notes: Patchouli, Saffron, Orange Blossom, Anise, Geranium, Rose, Coriander, Cumin Base Notes: Vanilla, Benzoin, Amber, Labdanum, Oud, Opoponax, Frankincense, Birch, Musk

missing_other.title: Compound Pink
missing_other.description: Launched in 2018 and originally crafted by Givaudan's Quentin Bisch, this is an oriental fragrance built around fruit, flowers and luxurious woods. This is enormously popular in the lab, amongst both male and female staff. It is one of our most universally requested compounds in fact. The original formula contains a number of Givaudan captives which we have carefully replaced to great effect in this, our compound in the style of the original. This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Lychee, Pear, Bergamot, Pink Pepper, Grapefruit Heart Notes: Turkish Rose, Oud, Incense Base Notes: Vanilla, Amber, Woody Notes, Musk, Vetiver, Evernyl

missing_other.title: Compound Portrait
missing_other.description: Compound Portrait is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Portrait of a Lady from Frederic Malle. Launched in 2010, this is an opulent rose-patchouli fragrance with a distinctive dark, wine-like rose accord supported by frankincense and spices. This compound features an extremely high concentration of Turkish rose absolute combined with patchouli, frankincense, and sandalwood. The addition of cinnamon, clove and blackcurrant creates a rich, baroque composition with exceptional depth and longevity. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Cinnamon, Clove, Blackcurrant Heart Notes: Turkish Rose, Frankincense, Raspberry Base Notes: Patchouli, Sandalwood, White Musk

missing_other.title: Compound Privé
missing_other.description: Compound Privé is our internal formula for a perfume in the style of Patou Pour Homme Privé by Jean Patou. It was perhaps the greatest men's fragrance ever made and most certainly the finest lavender fougère in existence. Launched in 1994 and crafted by Jean Kerléo (who served as chief perfumer of Jean Patou from 1967 to 1998), it represents the perfecting of his celebrated Patou Pour Homme from 1980. Where the original was a bold oriental fougère built for the boardroom – dense with civet, castoreum and animalic leather – Privé took a different path. Kerléo softened the structure into something more intimate and bohemian whilst retaining the uncompromising quality of materials that defined the house. The result was a fragrance of extraordinary refinement: still unmistakably masculine, but approachable in a way the 1980 original never attempted to be. It rates a remarkable 4.6 on Fragrantica and commands four-figure prices on the secondary market for original bottles, on the rare occasion they come up for sale. This compound features an exquisite lavender opening tempered by bitter galbanum and bright citrus of bergamot and mandarin. The heart transitions through subtle florals lifted by black pepper, before arriving at what many consider the finest base accord in masculine perfumery: bone-dry hay intertwined with green patchouli, authentic oakmoss, powdery orris root and creamy vanilla, all grounded by vetiver and Virginia cedar. The hay note in particular – crinkly, tobacco-like, utterly distinctive – is what separates Privé from everything else. The longevity is exceptional; the sillage, quietly commanding. Jean Kerléo later founded the Osmothèque, the world's fragrance archive in Versailles, and his work on Privé represents the pinnacle of classical French perfumery before IFRA restrictions made such compositions impossible to replicate legally. The house of Jean Patou was eventually absorbed by LVMH in 2018, and fragrances like Privé now exist only in the memor

missing_other.title: Compound Red™
missing_other.description: Due to high demand, we are now selling "private label" compounds of some popular demonstration formulas. Compound Red™ is our internal version for a scent in the style of a very popular unisex perfume which was launched in 2015. The fragrance we are replicating here is built around a core of three accords, a mineral accord, a "fire and heat" accord, and a savoire-faire accord. Naturals such as Fir Balsam, Marigold, Jasmine and Saffron are found within those accords and add a surprising complexity. This compound is ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Did you know? : just 50g of Compound Red™ and 200g of Deluxe Perfumer's Alcohol gives you everything you need to fill two 100ml (or four 50ml) bottles at extrait strength.

missing_other.title: Compound Sauvage
missing_other.description: Compound Sauvage is our internal formula for a scent in the style of the best selling Sauvage crafted by François Demachy . This is neck and neck tied for best-selling men's fragrance with Aventus by Creed. Our private label compound contains all the luxurious naturals and premium aroma chemicals of the real thing. This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol . Top Notes: Calabrian bergamot and Pepper Heart Notes: Sichuan Pepper, Lavender, Pink Pepper, Vetiver, Patchouli, Geranium and elemi Base Notes: Ambroxan, Cedar and Labdanum

missing_other.title: Compound Seven™
missing_other.description: In 2002 the world of perfumery was changed forever when Yves Saint Laurent launched the first western styled Oud fragrance M7 (by Jacques Cavallier and Alberto Morillas under the creative direction of Tom Ford). As shocking as the scent was, the company went further by using a full frontal male nude in its marketing. The perfume was a masterpiece of perfumery but as so often is the case with fragrances released before their time (think Chanel Bois Noir), it was soon removed from general sale. An attempt in recent years has been made to re-release the scent in a new formulation but that new formula is as bad as the original was great. Fortunately we are able to offer our internal compound in the style of the original. It is Compound Seven and, despite containing all the original materials we can determine by GCMS (including the luxurious woods), it is IFRA compliant to a whopping 48% today. The original contained the merest trace of Lyral which we have sympathetically replaced for full EU compliance also. This compound is ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Did you know? : just 50g of Compound Seven™ and 200g of Deluxe Perfumer's Alcohol gives you everything you need to fill two 100ml (or four 50ml) bottles at extrait strength.

missing_other.title: Compound Tobacco Vanille
missing_other.description: Compound Tobacco Vanille is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Tobacco Vanille by Tom Ford. Launched in 2007 as part of the original Private Blend collection, this is a rich oriental spicy fragrance built around opulent tobacco leaf and creamy vanilla with warm gourmand facets. This compound features a sumptuous tobacco accord enhanced with tonka bean and cacao for depth and indulgence. The top notes of tobacco leaf and warm spices including ginger provide a bold, aromatic opening, while the heart reveals tobacco blossom alongside rich vanilla. The base delivers dried fruit nuances and woody undertones that extend the fragrance's considerable longevity. The result is a warm, enveloping scent with exceptional projection and outstanding lasting power – confident and unapologetically luxurious. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Tobacco Leaf, Ginger, Spicy Notes Heart Notes: Vanilla, Cacao, Tonka Bean, Tobacco Blossom Base Notes: Dried Fruits, Woody Notes

missing_other.title: Compound Tweed™
missing_other.description: Due to high demand we are now selling a complete compound of the our private label formula for a perfume in the style of Green Irish Tweed , a popular Creed men's fragrance launched in 1985. Because of the recent European ban on some raw materials this can not be combined with alcohol and sold as a finished perfume in Europe but it can be purchased for personal use and evaluation. If you would like to purchase a European safe version, we can supply that with a minimum order quantity of 1 kilogram. This is an incredible fragrance you will want to wear a lot so be sure to buy more than you think you need. It is particularly expensive because it has a high amount of natural Mysore Sandalwood.

missing_other.title: Compound XJ 1861™
missing_other.description: Due to high demand we are now selling "private label" compounds of some popular fragrances. Compound XJ 1861 is our internal formula for a scent in the style of XJ 1861 Naxos from Xerjoff. This is a celebration of Sicily and one of the top sellers for the brand. The notes are: Top: Lavender, Bergamot and Lemon Heart: Honey, Cinnamon, Cashmeran and Jasmine Sambac Base: Tobacco Leaf, Vanilla and Tonka Bean This is a very gourmand scent with the sweet vanilla/honey taking pride of place in the opening. This compound is ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol.

missing_other.title: Contract Compounding
missing_other.description: We provide expert toll blending and contract manufacturing for your proprietary oil formulations. Simply share your formula* (protected under our confidentiality agreement), and we'll prepare a tailored pricing proposal using materials from our own range. Major Change: a material added, removed, or substituted (per material). A substantial reworking of the formula is treated as a new formula and requires fresh pricing, reflecting

missing_other.title: Copaiba Oil Coeur
missing_other.description: Copaiba Balsam Coeur is one of those wonderful naturals which blends with virtually everything and is a great fixative. This Copaiba is especially luxurious as it the pure fractionated heart of the balsam made by one of the finest suppliers of natural oil in the world: LMR. The key components of the product are alpha-copaene, beta-caryopyllene, and alpha-humulene. Copaiba Coeur has great value as a blender for more powerful materials used in making oud reconstructions. It is found in such fragrances as Tom Ford's Black Orchid, Tabu by Jean Carles and classic M7 of YSL. Origin: Brazil Method: Hydro distillation followed by fractionation Part: Plant exudate

missing_other.title: Coriander Seed Oil
missing_other.description: A high quality coriander seed oil is essential for perfumers. It adds freshness, links richer spice notes to the top of a scent and adds discreet warmth when dosed correctly. Our Coriander seed oil is from Biolandes, a company that really excels in a number of areas such as Ylang-ylang and spices. You will definitely not be disappointed by this excellent quality and great priced product. Origin: France, Russia, Moldova Part: Roots Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Cornmint Oil
missing_other.description: Cornmint Oil hits you with bold, clean mentholic freshness — brighter and more assertive than true peppermint. A harsh-woody undertone gives it raw, unpolished character. The dryout turns bitter-herbaceous, with a cooling sensation that lingers on skin. This is the workhorse of the mint world — produced in vast quantities and far cheaper than true peppermint oil. It drives fresh colognes, fougères, and aftershave accords where raw minty power matters more than peppermint's balsamic refinement. The harsh-woody character adds masculine edge to cooling compositions. Blend with lavender and rosemary for classic fougère freshness, or pair with eucalyptus and camphor for bracing aromatic intensity.

missing_other.title: Coroliane
missing_other.description: Coroliane was an elegant De Laire lily of the valley base that, in combination with Mayciane and Mousse de Saxe provided the key character to No 19 by Chanel and many other fragrances of the 20th century. It was originally created by Edmond Roudnitska. Coroliane is here restored to its original glory and IFRA compliant up to 6.3% of the finished product. It is a wonder of perfume art and is a very modern muguet that will suit any fragrance of today.

missing_other.title: Cosmonex 1485B
missing_other.description: Cosmonex 1485B rebuilds the scent of the Givaudan musk Cosmone (CAS 259854-70-1). With supplies collapsing, prices increasing dramatically and rumours of a complete discontinuation, a replacer base was needed. Cosmonex opens warm and powdery, a rounded musk threaded with sweet ambergris and the softest clean-skin animalic hum. The impression is elegant, cosmetic, and quietly glowing. It is, in fact, an elegant musk blend in its own right. Rebuilt one-for-one from rare musks and accessory notes, a trace lends outstanding cosmetic volume and a soft, second-skin warmth to florals, woods and amber accords. Use it to round rough edges, add lift, and make a composition feel finished and expensive. Cosmone always shone in chypres and fougères, and Cosmonex slots straight into those accords with no reformulating. Slip it beneath white florals for a warm, powdery skin effect, or thread it through citrus and green tops to add body and glow. Even a single drop reads as pure luxury. Analyses of finished perfumes show how widely the Cosmone character travelled: the musk this base reproduces appears in Chanel Pour Monsieur at around 0.09% and in Serge Lutens Tubéreuse Criminelle at roughly 0.36%. Cosmonex 1485B lets you build that same effect into your own work.

missing_other.title: Costus Oil
missing_other.description: Costus oil opens with a startling animalic warmth — the smell of fur, wet hair, and human scalp. Beneath that surprising start, you find a soft woody-rooty core threaded with violet and orris facets. The fatty quality lingers and slowly turns powdery. This is your secret weapon for vintage chypres, orientals, and any composition that needs a pulse of human warmth. A trace dose lifts a floral heart into something animal and alive. Pair it with rose absolute and orris butter for a richly warm natural accord. Jean Carles famously used a whopping 0.6% pure in Miss Dior. Our oil comes from costus farmed in its native Himalayan habitat — same soil, same altitude, same climatic stress that shapes the wild plant. The result preserves every facet of the wild character. Use it in trace amounts; even a tiny addition reshapes the composition entirely. Costus features in several of our demo formulas (see below), such as YSL Homme, Dana Tabu, Femme by Rochas, and Patou Pour Homme. Costus Root Tincture , a related preparation made from the same root, also threads through our Mitsouko, and L'Origan reconstitutions. NOTE: Costus oil has an IFRA prohibited specification so this should not be used in fragrances that are required to comply with IFRA standards. Costus Oil is on CITES Appendix I. That means, for now, we can't sell it from New Zealand. We are working on a solution.

missing_other.title: Costus Oliffac
missing_other.description: Costus root oil is now prohibited by IFRA and its trade is highly restricted due to CITES. Fortunately IFF produce this wonderful base which, as far as natural replacers go, is an extremely good facsimile of the wild variety. Costus oil is a rather unusual oil, having a distinctly animal odour (in the direction of wet dog or goat). It is particularly good blended with orris materials and it probably had its greatest outing as a key player in the original Miss Dior (1947) by Jean Carles for Dior. Use this base one for one as a replacer whenever Costus Oil is called for in an old formula.

missing_other.title: Costus Root Tincture 20%
missing_other.description: Costus root is one of those strange odours from history. Upon first smelling it, people often recall the scent of wild goats and wet dog hair but as every perfumer knows, it is often the "ugly" smells that add the final touch of beauty to a scent. Costus root was used in very high doses in fragrances such as My Sin by the mysterious Madame Zed for Jeanne Lanvin and at 0.6% in the form of pure essential oil in the original Miss Dior by Jean Carles. Unfortunately regulations have now excluded costus and all its extracts from fragrances, but we offer it for those who wish to faithfully recreate historic masterpieces and for the lucky few who live in nations in which this precious material is not restricted. This Fraterworks tincture is made according to the oldest traditions of French infusion manufacture with purest glacial food grade alcohol. It makes for a wonderful addition to fragrances already taking advantage of costus root oil. Origin: India Variety: Sausurea Costus Part: Dried roots Method: Cold ethanol tincture

missing_other.title: Cresylex™
missing_other.description: A powerful base to be used in place of a 10% dilution of para cresol. The IFRA 51 guidelines allow for a maximum use of 0.005% para cresol in your finished fragrance. Para cresol is incredibly strong but with the right balance of other materials, it can be an invaluable note at quite high doses. For that reason, Fraterworks is making this para cresol alternative available. This is a slightly more floral alternative to Para Cresol and can be used at up to 100 percent of your finished product.

missing_other.title: Cuir de Russie
missing_other.description: Cuir de Russie (Russian leather) is a classic base originating in the late 1800s. First appearing as a fragrance by Amie Guerlain in 1875, Cuir de Russie is a rich and intensely smoky animalic leather with rose and jasmine nuances. It has been used in countless fragrances and upon smelling its influence is clear in Knize Ten by Coty, Cuir de Russie by Ernest Beaux for Chanel, and numerous others. Cuir de Russie is in the DNA of many Chanel fragrances and may even offer a key to the authorship of Mademoiselle Chanel No 1 , the illicit fragrance Coco Chanel had made during the second world war. This enriched leather scent is not far removed from the original Russian Bouquet de Catherine , the fragrance chosen by Chanel to become No 5 . Cuir de Russie can be used in place of birch tar for a sweeter and more refined smoke note. Fraterworks® Cuir de Russie is a classical leather base. If you are looking for a more modern leather, see our Royal Leather 674276 .

missing_other.title: Cumin Seed Oil
missing_other.description: Cumin is an extremely powerful spice that can contribute unusual and interesting human skin like notes to the dry down of a fragrance. Cumin blends extremely well with rich florals, particularly Jasmine and Rose , and other spices and spiced bases like Jasmin Épicé . Origin: Egypt Part: Seeds Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Cyclamen des Alpes
missing_other.description: Cyclamen des Alpes was one of two great De Laire bases created around the scent of two varieties of cyclamen flowers. “The wild Cyclamen which grows in Switzerland is called Alpine Violet, and possesses a very delicate and sweet odour. That botanically known as Persian Cyclamen has a somewhat harsher odour.” Cyclamen des Alpes reproduces the odour of the former. The scent of cyclamen flowers is something of a blend of white lilac, lily and violet flowers (hence its sobriquet) with a suspicion of hyacinth. This base is enriched with many luxurious floral absolutes and thanks to its delicate nature makes a perfect overdose material for the heart of a novel modern fragrance.

missing_other.title: Cypress Oil
missing_other.description: Cypress oil offers a fresh, woody, and resinous scent, often described as dry, green, and slightly spicy. It evokes clean, invigorating forest air with distinct pine and cedar nuances, providing a sophisticated, natural character. Primarily a top/middle note, cypress adds structure, lift, and natural freshness to blends. It excels in masculine, fougère, woody, and citrus compositions, harmonising well with diverse ingredients like woods, herbs, and spices.
