missing_other.title: Cypriol Heart “Superior” Rect.
missing_other.description: This natural Cypriol Heart from Floral Concept (the finest quality as of 2026) opens with a polished woody-earthy character, cleaner and more refined than standard nagarmotha oil. You get the same smoky-leathery depth but stripped of harsh edges, revealing subtle saffron-like warmth beneath. The dry spiciness sits beautifully between patchouli and vetiver territory. This rectified heart fraction excels in building convincing oud accords without the price tag of genuine agarwood. Pair it with sandalwood to soften its intensity and reveal sweeter undertones. It transforms leather compositions with authentic smokiness and adds mysterious depth to chypres and oriental bases. Try Cypriol Heart as a modifier in florals where a touch of darkness elevates the composition. Combine with benzoin, labdanum, and frankincense for incense-style warmth. Start at low dosages—its tenacity and richness can dominate if overdosed.

missing_other.title: Cypriol “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: The smoky nuance of a winterly campfire smoulders beneath the surface of this marvelous oil from LMR. Cypriol (or Nagarmotha) is frequently used (often in large doses) to recreate the scent of Oud in a fragrance because Cypriol is something of a chameleon oil. A good example of this is Ajmal Dahn Oudh Al Shams in which Cypriol is blended with Guaiac Wood Oil and Gurjun Balsam Oil . At first Cypriol is spicy with aspects of Cinnamon and Cascarilla, and the next minute it is earthy green and vetiver like. But then, from out the blue, it reveals the mystical scent of frankincense before retreating back to its woody default. LMR, one of the finest makers and suppliers of natural oils in the world, has created a genuine masterpiece in their handling of this treasured oil. There are more facets in this Cypriol than any we sampled from other suppliers and so it is our Signature oil.

missing_other.title: Dahna
missing_other.description: Compound Dahna is our internal formula in the style of Les Sables Roses by Louis Vuitton. Launched in 2019 and created by Jacques Cavallier Belletrud, the original is an oriental floral built on a deliberately simple contrast: two qualities of rose set against oud wood, with nothing crowding them out. This compound features a bright, faintly watery rose accord — more red and spicy than powdery — carried over a clean oud that stays smooth rather than barnyard. Saffron and black pepper sharpen the opening and give the composition its characteristic edge, while ambergris lifts and warms the drydown without adding sweetness. The result is a refined Arabian-style rose oud with above-average projection and excellent longevity – opulent but uncluttered. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Saffron, Black Pepper Heart Notes: Rose, Bulgarian Rose Base Notes: Oud, Ambergris

missing_other.title: Daphne Supreme
missing_other.description: As the gloomy days of winter near their end, the burgeoning flowers of Daphne Odora begin to appear. Daphne has one of the most beautiful scents in the entire world of flowers and yet it is relatively unknown in its true form in Western perfumery. Historically many Daphne bases existed, but they were of a fantasy type and not reflective of the true Daphne shrub. Adding to its scarcity in fine fragrances is the fact that Daphne plants are highly toxic to man and brute and so extracts do not exist. Fraterworks Daphne Supreme is not a fantasy base but rather a wonderful representation of the flowers in full bloom. As is often the case with winter flowering plants, Daphne is extremely powerful and its odour is one of penetrating citrus, green leaves and white flowers. This is perhaps the most beautiful of all our modern floral bases and one that we are certain will form part of a world class fragrance in the near future. Daphne Supreme blends extraordinarily well with Jasmolactone® Delta , Jasmin Fleurs , Verdantol ™, Suralette Extra and Gardenia J. Ellis .

missing_other.title: Dark Ginger CO2, P. Jungle Essence
tags: locale:NOTE - this is not cote divoire or CO2 Top Note.
missing_other.description: Upon first smelling this dark Ginger Oil CO2 (Pure Jungle Essence), my heart skipped a beat. In a moment not only did I experience an incredibly true to life and beautiful scent of ginger, but a million nuances hit me invoking a flood of memories. Wood notes reminding me of childhood years spent wandering through the building sites of homes crafted from fine timbers in a relative's luxury construction business, the scents of dank earth from rugby fields at school and walks in the forested hills surrounding my childhood home, and rich gingerbread fresh from the oven on winterly days. Unlike the lighter "Top Note" variant (M51690), this standard version (M51689) delivers full-spectrum richness with deeper base notes. Use it to energise woody bases with vetiver and sandalwood, cut through heavy white florals, or build authentic gingerbread accords with vanilla and tonka. Its unmatched realism makes it indispensable for contemporary compositions demanding genuine naturalness. Like all MANE products you are not just buying beautiful scents, you are buying art. In this CO2 extracted oil, MANE has managed to encapsulate a lifetime of wonderful odours and memories. For an inimitable fragrance of exquisite elegance we recommend a pairing of Ginger Oil Pure Jungle Essence with Payan Bertrand's dazzlingly citrus-fresh Ginger Oil Fresh, Côte d'Ivoire, the rare top note CO2 extraction, also from MANE, or LMR's marvellous Madagascan Fresh Ginger essential oil . For something a little different you may also like our Red Ginger oil .

missing_other.title: Davana Oil
missing_other.description: Smelling Davana oil for the first time you would be forgiven for thinking you are smelling a fine aged bourbon or rum. Beloved for its fruity and liquor top notes, this luscious oil comes from many of the same areas as Indian Sandalwood Oil and it is prized, especially amongst natural perfumers, for contributing a fruit note that is otherwise difficult to obtain. It is a member of the Artemisia family and not surprisingly it modifies and blends well with its relatives (particularly Armoise ). Note: Fraterworks is not a registered COSMOS company so while this product is CSM certified when it reaches us, we cannot use that terminology when we resell. Part: Foliage and stems Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Deluxe Attar Bottle
missing_other.description: These deluxe attar bottles are thick cut polished glass with zamac cap and base. They have a serious heft and ideally suit luxury contents such as attars, ouds, mukhallats and costly oils such as Sandalwood Mysore Oil. The bottles have a glass dipper (affixed to the lid) to make application of the contents easier. These are beautiful bottles which truly elevate their contents. Photographs don't do justice to how deluxe these bottles are.

missing_other.title: Deluxe Sample Spray Bottles, 2ml
missing_other.description: These deluxe sample vials are the industry standard for high end and artisanal perfumery. Each vial can hold 2ml (around 1.7 grams) of perfume. No tools are needed — simply fill and push the closure mechanism into the bottle until it snaps in place. These are highly resistant to leaking and the spray pump offers consistent and uniform dispersion. Bottles (including pump) are 60 mm high and 10 mm wide. These luxury sample bottles are made in France.

missing_other.title: Dewfruit
missing_other.description: Dewfruit opens with an exotic burst of lychee and raspberry, both fresh and sophisticated. The cassis heart emerges powerfully—this is the base's signature, built around Givaudan's molecule Neocaspirene. Subtle herbal-green undertones keep the fruit from becoming candied, lending an elegant naturalism. This iconic base originated at Quest International before Givaudan's acquisition and has become essential in modern perfumery. The sparkling fruity top note in Thierry Mugler's Angel came from Dewfruit, demonstrating its power to define legendary compositions. Use this base specifically to access the Neocaspirene molecule, which delivers cassis character that was difficult to achieve before its development. Use Dewfruit between 0.1% and 5% in your compositions. It transforms rose, violet, and cassie accords with fruity radiance. The base works beautifully in chypres needing modern fruit, gourmand compositions, and abstract contemporary designs. Expect bright, happy complexity without excessive sweetness.

missing_other.title: Dianthine Extra
missing_other.description: Dianthine Extra is a classic early 20th carnation base built around luxurious and rich essential oils and absolutes. Overloaded with iris roots, Bulgarian rose oil from LMR and finest ylang-ylang Comoros, this is our first choice carnation. Fully present in the top notes of a fragrance but also very long lasting despite no reliance at all on highly restricted chemicals such as Isoeugenol. Overdose it in our L'Origan replica formula instead of Dianthus for a richer and perhaps even better balanced fragrance than the original!

missing_other.title: Dianthus
missing_other.description: From traces for warmth to overdose (3.7% of the finished product according to IFRA 50), Dianthus can be used in virtually every fragrance type. Fraterworks Dianthus is a famed carnation base from the early 20th century. Anywhere eugenol finds a place, Fraterworks® Dianthus can be used. The spicy clove heat of the opening is balanced with a balsamic vanilla and heliotrope accord that is perceptible through the whole product. Dianthus is a masterpiece in classical perfume arts which adds richness to even the most modern scents. For a synergistic longer lasting and equally great historic carnation base, we also stock Oeillet .

missing_other.title: Dorinia SA E
missing_other.description: Dorinia revolutionised rose bases when Firmenich launched it alongside Damascone Beta in 1975. The prominent apple note from damascones defines this material's character. Deploy this powerhouse at 0.1-2% maximum—its diffusive strength overwhelms inexperienced noses. This polycyclic musk-free reformulation offers superior skin affinity compared to its predecessor Dorinia SA, making it ideal for premium fine fragrance applications. The material functions as complete rose accord, eliminating need to build complex rose hearts from individual components. Combine Dorinia SA E with natural rose absolutes where it lifts and brightens extraction-dulled facets. Blends seamlessly with white florals (jasmine, peony, violet) for sophisticated bouquets, or pair with fruity notes (lychee, raspberry, cassis) for modern fruity-florals. Works beautifully in woody-oriental structures as elegant floral counterpoint to sandalwood, amber, and gourmand notes. Add dimethyl sulfide at 0.001% for authentic rose absolute depth. Incorporate phenyl ethyl phenyl acetate for rosy-honey sweetness that bridges the damascone intensity.

missing_other.title: Douglas Fir Needle Oil
missing_other.description: If you wanted to distill the scent of Christmas, this precious New Zealand Douglas fir oil ( Pseudotsuga menziesii) is just that. Despite being unrelated, It melds together aspects of the very best of the two more well-known perfumery products of Siberian fir needle oil (Abies siberica) and f ir balsam absolute ( Abies balsamea) but adds a wonderful (and unexpected) sparkling citrus note. Every drop exudes the fresh wild scent of nature. This is a superior oil in every way. This fir oil is grown and harvested in the pure unspoilt regions of the South Island of New Zealand and uses only young branch tips and needles. It is steam distilled. According to Steffan Arctander, Douglas fir needle oil exhibits “a softness and a sweetness, a very rich bodynote and a great odour tenacity which exceptional for a ‘pine needle oil’.” Blends well with: other conifer oils, oakmoss, citrus oils (particularly grapefruit), labdanum. Origin: Otago, South Island, New Zealand Part: Young needles and branches Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Driftwood
missing_other.description: Driftwood is a speciality amber base by V. MANE Fils built around their captive molecule Ambramone®. It has a lovely soft cedar quality with the faintest hint of suede and ambergris. It can be used in overdose (and indeed I would recommend its use that way) when you want an elegant wood note to use in place of the more common Vertofix , Vertenex or Iso E Super . But in small amounts it is a great nuancer with captive character. There is nothing unpleasant in Driftwood and as a foundational wood it is a great addition to the perfumer's organ. Blend this with green or fruit notes to emphasise those facets in the base. For richness and beauty, boost it with Miraclewood .

missing_other.title: Dynamone
missing_other.description: Dynamone is a natural Biolandes speciality in which labdanum (cistus) resin is transformed by a proprietary process into a refined and unique extract. In the words of the manufacturer: “In fine perfumery, this mythical extract from the cistus offers mineral and metallic notes allowing the contribution of dark and deep notes. Perfect for the creation of leather bases, in association with amber notes, ideal to bring a very original oriental touch.” This is a really excellent material to add a kinder and gentler animalic tinge to a perfume when straight up labdanum can be a tad dominating. Origin: Spain Part: Resin from leaves and stems Method: Proprietary extraction

missing_other.title: Eau de Brouts Absolute
missing_other.description: "Brouts" is old Provençal for the young shoots and leafy twigs pruned from bitter orange trees. When those cuttings are steam-distilled to make petitgrain oil, the leftover water holds a faint, beautiful fragrance of its own. Extract that water with solvent and you get this — eau de brouts absolute — deep green, smoky, watery, and unlike anything else in the palette. It smells of freshly torn bitter orange leaves, but airy and subtle in a way that petitgrain oil itself is not. Not to be confused with Orange Flower Water Absolute , which comes from neroli distillation and is floral, indolic, and honeyed. Eau de brouts is purely green and herbaceous. Arctander described it as "musty, dry, faintly floral, more herbaceous" — though his definition blurred the line by including mixed flower and leaf waters, which modern producers keep separate. Use it to build convincing neroli and bitter orange accords — it fills the gap between bright neroli on top and petitgrain in the heart. It brings naturalness to jasmine, ylang-ylang, and gardenia compositions too. Pair it with bergamot, sandalwood, and olibanum for a green-woody cologne effect. Use sparingly — it is potent and easily dominates.

missing_other.title: Elderflower TruAbs
missing_other.description: This 100% natural Elderflower base has to be smelled to be believed. While the natural absolute is available, it is somewhat disappointing (even from great vendors like Firmenich). Fraterworks' Elderflower TruAbs® on the other hand is simply sublime. In the words of our founder Jamie Frater: "Elderflower TruAbs carries me back to my carefree youth in New Zealand and the scent of warm Southern Hemisphere Christmas mornings with all the pleasure and optimism that implied. No singular base moves me quite so emotionally as this one. Elderflower TruAbs is pure bliss." Elderflower TruAbs® has nuances of honey, new mown hay, fresh country air and orchard fruits. It is so beautifully constructed that you cannot tell it is a crafted blend. Use this product one for one in place of Elderflower Absolute. From traces this product has impact and will add richesse and elegance to your fragrances. Like our amazing Hyacinth , Rose de Mai and Boronia TruAbs' this base is created especially for Fraterworks in Grasse and is so good it is practically impossible to differentiate it from a single plant extract. Due to the high cost of this replica, we also sell it at 10% dilution in odourless natural triethyl citrate — just make your selection above. We can supply an unlimited quantity of Elderflower TruAbs®, just contact us for pricing.

missing_other.title: Elemi Oil
missing_other.description: Elemi is a perfumer's secret weapon, possessing a dynamic dual character. It provides an initial peppery-citrus lift while anchoring compositions with resinous depth. This versatility makes it an unparalleled bridge ingredient, connecting disparate olfactory families. Pair Elemi Extra strategically with bergamot and pink pepper for contemporary masculine openings, or blend with frankincense and cedarwood for sophisticated woody accords. The elemol content provides exceptional tenacity—lasting over 400 hours on blotters—making this material invaluable for anchoring volatile compositions. Deploy lower concentrations as a radiance enhancer, higher percentages to feature its unique lemony-peppery signature.

missing_other.title: Elemi SFE
missing_other.description: Supercritical CO2 extraction captures what steam distillation cannot — the full aromatic spectrum of fresh elemi resin, including volatile compounds that heat would destroy. The result is cleaner, greener, and more vertical than the conventional oil. You smell the resin as it actually is: bright, peppery, lemony, with a green facet the distilled version lacks. Where the steam-distilled oil can feel broad and slightly blurred, this SFE reads as focused and precise. The peppery-citrus top is sharper, the balsamic background is smoother, and the whole profile hangs together more naturally. In fine fragrance, that clarity translates to better integration — the elemi character supports without muddying surrounding notes. Use it wherever you would use elemi oil but want a more refined result. In spicy compositions, the green facet adds a botanical freshness. In citrus-woody accords, the peppery brightness provides lift without the instability problems of the conventional oil. Pair with pink pepper, cardamom, and olibanum for a resinous spice accord with genuine aromatic depth.

missing_other.title: Epice FW
missing_other.description: In 1926 Hubert and George Fraysse founded Synarome and produced the greatest bases of their time: Animalis and Ambrarome . The following year their brother, André, became in-house perfumer for Lanvin and created the masterpiece Arpège in collaboration with Paul Vacher. Fraysse and Vacher crafted Arpège around one of Synarome's lesser-known (but in many ways equally influential) bases called Epicea, which remained in production right up to the twenty-first century. Fraterworks Epice FW revives that forgotten masterpiece, rich in nutmeg, pepper and allspice. While Epice FW has a somewhat ancient pedigree it is beautifully suited to modern fragrances and would make a wonderful starting point for a sophisticated and rich spicy gourmand fragrance.

missing_other.title: Espicene Gamma
missing_other.description: Gone (until now) but not forgotten, Epicene Gamma from IFF was a classic masterpiece — a veritable panoply of herbs, woods and spices blended perfectly and used in such classics as Guerlain's Vetiver (2000), Opium Pour Homme (1995, formula below) and Equipage by Hermès (1970). It was an IFF captive and recently discontinued which is regretful as some great fragrances will now be reformulated to accommodate the loss. In a modern context this base is usable up to 1.2% and lends a wonderful spice vibe to a fragrance without the need to balance individual spice materials. This product has been slightly reformulated to remove an EU prohibited aroma chemical. Espicene Gamma contains 8% musk ketone which is unrestricted by IFRA but has a use limit in the EU of 1.4%. Afterword: this base should not be confused with Epice FW which was a classic Synarome base Epicea used in Arpege.

missing_other.title: Eucalyptus By-Absolute
missing_other.description: This material opens with a warm, softly green character that completely reframes what eucalyptus can smell like. The sharp medicinal brightness of the essential oil is gone, replaced by something richer, more textured, and far more complex. What you smell is balsamic, slightly waxy, and herbaceous, with a woody-spiced undercurrent that builds rather than fades. That depth makes it a natural architect's material: use it to introduce a naturalistic eucalyptus signature without the clinical edge that the oil brings. In fougères and aromatic compositions, it sits beautifully in the heart without overwhelming the structure. Try it alongside lavender, clary sage, or labdanum to amplify its balsamic green facets - it strengthens the accord without demanding the spotlight. Where it surprises is in fine fragrance. Pair it with patchouli or cedarwood and the by-absolute's resinous, almost leathery warmth comes forward. It also works as a sophisticated counterpoint to bright citrus or ozonic top notes, grounding the freshness with something altogether more earthy and substantial. This is a material that rewards experimentation.

missing_other.title: Eucalyptus Oil, Citriodora
missing_other.description: Eucalyptus citriodora delivers a striking opening punch that smells like fresh-crushed citronella leaves dipped in rose petals. The citronellal-dominant profile gives way rapidly to citronellol's soft floralcy, revealing a dewy rose heart. The drydown settles into a sweet, almost balsamic finish without the camphoraceous medicinal notes typical of other eucalyptus species. This oil serves two distinct purposes in your perfumer's organ. First, it provides unparalleled naturalistic lift to synthetic rose accords. Second, it anchors fleeting citrus top notes, extending lemon perception well into the heart. Blend citriodora with terpinyl acetate to soften its aldehydic bite into sophisticated cologne territory. Pair it with rhodinol ex geranium or geraniol ex palmarosa to reinforce the rosy facets, or use cedarwood and vetiver to exploit its balsamic undertones.

missing_other.title: Eucalyptus Oil, Globulus
missing_other.description: Classic Eucalyptus globulus oil opens with a blast of icy, camphoraceous freshness that physically cools the nasal passages. The medicinal sharpness quickly reveals herbal-green facets reminiscent of crushed leaves and pine forest after rain. As it develops, subtle woody-sweet undertones emerge before the characteristic clean dryout. This oil excels at adding verticality to heavy compositions—a trace amount lifts dense orientals, ambers, and white florals without announcing its presence. In fougère accords, it reinforces the camphoraceous aspect of lavandin and sharpens the overall freshness. Pair it with cardamom for a sophisticated spicy-cool vibration, or blend with cedarwood to create freshly-cut forest effects. Use eucalyptus judiciously—its power lies in small doses where it acts as an invisible structural element. Combine with calone for enhanced marine accords, or with incense for that steamy hammam contrast. Rectified grades offer linear cleanliness for functional work, while crude oils provide textural complexity and better fixation for fine fragrance applications.

missing_other.title: Fauxmoss®
missing_other.description: Oakmoss is now restricted to 0.1% of a finished product and only if the natural material is stripped of certain chemicals. This has resulted in the destruction of more fragrances than any other single product restriction or ban. That's where Fauxmoss® comes in. Fauxmoss® is a rich blend of naturals and synthetics that mimic the properties of genuine oakmoss, right down to its intensely green colour (the finest quality of Oakmoss is dark green rather than the more common brown seen today). Use it as a one for one replacer for a 50% dilution of Oakmoss absolute. And best of all, Fauxmoss® can be used with absolutely no restrictions! It is IFRA compliant to 100% of your finished fragrance.

missing_other.title: Fennel Seed Oil
missing_other.description: Use Sweet Fennel at 0.06-4.4% for gentle anisic warmth in floral accords and gourmand compositions. The powdery, vintage effect works particularly well with rose and white florals. Bitter Fennel functions as a sharp aromatic top note that cuts through overly sweet compositions whilst providing the signature lift in classic fougère structures. Sweet Fennel integrates smoothly into oriental and floral bases where you need herbaceous sweetness without harshness. Fennel oil delivers the essential masculine edge in aromatic compositions, bridging lavender top notes with coumarin bases through its unique anisic-camphoraceous character. This oil functions primarily as top to middle notes with excellent tenacity. Fennel seeds have a similar appearance to caraway and cumin seeds; the main differentiator is that fennel seeds are distinctly green in colour. Synergies: Lavender, Geranium, Rose, Sandalwood, Bergamot, Basil, Clary Sage, Coumarin, Oakmoss.

missing_other.title: Fenugreek “Signature” Absolute
missing_other.description: This absolute opens with an almost overwhelming savoury intensity that can shock the uninitiated—pure celery seed, lovage, and curry spice. When you first smell this material neat, you encounter what seems like concentrated vegetable stock. This raw potency contains the secret to its brilliance. Diluted properly, fenugreek reveals its true character as nature's maple syrup concentrate. The savoury notes recede to unveil deep caramel, burnt sugar, and toasted nuts—gourmand notes that vanilla simply cannot replicate. You'll find this transformation creates sophisticated sweetness in tobacco accords, adds unexpected warmth to woody bases, and introduces authentic nutty facets to amber compositions. Use fenugreek when you need to transcend ordinary gourmand territories. Its coumarinic hay-like facets bridge perfectly into fougère structures, whilst its tenacious maple character anchors gourmand florals. This material demands respect—work from extreme dilutions and build slowly. This comes pre-diluted to 90% in IPM by LMR so it is not suitable for all natural perfumers.

missing_other.title: Feuille de Cassis
missing_other.description: Feuille de Cassis is our blackcurrant leaf base, built around an overdose of green naturals to give a vivid leafy effect rather than a bud note. In perfumery it reads as crushed blackcurrant leaves, tart green sap, stems, and sharp botanical freshness. The effect is bright, penetrating, and naturalistic, with more of the living plant than the fruit. It is useful wherever a perfume needs real greenness, lift, and that unmistakable cassis-leaf snap without moving into the darker, more animalic territory of the buds. This base completely transforms run-of-the-mill top notes, adding verdant grace, naturalness and radiance. I guarantee it will become part of your regular use green materials. Pairs perfectly with Cassis Base 345 B to which it adds volume and bloom, and blackcurrant bud absolute, both 37% Molecular Distilled and fine Burgundian absolute .

missing_other.title: Fig Signature
missing_other.description: Fig Signature is a masterful interpretation of the lush, sun-drenched aroma of fresh figs, capturing both their creamy sweetness and green, slightly woody undertones. Unlike many fig bases that lean too milky or artificial, this one strikes the perfect balance—ripe, pulpy fruit wrapped in crisp fig leaf and a touch of coconut lactone for that unmistakable Mediterranean warmth. Whether used to lend natural richness to a fragrance or to add a novel green facet to florals and woods, Fig Signature is an indispensable tool for the perfumer seeking authenticity with effortless blending.

missing_other.title: Fir Balsam Absolute 50% TEC
missing_other.description: Fir Balsam is the scent of winterly days, the great outdoors and Christmas festivities; perhaps no other material is so deeply entrenched in our shared scent-memory. It is also incredibly versatile, with fruit notes that can subtly enrich a gourmand to woody notes that blend well with all the classics such as vetiver, cedarwood and sandalwood. This V. MANE Fils extract is rich, green, woody and sweet. It is a truly wonderful specimen of Fir Balsam and a must-have for all perfumers. Fir Balsam is found in Polo Green (1978, our Compound Green), Drakkar Noir (1982), Rubenstein's Men's Club (1966), Patou Pour Homme (1980) and Patou Pour Homme Prive (1994), and Oscar de la Renta's Pour Lui (1980), amongst many others. Because Fir Balsam is extremely thick we offer it at 50% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless isolate from citrus). It may still require gentle heating to make it fully mobile depending upon your room temperature.

missing_other.title: Fir Oil, Canada
missing_other.description: Canadian Fir Oil opens with an immediately recognisable burst of fresh pine needles—that clean, slightly tart terpenic quality that transports you directly to a snow-covered forest. This initial brightness quickly reveals the oil's distinctive character: a remarkably sweet, soft balsamic richness that sets it apart from harsher coniferous oils. The sweetness isn't cloying but rather reminiscent of fresh sap weeping from bark, providing a well-rounded, mild character that makes this oil exceptionally versatile in perfumery applications. Use Canadian Fir Oil when you need authentic evergreen freshness with sophistication. Its balanced profile makes it ideal for creating Christmas-themed compositions that avoid the harsh, medicinal notes of cheaper pine oils. Use it to add energising lift to masculine fougères, where its clean terpenic facets complement lavender beautifully. In functional perfumery, it excels in premium air fresheners and household cleaners, providing that coveted "fresh forest" effect while its natural sweetness prevents the sharp, synthetic character common in coniferous compositions. The distinctions between Canadian, Siberian, and Douglas Fir oils fundamentally shape your formulation choices. Canadian Fir (Abies balsamea) delivers sweeter, richer, more immediately appealing evergreen notes with its characteristic balsamic warmth and grassy roundness. Siberian Fir (Abies sibirica) presents a more complex, woody profile with distinctive aldehydic top notes and fruity-balsamic undertones that some find overpowering. Douglas Fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii) stands apart entirely with its remarkably citrusy-floral character layered over woody pine—the least medicinal and most sophisticated of the three, offering exceptional tenacity that rivals many base notes. Where Canadian Fir energises with fresh, approachable sweetness ideal for traditional applications, and Siberian Fir intrigues with deeper complexity suited to unconventional perfumery, Douglas Fir br

missing_other.title: Fireside
missing_other.description: Compound Fireside is our internal formula for a scent in the style of By the Fireplace by Maison Margiela. Launched in 2015 and created by Marie Salamagne for the Replica collection, this is a woody gourmand fragrance built around smoky guaiac wood and roasted chestnut with warm spice and vanilla. This compound features a creamy chestnut accord wrapped in smoky guaiac wood and musky cashmeran. The top notes of clove and pink pepper provide a warming spiced opening, while orange blossom and juniper lift the heart before the woods take hold. The base delivers rich vanilla and Peru balsam for a sweet, resinous finish. The result is a photorealistic woodsmoke effect – cosy rather than harsh – with good longevity and moderate to strong projection in the first hours before settling close to the skin. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Cloves, Pink Pepper, Orange Blossom Heart Notes: Chestnut, Guaiac Wood, Juniper Base Notes: Vanilla, Peru Balsam, Cashmeran

missing_other.title: Fixomusk™
missing_other.description: Fixomusk™ is an elegant restoration of the original Fixomusc of Chuit Naef & Cie popularised by fragrances such as Styx by Coty, Après L'Ondée and L'Heure Bleue by Guerlain and great later 20th century scents such as Poison by Dior, Oscar de la Renta , Parfum Sacré by Caron and Gianfranco Ferré for men. Fixomusk is a soft and sweet animalic fixative base loaded with luxurious natural oils and absolutes. It is synergistic with Ambreine , Opoponax Doux and Irrozol . Use traces to add incredible longevity to your perfumes and cosmetics, or overdose it for its unique scent profile. Due to the presence of musk ketone at a whopping 17%, Fixomusk should be restricted to 8.2% of a finished fragrance for customers requiring compliance with EU 1223/2009. Musk ketone is legal and unrestricted by IFRA but limited in quantity in European cosmetic products (including fine fragrance). This crystallises slightly in cold environments. Apply gentle heat to dissolve. Note: in preparation for IFRA 51 this product has been slightly reformulated and Benzyl Benzoate has been entirely eliminated.

missing_other.title: Fleur D'Heliotrope
missing_other.description: Heliotrope is an elegant flower with a sweet almond and vanilla character. While heliotropin has been the classic way of adding this note to a fragrance, restrictions on the material have made it impossible for many to obtain. Fraterworks® Fleur D'Heliotrope is a full flower De Laire base incorporating all of the classic elements of the heliotrope flower in combination with rich absolutes and essential oils to give you a sultry drydown but extending the floralcy into the heart of the scent. This is a must-have base for those wanting to add an elegant heliotrope notes to their fragrances without the complications that go with the use of pure heliotropin.

missing_other.title: Fleur D'Oranger
missing_other.description: Fleur D'Oranger is an orange flower absolute type base. It can be used as a direct one for one replacer or in combination with other similar bases such as Floronol which imparts the note of neroli oil. Fleur D'Oranger is a long lasting rich and extremely natural base. This is a must have given the incredibly high prices of raw materials. Fraterworks Fleur D'Oranger is enriched with natural orange blossom absolute. This base was used in L'Origan by Coty and Tabu by Jean Carles for Dana.

missing_other.title: Fleur De Cassie
missing_other.description: Cassie is a complex sweet floral note of the Acacia family (specifically Acacia Farnesiana ). It can be used to enhance and add complexity to violet and iris notes as well as blending well with gourmand and fruit notes due to its creamy anisic dry down. Fraterworks Fleur De Cassie (a classic De Laire base) is rich with natural oils, madagascan vanilla, French mimosa, orris butter and more. At levels below 1% in your juice it adds volume and in higher amounts is a wonderful nuancer. Can be used safely up to a whopping 22% of your finished product according to IFRA 51. Fleur de Cassie is a wonderful blender with mimosa and cherry notes.

missing_other.title: Fleur De Reseda
missing_other.description: Reseda is an unusual floral note that was far more popular in the past than it is today. And for that reason it deserves a renaissance! Fleur De Reseda (also known as Mignonette) is fruity and floral whilst having a striking green heart. Its sweet strawberry nuances make it perfect to add character to a contemporary gourmand fragrance. First cultivated in England during the mid-18th century, mignonette quickly became a popular scent amongst the well-to-do. If you are looking for the "next big thing" or just want a striking and unusual note to make your fragrance stand out, look no further than Fraterworks Fleur de Reseda .

missing_other.title: Fleur De Tabac
missing_other.description: Fleur de Tabac is an incredible tobacco flower type base created by the master perfumer Jean Carles at the end of the 1920s when he worked for Roure. It encapsulates not just tobacco flowers, but the distinct scent of the entire plant as it would have existed in the early 20th century before genetic modification and cross breeding altered it forever. Fleur de Tabac was most likely the foundation of the now all-but-disappeared perfume of the similar name by Cherigan in 1929 but its most famous outing was as a key note in Schiaparelli's groundbreaking 1937 fragrance Shocking (also by Jean Carles) as part of its central pink flower accord. The base is presented here in an essentially unmodified form. Miraculously the formula of Mr Carles has survived the onslaught of regulations and the only necessary tweak was the replacement of a trace amount of a prohibed musk. Fleur de Tabac is like nothing you have experienced before. It is a truly unique and astonishing piece of fragrance history. This base is proof that perfumery has been, and can again be, an art form.

missing_other.title: Fleurs Deluxe № 1
missing_other.description: Fleurs Deluxe № 1 is a sublime modern floral base that perfectly balances Jasmine, Rose, tuberose and Hyacinth, with accents of other luxury flowers. It is a classic French blend that is modernised with the most radiant and current molecules thus combining the peak of historic perfumery with the best of aroma science. The purpose of this base is to allow perfumers to incorporate a rich natural floral fond into their fragrances without having to outlay enormous amounts to buy the various precious absolutes and essential oils that are needed for this high level of fine fragrance making. The base includes aroma molecules that are rarely used by artisans due to the high cost (in some cases many times higher than natural floral oils). Dilute it “as-is” for a fragrance that matches the elegance and quality of Patou's famous Joy , or use it as a floralising element in a more complex fine fragrance.

missing_other.title: Fleurs Deluxe № 3
missing_other.description: Fleurs Deluxe № 3 is the floral core of the great Iris Gris (1946) by Vincent Roubert for Jacques Fath. Containing every orris product available in combination with the great Persicol base and luxurious absolutes of French rose de Mai, jasmine, tuberose and more. It is easy to understand why this fragrance is considered by many to be the greatest perfume ever made. Iris Gris is comprised of 65% of Fleurs Deluxe № 3 — unchanged and unadapted; this is the pure heart of the fragrance. Compound the demonstration formula below for an exact replica of the original Iris Gris or use Fleurs Deluxe № 3 as the starting point for your own modern luxurious orris based fragrance. The original Iris Gris was a multifloral perfume of carnation, iris, violet, rose, jasmine, tuberose, woods and musks (including a hefty dose of civet absolute!). This was all wrapped in a delightful sweet peach note from Firmenich's famous Persicol base. We also have Fleurs Deluxe № 1 if you are looking for a rich French rose and jasmine fragrance in the style of Patou's Joy.

missing_other.title: Floranol
missing_other.description: Floranol is a fantasy replacer for Neroli bigarade oil which is now beyond the budget of most perfumers. Keeping its roots in the classical bases of De Laire, our Floronol is updated for modern tastes and can be effectively used from Fraterworks Floranol has a wonderful ability to add freshness to heavy floral rich fragrances and orientals, whilst also sitting beautifully in a classic cologne fond. Floranol is a must-have base for all perfumers and is rich with naturals oils and absolutes. If you are looking for a more true to life Neroli oil replacer, you may prefer our Neroli Supreme TruEss ™.

missing_other.title: Florapeel
missing_other.description: Florapeel from V. MANE Fils is a highly diffusive floral grapefruit base built around their captive molecule Bigarane. It shares a clear familial connection to Bigaflower and Green Catcher and can be combined with either or both of those bases to great effect. In a world where grapefruit notes are extremely popular and natural grapefruit , while readily available, often needs some help from synthetics — invariably methyl pamplemousse — this is a welcome addition to the perfumer's palette. This joins our two other great bases: Firmenich's Grapefruit Base 184062D and our own highly popular Pomelo Grandis (“ This captures the essence of the entire fruit, without the risk of degradation. ” — J. Y. S. ).

missing_other.title: Flouve “Signature” Absolute
missing_other.description: Flouve is the luxury member of the hay family, and while our Hay Absolute from V MANE Fils is incredibly beautiful, Payan Bertrand's Flouve “Signature” Absolute is sublime. It carries the IG Absolue Pays de Grasse marque, the highest form of certification for fragrance materials grown and processed in Grasse. Steffan Arctander describes it thus: "[Flouve absolute has] a very sweet, herbaceous, tobacco-like and coumarinic odor. The odor is so rich and so complex that one can keep on finding notes in it. However, the overall fragrance is a sweet, licorice-like, root-like, somewhat mossy-herbaceous like wet underforest and meadows, of exceptional tenacity and high penetrating power. [… U]seful in chypre, fougere, pine, oriental bases, and in traces as a sweetener for dry-woody notes which can be modified in a very pleasant way.” Flouve blends excellently with bases Artemal ™, Suralette™ Extra , Verdantol and Amazonia , as well as with French Lavender Oil , Douglas Fir Needle Oil , Oakmoss Absolutes , Roman Chamomile , Labdanum and petitgrain oils (especially LMR's marvellous Petitgrain Oil Terpeneless ). Lovely accords can be made with aroma chemicals Fenchone Alpha , Linalool Oxide , Vetimoss , Azarbre , and Geosmin . Because flouve absolute is so thick, we now optionally supply it at 10% dilution in Triethyl Citrate Natural making it ISO 9235 compliant. Origin: Grasse, France Part: Dried flowering tops of grass Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Foin Coupé
missing_other.description: Foin Coupé is the scent of freshly mown hay. It is an incredibly diffusive sweet coumarinic base with orange blossom nuances loaded with natural oils, including pure and natural French hay absolute. Use it as a modifier for coumarin or herbal notes, or as a radiant and earthy nuancer for a gentlemen's fragrance. Featured in Patou Pour Homme Privé , one of the most highly regarded scents for men gaining a near-mythical status, this fresh cut hay base is sublime. We also offer the original crystalline Foin Rigaud — an intensely powerful and penetrating base note product.

missing_other.title: Foin Rigaud
tags: locale:glass pot for 1 5 and 15 grams then powder pots
missing_other.description: Foin bases encapsulate the dreamy scent of the wild French countryside where ribbons of orange blossom, geranium and wild flowers float on the warm hay-soaked air. Foin Rigaud was one of the earliest types of foin (new mown hay) base. It was, in reality, an embellished form of coumarin - born from the practice by which powerful new molecules were made available to perfumers as the lead character in accords and bases. Despite being used in a relatively small amount, Foin Rigaud played a vital role in Coty's L'Origan . An update to our earlier formula can found below. Foin Rigaud is presented here in its original powder form. This product is very intense and powerful. If you prefer a more classic top to bottom fantasy hay base we recommend Foin Coupé which comes in liquid form.

missing_other.title: Forest Pepper, P. Jungle Essence
missing_other.description: Forest Pepper CO2 (Pure Jungle Essence) opens with a tingling spicy-citrus burst — pink pepper warmth shot through with bright aldehydic orange and lemon. Underneath sit soft tropical-fruit and floral facets that round the spice. The metallic-citrus character is closer to Sichuan pepper than to black pepper, despite the name. Use Forest Pepper CO2 to bring authentic peppery sparkle and citrus lift to colognes, modern fougères and spicy-woody accords. It works as a top-note enhancer that carries spicy presence into the heart of a composition. It also lifts dull citrus accords with a tingling, modern edge. Pair with bergamot, pink peppercorn oil and aldehyde C-10 for a sparkling modern citrus top, or use alongside cardamom, ginger CO2 and incense for a tingling oriental opening. A trace under rose lifts the floral with peppery warmth. Dose carefully — overdose pushes the metallic sparkle into harshness. Forest Pepper CO2 is extracted via supercritical CO2 from the dried fruits of Zanthoxylum rhetsa, known locally as Ma Khaen, a tree that grows wild in mountainous regions of northern Thailand and across Southeast Asia. The Pure Jungle Essence process uses CO2 alone — no co-solvents — at low temperature, preserving the volatile top notes that conventional steam distillation destroys. Despite its name, the species is unrelated to true black pepper (Piper nigrum) and belongs to the citrus family.

missing_other.title: Four Corners Resinoid
missing_other.description: Four Corners Resinoid opens with a dark, fruity sweetness evoking dried tamarind and rum-soaked raisins. Nutty caramel, gentle balsamic warmth, and a faint costus-like earthiness follow. Extracted from the four-ridged pods of the Cameroonian aidan tree (Tetrapleura tetraptera), this is an uncommon and distinctive material for your palette. That rich fruity-balsamic character fits naturally into gourmand and oriental bases, where it furnishes a dried fruit facet sitting somewhere between rum and benzoin. You can also use it to warm woody accords or steer amber compositions toward something more exotic and unexpected. Think of this as the link between the balsam shelf and the rum cabinet in your collection. It grounds gourmand accords when paired with vanillin, coumarin, and tonka, and enriches labdanum-heavy amber bases with a distinctive dried-fruit twist. This material is sold only at 10% in TEC which is how V. MANE Fils manufactures it. Image Copyright Marina Khaytarova.

missing_other.title: Frangipani Absolute
tags: locale:heat needed for pure. Diluted is still thick.
missing_other.description: Frangipani Absolute opens with intoxicating exotic florality—heady, creamy, and immediately evocative of warm tropical nights. Soft peachy facets mingle with sweet orange blossom character, while gardenia-like richness adds opulent depth. Balsamic undertones of almond and vanilla emerge in the drydown, creating a complete floral portrait that feels both delicate and seductive. This precious absolute comes from Plumeria alba flowers, harvested between March and April from shrubs native to the West Indies. The name itself tells a fascinating story: when a French colonist encountered plumeria in the Caribbean, its scent reminded him of a famous Renaissance perfume created by the Roman Frangipani family—making this the only plant named after a fragrance rather than the reverse. Blend with tropical fruits, coconut, tuberose, gardenia, and orange blossom for authentic compositions. The high benzyl salicylate and benzyl benzoate content provides natural fixative properties. Frangipani absolute has a wax-like consistency when pure, and so we also sell it diluted to 20% for ease of use. Both forms may still need a small amount of gentle heat for full solubility.

missing_other.title: Frankincense Oil, Somalia
missing_other.description: Also known as olibanum essential oil, this oil is a bright and fresh top note resin with long lasting effects. It works wonders with citrus oils to give longevity and interesting effects and is vital in the creation of Church incense notes. This fine oil is sourced from Somalia and is intoxicating. There are no bad notes here, just pure incense goodness. Origin: Somalia Part: Exudate from bark Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Frankincense Sacra Oil, Oman
missing_other.description: Frankincense can be a little confusing because it has multiple names. The classical name is Olibanum (from an Arabic word meaning milk) while more recently the term Frankincense has become the norm. To further complicate things we have two common types used in perfumery:Boswellia carterii and Boswellia sacra. The differences between these two varieties is minuscule and basically the region of growth determines the term used (inconsistently from supplier to supplier) with the sacra type coming from Oman and Yemen and the carterii coming from Somalia and East Africa. The Frankincense Sacra oil we offer here is from Oman and it is a spectacular version, being sweet and perfumistic with a less camphoraceous opening than the Somalian frankincense oil we also stock. Origin: Oman Part: Pathological exudate from bark Method: Steam distillation
