missing_other.title: Fruit Sec
missing_other.description: Fruit Sec 184078D opens with an intoxicating burst of concentrated dried fruits—imagine sun-ripened plums and apricots transformed through desiccation into something far richer. This isn't simple fruit juice sweetness but rather the complex depth of preserved fruits with their concentrated sugars, subtle fermentation notes, and that characteristic skin astringency. The damascone-rich heart radiates powerful jammy facets while ionones add sophisticated powdery nuances. This material transforms compositions at every level—use it at trace amounts to add mysterious depth to roses or woody accords. At 1-5%, it becomes a recognisable dried fruit signature that elevates fruity-florals and adds gourmand warmth to orientals. The creamy lactonic base notes ensure smooth blending without harsh edges, solving the technical challenge of incorporating powerful materials like damascones into balanced accords. Reach for Fruit Sec when you need instant sophistication in gourmand creations or unexpected richness in florals. It pairs brilliantly with cassis bases for dynamic tropical effects, adds unctuousness to rose accords, and creates enveloping warmth with vanilla, benzoin and spices. At higher doses (5-8%), it becomes your composition's star—perfect for modern oriental gourmands where dried fruit opulence defines the fragrance.

missing_other.title: Fumencens HTC
missing_other.description: Upon the first sniff of Fumencens HTC one immediately recognises the scent of fragrant ribbons of incense swirling heavenwards in an old stone Church. Fumencens HTC is a masterpiece of modern perfume technology in which frankincense resin is blended with natural triethyl citrate and heated to extremely high temperatures in a technique known as hydrothermal carbonization. This produces a near-burnt effect in the frankincense resin that replicates masterfully the scent of incense on red hot coals in a censer and hundreds of burning memorial candles. This technique is very similar to the pyrogenation process used by Firmenich in making their Olibanum Resinoid Vulcain, however unlike that material Fumencens HTC has an additional (and very long lasting) aspect of cade or birch tar. It is the smokiness and mahogany-like woodiness that sets Fumencens HTC apart. I won't say it twice: you need this.

missing_other.title: Galbanum Resinoid
missing_other.description: Galbanum Resinoid opens with the same characteristic burst of intense greenness familiar from the essential oil—crushed bell peppers, torn leaves, and fresh-cut grass—but quickly reveals its distinctive personality. Where the oil remains sharp and volatile, the resinoid settles into a rich, dark green depth with pronounced balsamic warmth. This thick, viscous material carries the forest within it: coniferous resins, damp earth, and woody undertones that ground its vegetal sharpness in something more profound and lasting. Galbanum Resinoid is best used at 0.5-3% when you need green notes with genuine staying power and complexity. Unlike the essential oil's fleeting pine-like top notes, the resinoid provides sustained green depth throughout a fragrance's evolution. Its superior fixative properties anchor volatile materials while contributing its own sophisticated woody-balsamic character. Use it as the foundation for chypre green compositions where longevity matters, or to create authentic forest atmospheres that persist from first spray to final drydown. The differences between Galbanum essential oil and resinoid transform your formulation approach entirely. The oil delivers sharp, penetrating greenness with distinctive pine-like top notes—perfect for immediate impact but lacking persistence. The resinoid trades some of that initial sharpness for profound depth: less volatile, less harsh, more balsamic and woody. Where the oil acts as a fleeting green modifier, the resinoid functions as a true base note with exceptional fixative power. The oil's clean, almost metallic green suits modern compositions; the resinoid's complex forest character enriches traditional chypres and fougères. Most importantly, the resinoid's thick consistency and tendency to resinify demands careful handling—pre-dilution in TEC (as supplied here) prevents solidification while maintaining its extraordinary longevity. Choose the oil for bright green accents; choose the resinoid for lasting green

missing_other.title: Galbanum “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: Galbanum oil is powerful green oil which gives the well known distinctive odour to Chanel No 19 and the original Miss Dior by Jean Carles. Galbanum in small amounts adds a wonderful green floralcy and its blends with muguet materials are unsurpassed. Payan Bertrand's Galbanum oil (one of their signature products) is a truly luxurious quality which surpasses all others we tested. Origin: Persia Part: Resin Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Gardenia J. Ellis
missing_other.description: Named after the great 18th century naturalist who discovered the flower, Gardenia J. Ellis is a profoundly beautiful representation of the full flowering majesty of one of the most beloved flowers. Lactonic, sweet, green and strikingly true to life, this is the finest gardenia base on the market today. Traces add creamy elegance to any multiflor while an overdose gives you a hyper-realistic floral heart. Sublime. Gardenia In Perfume History Gardenia has long captivated perfumers as one of the most elusive and challenging white florals to capture in a bottle. Unlike jasmine or tuberose, which yield essential oils or absolutes, gardenia's delicate petals refuse to surrender their scent through traditional extraction methods, making the true gardenia absolute extraordinarily rare and prohibitively expensive. This scarcity sparked decades of creative reconstruction, with perfumers building gardenia accords from jasmine, tuberose, and ylang-ylang, enhanced by mushroom-like methyl anthranilate and creamy benzyl acetate. The breakthrough came with synthetic molecules like styrallyl acetate (gardenia acetate), which captured gardenia's distinctive fresh-green floralcy. Classic fragrances like Chanel's Gardénia (1925), created by Ernest Beaux, established the archetypal gardenia: creamy, narcotic, slightly mushroomy, with green freshness balancing the heavy white floral heart. The note reached new heights of naturalism in Estée Lauder's Private Collection Tuberose Gardenia (2007), where headspace technology finally allowed perfumers to analyze living gardenia's true molecular fingerprint. Today, gardenia remains a perfumer's proof of skill—a note that exists more perfectly in the imagination than in nature, requiring artistic interpretation rather than mere extraction.

missing_other.title: Genet “Signature” Absolute
missing_other.description: Of the myriad absolutes of genet (aka broom), this is the finest French product. It is the highest quality genet on the market today, being produced by one of the top suppliers of high end naturals from Grasse. Genet absolute is one of the most treasured of all the naturals, imparting a warmth and sweetness that naturalises and enriches a wide range of fragrances. Traces add interest and complexity, while larger doses add an incredibly luxurious and rich nuance of verdant fields and rolling green hills stretching far into the horizon. Blends of genet with tuberose and other floral absolutes are out of this world. Because genet absolute is so thick and costly, we also offer it at 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate making it ISO 9235 compliant. This replaces our previous offering of 50% dilution only. Origin: France Part: Flowers Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Gentian “Signature” Resinoid
missing_other.description: Gentian resinoid smells of damp earth, bitter roots, and cool Alpine air. The bitterness is striking — green, vegetal, almost medicinal — but underneath sits a quiet honeyed warmth and dry woody depth. It is one of perfumery's rarest and most unusual natural materials. Jean-Claude Ellena chose gentian for Hermès Eau de Gentiane Blanche — proof that this obscure root material can anchor a major luxury fragrance. Use it sparingly to add bitter-earthy originality to green compositions, chypres, and iris accords. It shares the powdery, rooty quality of orris but with a cold, bitter twist. Gentiana lutea — the great yellow gentian — grows wild in Alpine meadows and takes a decade to reach maturity. Its roots give Suze, Salers, and Avèze their famous bitterness. Pair it with vetiver, oakmoss, angelica root, and bergamot for compositions that smell like nowhere else. This extract is a signature speciality of Payan Bertrand.

missing_other.title: Geranium Bourbon “Supreme” Oil
missing_other.description: Geranium Bourbon or rose geranium is native to South Africa but it was transplanted to Réunion island (known as Île de Bourbon from 1665–1793) by the French colonists in the 1840s after natural disasters destroyed the coffee industry in 1806 and 1807. In time the importance of the Island in international trade fell and most geranium Bourbon is now produced on the neighbouring island of Madagascar, from whence this essential oil comes. Our geranium Bourbon essential oil is, for all intents and purposes, the closest in scent you can find to the odour quality loved by the great perfumers of the 20th century who particularly enjoyed the balanced and easily managed green and floral scent. It is a key note in most of the earliest fougère fragrances.

missing_other.title: Geranium Oil, China
missing_other.description: Geranium Oil, from Pelargonium graveolens , adds fresh green notes and a touch of rose-like sweetness. This makes it a key ingredient in numerous perfumes — particularly fougères. Its blend of floral and herbal tones gives balance and brightness. Chinese geranium oil differs from Geranium Bourbon which is typically known for its rich, sweet rose smell with a minty hint. On the other hand, the Chinese variety has a sharper, greener scent with herbal undertones, so it works well in fresh blends. It is also a more budget-friendly option. This oil works well with citrus, floral, and woody scents. It brightens top note blends based on lemon or bergamot , melds smoothly in the heart with rose or jasmine, and pairs beautifully with sandalwood or patchouli for a deep, rich base. Its versatility makes it a must-have for every perfumer. And of course our supplier, LMR, is world class so you know you're getting the absolute finest quality on the market.

missing_other.title: Geranium Oil, Egypt
missing_other.description: Geranium Oil, from Pelargonium graveolens , adds fresh green notes and a touch of rose-like sweetness. This makes it a key ingredient in numerous perfumes — particularly fougères. Its blend of floral and herbal tones gives balance and brightness. This marvellous Egyptian extract is sharper and fresher than the classic Bourbon type and has a more obviously citrus aspect. It's low cost should not be deemed to imply low quality, as this LMR version is really the finest on the market; so good, in fact, it is better than many Bourbon offerings from other manufacturers. We also stock Chinese Geranium oil (fresh and herbal) and Geranium Bourbon (floral and rose-like).

missing_other.title: German Chamomile “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: German chamomile bears an intense ink-blue colour (hence its nickname of blue chamomile or chamomile blue oil). It has wonderfully sweet notes making it a hidden gourmand treasure. Our German chamomile is from a single estate in England, a nation that is regarded as the finest source of this oil. Unlike most commercial blue chamomiles which can be quite heavy, ours practically dances. It is delicate and refined - a real treasure. We love this quality of oil so much that it is the only German chamomile we use in our products. The care that has gone in to the manufacture of this essential oil is obvious from first sniff. Once you have tried our German Chamomile “Signature” Oil, you will be a convert for life. If you are wondering, the difference between the German and Roman chamomile plants is that German chamomile flowers grow in clusters, while Roman chamomile flowers grow singularly atop a hairy stem. We also stock a wonderful Roman chamomile oil . Origin: England Variety: matricaria recutita Part: Flower heads Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Ginger "Top Note" CO2, P. Jungle Essence
missing_other.description: The prestigious V. MANE Fils offers two ginger Pure Jungle Essences (CO2 extracts). They are this Ginger "Top Note" CO2 with dazzling bright top notes, and the rich, Dark Ginger CO2 , a heart / base note variety. This material opens with an explosive burst of fresh-cut ginger that hits you immediately with sharp, lemony brightness. The effervescent quality feels alive and electric, capturing the exact moment when you slice open a fresh rhizome. Nothing about this extract feels cooked or processed—it's pure, vibrant ginger in its most energetic form. You'll find this CO2 extract transforms compositions by adding incredible lifting power and naturalistic warmth simultaneously. Unlike steam-distilled ginger oil, which carries heavier cooked notes, this fractionated extract isolates only the brightest volatile compounds. Use it to energise woody bases, cut through rich florals, or create sophisticated gourmand accords where authentic ginger character matters most. The persistence surprises many perfumers—while it functions as a brilliant top note, it maintains presence throughout the heart. Combine with citrus for explosive freshness, pair with pink pepper for modern spice blends, or use alongside vanilla for authentic gingerbread effects. This extract bridges traditional spice work with contemporary perfumery's demand for hyper-realistic naturals. We recommend a pairing of this top note ginger CO2 with Payan Bertrand's dazzlingly citrus-fresh Ginger Oil Fresh, Côte d'Ivoire, the rare Dark Ginger CO2 extraction , also from MANE, or LMR's marvellous Madagascan Fresh Ginger essential oil . For something a little different you may also like our Red Ginger oil .

missing_other.title: Ginger Oil Fresh, Côte d'Ivoire
missing_other.description: This is, in our opinion, the finest fresh ginger essential oil you will ever experience. Once again the master distillers at Payan Bertrand have managed to capture the very soul of the plant in producing this masterpiece of perfumery art — and it's not a CO2 or molecular distillation! When compared against the far more common Ginger Fresh (or fraiche) essential oils from Indonesia, Madagascar and China, this Ivorian oil is not just a step up… it is a total reinvention of what ginger oil should be. Smelling this oil is like smelling ginger for the first time. It will take your breath away. Ivory Coast ginger has all the expected character of fresh ginger but with a whole extra layer of dazzle. There is no dustiness here (often characteristic of poor quality oil) just pure effulgent ginger. 2026 Update: due to weather events in the region, this oil has more than doubled in price. We hope to see a drop in the future but for now we have had to increase the cost accordingly.

missing_other.title: Ginger Oil Fresh, Madagascar
missing_other.description: This exceptional essential oil opens with an explosive burst of sparkling, fizzy freshness that immediately energises your compositions. The initial citrusy-lemony effervescence, reminiscent of verbena or crushed lemongrass, provides tremendous lift and radiance. Unlike typical ginger oils, the finest Madagascar qualities reveal an unexpected floral heart with distinct rose and geranium facets. What sets this material apart is its "Blue Ginger" chemotype containing geranyl acetate—a rare component that bridges spicy and floral families with remarkable elegance. Fresh distillation from rhizomes harvested within hours preserves delicate aldehydes while preventing the harsh, turpentine-like notes found in oils from dried material. This creates a clean, sophisticated warmth devoid of earthy off-notes. Use it strategically as an olfactory binder to create seamless transitions between different fragrance families. It excels at cutting through excessive sweetness in gourmand compositions while adding sophisticated contrast to heavy ambery bases. The material's complete olfactory journey—from vibrant citrus opening through complex spicy-floral heart to warm woody-gourmand drydown—functions as a "perfume-in-itself" that enriches entire compositions from initial spray to final moments on skin. Madagascar vs Ivory Coast and CO2 Madagascar ginger oil differs significantly from other origins and extraction methods. Ivory Coast ginger oil delivers a more direct, powerfully peppery character with higher α-zingiberene content (23-45%) but lacks the signature floral complexity. It provides bold, invigorating spice but without Madagascar's sophisticated rose-geranium facets. Ginger CO2 extract offers a hyper-realistic, full-spectrum aroma identical to fresh-cut rhizome, containing both volatile aromatics and non-volatile pungent compounds (gingerols and shogaols) that create actual warmth and mild skin irritation. Choose Madagascar steam-distilled oil for sparkling floral elegance, I

missing_other.title: Gnidia Flower Absolute
missing_other.description: Once again V. MANE Fils hits a home run with this marvellous and unusual floral absolute. Gnidia has one of the highest amounts of natural maltol and it is very obvious. With an odour somewhat resembling stewed bananas, flowers and brown sugar this is a truly novel material for perfumer's who seek something extraordinary. According to MANE, “The multifaceted scent of the flowers unveils notes of narcissus, violet, cucumber, tea, and tuberose. The extract contains natural maltol, which brings a note of delicious sweetness.” The Gnidia flowers are hand picked by two associations of women living in Madagascar. We offer this incredible product from V. MANE Fils at 10% dilution in pure and natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless isolate from citrus) or pure. Undiluted the material has a thick paste-like consistency that requires warmth to liquify. Origin: Madagascar Part: Flowers Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Grapefruit Heart
missing_other.description: Grapefruit is one of the most recognisable citrus notes in perfumery and one of the hardest to sustain. Standard grapefruit oil blazes brilliantly for twenty minutes and then vanishes. Grapefruit Heart solves that problem. This is an LMR speciality — a concentrated citrus fraction designed to boost the grapefruit profile of your formula, even at very low dosage. LMR describes it as juicy and bitter-fruity with a hint of sulphurous undertone — that distinctive metallic, almost tropical edge that separates grapefruit from every other citrus. Here it is cleaner, more focused, and far more tenacious than the standard oil. A small amount provides grapefruit character that conventional oil cannot sustain past the first half hour. Use it alongside our Grapefruit Oil Pink for a complete grapefruit statement — the pink oil gives natural breadth and juicy sweetness in the opening, the Heart extends it into the heart and beyond. Essential for any serious citrus composition, aquatic accord, or fresh fragrance that needs grapefruit to last.

missing_other.title: Grapefruit Oil 5 Fold
missing_other.description: Standard grapefruit oil is almost entirely limonene — pleasant but generic. This 5-fold version is still mostly limonene, but vacuum distillation has concentrated everything else roughly fivefold. Those trace compounds are what make grapefruit smell like grapefruit, and now they come through with real authority. With the character compounds amplified, you get the woody-bitter quality that links grapefruit to vetiver, the bright aldehydic sparkle, and the subtle sulphurous-tropical facet that gives grapefruit its identity. The oil is stronger and more persistent than standard cold-pressed grapefruit. Far more useful in fine fragrance. Pair it with vetiver for a natural woody-citrus accord, with bergamot and neroli for a sophisticated citrus heart, or with black pepper and cedarwood for modern masculine compositions. It still functions as a topnote, so layer it over longer-lasting base materials. Worth every penny of the premium over standard oil. We also stock 10-folded orange Oil , terpeneless orange , terpeneless Lemon oil, and terpeneless Bergamot oil .

missing_other.title: Grapefruit Oil, Pink
missing_other.description: Pink grapefruit opens brighter and sweeter than its white counterpart. The bitter, almost quinine-like edge of white grapefruit is dialled back here, replaced by a rounder, juicier, almost berry-tinged citrus that feels more approachable from the first sniff. The colour difference in the fruit translates directly to the oil. Where white grapefruit excels in sharp masculine colognes, pink grapefruit moves naturally toward fruity-floral and feminine territory. It bridges citrus and fruit accords in a way that few other naturals can — try it alongside peach, raspberry, or blackcurrant materials and the results feel effortless. The characteristic sulphurous bite underneath the sweetness keeps it honest and unmistakably grapefruit. Use it generously as a sparkling top note. It pairs beautifully with rose, neroli, and white florals where you want citrus freshness without the austerity of lemon or the heaviness of orange. A natural companion to our Grapefruit Heart for extended citrus impact through the drydown. Note: This oil is rectified to reduce furocoumarins and fortified with a trace of natural tocopherol to extend its life on the shelf. That gives it an IFRA category 4 usage of a whop[ing 40% rather than the typical 4% for grapefruit oils.

missing_other.title: Grapefruit Oil, White
missing_other.description: Despite the enormous popularity of grapefruit notes in perfumes (usually through the use of Methyl Pamplemousse), the essential oil is less often seen in mainstream scents though masterpieces such as Bleu and Égoĩste by Chanel both incorporate the natural oil and Dolce & Gabanna Light Blue has 1%. This grapefruit oil from the United States is robust and rich. Oftentimes grapefruit can be disappointingly thin but Payan Bertrand once again has perfected the extraction process and this oil is outstanding. Because this is American oil, it has far less of the bitterness associated with European grapefruit oils. It blends beautifully with our Pomelo Grandis base, Methyl Pamplemousse and Thiocineole when an extra bitter note is wanted. Note: This oil is rectified to reduce furocoumarins and fortified with a trace of natural tocopherol to extend its life on the shelf.

missing_other.title: Greencatcher™
missing_other.description: Arguably the finest producer of naturals in the world today, V. MANE Fils also produces a few very special bases. Greencatcher ™ is one such. Built around an overdose of the MANE captive Bigarane ™ and containing absolutely no sensitising materials, this base is pure magic. Greencatcher ™ is not just another green base loaded with the usual suspects of Cis 3 Hexenol and its esters , instead it is fruity, woody, tropical and incredibly addictive. This is one of those rare products that upon first sniff triggers an instant desire to create with it. Blends with Celestafleur ™, Cassis base , Rose Oxide Laevo , Robertet's natural Cucumber and pineapple are sublime. Also blends with most green materials and fresh or fruity chemicals. Use it to add a twist to Amazonia ™ and Verdantol ™ or just put a drop on a smelling strip and enjoy it all day long.

missing_other.title: Grojsman Plus
missing_other.description: In 1990 IFF perfumer Sophia Grojsman changed the face of perfumery when she created Trésor for Lâncome with an accord which overdosed four materials ( Hedione ®, Galaxolide ®, Gamma Methyl Ionone and Iso E Super ™). In so doing she created a canvas style accord (nicknamed a "hug me" accord) which can be used as the basis for virtually any type of perfume. What we present here is that great accord in a low-ionone form with Paradise Molecule ® and discreet enhancements to add radiance and extend longevity. This is the ultimate Grojsman accord and it can be used at up to 55% of your finished fragrance. Just add your favourite blend or base to Grojsman Plus and you have a complete modern perfume. See the formula below for our re-envisioning of Guerlain's Champs Élysées (1996) fragrance to understand how to work with this base.

missing_other.title: Guaiac Wood Oil
missing_other.description: Pure classical guaiac wood (pronounced “gwy-ack”) essential oil is getting more difficult to obtain these days and recently Robertet has discontinued their rectified or so-called "heart" fraction which, while beautiful, lacked the entire spectrum of the wood that was loved by the great perfumers of days gone by. We are offering here the finest single origin (Paraguay) true guaiac wood in all its glory, completely unchanged by post-processing. Upon smelling this wood for the first time you may be surprised just how rich and luxurious it is. If you only know guaiac essential oil in its fractionated form, you are in for a real treat. Guaiac, in addition to its smoky and woody scent also has facets of spice and tea rose. It is a very versatile natural and is indispensable when making an Oud accord. This product is solid in pure form and needs heating to liquify. For convenience we also sell it at 50% in natural odourless triethyl citrate to render it easier to use. Pure Guaiac Wood Oil (Bulnesia sarmientoi) is a CITES appendix II product. In most countries this can be lawfully traded without extra paperwork if purchased for personal use. We recommend checking in advance with your own regulatory bodies. If you are purchasing pure Guaiac Wood Oil for commercial reasons you may need a CITES re-export or origin certificate to accompany your purchase. Again, you should check with your national authorities. We charge $60 USD for this certificate and it takes approximately ten days for us to apply and provide it. Simply contact us for help. We will endeavour to make the process as seamless and speedy as possible. Diluted Guaiac Wood Oil is deemed a “finished product” so no additional paperwork is necessary.

missing_other.title: Guided Smelling Experience
missing_other.description: We offer a deluxe sit-down smelling experience at our workshop in Lower Hutt (15 minutes from Wellington City). Discover our entire range of raw materials and see how the business operates. Visit prices starts from $80 US for thirty minutes. During the experience you will be accompanied by a trained member of staff who will assist you. You will have access to all of our raw materials (including many that we don't list on the website). This is a perfect opportunity to get advice, make notes on materials you may want to purchase or simply spend time with like minded lovers of the fragrance industry. As a bonus we have an extensive collection of historic and luxury fragrances which you may sample at your leisure. We have perfumes from Creed, Clive Christian, Chanel, Dior, Coty, Guerlain and many more. When you purchase we will contact you to arrange a time that is most suitable for you. This experience is available from Monday to Saturday inclusive. Light refreshments are provided for bookings of 60 minutes or greater.

missing_other.title: Gulab Attar
missing_other.description: A rich, jammy damask rose over soft, creamy sandalwood — Gulab Attar is the classical Indian co-distillate, produced in Kannauj by the traditional deg-bhapka method. The rose reads honeyed and lush, with faint spicy and green facets. Sandalwood sits underneath, giving body to the rose without muting it. In blends it works as the anchor of classical Indian floral accords. Use it as the central note in rose soliflores, as the rose voice in mukhallats, or to give warmth and body to oriental rose-oud structures. It also enriches modern rose fragrances that feel thin at the base. Pair with oud and saffron for a mukhallat base , or use alongside labdanum, benzoin and a trace of clove for an amber-rose oriental. In a soliflore it carries the rose without needing a separate fixative. Undiluted the sandalwood reads heaviest; in dilution the rose opens up properly.

missing_other.title: Gurjun Balsam Oil
missing_other.description: Gurjun Balsam Oil is a mild oil distilled from the pathological resin of the Dipterocarpus turbinatus tree. Despite its light odour, it is a very useful wood oil for blending stronger wood notes and setting a delicate background when something more interesting than Iso E Super is called for. With a gentle spice running through it and a very long drydown (over 400 hours!) it is an excellent fixative that blends with a great variety of other materials - including florals. Use it with Guaiyl Acetate and Cypriol for the beginnings of your very own luscious agarwood accord. Gjurjun Balsam Oil features in Tom Ford's Black Orchid fragrance, Duro and Baraonda by Nasomatto, Kilian's Apple Brandy and M7 by YSL. It also contributes to the wonderful Oud character of Dahn Oudh Al Shams by Ajmal.

missing_other.title: Hawthorn Extra
missing_other.description: Hawthorn Extra is the wonderful classic De Laire Aubepine Extra base. Under IFRA regulations the key synthetic material used to create this base (anisaldehyde) was heavily restricted. Under IFRA 51 that restriction has been considerably relaxed and consequently it is now possible, once again, to exploit this magnificent floral scent (up to 4.4% of your finished product). Having use of Hawthorn Extra allows perfumers to add an interesting colour and nuance to perfumes that have been all but forced to rely on muguet and lilac florals due to regulations and prohibitions. We are thrilled to put this base back in the spotlight where it belongs. The scent of hawthorn (also known as May flower) shares much in common with lilac but with a distinctly anisic / almond quality. In May, a profusion of hawthorn blossoms soak the air with their gourmand aroma. Hawthorn Extra allows you to recreate that magical moment of nature in your perfumes. “Ne'er cast a cloot til Mey's oot!”

missing_other.title: Hay “Signature” Absolute
missing_other.description: Hay absolute, otherwise known as foin or foin coupé (literally meaning "cut hay") is one of the most beautiful of all the absolutes. Critic Chandler Burr said: " One of the most sublime of all perfume materials. Hay is, as literally as possible, the smell of liquid summer sunlight." Combined with our stunning classic Foin Coupé base and a fond of green oakmoss and lavender "Avice Hill" , you have the tools for truly remarkable fragrances. In addition to the expected coumarin notes, this absolute from the high French Alps is fruity, tobacco like, sweet and radiant. In traces it imparts a special je ne sais quoi , and in larger amounts it can become the star of the show. Steffan Arctander had this to say: " Hay absolute is used in perfumery not only in “new mown hay” bases, or in combination with flouve, melilotus, tonka, woodruff, deertongue, etc., but also as an individual note to be introduced whenever a truly herbaceous-sweet undertone is required: in lavender, fougere, chypre, colognes, tea-notes, tabac-notes, forest notes and various bouquets." Because hay absolute is so thick, we now optionally supply it at 10% dilution in Triethyl Citrate Natural making it ISO 9235 compliant. This product will replace our previous hay sold at 50% dilution. If you are seeking a similar product with a different profile, we also offer Flouve “Signature” Absolute (an IG Pays de Grasse product ). Origin: France, High Alps Part: Dried leaves Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Hay “Super Premium” Absolute
missing_other.description: An extraordinary evolution of hay absolute, this Super Premium edition captures the very essence of golden fields at their peak ripeness. Where our V. MANE Fils Signature Hay Absolute evokes liquid summer sunlight, this LMR produced gold hay transcends into pure solar opulence - a more intensely coumarinic experience that borders on the divine. This exceptional absolute from select parcels in the high French Alps presents an amplified gourmand character that sets it apart. The coumarin heart pulses with unprecedented richness, revealing layers of caramelised honey, vanilla-touched tobacco leaf, and sun-warmed tonka bean . The familiar fruity radiance of hay is here transformed into something more indulgent - think dried figs and golden raisins nestled in fresh-cut grass. The gourmand facets make this absolute particularly suited for: Oriental compositions seeking herbaceous depth Modern fougères requiring extra warmth and sweetness Tobacco accords demanding authentic hay-cured richness Gourmand creations needing natural sweetness without sugar molecules Luxury bases where only the most precious materials will suffice You will appreciate how this Super Premium edition bridges the gap between green and amber families with remarkable finesse. Its enhanced coumarinic profile provides exceptional longevity and sillage, whilst maintaining the authentic hay character that makes this material irreplaceable. Like our Signature edition, this absolute is available at 10% dilution in Triethyl Citrate Natural for ISO 9235 compliance, ensuring both ease of use and regulatory peace of mind. For those seeking the full spectrum of our hay collection, we recommend exploring this alongside our Signature Hay Absolute and Flouve "Signature" Absolute (IG Pays de Grasse) to discover the unique character each brings to your palette. When only the most luxurious interpretation of summer's golden harvest will do.

missing_other.title: Hazelnut CO2
missing_other.description: Open the bottle and you smell freshly roasted hazelnuts — warm, creamy, unmistakable. There is praline sweetness, a buttery depth, and the faintest coffee-like warmth underneath. The CO2 extraction captures the full roasted character with remarkable fidelity to the real thing. This is the alcohol-soluble fraction — the fats and waxes stripped away, leaving behind only what carries the scent. It dissolves cleanly in perfumer's alcohol for direct use in fine fragrance. Build praline accords, chocolate-nut compositions, and gourmand bases around it. Pair with tonka bean and vanilla for praline effects, with coffee CO2 for a hazelnut latte accord, or with cocoa absolute for something approaching Nutella in a bottle. We also stock Filbertone — the single molecule that defines hazelnut character — for when you need just a trace.

missing_other.title: Heliotrope Flowers, Natural
missing_other.description: Heliotrope notes are difficult to obtain within natural perfumery as the high cost and potential misuse of the raw materials put them out of reach of most. That's where our 100% natural Heliotrope Flowers base comes in. Built around a heart of the most wonderful natural isolates, including the much sought after natural heliotropin (piperonal), with resins, luxurious and costly floral oils and a sympathetic and truly perfumistic approach to natural bases, Heliotrope Flowers is the only heliotrope product you need. In traces this base adds anisic sweetness, in overdose it is a complete floral bouquet.

missing_other.title: Hinoki Wood Oil
missing_other.description: The scent of Shinto shrines, Buddhist temples and palaces in Japan, Hinoki Wood is a type of cypress with a distinctive top note character with a rounded camphoraceous quality. It is softer than pine and fir oil and has a very lovely smoky and leathery facet. It would be ideal in a forest based scent or a fantasy fresh fragrance and would be very interesting with Dihydromyrcenol as the main part of a modern top note accord. IFRA: Hinoki Wood has no limitations under IFRA however LMR undertakes internal testing and they use that testing when they produce their “IFRA” documents. Consequently while LMR says the limit is 0.02% in this product, that is not the IFRA limit. This is a quirk of LMR. We supply their IFRA document as a matter of reference only. Hinoki wood oil blends with Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 , Apo Patchone Coeur , Royal Leather , Pineapple Supreme , and Oud Intense .

missing_other.title: Ho Wood “Superior” Oil
missing_other.description: While many companies produce Ho Wood oil, it is often from a blend of branches and leaves and is rarely treated as a luxury oil owing to its low cost and abundance. But Payan Bertrand have produced what we would consider the finest of all the suppliers bar none. This oil is so good it is practically on a par with Brazilian Rosewood which is now virtually impossible to obtain due to CITES regulations. This oil can be used in very much the same way as Linalool but it is, of course, 100% natural. This oil forms part of Mandy Aftel's naturals starter kit. Origin: China Part: Wood Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Homage Attar Type Formula
missing_other.description: Homage (in homage to the rose and the 25th anniversary of Amouage) was released in 2008 as a limited edition 12ml luxury attar. This is our reconstruction of the original formula based on a GCMS of the red wooden box release which we are fortunate to have in our perfume vault. While Amouage has a bit of a rocky reputation for quality (especially with some of its newer scents), the Attars are unimpeachable. Homage is a magnificent example of how great this house can be when it puts its mind (and dollars) where its mouth is. This is a complex formula with many luxurious naturals and it is a surprisingly light scent for an attar type. Wear it as is without diluting, or dilute it for more of a European fragrance experience. Top Notes: Taïf Rose, Frankincense, Petitgrain, Lavender, Lemon, Orange Heart Notes: Jasmine, Geranium, Helichrysum, Orange Blossom Base Notes: Cedarwood, Oud, Sandalwood, Patchouli, Guaiacwood Total Lines: 58 Bases: 1 — Rose Taïf

missing_other.title: Honey Provence Firabs
missing_other.description: Honey Provence Firabs opens with the unmistakable aroma of honeycomb freshly broken from the hive—sweet, gooey, and irresistibly appetising. Smooth beeswax depth grounds the sweetness, while subtle chocolate nuances add sophisticated complexity. This is honey done in the modern gourmand style: indulgent and edible without the animalic weight of traditional honey materials. This Firmenich base belongs to their Firabs range—specialties created through co-extraction of natural materials with carefully selected synthetic molecules, including proprietary captives. Firabs products contain the actual named natural ingredient (in this case, beeswax and honey extract), distinguishing them from Firbest bases which recreate scent profiles without the named natural. The co-extraction process captures authentic honeycomb character while synthetic additions enhance intensity and performance. Work with Honey Provence Firabs sparingly—its power demands a light hand. The semi-solid consistency becomes pourable with gentle warming. Blend with florals like rose, orange blossom, and osmanthus, or use in amber, tobacco, and oud compositions where honeyed sweetness adds warmth. Excellent diffusiveness makes it project beautifully in fine fragrances.

missing_other.title: Honey Supreme
missing_other.description: Fraterworks Honey Supreme is the ultimate honey base. It blends a heart of finest French beeswax absolute with radiant modern molecules. Honey Supreme encapsulates the scent of a long-abandoned bee hive bursting with sweet honey that hints of the wild flowers and fields that nourished the golden bees that produced it. Pure Honey Supreme is IFRA safe at doses up to 5% of a finished product, however we recommend working with a 10% dilution due to its incredible power. Honey supreme adds a truly modern note of luxury to fine fragrances and works as a one for one replacer of Firmenich's Honey Signature ( Honey Provence Firabs ). Fraterworks also sells the classic non-discolouring De Laire Miel Blanc base restored in all its Belle Époque glory, and the vegan compatible Mielarome of Chiris featured in masterpieces like La Rose Jacqueminot by Coty.

missing_other.title: Honeysuckle
missing_other.description: Honeysuckle is one of those most beautiful spring floral scents that seems to float on the air and greet you before you even see it. Fraterworks® Honeysuckle 584569 is a thoroughly modern base built around a luscious core of natural oils and absolutes enhanced by scientifically accurate synthetics as found in the headspace of the living flowers in the wild. This is a sweet, elegant and rich floral base that can be used at up to 19% of your finished product. Despite the beauty of the flower's scent, honeysuckle bases are rare and the historic Honeysuckle No 6 and Chevrefeuille 70 of De Laire were long ago discontinued. For the sake of historical interest we will be re-introducing the classic Chevrefeuille 70 in the future.

missing_other.title: Hyacinth Storm
missing_other.description: Hyacinth Storm is so named because it is an effusion of glittering green, floral and aldehydic notes. While we also sell the beautiful classical Jacinthia , Hyacinth Storm is modern, radiant and utterly beguiling. One sniff draws you in and you find yourself going back to the bottle over and over to inhale once again a marvel of perfumery. This base is the only hyacinth you need. It fits readily into any modern perfume or can be used as a luxurious green starting point in overdose for a new masterpiece in the direction of such scents as Oscar (1977) by Oscar de la Renta, Ombré de Hyacinth by Tom Ford (private blend), Malle's Synthetic Jungle (2021), Accento by Xerjoff (2019), or Nasomatto's Narcotic Venus (2007). Pair it with a modern jasmine base like Jasmin Fleurs , Pineapple Supreme and Neobutenone Alpha and you have the start of something wonderful. If you are looking for a Hyacinth absolute replacer, we also have the incredible 100% natural Hyacinth TruAbs ®.

missing_other.title: Hyacinth TruAbs
missing_other.description: It may not exhibit the prettiest smell (though it comes from what could certainly be considered the prettiest bloom), but Hyacinth absolute does exist and has some practical use as a floraliser, complexor and nuancer. However, it is almost impossible to obtain in the 21st century and certainly not consistently enough for use in commercial fragrances. Enter Fraterworks' Hyacinth TruAbs®. This 100% natural blend replicates with astonishing accuracy the genuine absolute and can be used one for one in the same manner. It is deep yellow, thick and incredibly realistic. It is best used at below 1% for adding a je ne sais quoi to fragrances. It's ability to impart naturalness and character to the mostly chemical classic Hyacinth ( Jacinthe ) bases is extraordinary. Like our amazing Rose de Mai and Boronia TruAbs' this base is created scientifically for Fraterworks in Grasse and is so good it is practically impossible to differentiate it from pure and natural (albeit practically non-existant) true hyacinth absolute. Due to the high cost of this replica, we also sell it at 10% dilution in odourless natural triethyl citrate — just make your selection above. We can supply an unlimited quantity of Hyacinth Supreme TruAbs®, just contact us for pricing.

missing_other.title: Hydrocarboresine
missing_other.description: “ Ab illo benedicáris, in cujus honóre cremáberis .” or “May you be blessed by Him, in Whose honour you will be burnt.” This is the blessing said over the incense as it is set alight during Holy Mass. And anyone who has been present at that moment will recognise immediately that most wonderful smoky scent of incense when they first smell Biolande's Hydrocarboresine. Despite the incense connection this is a labdanum product, but through the proprietary pyrogenation technique (the process of overheating or burning) it is transformed into one of the most popular cistus specialities on the market. To create a full blast Three Kings Incense replica, blend Hydrocarboresine with Myrrh Absolute and Robertet's wonderful Olibanol .

missing_other.title: Hyraceum Tincture 10%
missing_other.description: Resembling a rodent but related to elephants, the rock hyrax is a wild animal from Africa that marks its territory with a thick pheremone-laden spray which petrifies over time. It is the rock-like nature of the aged material that leads to its nickname: “hyraceum stone”. The animals that produced the fossilised material we tincture at Fraterworks lived hundreds (and even potentially) thousands of years ago. Hyraceum tincture exudes a wonderfully complex barnyard-like odour crossed with wild honey which immediately transports you to the unspoilt savannahs of Africa. A most interesting and unique animalic, hyraceum blends beautifully with the other classic perfumery animalics .

missing_other.title: Hyraceum “Signature” Absolute
missing_other.description: In 2024 Firmenich announced the discontinuation of their acclaimed Hyraceum Absolute 60% DIPG. In 2025 Fraterworks began manufacturing its replacement in Grasse. We are now the only supplier of this wonderful natural musk absolute. Hyraceum Absolute opens with fierce animalic intensity—phenolic, urinous notes mingle with tarry leather and scorched earth. This fossilised essence captures millennia of African sun and stone. Use it where you need uncompromising animalic depth without ethical compromise. This material transforms on warm skin from challenging rawness to seductive warmth. Build leather accords with unprecedented realism or add subliminal sensuality to florals. Master perfumers reach for Hyraceum when synthetic musks lack soul and natural alternatives prove too tame. Dose carefully—traces add mysterious depth whilst higher amounts create bold animalic statements. Combine with labdanum for rich leather effects or blend into oud reconstructions for authenticity. In chypres, it provides the dark foundation modern regulations have diminished in their restriction on oakmoss. What is Hyraceum? Hyraceum comes from the fossilised urine and faeces of the Rock Hyrax (Procavia capensis), a small mammal native to Africa and the Middle East. These rabbit-sized creatures live in colonies and use communal latrines in protected rock crevices over many generations. The hyrax produces unusually viscous, jelly-like urine that's exceptionally rich in calcium carbonate and other minerals. When deposited repeatedly in the same sheltered spots by entire colonies, this material dries, hardens and petrifies over centuries. Some deposits are over 50,000 years old. Collection involves mining these ancient, fossilised middens - the rock-like masses that have accumulated in caves and crevices. The material is literally chipped away with hammers and chisels, as it's extremely hard and dense. Collectors harvest only from abandoned sites where no living hyrax colonies are present. The ra

missing_other.title: Hyssop Oil
missing_other.description: Hyssop oil opens with a bracing camphoraceous freshness that feels cool and mineral, almost crystalline. As this initial diffusive blast settles, warm spicy-herbaceous notes emerge alongside a distinctive tea-like dryness. The effect recalls sun-baked Mediterranean hillsides studded with wild herbs. This oil excels at bridging fresh top notes to warmer base materials in complex compositions. Pair it with lavender and coumarin in fougères, where it reinforces the herbal architecture while adding vertical lift. Blend with citrus oils for colognes that smell authentically botanical rather than synthetic, or use it with labdanum and patchouli in chypres where its bitterness cuts through sweetness beautifully. Work at trace levels - a little goes a long way. Combine with clary sage to amplify the hay-like facets, or with frankincense where hyssop extends and freshens resinous top notes. Classic masculine fragrances like Hermès Equipage and Caron Yatagan showcase its structural power in aromatic-woody compositions.

missing_other.title: Immortelle Absolute
missing_other.description: Immortelle absolute (also known as Everlasting and more technically as helichrysum) is a wonderful floral absolute that has no equal. It has complex notes of hay, tobacco, caramel, fruit, honey and tonka. Our variety (replacing the previous by MANE) is by LMR and it is part of their "For Life" range. With this update we get a more beautiful and truer scent profile, as well as an easier to use pure absolute as its viscosity, whilst thick, is pourable with just a little warmth. A key component of Sables (1985) by Annick Goutal and L'Heure Bleue (1912) by Jacques Guerlain for Guerlain, this absolute combines beautifully with wood notes (especially Sandalwood ), ionones, orris and violet and suits modern gourmand type fragrances where its sweetness is especially favoured. Blends with Sotolone are interesting. Note: Immortelle absolute is prized for perfumery especially, while the essential oil is preferred by aromatherapists. Immortelle is quite viscous so in addition to pure, we offer it at 50% in natural triethyl citral, an odourless isolate from citrus.

missing_other.title: Irival Oliffac
missing_other.description: Irival Oliffac opens with distinctive fatty-floral richness reminiscent of precious orris butter. Its powdery violet character emerges alongside camphoraceous-woody facets. The initial sharpness softens into sophisticated iris root with subtle gourmand undertones. You'll find this base invaluable when building iris accords without natural orris's prohibitive cost. It excels when combined with ionones where it amplifies violet powder effects whilst adding rooty depth. Use it at 0.5-2% to create the ethereal grey quality found in modern iris fragrances without overwhelming delicate florals. Blend Irival with beta-ionone and methyl ionone for complete violet-iris reconstructions. Combine with woody molecules like Iso E Super to enhance the rooty facets. Pair with aldehydes (especially compatible is Aldehyde C-12 Lauric) where its fatty character adds creamy sophistication to powdery accords.

missing_other.title: Irrozol
missing_other.description: The sophisticated Irrozol base was launched in the early 20th century by Chuit Naef & Cie and very quickly adopted by all of the great perfumer's of the time. It remained in constant demand until the ravages of the late 1990s led to its disappearance. Today it returns in the form of Fraterworks Irrozol in all its complex glory, loaded with iris naturals and synthetics as well as muguet, rose, jasmine, orchid, woods and a particularly lovely ambrette seed note. Use it in overdose as the core of a multiflor fragrance or in smaller quantities to simply add floral interest to the heart of a scent.

missing_other.title: Jabir Type Formula
missing_other.description: Introduced in 2014, Jabir by Kemi Blending Magic—a prestigious line under the Xerjoff umbrella—emerges as a captivating highlight in the brand’s alchemical-inspired portfolio. Crafted by perfumer Chris Maurice, this oriental floral fragrance unfolds with a vibrant opening of freesia, violet, and strawberry, setting a lively yet refined tone. The heart reveals a lush bouquet of rose, peony, and lily-of-the-valley, evoking an enchanting floral elegance, before settling into a rich base of agarwood (oud), musk, vetiver, patchouli, and vanilla—blending woody depth with a sensual, lingering warmth. Kemi Blending Magic, founded by Xerjoff’s Sergio Momo, channels the mystique of alchemy into its creations, and Jabir pays homage to Jabir ibn Hayyan, the legendary ‘father of alchemy.’ Xerjoff’s reputation for opulence shines through here, with a composition that balances intricate floral notes against an oriental-woody foundation, delivering a fragrance that’s both sophisticated and evocative. Top Notes: Freesia, Violet, Strawberry Heart Notes: Rose, Peony, Lily-of-the-Valley Base Notes: Agarwood (Oud), Musk, Vetiver, Patchouli, Vanilla

missing_other.title: Jacinthia Extra
missing_other.description: Jacinthia is a jewel of classical floral perfumery. It was used in the original No 19 for Chanel with traces of Z-11 10 MIP in another base illustrating the wonderful ability of these classical bases to blend with extremely modern synthetics. Use in traces to enrich your scent or in a larger dose for an obvious hyacinth note. This luxurious base is enriched with many high class natural absolutes and oils, including the rare treasure: hyacinth absolute. Jacinthia is wonderful in the classic French trilogy of Muguet, Hyacinth and Lilac. We recommend Lilac A07 and Coroliane for this purpose.

missing_other.title: Jacée Extra
missing_other.description: Centaurée jacée ( centaurea jacea ) is a French meadow flower that has vanished from the perfumers palette in the 21st century. Once a beloved member of the esteemed violet / iris family it so inspired François Coty that in 1905 he released a fragrance named La Jacée based entirely on its delicate scent! Blending beautifully with hawthorn , iris , violet , mimosa and cassie this really is a wonderful flower that should stage a comeback. As with all our classical bases, Jacée Extra is enriched with large doses of the finest floral absolutes and oils. A mere trace adds complexity and luxury while an overdose can form the heart of an innovative perfume. What was old is new again.

missing_other.title: Jasmin 1109
missing_other.description: Copying in the perfume industry is no new thing. Just as every perfume company has their own variant of Aventus these days, the perfumers of the past also made products inspired by their competitors. Jasmin Blanc (231) of Chuit Naef & Cie so inspired master perfumers of Roure Bertrand that they came up with Jasmin 1109, a wonderful jasmine base with nuances of narcissus that would go on to become wildly popular and feature in the some of the greatest fragrances. Bernard Chant took the base with him to IFF where he was the head perfumer and used it liberally and often. Jasmin 1109 was used in Aramis (9% along with 23 natural oils and absolutes!), Calandre, Oscar (1977) for Oscar de la Renta, Miss Dior (16%) and so many more. And now it can be used in your fragrances. Jasmin 1109 in its original form is IFRA compliant and so we present it to you completely unaltered.

missing_other.title: Jasmin Blanc
missing_other.description: Perhaps the most famous jasmine base in history, this is the Fraterworks restoration of Jasmin blanc ( Jasmin 231 ) of Chuit Naef & Cie. Used in such masterpieces as Joy by Jean Patou and First by Van Cleef and Arpels. Luscious sweet jasmine blends with the seductive note of narcissus in this classic base updated for today. Overdose or under dose, it doesn't matter; Jasmin Blanc adds radiance and beauty. This base was later copied by Roure as their Jasmin 1109 and it works perfectly well as a substitute.

missing_other.title: Jasmin Fleurs
missing_other.description: The original Jasmin A490 by Chiris featured in such blockbuster fragrances as La Rose Jacqueminot and Jasmin de Corse by Coty — much loved by the Grand Duchess Olga Romanov. This base is the scent of wild jasmin blossoms floating on a warm breeze across the distance. It is an "absolute" type base but with a delicate softness that makes it far easier to work with at high doses than a true absolute replacer like Jasmin Imperial . Slightly updated from the classic formula to take advantage of the latest radiant jasmine molcules. Usable at a massive 12% of your finished product, this is a perfect jasmin base for modern fragrances to add a touch of classic opulence and class.

missing_other.title: Jasmin Imperial
missing_other.description: Jasmin Imperial is a French jasmine grandiflorum absolute replacer. In the words of M. De Laire, "Jasmin of Grasse is perfect" and if we may be so bold as to add, nothing but the flower itself can surpass the beauty of our Jasmin Imperial base. Richly complex and constructed on the basis of the chemical composition of a particularly fine historic crop of genuine French jasmine absolute, Jasmin Imperial allows perfumers to return to the golden days of overdosing floral absolutes as it can be used at up to 2.5% of your finished product for IFRA 51. This complex and true to life base is enriched with luscious and expensive natural absolutes and oils.

missing_other.title: Jasmin Russe
missing_other.description: A warm spiced classic jasmine base in which Russian coriander takes pride of place to add natural freshness and a novel tone. Jasmin Russe is a beautiful companion to orange blossom and Dianthus notes, but holds its own as a jasmine soliflore. Reminiscent of classical Jasmin Invar , a companion to the more well-known Muguet Invar , Fraterworks Jasmin Russe is a truly special jasmine that you will fall in love with. This is a base so beautiful that it makes you seek a reason to use it. For a base that mimics the scent of jasmine blossoms floating on the air across fields of hay in the summer morning sun, you need look no further.

missing_other.title: Jasmin Épicé
missing_other.description: Jasmin Épicé meaning "spicy jasmine" is one of the earliest Jasmin bases. It was used to great effect in L'Origan by Coty in synergy with the glorious Rose D'Orient base. It was created to utilise the most recently discovered jasmin molecules during perfume's age of discovery (the early 20th century) in conjunction with the finest spice oils. Despite its vintage, Jasmin Épicé is still a truly capable workhorse jasmine base and it blends beautifully with citrus notes (especially bergamot and orange) and spices (including carnation bases such as Dianthus ), making it ideal for oriental types.

missing_other.title: Jasmine Absolute, Egypt
missing_other.description: While India is the largest general supplier of Jasmine Grandiflorum to the world, Egypt also has a roaring trade. Despite being the same species, the three main origins (India, Egypt and France) are very different. Egypt: Light, diaphanous, delicate. India : Rich, almost tuberose-like, intense France : Creamy and unctuous, almost enfleurage-like The Egyptian oil is the most "classic" and lends itself very well to modern fragrances when you need an obviously natural luxurious jasmine note to blend with a lighter minimalistic profile. It can also be used in richer floral blends where its sheer quality can add space and freshness without sacrificing volume. Very small amounts are all that are needed to floralise a fragrance, but as history has shown us (see the demo formulas below), overdoses are also effective and incredibly beautiful. The only limit nowadays is the IFRA restriction of 0.6% of your finished product. With supreme beauty comes high cost and cognisant of that we also offer this incredible absolute diluted to 10% with natural (EU & US) Triethyl Citrate, an odourless diluent derived from citrus. If the cost of the natural oil is too prohibitive, we also sell the finest jasmine grandiflorum replacer on the market: Jasmin Imperial . Origin: Egypt Part: Flowers only

missing_other.title: Jasmine Absolute, France
missing_other.description: Formerly the premiere source of Jasmine, Grasse in France (the epicentre of the perfume industry) has now but one supplier left. Most of the treasured oil from the small French harvest goes to houses like Chanel and Dior who still use it (albeit in traces) in some of their hallowed scents. French Jasmine, despite being of the same type as Indian and Egyptian (Grandiflorum), is absolutely unique in its odour profile. It has a soft delicateness and full bodied naturalness that other jasmine oils, no matter how good, exhibit. This extraction from V. MANE Fils is so unctuous it seems like it is the result of an enfleurage extraction. When smelling the original classic fragrances of Roudnitska and Jean Carles it becomes very obvious that their luscious and rich style was inspired by this oil and its sister: Rose de Mai from Grasse which exhibits a similarly complex and yet demure quality. Pair this sublime Jasmine absolute with Orris Absolute Landes, French Violet Leaves and Rose De Mai from Grasse in our stunning restoration of the classical masterpiece 1000 by Jean Kerleo for Jean Patou (formula below). Origin: Grasse, France Part: Flowers only

missing_other.title: Jasmine Absolute, Select
missing_other.description: Our Jasmine Select is an authentic Indian jasmine grandiflorum absolute - the quintessential white floral that has defined luxury perfumery for over a century - at a price that makes this precious material accessible for regular use. This product delivers the full character of jasmine grandiflorum: its intoxicating floral sweetness, warm honey-like facets, and the distinctive indolic richness that makes jasmine irreplaceable in perfumery. While our signature Floral Concept jasmine offers the classic Indian-style profile found in masterpiece fragrances, and our opulent "gold" MANE jasmine provides an almost tuberose-like intensity, this Fraterworks® jasmine absolute captures the essential beauty of Indian grandiflorum in a form that's practical for daily work. It maintains jasmine's transformative power - its ability to add luminous floralcy in traces or create stunning soliflores when used more generously (within IFRA limits of 0.6%). Available pure and in 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate. Origin: India Part: Flowers Process: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Jasmine Auriculatum Absolute
missing_other.description: Jasmine auriculatum does not smell like the jasmine you know. The first impression is green, grassy, and almost gardenia-like, with a surprising frankincense-like top note and rich balsamic warmth underneath. It is the most herbaceous and least conventionally floral of the three commercial jasmines. Use it to bring green complexity to white floral compositions — it lifts jasmine accords out of the familiar and into the exotic. It pairs beautifully with tuberose, ylang ylang, and frankincense. A few drops add tropical depth and waxy richness to any floral heart. Three jasmines, three entirely different flowers. Grandiflorum is the classic — clean, fruity, universally floral — while sambac is headier, more indolic, with orange blossom facets and narcotic richness. Auriculatum stands apart from both: greener, more gardenia-like, with a frankincense-balsamic dimension neither of the others possess.

missing_other.title: Jasmine DEC Abs MD, India
missing_other.description: Jasmine DEC Abs MD opens with intensely sweet, narcotic white floral character—immediately recognisable as true jasmine. Rich fruity-banana facets emerge alongside the heady floral notes, while warm indolic undertones provide the carnal, sensual depth that defines this material. A herbaceous-tea quality and subtle clove-like spiciness add complexity that synthetic jasmine bases cannot replicate. This decolourised absolute from LMR (Laboratoire Monique Rémy, now part of IFF) represents the pinnacle of jasmine extraction technology. The "DEC" indicates decolourisation via molecular distillation—a technique pioneered by Monique Rémy herself to remove colour while preserving the full olfactory profile. The "MD" confirms molecular distillation processing. This yields a pale, workable material rather than the typical dark reddish-brown of standard jasmine absolute, making it invaluable for light-coloured formulations without sacrificing any aromatic richness. Indian jasmine (Jasminum grandiflorum) from Tamil Nadu delivers exceptional quality—richer and denser than Egyptian material with pronounced musky-coumarin undertones. Eight million hand-picked flowers yield just one kilogram of absolute, explaining both its cost and its irreplaceable value. The substantivity ensures your jasmine heart persists beautifully into the drydown. Blend with rose, ylang-ylang, tuberose, and sandalwood for classic floral orientals. If the cost of the natural oil is too prohibitive, we also sell the finest jasmine grandiflorum replacer on the market: Jasmin Imperial . We also stock French Jasmine absolute from Grasse, Jasmine Sambac Absolute , Egyptian Jasmine Absolute , and, as mentioned above, we also have Indian Jasmine Absolute from MANE, and Floral Concept's classic signature Indian Absolute . Origin: India Part: Flowers only

missing_other.title: Jasmine Enfleurage Tincture 2%
missing_other.description: This product is now out of stock. It was a once-off product which will not be returning. In the early days of the golden age of perfume (late 19th century to mid 20th century) jasmine oil was extracted by the only means known: enfleurage from animal fat pomade. This involves the repeated laying of thousands of single jasmine blossoms on a bed of highly purified and odourless fat. As the old flowers lost their scent, the fat (or pomade as it is known) was recharged with fresh flowers. Most modern producers of enfleurage products now use palm or other vegetable oils, but in 2015 in collaboration with a producer of traditional enfleurage products, we commissioned a large quantity of classical jasmine enfleurage oil, known in French as “extrait (de pommade aux fleurs), № 36, de jasmin ”, produced using the ancient method of extraction via animal fats. We are very excited to be the only company offering this truly remarkable piece of fragrance history for sale. Our 2% tincture of that Jasmine extract is a work of perfume art. It is like no other jasmine product on the market, bearing many more of the natural facets of genuine jasmine flowers than any other extraction method. There is a magical quality to this product which is not apparent in plant oil based enfleurage. The alcohol we use in all of our tinctures is purest food grade ethanol produced in New Zealand by a small batch distillery in the foothills of the glacier covered Southern Alps. The flowers used to create this product are organically farmed and are from the Jasminum officinale variety. If you use this product — or any extrait (de pommade aux fleurs) — it is essential to chill and filter your finished product to ensure that no excess fats remain to cloud your fragrance. French Name: Infusion d'extrait (de pommade aux fleurs) de Jasmin. WARNING : this jasmine tincture may contain traces of lard remaining from the extraction process. We keep this tincture apart from our other offerings and we fill orders con

missing_other.title: Jasmine Grand “Enfleurage” CO2
missing_other.description: Jasmine Grandiflorum E-Pure Jungle Essence opens with the unmistakable scent of jasmine petals still dewy from morning mist. This revolutionary extract captures the living flower's ephemeral beauty through MANE's proprietary low-temperature extraction technology. The characteristic indolic richness remains present but softened, allowing delicate fruity nuances and green freshness to shine through. This is the most refined and true to life jasmine extract you'll find. Jasmine E-Pure Jungle Essence from V. MANE Fils uses MANE's special CO2 extraction process (called Pure Jungle Essence) but with a twist: the starter material (jasmine flowers) is first extracted by modern enfleurage techniques using vegetable oils rather than animal fat as in times past. And so we have E-Pure Jungle Essence, rather than just regular Pure Jungle Essence. Until now a MANE captive, this treasure is sublime in the extreme and one of the surest ways to get a rare natural into your fragrant creations. Due to the high price and the hot demand, we offer this in its pure form (supplied by MANE as a 10% ethanol solution) but also in a 10% solution (so 1% pure jasmine extract) with naturally isolated triethyl citrate, our preferred odourless diluent which allows natural perfumers to have access to this precious material at reasonable rates whilst retaining their fragrances' "all natural" designation. Use this extract when traditional jasmine absolute feels too heavy or animalic for modern compositions. Its reduced fatty notes and enhanced petal transparency make it perfect for sheer florals and contemporary clean fragrances. Layer it with citrus top notes without the muddying effect of traditional absolutes, or use it to brighten heavier oriental bases. This is Jasmine Grandiflorum E-Pure Jungle Essence. We also stock Jasmine Sambac E-Pure Jungle Essence and Green Jasmine E-Pure Jungle Essence.

missing_other.title: Jasmine Green “Enfleurage” CO2
missing_other.description: Jasmine Green E-Pure Jungle Essence from MANE has all the beauty of enfleurage extracted jasmine flowers but with a decidedly green and earthy quality. Additionally the special process by which it is made brings cinnamic and spicy notes to the fore that might otherwise be missed in a jasmine extract. Combine this with Jasmine “ Grand ” E-Pure Jungle Essence for a truly complete jasmine note (a note you can't really obtain with regular solvent extraction of the flowers). Or use it with Jasmine Sambac E-Pure Jungle Essence to temper its sweetness and add natural depth. Modern Enfleurage Until recently a captive, E-Pure Jungle Essence from V. MANE Fils uses a non-destructive CO2 extraction process but with a twist: the starter material (usually floral matter) is first extracted by enfleurage using vegetable oils rather than animal fat as in times past. And so we have E-Pure Jungle Essence, rather than just regular Pure Jungle Essence. This process is extremely time consuming and costly and so MANE offer it in a 10% ethanol solution only. Due to the high price and the hot demand, we offer this in its original 10% form but also in a further 10% solution with naturally isolated triethyl citrate, our preferred odourless diluent which allows natural perfumers to have access to this precious material at reasonable rates whilst retaining their fragrances' "all natural" designation. This is Jasmine Green E-Pure Jungle Essence. We also stock Jasmine Sambac E-Pure Jungle Essence and Jasmine Grandiflorum E-Pure Jungle Essence.

missing_other.title: Jasmine Petals
missing_other.description: Jasmin Petals is one of the nicest classic De Laire jasmine bases. Characteristic of its time, it is build around an overload of the known synthetics of the time, particularly benzyl acetate and is very powerful. Henri Robert used it in Chanel No 19 (1970) and it also features in the Guerlain men's chypre Derby (1985). Demo formulas of both are below. Use it alone where you might normally use Benzyl Acetate for a more complex and beautiful jasmine note, or in combination with natural jasmine absolute or other jasmine bases for your own special accord.

missing_other.title: Jasmine Sambac “Enfleurage” CO2
missing_other.description: Jasmine Sambac E-Pure Jungle Essence from MANE is one of the most extraordinary jasmine extracts I have experienced. missing_other.title: Jasmine Sambac “Signature” Absolute
missing_other.description: From Floral Concept comes the most spectacular Jasmine Sambac you will ever experience. With the richest and most beautifully indolic dry down, this oil is the very same one used by Olivier Polge in Chanel's Gabrielle (2017) — see our "smells-like" formula for this perfume below. Jasmine Sambac has a much greener character than the Grandiflorum type (French, Indian and Egyptian) and immediately recalls the lovely scent of Chinese tea. Also, due to the chemical composition of extracts of Jasmine Sambac this product can be used at a much higher 4.1% of your finished fragrance, so really only price limits its high use.

missing_other.title: Jasmine Sample Kit
missing_other.description: This deluxe sample kit gives you a broad overview of our most beloved jasmine bases, naturals and aroma chemicals. missing_other.title: Jasmine “Gold” Absolute, India
missing_other.description: Jasmine grandiflorum absolute is a luxurious oil that has been the trademark of fine fragrances (particularly the French type) for more than 100 years. This Indian absolute from MANE is rich, long lasting, and powerful. It is unquestionably the richest Indian jasmine on the market. It is, in fact, so opulent it presents with almost the same power as Tuberose absolute. That is the reason we call it our "Gold" type. With supreme beauty comes high cost and cognisant of that we also offer this incredible absolute diluted to 10% with natural (EU & US) Triethyl Citrate, an odourless diluent derived from citrus. This is what you will find in the masterpiece perfumes of companies like Dior, Chanel, Tom Ford and Amouage, while the MANE product suits luxury niche brands and artisanal products.
