missing_other.title: Jasmophore® 184195
missing_other.description: Jasmophore, famed for its use in the original Joy formula, opens with a wall of dense, heady jasmine that immediately conjures the richness of natural grandiflorum absolute. The character is profoundly indolic with a slightly rubbery, lactonic warmth that sits between salicylate freshness and animalic depth. It smells unashamedly vintage — full-bodied, opaque, and intensely diffusive. This is a jasmine base engineered for classical composition styles: aldehydic florals, opulent chypres, and grand floral bouquets built with rose, civet, and amber. The thiophenes and furans within the formula provide a naturalistic complexity that single jasmine molecules cannot achieve alone. Pair it with aldehydes, galbanum, and musk to build a convincing 1930s floral structure, or blend with rose absolute and sandalwood for a lush white floral heart. Use Jasmophore sparingly — its projection and opacity can dominate a composition quickly. Temper the indolic character by layering with lighter jasmine molecules like Hedione or methyl jasmonate. It rewards patience: the drydown softens into a creamy, animalic warmth that lingers for hours on skin and fabric.

missing_other.title: Jonquil Extra
missing_other.description: Jonquils are members of the narcissus family. They have multiple blooms on each dark green stalk and they are a uniformly deep gold in colour. Their scent is sweetly cinnamic and rich with nuances of orange blossom. Fraterworks Jonquil Extra (formerly just "Jonquil") is enriched with genuine jonquil absolute and its presence in a blend can be felt at very low quantities. This is the same jonquil type used at 2% in Je Reviens by Worth and also used by Coty in his great Jasmin de Corse (see demo formula below).

missing_other.title: Jonquille Absolute, France
missing_other.description: Jonquil and Narcissus are variants of the same plant family (Narcissus). Visually the jonquil is all yellow (sometimes with a darker orange corona) while narcissus flowers have a golden corona surrounded by white petals. Olfactorily, the Jonquil is warm, honeyed, fruity and floral while the narcissus is green, leathery and indolic with a vaguely animalic facet. These extracts are beautiful materials, and some perfumers blend them together for a layered floral complexity but there are also distinct uses for each so we highly recommend including both in your palette. This Jonquil absolute is the finest on the market today. It is produced by LMR and comes from freshly gathered blossoms from the French countryside. Due to cost and power, we offer this pure and diluted to 10% in natural TEC with a touch of natural benzyl benzoate as a co-diluent to ensure complete solubility. We also offer the very cost effective classical base Jonquil Extra (as seen in Coty's Jasmin de Corse , and Je Reviens by Worth). Origin: France Part: Flowers only Process: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Juniper Berry Oil, Rectified
missing_other.description: This wonderfully fresh and fizzy rectified Juniper Berry oil is a signature speciality of LMR. With no off notes at all, this should be every perfumer's go-to Juniper oil. Juniper features at 1.5% in The Dreamer byVersace, Aventus by Creed, Light Blue Pour Homme (2007) by Dolce & Gabbana, and Chanel's Sycomore (2016). Juniper blends beautifully with Frankincense Oil , Armoise Oil , Ginger Oil and bases such as Pineapple Supreme and Permawood ®. Origin: Balkan Peninsula, Italy Part: Berries Process: Steam distillation and rectification

missing_other.title: Karo Karounde TruAbs
missing_other.description: Karo karounde is one of perfumery's lost treasures. The original absolute came from the flowers of Leptactina senegambica, a wild shrub from the Fouta Djalon mountains of Guinea — related to gardenia and coffee. Early European botanists mistook it for a new species of jasmine. Production has effectively ceased: fewer than 50 kilos a year were ever made, and regulatory pressures have shut down the African extraction operations entirely. The smell is extraordinary — intensely floral and narcotic, with the richness of gardenia, the sweetness of jasmine, and the waxy warmth of orange blossom, all layered over an unexpected chocolate-orange depth and faint bitter almond undertone. It appeared in Cartier Panthère , Estée Lauder Pleasures , and Bertrand Duchaufour's Timbuktu , where it anchored the exotic floral heart. In West Africa, the flowers have been used for centuries to perfume hair, linen, and baths. This TruAbs® base is a 100% natural reconstruction — no synthetics — built to deliver the same olfactory profile now that the genuine absolute is unobtainable. Use it in tuberose and gardenia accords, heavy oriental florals, or anywhere you want narcotic white-flower richness with depth. It pairs beautifully with ylang-ylang, jasmine, orange flower absolute, styrax, and isoeugenol. Available pure and at 10% in natural TEC for easier blending. A little goes a very long way. Image (c) Eric Gren – some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)

missing_other.title: Katafray “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: Absolutely underrated and absolutely beautiful, Katafray Bark Oil is the next great men's fragrance just waiting to happen. With a light wood heart and a character that seems to float between a lighter gentler cascarilla bark and buddhawood, this is almost the perfect canvas for something novel and unique. Blends wonderfully with Geosmin 1% , Cascarilla Oil , Mulacro Oil , Thujopsene ex Cedarwood , and Fleur de Cuir as well as Animalia™ CMP and Ambergris Intense . Origin: Madagascar Variety: Cedrelopsis grevei Part: Tree bark Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Kewda Attar
missing_other.description: _*]:min-w-0 gap-3"> kewda — also spelled kewra — comes from the male flowers of the screwpine (Pandanus), a spiky coastal plant that grows along the Bay of Bengal. The flowers are picked at dawn and distilled into sandalwood oil over twelve to fifteen days, each day's batch of fresh flowers adding more depth. The Mughal emperor Babur described the scent as "moist musk" — an apt description of something humid, radiant, and honeyed. The first impression is almost overwhelming: sharp, penetrating, intensely sweet. Let it settle and a luminous honeyed-hyacinth character emerges, greener and brighter than any European floral you have worked with. There is something of wind and salt in it — a solar, coastal quality that reflects where the plant grows. It opens like a top note but persists like a heart, and can cut through heavy bases with ease. Use kewra attar as a floral heart in orientals, or to sweeten woody bases with green-honeyed radiance. It pairs beautifully with rose, cardamom, saffron, and sandalwood. Keep doses restrained — kewra has extraordinary projection and easily dominates a composition. Best appreciated well diluted, where its complexity unfolds. The screwpine (Pandanus odoratissimus) is a dioecious plant — male and female flowers grow on separate plants. Only the male flower spikes are used for kewra attar; the female produces a segmented pineapple-like fruit with no fragrance value. You may already know the pandanus plant from Southeast Asian cooking, where the leaves are used to flavour rice and coconut desserts — but that is a completely different scent profile (green, grassy, vanilla-like) and has nothing to do with the floral attar. Kewra water — the hydrosol by-product of the same distillation — is a staple of Mughal cuisine, used to perfume biryanis, gulab jamun, and ras malai.

missing_other.title: Kyphi Vert
missing_other.description: Kyphi Vert is a co-distillation — vetiver distilled directly onto gurjun balsam, producing aromatic compounds that neither material creates alone. This is not a blend. When two botanicals are distilled together, heat and steam generate new molecules at the interface, yielding a material with qualities impossible to achieve by simply mixing the finished oils. The result here is vetiver taken somewhere it has never been: darker, more resinous, genuinely oud-like. The vetiver is immediately recognisable — earthy, rooty, green — but the gurjun co-distillation introduces a remarkable labdanum-like warmth and a cinnamic nuance reminiscent of methyl cinnamate. This combination pushes the material into territory that recalls Guerlain's Djedi (1927), Jacques Guerlain's legendary vetiver pushed to its smoky, animalic extreme. There is genuine oud-like depth here. This is, effectively, a prêt-à-porter attar. Use it wherever you want vetiver with ritualistic weight. It bridges Western vetiver compositions and Middle Eastern oud traditions without synthetics. Layer it with rose for an instant oriental, or let it stand alone as a base that needs nothing else.

missing_other.description: We are very excited to be able to offer this intense and rich “super premium” labdanum (cistus) absolute, a speciality of Floral Concept in Grasse and certainly the finest we have seen. It is a near-black and extremely viscous extraction and consequently is offered here either pure or at a 50% dilution in odourless Triethyl Citrate (100% natural isolate from citrus). In comparison to labdanum resinoid, this absolute is lighter, more volatile, and has a cleaner floral-balsamic scent that outshines the thicker, earthier resinoid. This is the labdanum of the golden age of perfumery. You will never need another. Part: Exudate of leaves and flowers Method: Ethanol extraction of concrete.

missing_other.title: Labdanum Light Absolute
missing_other.description: This honey-sweet light labdanum absolute (sometimes referred to as labdanum clear) is a truly sublime cistus material. This light product has a clear and bright tonality and can act to bridge the gap between the deep intense base notes. of standard dark labdanum absolute and resinoid and the dazzling vibrant top notes of cistus essential oil (AKA rock rose). Our light labdanum is a specialty product of our supplier and is simply the most elegant light product on the market. This is a kinder gentler labdanum that is perfect when you want the rich balsamic effects without the intense animalic notes of some absolutes. Origin: Spain (processed in Grasse, France) Variety: Cistus ladaniferus Part: Exudate of leaves and flowers Method: Ethanol extraction of Cistus ladaniferus L.concrete.

missing_other.title: Labdanum Resinoid
missing_other.description: Labdanum resinoid opens with a dark, honeyed sweetness layered over balsamic warmth. An unmistakable ambergris-like richness defines its heart. Beneath that, you find dry leather, aged tobacco, and a faintly animalic depth that makes this material utterly captivating. This is the material that built the amber accord. Pair it with vanillin and benzoin for the classic combination, or lean into its leathery side alongside oakmoss and patchouli for sophisticated chypres. It excels as a fixative, anchoring volatile top notes and extending the life of your blend. Use labdanum resinoid to add warmth and body to oriental bases. Try it with bergamot and vetiver for a refined masculine accord. Its dark colour limits use in pale formulations, but that rich resinous character is irreplaceable when you need genuine amber depth. Labdanum resinoid and labdanum absolute both come from the same crude gum harvested from the rockrose shrub, but they differ in extraction and character. The resinoid is extracted with a hydrocarbon solvent, producing a thick, dark, waxy material with full-bodied earthy depth. The absolute is the alcohol-soluble fraction, cleaner and brighter with a more refined sweetness. Use the resinoid when you want raw depth and body in your base. Choose the absolute when your formula needs clarity and elegance.

missing_other.title: Lactone Storm
missing_other.description: With decidedly peachy and apricot nuances, Lactone Storm is a balanced base of classic fruit aroma chemicals and deluxe lactones. Lactone Storm works as an alternative to the more common Undecalactone Gamma (Aldehyde C-14 so called) and imparts a far more modern and interesting character to a scent. This base takes the popular peach fruit note and makes it more diffusive, radiant and long lasting. As well as being used for fruit notes, Lactone Storm blends beautifully with white florals, particularly Florol , Mayol and Cyclomethylene Citronellol. Blend it with Irotyl (Orris Capronate) and Iralia ® for a radiant fruity orris. Lactone Storm is sublime with Gardenia J. Ellis and transforms the marvellous Visa (2007) by Aurélien Guichard for Piguet, the demonstration formula for which can be found below.

missing_other.title: Laurel Noble Oil
missing_other.description: Laurel Noble oil delivers an uncompromisingly fresh, spicy-camphoraceous signature . Its robust, diffusive power is the very backbone of classic aromatic Fougères, lending an iconic, invigorating profile that defines quintessential masculine elegance . Use this material to build the aromatic heart of Fougère and Chypre structures . Combine it with lavender, bergamot, and cedarwood to amplify its signature herbaceous character . Dose below 0.5% for a subtle lift or use at 1-5% for a dominant, bracing effect .

missing_other.title: Lavandin Abrialis Oil
missing_other.description: Lavandin is a cross between high altitude "true" lavender ( Lavandula angustifolia) and low altitude spike lavander ( Lavandula spica ). The resulting oil is a bolder and more complex oil than either of its parents. The most popular forms are Lavandin Grosso, Lavandin Super and Lavandin Abrialis. The Abrialis cultivar was the first to be created in the 1920s and was, for a very long time, the most popular. Due to disease, Abrialis fell into disuse and the stronger (and newer) Lavandin Super became the favoured breed. However, in the 1970s Pierre Grosso created the eponymous Lavandin Grosso which was stronger and more prolific. Nowadays the Grosso type sees more sales and wider use but the Abrialis has a charm all of its own and is more floral than the other two making it particularly well suited to that rare gem: the feminine lavender scent. Lavandin is most often found in gentlemen's perfumes (such as Azzaro and Paco Rabanne ) but can be a wonderful addition to unisex and female scents (as demonstrated by our formula Ravishing which is derived from a GCMS of Musk Ravageur by Frederic Malle). It also works well as a naturaliser in linalool rich bases (some muguet types for example). We also have a lovely New Zealand grown Lavandin Grosso Oil and Lavandin Super (which, like this Abrialis oil, is also from France). Origin: France Variety: Lavandula hybrida Reverchon Part: Flowers

missing_other.title: Lavandin Absolute
missing_other.description: Lavandin (a cross between spike and regular Lavander) should not be passed over for its more dignified and popular ancestor Lavender. It may be the rought and tumble little brother but it has a majestic richness all of its own and for those looking for a decidedly present lavender note, this wonderful Lavandin Absolute from Payan Bertrand it just what you need. It has 6% coumarin, doubling that of our decolourised Lavender Absolute (and matching that of our pure Lavender “Signature” Absolute) and it shows. Despite being a Lavandin product, this is sweeter and more hay-like in the drydown but having a more camphoraceous top note. But don't be put off, the camphor is so well balanced that this could easily pass as a lavender absolute or even oil (despite its intense green). Origin: Provence, France Part: Flowers only Method: Solvent extracted

missing_other.title: Lavandin Absolute Enfleurage
missing_other.description: This is not ordinary lavandin absolute. LMR's Enfleurage 2.0 process uses a fully organic, bio-sourced solvent at low temperature — no hexane, no petrochemicals — to capture lavandin's fragrance with extraordinary fidelity. The result opens with fruity pear notes and fresh herbs, develops into a rich coumarinic hay-like heart, and dries down warm and tea-like. This has become my personal favourite lavandin. The elegance of this luscious absolute cannot be overstated. Standard lavandin oil is camphoraceous and short-lived. Conventional lavandin absolute is richer but carries faint solvent traces. This enfleurage version preserves delicate top notes that both methods lose, giving you the most complete, most luminous lavandin extract available. The coumarin content provides natural fixation and a rounded, long-lasting sweetness. Pair it with bergamot and oakmoss for refined fougère construction, with clary sage and tonka for warm herbaceous depth, or with patchouli and labdanum for a dark aromatic base. It works beautifully in colognes, where its fresh-fruity opening and hay-sweet drydown create something that smells simultaneously classic and modern.

missing_other.title: Lavandin Grosso Oil
missing_other.description: Lavandin Grosso opens with fresh herbaceous-floral character—clean, camphoraceous, and immediately evocative of lavender fields in Provence from which our oil hails. The sweet floral heart develops quickly, while woody undertones add depth without heaviness. The linear quality that some consider a limitation is actually a strength: predictable, consistent, and exceptionally versatile. Lavandin is a cross between high altitude "true" lavender ( Lavandula angustifolia) and low altitude spike lavander ( Lavandula spica ). The resulting oil is a bolder and more complex oil than either of its parents. An excellent blender for l abdanum ( essential oil , resinoid and absolute ), Oakmoss , Vetiver and its by-products , Patchouli , Douglas fir needle , Coumarin , Clary sage , chypres and fougeres.

missing_other.title: Lavandin Heart
missing_other.description: Lavandin Heart smells like lavandin with its best face forward: clean, fresh and floral, with a soft herbaceous body. The harsh, camphor-like sharpness of ordinary lavandin is gone. In its place sits a warm, hay-like, almost gourmand sweetness that reads close to fine lavender. Use it as a cleaner, rounder lavender at the top and heart of fougères and colognes, where it lifts without the medicinal bite. Its gentle sweetness sits beautifully with coumarin and tonka, and it bridges into gourmand territory. Bergamot, oakmoss and clary sage all sharpen and extend it.

missing_other.title: Lavandin Super Oil
missing_other.description: When the original Lavandin (Abrialis) began to vanish due to disease, a new cultivar arose. That cultivar was a super hero in the commercial lavender and lavandin market as it saved the day. Appropriately named Lavandin Super Oil remained the most common oil until the 1970s when a stronger and larger variety called Lavandin Grosso began to replace it. Lavandin is a cross between high altitude "true" lavender ( Lavandula angustifolia) and low altitude spike lavander ( Lavandula spica ). The resulting oil is a bolder and more complex oil than either of its parents. We also have a lovely New Zealand grown Lavandin Grosso Oil and an intense classical Lavandin Abrialis oil . Origin: France Variety: Lavandula hybrida Reverchon Part: Flowers

missing_other.title: Lavender Absolute, Decolourised
missing_other.description: From Payan Bertrand, one of the leading producers of luxury essential oils in Grasse, comes a truly beautiful lavender absolute which is, for all intents and purposes, colourless. While lavender absolutes are usually intensely green, this product maintains a classical lavender scent without the risk of staining your fragrance. With 3% coumarin (around half the amount in our full-colour Lavender “Signature” Absolute ) this French lavender extract has a lovely balanced hay note in the dry down and a tempered top note, this is a must-have for modern perfumers. Origin: Provence, France Part: Flowers only Method: Solvent extracted and molecular distilled

missing_other.title: Lavender Diva Oil
missing_other.description: Lavender Diva opens with remarkably clean, precise floralcy that immediately distinguishes it from standard lavender oils. This sophisticated cultivar delivers pure lavender sweetness without the mushroom-earth secondary notes that mark traditional varieties. The exceptional 50-55% linalyl acetate content creates green-citrus facets with subtle mint-caraway nuances, while lower linalool levels provide fresher, sweeter floral attributes without sharp herbaceous edges. You'll find Lavender Diva invaluable for modern compositions requiring lavender's signature without rustic character. Use at 1-10% where its linear, soft profile won't overwhelm delicate florals. The material's 1.2% borneol content adds subtle camphoraceous-pine undertones that enhance rather than dominate. Its beautiful warm amber drydown distinguishes it from the dusty-earthy finish of standard lavenders, maintaining floral elegance throughout wear. The cultivar excels in fine fragrance applications where traditional lavender reads too agricultural or medicinal. Combine with bergamot for sophisticated colognes, coumarin for modern fougères, or rose absolutes for refined floral bouquets. Its cleaner profile makes it perfect for contemporary interpretations of classic aromatic structures without vintage heaviness. Difference from Other Lavenders Traditional French lavender (25-45% linalyl acetate, 25-38% linalool) provides the classic aromatic profile but often carries earthy-mushroom undertones and dusty drydown. Lavender Diva's higher linalyl acetate (50-55%) and lower linalool create cleaner, more linear sweetness. Lavender Avice Hill , Fraterworks' New Zealand speciality, represents the pinnacle of lavender refinement - grown on glacial water, distilled within one hour of harvest, maintaining superb floral character where others turn dusty. While Diva offers clean precision through selective breeding, Avice Hill achieves transcendent quality through terroir and processing, rivalling the near-mythica

missing_other.title: Lavender Oil “Avice Hill”
missing_other.description: Lavender “Avice Hill” NZ ALPS P&N is an incredibly fine lavender angustifolia variety grown in New Zealand at the foothills of the rugged and wild Southern Alps (pictured), located in the South Island. The lavender plants are raised on glacial water which takes thirteen years to travel down the alpine slopes in the form of purified ice. Because every second counts when working with cut lavender, our partner farm distills the oil-rich flowers in under one hour of harvesting. No other producer boasts this speed and the resulting oil is one of the best in the world. In comparative testing against the finest lavenders from the fragrance industry, this oil comes first every time. When other lavenders dry to a dusty or earthy note, our Lavender “Avice Hill” maintains is superb floral character with a sweetness and intensity not found in any other variety. The near-mythical lavender Barreme is the oils that would have been the closest match to the sublime scent, longevity and elegance of this pure New Zealand essential oil. Tragically true lavender Barreme is now extinct due to French growers adopting genetically modified varieties to replace the old wild lavender fields due to higher yields of oil - an oil inferior in quality. L avender “Avice Hill” is astonishingly high in linalyl acetate content giving it a more elegant and refined floralcy than most. This is the mark of true quality in lavender. Our partner farm neither spikes nor blends across harvests to meet commercialised standards. With Lavender “Avice Hill”, What you get is what nature gives … and nothing more.

missing_other.title: Lavender Oil, Balkans
missing_other.description: Balkan lavender oil opens with balanced floral sweetness where linalool's fresh character meets linalyl acetate's fruity depth. Grown in Vojvodina's semi-dry Mediterranean climate, it presents gentle herbaceous notes without excessive camphor. The higher sesquiterpene content adds subtle woody complexity distinguishing it from other origins. You'll find this oil valuable for creating authentic lavender accords with distinctive character. It excels where balanced composition matters, with 24-40% linalool and 7-32% linalyl acetate providing versatility across applications. Use it in aromatic compositions where its moderate pricing and consistent quality offer excellent value without compromising sophistication. Blend Balkan lavender with bergamot for fresh cologne structures or combine with rosemary for herbaceous depth. Pair with eucalyptus where its balanced character prevents medicinal dominance. This oil performs beautifully in both fine perfumery and functional fragrances. Lavender Variety Comparison Provence Lavender “Signature” Oil delivers supreme refinement with highest linalyl acetate (40-45%) and minimal camphor. Avice Hill excels with 40-50% esters creating refined fruity-floral sweetness with candy undertones. Diva presents sweeter, less herbaceous character ideal for softer applications. Lavandin oils offer intense herbaceous aromas with 6-12% camphor at lowest cost for functional perfumery.

missing_other.title: Lavender Oil, English
missing_other.description: Grown on a single estate in the Hampshire chalk downs, this oil is a quintessential expression of the English landscape. Unlike the sweet, "jammy" profiles typical of Provencal harvests, this variety is defined by a crisp, silver character. It offers an austere, herbal profile that prioritises clarity over balsamic weight, making it the definitive choice for those seeking a traditional, dry lavender. The olfactory profile is remarkably bright, leaning into a medicinal clarity that provides immediate impact in the top notes. It possesses a refined camphorous edge that lends a soapy, starched-linen freshness to formulations. This lack of heavy sweetness allows the oil to remain transparent and bracing, maintaining its integrity even when used in high concentrations. For the perfumer, our English lavender provides a vertical, piercing light that is indispensable for recreating 19th-century-style colognes and British lavender waters. It is a functional and aesthetic staple, offering a hygienic purity that anchors a composition in the noble tradition of English horticulture. It is a rigorous, honest botanical. In contrast, our Signature French Lavender (LMR Provence) represents the height of Provencal luxury, leaning away from herbal austerity and into a profound floral sweetness. While the English variety provides a bracing, vertical top note, this French oil offers a tenacious, "golden" warmth that acts as a link to the heart for fine fragrance.

missing_other.title: Lavender “Signature” Absolute
missing_other.description: It is almost impossible to put into words how truly incredible this Lavender “Signature” Absolute is. This is so rich it is a solid mass, not a liquid. There is not a single bad note here, just 100% pure lavender. This is so universally loved by our staff that we keep a small container in the laboratory so we can have the pleasure of smelling it through the day. We have tested many lavender absolutes from all the top French houses and this is not just better than everything we sampled - this is better than anything we ever imagined possible with a lavender product. A single sniff transports you to the middle of Provence where the scent of lavender soaks the air. This absolute is rich with notes of dried fruits, tonka beans and herbs. There does not exist under the sun a more profoundly beautiful expression of French lavender. Pair this with Lavender “Avice Hill” (nourished by the glacial waters of the Southern Alps), our exquisite small batch Lavandin, Grosso Oil , and the classic De Laire Foin Coupé base for a truly sublime fougère. NOTE: this absolute is extremely thick (to a point of being nearly solid) but can be added directly to your fragrance compound as-is. To bring it to melt point a fairly significant amount of heat is required. For that reason we offer it at 50% dilution in a blend of 50% triethyl citrate. This creates a viscous but pourable solution making it far easier to work with than pure. We also stock a beautiful practically colourless lavender absolute . Origin: Provence, France Part: Flowers only Method: Solvent extracted

missing_other.title: Lavender “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: Renowned through the centuries and found in so many masterpieces of fragrance history, Provence Lavender is truly the Crème de la Crème, and LMR is the finest producer and supplier today. In the 1960s the Provençal wild high altitude lavender supply began to dry up and so farming became the norm. Lavandula angustifolia Mill. was the variety of choice and all major regional suppliers took stakes in various farms to maintain their own special quality of oil. Over the course of many months we have gathered lavender samples from all of our suppliers (MANE, LMR, Payan Bertrand, Floral Concept, Biolandes and Robertet). We have tested them in every way possible, from the sniffing of mouillettes to including them in various demonstration formulas. Each oil has its own character but ultimately one stood out as the true reference for French lavender oil; that oil was the COSMOS certified Lavender Oil Provence from LMR (Laboratoire Monique Remy, part of IFF). It is so good we call it our signature lavender. Lavender “Signature” Oil opens with the most classical lavender scent - it is the epitome of fine French lavender and it's superior quality was demonstrated time and again through trials. This lavender has a diffusion that far surpasses all others and a stable drydown that never seems to reach an earthy conclusion; its sweetness and floralcy just go on forever. Lavender “Signature” Oil is a masterpiece of meticulous farming and skilful distillation. For a lavender extravaganza pair this oil with our impossibly beautiful Lavender Absolute from V. MANE Fils. Origin: Provence Part: Flowers and stems

missing_other.title: Leather Oud
missing_other.description: Leather Oud is a synthetic base created around a captive molecule found in natural oud. This material is a beast - extremely strong and doesn't smell good at all until you dilute it considerably. The material delivers primarily a leather accord with a nice oud bed, ranging from saddle leather to biker jacket profiles. You should deploy Leather Oud 293316 with pre-dilution to 10% or 1% solutions due to its overwhelming neat potency. This specialty base transforms dramatically upon dilution, revealing sophisticated leather-oud character impossible to achieve from individual components. Use at 0.1-2% in final compositions depending on desired intensity - even trace amounts provide profound impact. Combine Leather Oud 293316 with Rose Imperiale for the signature leather-rose-oud triad explicitly recommended by the manufacturer. Veil harsh aspects with sweet woody notes like Mysore sandalwood oil or our acclaimed Vanilla Supreme , or amplify richness with patchouli and labdanum. Enhance with Saffron Attar FW for spicy-metallic brightness whilst maintaining leathery character.

missing_other.title: Lemon Heart
missing_other.description: Standard lemon oil gives you thirty minutes of brilliance and then vanishes. Lemon Heart gives you the same brilliance anchored into the heart of your composition. This is an LMR speciality — a concentrated citrus fraction developed to boost the citrus profile of your formula, enhancing the sparkling zesty character even at very low dosage. LMR describes this as fruity and zesty, very sparkling and mouthwatering. The citral-driven brightness that makes lemon so valuable in eau de colognes, fougères, and fresh florals is preserved and amplified. What is removed is the terpenic bulk that contributes volume without character. Use it in small amounts alongside standard lemon oil for a citrus opening that sustains itself. It transforms hesperidic accords that normally collapse within an hour into structures that carry bright citrus well into the drydown. Pair with Lime Heart and Orange Heart for a complete LMR citrus heart foundation.

missing_other.title: Lemon Oil FCF, Terpeneless
missing_other.description: Terpeneless citrus oils are useful for two reasons: concentrated odour and solubility in alcohol. If you have made fragrances using high amounts of citrus you will know that there can be problems with clouding in the final solution, and so chilling and filtering is absolutely essential to get a perfectly clear perfume. Lemon Oil, Terpeneless solves that by considerably reducing the non-soluble materials (mostly limonene). The end result is a lovely and intense lemon scent that can be used with other citrus oils or blended with the classic top note products like linalool its esters. This lemon oil contains no furocoumarins. Origin: Sicily, Italy Part: Peel Method: Cold pressed at source then molecular distilled

missing_other.title: Lemon Oil Pelatrice, Messina
missing_other.description: Lemon oil Messina is the premiere fine Italian lemon oil with a high citral content (usually three to four percent) giving it a fresher and more powerful character than standard cold pressed lemon oil from other regions. Lemon Oil Messina blends beautifully with other oils within the citrus family, including our incredible Bergamot “Superior” Oil FCF , Cedrat oil, Sweet Orange, Distilled Lime, and Litsea Cubeba, another high citral oil. Also try it with the wonderfully rich Lemon Heart from LMR. Lemon Oil Messina has a synergistic relationship with Fraterworks' Magnificent Mandarin , Lemon Verbena , and Verdantol ™. NOTE: this oil is not furocoumarin free and so it should be counted towards the total furocoumarin content of your finished product.

missing_other.title: Lemon Oil, Washed
missing_other.description: Washed lemon oil has much value in the flavours world but it also has practical uses in perfumery. To wash lemon, the furocoumarin free essential oil (from cold pressing) is washed with food grade solvents (usually alcohol) to remove certain terpene fractions. The result is softer, sweeter and less toppy. Origin: Sicily, Italy Part: Peel Method: Cold pressed at source and post-processed

missing_other.title: Lemon Tetrarome®
missing_other.description: You will never find a more gourmand lemon oil as Lemon Tetrarome® from Firmenich. First developed in the 1950s, the Tetrarome range featured highly concentrated citrus oils with low terpenes (meaning low-volatility) that express their edible side in a far greater way than comparative terpeneless oils. They are particularly sweet and candy-like. Owing to its very common use in flavours (especially sweets), a sniff of Lemon Tetrarome immediately conjures up images of hard candy, citrus-based power drinks, lemonade and lemonade ice blocks. Lemon Tetrarome blends elegantly with fresh citrus essential oils, offering incredible long-lasting effects and pure performance. “All is in the citrus peel! Tetrarome® are like pure magic zesty concentrates. They give the impression we crunch the entire fruit and bring to composition an incredible long lastingness.” Loic Bisceglie, Firmenich Perfumer Pair this with Bergamot and Cedrat oils from CAPUA 1880, Maltol Isobutyrate for caramellic sweetness and a splash of aldehydes for fizz and you have the beginnings of a superb gourmand scent.

missing_other.title: Lemon Verbena
missing_other.description: Lemon verbena is an incredibly beautiful essential oil which is now completely prohibited from perfume use. It was a key to the olfactory style of numerous perfumes including Chanel's Pour Monsieur and the classic YSL Pour Homme . Fraterworks® Verbena is an incredibly true-to-life replica of lemon verbena oil that is absolutely safe for use in fragrances at up to 4% of the finished product for IFRA compliance. It is loaded with natural essential oils and absolutes for a truly natural result. Lemon verbena is sweet, herbal and bursting with lemon freshness.

missing_other.title: Lemon “Superior” Oil, FCF
missing_other.description: First we brought you superior Bergamot Bergaptene Free , now we bring you Capua's beautiful Lemon Furocoumarin free. Regular cold pressed lemon can be used to an IFRA limit of 2% of your finished product, but Lemon “Superior” Oil FCF can be used up to 28%. That is because the dangerous furocoumarins are removed from the oil without harming its beautiful scent. Origin: Calabria, Italy Part: Peel Method: Cold pressed at source

missing_other.title: Liatrix TruAbs
missing_other.description: Liatris flowers have a scent as unique as their appearance. Also known as deer tongue, liatris provides us with liatrix absolute, perhaps the finest of all the coumarin rich plant oils. Liatrix absolute takes the best of hay, vanilla, tobacco and genet and combines them into one: a floral herbaceous almost creamy scent that is the olfactory equivalent of a bright sunny day. Smelling liatrix you simply can't help but smile with sheer pleasure. Use this base when building sophisticated tobacco accords that demand authenticity with fewer regulatory constraints. Its complex profile bridges the gap between gourmand sweetness and masculine hay-leather dryness. Layer it beneath rose and geranium for vintage barbershop fougères, or combine with vanilla and benzoin for opulent oriental bases. Because liatrix absolute is now virtually impossible to obtain, we have produced this marvellous TruAbs, a 100% natural replica that is truly to die for.

missing_other.title: Lilac A07
missing_other.description: Lilac A07 is the original unaltered formula of the same name by Chiris in Grasse. This is our finest Lilac base and if you wish to have only one, this is the one we recommend. It is painstakingly crafted over a period of days in a traditional multi-step process to carefully control all the chemical reactions that take place. The result is tranquility, softness and beauty encapsulated. Chiris (founded in 1768) was a French fragrance house specialising in highest quality essential oils and absolutes and it is from their prestigious school that François Coty emerged after just one year in the early 1900s. But perhaps the most esteemed name connected to the company was Ernest Beaux. Upon fleeing Russia after the communist revolt, Rallet (Beaux's employer) set up shop at Chiris and it was there that he met Madame Chanel. The rest, of course, is history. Chiris made heavy use of the naturals they produced and so their bases tend to be even richer and more expensive than many others. Lilac A07 is no exception to that rule being enriched with luscious French jasmine and rose absolutes. Lilac A07 featured alongside natural jasmine extract and Jasmin Fleurs in Jasmin de Corse (formula below) by Coty where it sets the tone for the whole scent. It was a perfume fit for a princess as it was the favourite of Russian Grand Duchess Tatiana Nikolaevna. Chiris's Lilac A07 was so popular that Givaudan made and sold its own replica which was also an acclaimed base in its own right. That Givaudan base was called Lilas 7 .

missing_other.title: Lilac Supreme
missing_other.description: With the recent news that Heliotropin may be heading for a total ban under the proverbial butcher's knife of the European Union bureaucracy very soon, it seemed timely for us to make available our Lilac Supreme base. Lilac Supreme is a beautiful and complex modern lilac base containing absolutely no heliotropin. That chemical has long been ubiquitous in Lilac bases but modern tastes (and now a potential ban on heliotropin in the EU) seek a less powdery and more transparent floral heart in fragrances. Lilac Supreme is perfect for that use. This base is not just interesting for its lack of heliotropin, but also because it featured in a number of Guerlain perfumes in the late 20th century. It is also extremely well priced. NOTE: We currently sell Heliotropin and Heliotropin Natural and will continue to do so despite any possible ban for EU cosmetics that may come to pass.

missing_other.title: Lilas Blanc
missing_other.description: Lilas Blanc (white lilac) is a delicate classic lilac base suitable for filling out the heart of a floral fragrance or even as the star of a soliflore. With a few minor additions Lilas Blanc can be an entire scent at a time when lilac is coming back into vogue. This base can be used up to 9.6% of the finished product, making it a great alternative to the abundance of muguet centred perfumes. This lilac is particularly soft and enticing and upon first sniff one has an overwhelming feeling of nostalgia. Lilas blanc is simply comforting.

missing_other.title: Lilas Pourpre
missing_other.description: Richer and more intense than our delicate Lilas Blanc , Lilas Pourpre is full bodied and powerful enough to hold its own in a multi-floral fragrance. Natural absolutes and oils add volume. This robust base is of an invar type - it performs consistently from start to finish without dramatic changes as it dries down. Wonderful for a general floraliser.

missing_other.title: Lime Heart
missing_other.description: Heart oils are not ordinary essential oils. They are LMR specialities — highly concentrated citrus fractions developed to boost the citrus profile of your formula, enhancing the zesty and fruity notes even at very low dosage. A trace of Lime Heart does what generous amounts of standard lime oil cannot — it persists. LMR describes this as fruity and zesty with clean, fresh, mouthwatering undertones. The fleeting top notes that vanish from conventional lime within minutes are captured here in concentrated form. What remains is the most intensely lime impression you can put in a bottle — bright, sharp, unmistakable. Use just a hint to extend lime presence from top note well into the heart. Layer it over our Persian Lime Oil FCF for a citrus accord that opens with natural breadth and refuses to fade. Essential in gin-and-tonic accords, mojito constructions, and any bright aquatic or citrus cologne that needs staying power.

missing_other.title: Lime Oil, Distilled
missing_other.description: Lime oil is one of the most (if not THE most) intense citrus oils. It practically explodes out of the bottle and is perceptible in very small amounts. For me it is about the scent of cocktails and VIP parties. It is an oil that, in the youthful slang of today, goes hard. Use it to brighten up a citrus accord, add a sparkle to a masculine or build a stunning key lime pie gourmand scent around its zesty magic.

missing_other.title: Linden Blossom Absolute
missing_other.description: Linden Blossom Absolute opens with an almost edible honey sweetness, immediately transporting you to a grove of blooming Tilia trees humming with bees. This extraordinarily rare absolute captures the narcotic warmth of sun-warmed blossoms with their distinctive citrus-green freshness. The material's rich farnesol content provides exceptional radiance while maintaining the delicate tea-like transparency that makes linden so prized. Utilise this precious absolute when creating compositions that demand authentic floral opulence without heaviness. Its honey-beeswax character transforms simple florals into luxurious nectarous bouquets. The material's natural complexity allows it to bridge bright citrus top notes with deeper woody bases, creating seamless transitions that synthetic recreations cannot achieve. Perfumers treasure its ability to add golden warmth to white florals without masking their individual characters. Combine with jasmine and orange blossom for intoxicating summer night accords. Build unexpected depth by pairing its honeyed sweetness with green tea notes and soft musks for contemporary clean luxury.

missing_other.title: Litsea Cubeba Oil
missing_other.description: Litsea Cubeba has a bit of a bad reputation owing to the fact that it has a fairly high amount of citronellal — a chemical people often attribute to pest repellant. But the complexity of this very lemony oil makes it a wonderful nuancer and it most definitely deserves a come back. In 1946, Jean Carles created Ma Griffe (1946) for Carven using 1% Citronella oil and 2% Styrallyl Acetate. Replacing the Citronella with Litsea Cubeba makes for a more subtle effect. With around 70% citral, this blends with all members of the citrus family and is a great booster for lemon especially. As it lasts around ten times longer than that oil, it is a perfect solution when you need to prolong lemon into the heart of your fragrance. Origin: Indonesia Variety: Litsea Cubeba Part: Berries Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Little Miss
missing_other.description: Little Miss is our internal formula for a scent in the style of Coco Mademoiselle by Chanel. Launched in 2001 and created by Jacques Polge, Coco Mademoiselle was an oriental floral fragrance built around a bright citrus opening and the patchouli-rose accord that defined the modern fruitchouli. Our compound features a substantial patchouli base softened with vanilla, tonka bean and opoponax. The top notes of orange, mandarin and bergamot give a sparkling citrus lift, while a rich heart of Turkish rose, jasmine, mimosa and ylang-ylang provides classic floral depth. White musk and vetiver round out the drydown. The result is a polished, instantly recognisable feminine fragrance with excellent longevity and strong sillage – confident without being heavy. This compound is IFRA and EU compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. Top Notes: Orange, Mandarin Orange, Bergamot, Orange Blossom Heart Notes: Turkish Rose, Jasmine, Mimosa, Ylang-Ylang Base Notes: Patchouli, White Musk, Vanilla, Vetiver, Tonka Bean, Opoponax

missing_other.title: Lotus Storm
missing_other.description: LOTUS STORM® is an exquisite base created by Master Perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour , exclusively for Fraterworks. Inspired by the iconic Blue Lotus (Nymphaea caerulea)—the sacred flower treasured by ancient Egypt—this innovative composition captures the flower’s rich floral elegance, captivating fruity nuances, and alluring earthy warmth and layers it with a diaphanous jasmine note and galbanum. Traditionally associated with ritual, trance, and twilight, Blue Lotus takes on a new dimension in The Night Garden: a sacred bloom that seems to awaken only when the world is quiet. Scent Profile LOTUS STORM® opens with the aroma of a serene, shadowed pond. Dew-kissed foliage entwines with the earthy depth of galbanum and warm whispers of beeswax, brightened by delicate fruity nuances. At its heart unfolds an entrancing bouquet, as the mystical fragrance of blue lotus flowers rises gracefully amid an abundant cascade of night-scented jasmine. Soft, creamy white florals lend a velvety finish. With the first light of dawn, the fragrance gently recedes, leaving behind a subtly spiced, musky echo of the Night Garden. Perfumery Usage LOTUS STORM® is formulated to deliver exceptional authenticity, longevity, and complexity, making it ideal both as a complete base or as a distinctive note within fragrance formulations. It blends seamlessly with aquatic materials such as Amazonia ®, Cascalone ®, Melozone ®, and luxurious florals like Tuberose Absolute and Egyptian Jasmine , opening endless creative possibilities for perfumers. Process Crafted from a carefully balanced combination of premium natural ingredients and specialised molecules, LOTUS STORM® embodies the highest standards of scent artistry. Its creation represents an unprecedented collaboration between Fraterworks’ creative leadership and Master Perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour, ensuring unmatched sophistication and quality. Background Fraterworks identified a unique opportunity in the fragrance market—the absence of an accessibl

missing_other.title: Lovage Root Oil
missing_other.description: Lovage root oil hits you with an intense wave of warm celery, angelica, and liquorice - spicy, sweet, earthy, and almost savoury. The power is remarkable; it ranks among the strongest-smelling natural materials in existence. A single drop perfumes an entire room. Use lovage root oil in micro-doses — it produces extraordinary effects even at trace levels. It adds savoury warmth to rose and carnation compositions and lends unique earthy depth to orientals, fougères, and spice accords. Pair it with oakmoss, opopanax, costus, and coumarin. Lovage belongs to the same botanical family as celery and angelica, and you can hear that kinship clearly. Try a trace in a rose or carnation composition — the warm, savoury effect is genuinely surprising. Always dilute heavily; this is one of perfumery's most concentrated naturals.

missing_other.title: Luxury Scent Bottle, 15ml
missing_other.description: French made by Brosse, the company that supplies perfume bottles to Chanel, this luxury scent bottle (No 7) has a 15ml capacity and a very hefty weight for its size: 65 grams. These bottles are stoppered so no tools are required for their use. Elevate your elegant scents with elegant bottles which are especially suited to very high concentrations. Ideal for Parfum and Extrait strengths. Brosse luxury bottles are made in France.

missing_other.title: Lyfral®
missing_other.description: Lyral® is one of the most beautiful floralising chemicals we have; it is soft, radiant and incredibly long lasting. Unfortunately it is also now banned by the EU and restricted to a mere 0.2% of a finished fragrance by IFRA. While patents have been filed for singular molecules that allegedly replace Lyral®, none are commercially available and neither are they likely to be so in the near future. Thus was born Lyfral ®, the Fraterworks alternative. In creating Lyfral® our first goal was to have a floralising base that was simply beautiful to smell — appealing at the most fundamental level. Next was the task of mimicking the essential aspects of Lyral® as best we could. The result is Lyfral®, a base which is lovely in its own right but also functions as a direct one for one stand-in for Lyral®. This can also stand in as a one-for-one replacer for captive Mahonial.

missing_other.title: Lys De La Reine
missing_other.description: A complex Lily base enriched with luxury floral absolutes, Lys de la Reine ("Queen's Lily" - formerly Lys de france) is an entire bouquet of flowers at its peak of blossoming. Lys de la Reine has a room filling diffusion and a wonderful naturalness. Traces add floral richesse and shimmer to a fragrance while an overdose can be used to replace muguet or generic white florals in a scent. Lys de la Reine is, like the lily flower itself, indolic, cresylic and powerful. It is constructed using only the finest aroma chemicals and naturals. This is a perfect base to use as a starting point for fragrances like Nasomatto's Narcotic Venus , Lys Mediterranee by Frederic Malle, Passage d'Enfer by L'Artisan Parfumeur, and Un Jardin Sur La Lagune by Hermès.

missing_other.title: Lysmerex™
missing_other.description: Lilial, one of the finest muguet chemicals of the late 20th century is now completely banned in fragrances in the EU and many other countries. It has a power and special character that is impossible to find in any one chemical. Consequently Fraterworks has produced Lysmerex™ a complex base which stands in as a one-for-one replacer. This base is sophisticated and true to the original. It is built around modern and classic molecules for a scent profile matching lilial and a chemical profile allowing for the formation of schiff bases. Synonyms for Lilial: lilestralis, lysmeral, mefloral, butyl phenyl methyl propional.

missing_other.title: Mace Oil
missing_other.description: Mace is the lace-like aril that wraps around the nutmeg seed, and the oil distilled from it is the more refined version of the same spice. Use it wherever you would use nutmeg but want something gentler — in fougères for sweet spicy warmth, in colognes for aromatic depth, in orientals for a natural richness that synthetic spice notes cannot replicate. Mace oil opens with warm, sweet spice — reminiscent of nutmeg and cardamom but softer, more delicate, without the rubbery sharpness that fresh nutmeg oil often has. Underneath sits a rich, almost balsamic warmth with a faint incense quality. It dries down woody, sweet, and lasting. This oil comes from Aceh in Sumatra, the heartland of Indonesian mace production, where volcanic soil produces a particularly fine, aromatic oil. Pair it with cardamom and black pepper for a full spice accord, with oakmoss and lavender for classic fougère construction, or with Peru balsam and sandalwood for dark oriental warmth.

missing_other.title: Magnificent Mandarin
missing_other.description: Green mandarin is the most elegant of all the mandarin oils (Red, yellow and green) but high prices and IFRA restrictions make it difficult to get a strong and clear mandarin top note from the pure and natural oil. Magnificent Mandarin by Fraterworks is just that: magnificent. It explodes with a citrus aldehydic quality from every perfume. In traces it is a beautiful nuancer. In overdose it is a dazzling top note refreshingly different from the far more common bergamot.

missing_other.title: Magnolia Flower Oil
missing_other.description: Magnolia flower oil is a hidden gem in perfumery. It opens with the sparkling luxury of a fine wine leading to a heart of creamy goodness with traces of delicate citrus, reminiscent of a bowl of thick medieval posset. Nuances of peach, apricots and freesias make this a really incredible oil that should have more use in perfumer's palettes. Long lasting and wonderfully characterful, this is the very finest magnolia flower oil supplied by one of the finest naturals companies. Small amounts are all that are needed in fine fragrance for an interesting twist, while larger quantities can provide unique and novel aspects to a multi-floral. We also manufacture and supply the finest complete magnolia base: Magnolia Plumier . Note: Due to weather conditions affecting harvets, LMR has increased the price of Magnolia flower oil considerably this year. We hope it will return to normal at the next harvest but have, accordingly, increased our prices to keep the product viable. We have added the option to purchase this oil in a 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless natural solvent) to help manage the cost. Synonyms: White Champaca Origin: China Part: Flowers only Method: Steam distilled at source

missing_other.title: Magnolia Leaf Oil
missing_other.description: Magnolia Leaf Oil delivers the quintessential green character that defines modern transparent florals. Its exceptional ability to inject a "dose of green goodness" into compositions prevents white florals from becoming cloying. Perfumers utilise this powerful modifier primarily at low concentrations where it significantly shapes accords. Use magnolia leaf oil to create photorealistic floral effects. Add to freesia bases where it becomes the crucial element transforming simple accords into living flower representations. Apply sparingly as its potency easily dominates compositions when overdosed. This material works effectively as a bridge note, connecting citrus openings to floral hearts. The relationship between Magnolia Leaf Oil and Magnolia Flower Oil mirrors that of petitgrain and neroli. While the flower oil presents a voluptuous, heady, sweet floral character with creamy vanilla accents, the leaf oil isolates and amplifies the fresh, crisp green "aura" surrounding the living bloom. This allows perfumers to deconstruct magnolia, building "transparent" or "green magnolia" compositions that feel contemporary and luminous—capturing the scent of the entire living branch rather than just the isolated blossom. We also stock a beautiful LMR Magnolia Flower Oil and a marvellous Magnolia Plumier base.

missing_other.title: Magnolia Plumier
missing_other.description: The creamy scent of magnolia blossoms is an elusive one but decidedly memorable once smelled with a heart of Ylang Ylang gently warmed by spices and refreshed by a delicate touch of lemon. Fraterworks® Magnolia Plumier (named for the French botanist who introduced the tree to France in the 1700s) is an elegant floral base enriched with precious magnolia flower oil. In low doses it adds volume and richness to a multi-floral bouquet, while in overdose it becomes the star of the show — and what a star it is! Magnolia Plumier can be used at up to 12.4% of a finished product.

missing_other.title: Mahua Pearl
missing_other.description: MAHUA PEARL® is a fragrance base created by Master Perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour for Fraterworks, inspired by the rare and sacred Mahua flower ( Madhuca longifolia ). Pale, round, and pearl-like, these fleshy blossoms fall silently to the forest floor during the night and are gathered by hand at dawn. Traditionally fermented into a sweet tribal spirit, the flowers carry a rich, nectarous scent touched by warmth, fruit, and fermentation. This base captures that transformation—soft, golden, and quietly intoxicating. The scent of Mahua Pearl is boozy, fruity, floral and sweet. It rests on a luxurious base of creamy sandalwood, vanilla and musk. Perfumery Usage MAHUA PEARL® is ideal for adding richness, sweetness, and complexity to florals, gourmands, and amber compositions. It harmonises beautifully with Beeswax Glacé Absolute , Immortelle , Rum CO2 , and tobacco . A perfect ingredient for perfumers looking to explore unconventional sweetness with story and soul. Process The base was developed through careful reconstruction of the Mahua blossom’s rare olfactory signature. Combining lactonic materials, honeyed accords, and subtle fruit notes, Duchaufour built a portrait of this wild bloom as it ferments in the shadows of the forest. Background Mahua is sacred in parts of India, yet almost completely unknown in the global fragrance world. MAHUA PEARL® introduces this hidden flower as a perfumery note for the first time—bridging ancient practice with modern scent design. MAHUA PEARL® is the Drunken Bloom of The Night Garden —wild, golden, and softly intoxicating. Creative Director: Jamie Frater Master Perfumer: Bertrand Duchaufour Fragrance Composition House: Fraterworks®

missing_other.title: Mandarin Oil, Green
missing_other.description: Our Green Mandarin Oil is, simply put, a work of extractive art. It is the finest mandarin oil we have had the pleasure of smelling — and we have smelled a lot of mandarin in our time. This Green Mandarin Oil is every bit the scent that remains on your hands after peeling the fruit. Every nuance from every drop of juicy goodness is found in this oil. Green Mandarin is the preferred variety (the others being red and yellow) and it has been used in numerous luxury fragrances, as evidenced by the demonstration formulas below. Oil Comparison Green Mandarin Essential Oil : Extracted from unripe green peels, this oil boasts a tart, sharp citrus scent with a floral hint. Its olive-green hue reflects its youthful vigor, offering an energizing boost in aromatherapy and perfumery. High in limonene (~70%), it’s prized for refreshing skin care blends. Yellow Mandarin Essential Oil : Derived from semi-ripe yellow peels, it delivers a balanced, semi-sweet citrus aroma. With a pale yellow tone and ~71% limonene, it strikes a middle ground between tart and sweet. It’s less common but shines in uplifting aromatherapy and cleansing applications. Red Mandarin Essential Oil : Sourced from fully ripened red-orange peels, this oil exudes a rich, sweet citrus scent with floral undertones. Its reddish-orange color and ~72% limonene content make it the sweetest, ideal for calming diffusion and cosmetics. It’s the most widely available of the trio.

missing_other.title: Mandarin Oil, Red
missing_other.description: Red Mandarin Essential Oil is the richest and sweetest of all mandarin varieties, offering a deep, intensely fruity citrus aroma with a soft, almost velvety character. Unlike the crisp zestiness of Green Mandarin or the balanced brightness of Yellow Mandarin, Red Mandarin is fully ripened, resulting in a scent that is smooth, warm, and lusciously sweet with hints of candied orange peel. Red Mandarin Oil stands out for its unique composition, containing a higher proportion of aldehydes and esters that contribute to its roundness and longevity. It pairs exceptionally well with vanilla , tonka bean , and creamy florals , enhancing their depth with a naturally sweet citrus glow. Oil Comparison Green Mandarin Essential Oil : Extracted from unripe green peels, this oil boasts a tart, sharp citrus scent with a floral hint. Its olive-green hue reflects its youthful vigor, offering an energizing boost in aromatherapy and perfumery. High in limonene (~70%), it’s prized for refreshing skin care blends. Yellow Mandarin Essential Oil : Derived from semi-ripe yellow peels, it delivers a balanced, semi-sweet citrus aroma. With a pale yellow tone and ~71% limonene, it strikes a middle ground between tart and sweet. It’s less common but shines in uplifting aromatherapy and cleansing applications. Red Mandarin Essential Oil : Sourced from fully ripened red-orange peels, this oil exudes a rich, sweet citrus scent with floral undertones. Its reddish-orange color and ~72% limonene content make it the sweetest, ideal for calming diffusion and cosmetics. It’s the most widely available of the trio.

missing_other.title: Mandarin Oil, Yellow
missing_other.description: While red mandarin is fruit and green mandarin is herbaceous, yellow meets them in the middle with its fresh and delicate scent. It still maintains a distinctly mandarin character when smelling pure while being great for adding lift and zest to a scent. Yellow mandarin is the lightest of the three in terms of impact which means you can dose it with more bravado than the others. Oil Comparison Green Mandarin Essential Oil : Extracted from unripe green peels, this oil boasts a tart, sharp citrus scent with a floral hint. Its olive-green hue reflects its youthful vigor, offering an energizing boost in aromatherapy and perfumery. High in limonene (~70%), it’s prized for refreshing skin care blends. Yellow Mandarin Essential Oil : Derived from semi-ripe yellow peels, it delivers a balanced, semi-sweet citrus aroma. With a pale yellow tone and ~71% limonene, it strikes a middle ground between tart and sweet. It’s less common but shines in uplifting aromatherapy and cleansing applications. Red Mandarin Essential Oil : Sourced from fully ripened red-orange peels, this oil exudes a rich, sweet citrus scent with floral undertones. Its reddish-orange color and ~72% limonene content make it the sweetest, ideal for calming diffusion and cosmetics. It’s the most widely available of the trio.

missing_other.title: Mandarinal® SAEF
missing_other.description: Mandarinal opens with a diffusive blast of sparkling aldehydes carrying the essence of ripe mandarin fruit on a wave of exhilarating freshness. This isn't your typical citrus - it's mandarin reimagined with a waxy, pillowy texture that removes all harshness while maintaining powerful projection. You'll find it captures not just the fruit but the entire sensory experience of a mandarin grove after rain. This material transforms traditional citrus structures by providing remarkable longevity and stability where natural citrus oils quickly fade. Reach for Mandarinal when you need a citrus note that carries from the opening through the heart of your composition. Its aldehydic engine provides exceptional lift and bloom, making surrounding notes feel brighter and more expansive while maintaining sophisticated elegance. Use Mandarinal at 2-4% in your cologne concentrate to create a modern citrus accord with unprecedented staying power. Combine it with bergamot and grapefruit for a sparkling citrus cocktail, or pair with neroli and orange blossom for seamless floral integration. The material excels in contemporary structures where its aldehydic freshness cuts through heavier bases while its unique texture prevents the soapy effect common with other aldehydic materials when properly dosed. Pairing this with Citroasis base, a long lasting lemon base from Firmenich, and a jot of Terpeneless Bergamot will give you a citrus melange that lasts long into the dry down of your scent. Temper it with a trace of Pineapple Supreme . A version of this product also exists under the name Mandarinal SAE K which is a newer reformulation to offer compliance with proposition 65 in California. Our SAE F version is the original unchanged version.

missing_other.title: Manuka Oil βTK25+
missing_other.description: Manuka is a shrub endemic to New Zealand and Australia and it is the source of the nectar from which honeybees produce the highly esteemed manuka honey, the finest honey in the world. Manuka oil is similar in chemical makeup to tea tree oil but it is softer, more elegant and more herbaceous. New Zealand manuka oil is beloved by herbalists and while it has yet to be exploited fully in a fragrance, it is not entirely absent from the industry. Being located in New Zealand, Fraterworks is in the position to find and supply the absolute crème de la crème of fine manuka oil, and indeed we have. The New Zealand East coast, in particular the East Cape is renowned for its high quality manuka oil and it is from that region that we source ours. Manuka oil was historically used to treat wounds as it was believed to have antibacterial properties and early colonial settlers to New Zealand made tea from the foliage of the plant. The presumed efficacy of the oil is typically determined by the beta-triketone level (sometimes indicated by the β TK or MβTK™ term). Our oil has as minimum of 25%. NOTE: This is sold for perfumery purposes only and should not be consumed or used neat on the skin. This is neither a food nor a health care product. Origin: East Cape, New Zealand Variety: Leptospermum scoparium Part: Leaves and twigs Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Mastic (Lentisque) Oil, Rectified
missing_other.description: This is a very fine quality of lentisque (mastic) oil from LMR. It is a top note herbaceous oil with a terpenic and almost cascarilla-like quality. Wonderful in colognes for a unique top note, this material blends very well with Galbanum oil. The strikingly unique scent of mastic oil conjures up images of antiquity — its rituals, traditions, and the warm sun-soaked breeze of the Aegean sea. Mastic oil is a star in niche and artisanal fragrances. Its inclusion in perfumes such as Diptyque’s Eau de Lierre highlights its fresh, green characteristics, while Serge Lutens' La Myrrhe showcases its resinous, balsamic richness. Other masterpieces like Amouage Jubilation XXV use touches to evoke a sense of ancient luxury. Origin: Morocco Part: Leaves Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Mate “Signature” Abs 40% TEC
missing_other.description: Mate (pronounced MAH-tay) absolute opens with the unmistakable warmth of steeped green tea — not bright or grassy but deep, dried, and slightly roasted. Hay and herbaceous facets emerge quickly, lending a sun-baked quality. Beneath it all sits a tobacco-leaf dryness that anchors everything to the base. This is the material when you need a convincing tea accord built on a natural foundation. It slots into fougères alongside lavender and oakmoss, adding an intellectual herbal dimension that synthetics struggle to replicate. In tobacco compositions it provides the leafy dryness of cured leaves without resorting to isolated pyrazines or coumarin alone. The phenolic undertow gives it backbone in chypres and mossy structures. Use mate to ground bright bergamot openings or to add bookish complexity to vetiver bases. It pairs exceptionally well with osmanthus, guaiacwood, chamomile, and hay absolute. At 40% in TEC this LMR material is ready to use — add it directly to your formula without further dilution. A touch of warmth may be needed to slacken the liquid in cooler climes. Mate has been used to great effect in modern scents such as Tempo (2018) by Olivier Pescheux for Diptyque, Louis Vuitton's Cactus Garden (2019) byJacques Cavallier Belletrud, Xerjoff's Torino22 (2022) and the luxurious Matsukita (2021) by Clive Christian.

missing_other.title: Mayciane
missing_other.description: One of the two great classical muguet bases from De Laire that gave the lily character to Chanel's No 19 (the other great base was Coroliane ). This soft and elegant base was also the key lily of the valley in 1,000 of Patou in concert with Aldehone . Use this base together with Coroliane , or on its own for a sweet and surprisingly modern muguet at up to 6.1% of the finished product for IFRA compliance. Mayciane was created by Henri Robert in 1953.

missing_other.title: Mellitis
missing_other.description: Mellitis is the classical Givaudan mellis base launched in 1921. It features a perfectly balanced heart of carnation accented by rose, jasmin and wild flowers. It was a favourite of Jean Patou's perfumer Henri Almeras who used it in overdose to great effect in Moment Supreme (1929) where he blended it with lavender and aldehydes. Mellitis can also be used as fixative base and small quantities add complexity and warmth to any fragrance dry down. Use up to 14.9% in your finished product for compliance with IFRA 50.

missing_other.title: Miel Blanc
missing_other.description: Miel Blanc was a classical honey base from De Laire that found its way into many great perfumes indirectly by way of the great Mousse de Saxe base and directly as a honey note. This non-discoloring almost clear formula is perfect for perfumes needing a sweet honey note without the intense colour of our other honey base Mielarome . While less floral than Mielarome , this base contributes a more powerful note and works very well in minute amounts up to overdose as it is completely IFRA compliant to a whopping 40% of your finished fragrance!

missing_other.title: Miel de Ciste
missing_other.description: Miel de Ciste is a co-distillation — labdanum distilled directly onto gurjun balsam, producing aromatic compounds that neither material creates alone. This is not a blend. When two botanicals are distilled together, heat and steam generate new molecules at the interface, yielding a material with qualities impossible to achieve by simply mixing the finished oils. The result here is labdanum taken back to its origins — raw, green, herbal, recalling the ancient Cretan tradition of dragging leather straps through wild cistus bushes to collect resin. What distinguishes Miel de Ciste from standard labdanum absolute is an unexpected honeyed facet. Not bright floral honey but something closer to honeydew — the dark, malty, almost mineral honey produced when bees feed on aphid secretions rather than flower nectar. This note exists only because of the co-distillation; the interaction between gurjun balsam and labdanum under steam creates byproducts neither material produces alone. The cinnamic warmth typical of labdanum is present but softened, less dominant. Use it in chypres and ambers where you want labdanum that feels wild-harvested rather than industrially extracted. It gives raw garrigue authenticity to Mediterranean compositions. The honeyed quality lets it double as a natural honey note in orientals without adding a dedicated honey material.

missing_other.title: Mielarome
missing_other.description: An intense and highly floral honey base in the clasical style enhanced with natural absolutes and essential oils. This base can be used at trace amounts to add sweetness and richness. Originally sold as Melarome by Chiris, this base was found in such fragrances as La Rose Jacqueminot , by Coty. Try it in larger doses with lavender and related notes for a unique and appealing modern fougere type fragrance. For a non-discolouring honey try our Miel Blanc.

missing_other.title: Mimosa Absolute, France
missing_other.description: Because the annual quantities of Mimosa absolute are dependent on weather, it is a material that can be difficult to keep in steady supply. Consequently we offer stock from the two finest suppliers, V MANE Fils and this beautiful product from LMR. In both cases the absolute comes from the same village in France but methods of extraction are unique to the two companies. Both are wonderful and interchangeable. We tend to fluctuate between liking one over the other. Mimosa has a delicate sweet odour somewhere between cassie and violet. It is perceptible in trace amounts and does an astonishing job of naturalising a fragrance. The lightest touch will elevate virtually all perfume types. Needless to say it blends exceptionally well with Violet Leaf “Signature” Absolute , Fleur de Cassie , Violette Bleue and the classic violet synthetics Iralia ® (Firmenich), Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur (IFF) and Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra (IFF). Unlike lesser qualities, our two mimosa offerings are not brittle but have rather a stiff honey-like consistency. However, it is still extremely difficult to work with so we also offer it at dilution in natural triethyl citrate. That means this is a 100% pure and natural ISO 9235 standard product. We also offer a wonderfully complex floral base in the form of our Mimosa De Provence .

missing_other.title: Mimosa De Provence
missing_other.description: Fraterworks® Mimosa de Provence (formerly just Mimosa ) is a beautiful recreation of wild harvested French mimosa smelling intensely of honeyed woods with fatty and violet nuances and an anisic drydown. Mimosa de Provence is an updated reconstruction of the classic base of the same name from Th. Mühlethaler S.A., the great Swiss early 20th century manufacturer of bases and fragrances. Mimosa de Provence is a sweet and refined note which can be used in large doses for an eccentric twist or in touches as a fixative and nuancer. This base is enriched with precious essential oils and rare absolutes. Classification: Mimosa ( Acacia d ealbata also sometimes called Acacia deccurens ) should not be confused with Cassie ( Acacia farnesiana ) or the entirely unrelated Pink Acacia (Robinia pseudoacacia), all of which are items of interest to perfumers and, consquently, for sale here.

missing_other.title: Mimosa “Supreme” Absolute
missing_other.description: Mimosa has a delicate sweet odour somewhere between cassie and violet. It is perceptible in trace amounts and does an astonishing job of naturalising a fragrance. The lightest touch will elevate virtually all perfume types. Needless to say it blends exceptionally well with Violet Leaf “Signature” Absolute , Fleur de Cassie , Violette Bleue and the classic violet synthetics Iralia ® (Firmenich), Methyl Ionone Gamma Coeur (IFF) and Methyl Ionone Alpha Extra (IFF). Unlike lesser qualities, our mimosa is not brittle but has rather a stiff honey-like consistency. However, it is still extremely difficult to work with so we also offer it at dilution in natural triethyl citrate. That means this is a 100% pure and natural ISO 9235 standard product. You will never use another mimosa product after you have experienced this jewel in the crown of France's finest naturals. We also offer a wonderfully complex floral base in the form of our Mimosa De Provence .

missing_other.title: Miraclewood™
missing_other.description: If you are looking for a megadose wood material like Iso E Super ®, Miraclewood™ is for you. Built around the finest and most radiant wood materials enriched by luxurious and rare natural oils such as “mulacro” oil, Miraclewood is the cedar of our time. Velvety smooth with subtle greenness and all the volume you desire but can never get from Iso E Super , Miraclewood is absolutely essential for all perfumers. Use Miraclewood as a one for one replacer for Iso E Super in your formulas and be amazed. Add a ribbon of warm animalics with our incredible Ambrexol ™ and a touch of Laevo Muscone and you have a complete perfume.

missing_other.title: Mitti Attar
missing_other.description: Mitti attar is the distillation of earth itself — that is not a metaphor. In Kannauj, India's perfume capital, clay from dried lakebeds is shaped into crude vessels, half-baked in small kilns, then distilled into sandalwood oil. The result captures something you already know: petrichor, the intoxicating smell of rain on dry ground. Indian perfumers have been bottling this scent for centuries. For all intents and purposes, this as close as you'll get to a natural geosmin . The opening is cool and mineral — baked clay, wet stone, a faint electric charge. There is nothing floral about it. A quiet, bread-like sweetness emerges as the sandalwood base rises, and the mineral edge softens over several hours into something serene and meditative. Mitti attar does not project aggressively. It radiates from the skin, intimate and contemplative. Use mitti attar to ground florals or add realism to green compositions. With vetiver it creates deep forest dampness; with rose, a garden-after-rain effect. It layers well with patchouli and oakmoss for a complete forest-floor accord. Dose carefully — too much flattens a composition into mud rather than enriching it with earth.

missing_other.title: Motia Attar
missing_other.description: Motia Attar opens with a sharp, bright jasmine character — narcotic and indolic in the way only Jasminum sambac can be — laid over soft, creamy sandalwood. The honey side of jasmine sits in the heart, lifting into faint green and tea-like nuances. Sandalwood underneath gives the whole composition body. Use Motia Attar where you want a true Indian jasmine anchored to sandalwood — oriental floral bouquets, mukhallats, soliflores and Mughal-style attar reconstructions. It bridges naturally to oud, saffron, rose and ylang-ylang. A small amount lifts simple white-floral bases into dense, Indian-style depth. Pair with rose otto and saffron attar for a Mughal mukhallat heart, or use alongside oud and ambergris for a luxurious oriental. A trace under champaca or magnolia adds Indian warmth without obscuring the lighter florals. Undiluted, the sandalwood reads heavier than the jasmine until a few minutes in. Motia Attar is the traditional Indian jasmine perfume — fresh Jasminum sambac flowers (locally called Bela), hand-picked at dawn in the monsoon and co-distilled by deg-bhapka into sandalwood oil. The night-blooming north-Indian jasmine was a Mughal-era court favourite and the signature scent of the Nizams of Hyderabad. This Motia is from M.L. Ramnarain Perfumers, a Kannauj distillery run by five generations of the Kapoor family using copper degs and the traditional water-distillation method.

missing_other.title: Muguet 16
missing_other.description: Muguet 16 was one of the greatest lily of the valley bases. Created by Marius Reboul in 1929 for Givaudan (founded by Léon Givaudan in 1895 at the young age of 20 with his brother Xavier, eight years his senior), Muguet 16 went on to feature in numerous fragrances over the decades, including Mais Oui by Bourjois. So popular was Muguet 16 that it was copied by every fragrance house (right up to Drogco as late as the 1960s in their Muguet Nouveau base). Muguet 16 is a real delight and despite the limited number of materials available to perfumers in the early 20th century is perhaps a more perfect fit for modern fragrances than most classical Muguet bases. Reboul constructed this base with a very light hand, using transparent materials over heavier ones, and so, for example, we find Cinnamyl Acetate taking the place of the far heavier Cinnamic Alcohol favoured at the time. Every material is balanced to perfection and the resulting base stands as a testament to the brilliance of this gentleman who is perhaps more famous for his bases than his perfumes.
