Long gone from the modern perfumer's palette (and tragically long forgotten by most), we are thrilled to be able to offer our restoration of this timeless masterpiece to our discerning clients. If you are interested in Marius Reboul's work, we also offer his Amarante base, Sophira (the key to Rigaud's Un Air Embaume from 1914).

missing_other.title: Muguet Chiris
missing_other.description: Chiris was the oldest of the French perfumery houses, also being the first to set up large scale manufacture of essential oils in Grasse and establishing a perfumery school there. The two most famous graduates of the school were François Coty and Ernest Beaux who, as fate would have it, ultimately ended up back there when he fled with Rallet to France from the murderous rampage spreading across revolutionary Russia. Chiris produced some wonderful bases and Beaux and Coty made much use of them in their early years. This one (originally called Muguet A204) was a vital floraliser in Chanel No 5 while Lilac A07 was the main ingredient in Coty's early Jasmin de Corse fragrance. Muguet Chiris is the most luxurious of the muguet bases and incorporates many extremely costly naturals and the very best aroma chemicals. It is a classic muguet base built around Hydroxycitronellal and despite its age is very useable in modern fragrances where it can replace the less interesting singular chemical floral hearts so often seen in department store brands today. For a simpler option, consider Muguet de Grasse , Ernest Beaux's own muguet creation (though not the one he used in the early versions of No 5).

missing_other.title: Muguet de Grasse
missing_other.description: From the great Muguet des Bois by Henri Robert to the masterpiece of Coroliane crafted by Edmond Roudnitska, we have your muguet needs covered... with one exception. That exception is Muguet de Grasse , this is the muguet beloved by Ernest Beaux who trained and worked at Chiris both before and after the revolution forced the company to relocate from Russia to France. Chiris had purchased the great Russian fragrance company Rallet the year Beaux started work there and it was during this employment that he created Bouquet de Catherine (Rallet le No 1) which later became Chanel No 5. As simple as simplicity itself, Muguet de Grasse is a diaphanous effusion of floralcy created with only the essential early muguet aroma chemicals and a delicate touch of natural absolutes. The very high concentration of hydroxycitronellal (then a revolutionary molecule) makes this a perfect muguet to use in place of that chemical for more character or as an accent in a lily of the valley fond. Muguet de Grasse is perhaps the most versatile of all our muguet bases, and most definitely one that suits a modern fragrance as much as it did the great classics of the early 20th century. For a dazzling and novel modern accord, try a blend of Muguet de Grasse with Mimosal ™ and the merest trace of cumin seed oil and Cassis Base 345B .

missing_other.title: Muguet Des Bois
missing_other.description: Important: This is not a perfume. It should not be applied to the skin directly. It is a blend of chemicals used in the manufacture of fragrances. This is the famed Muguet des Bois base made by Henri Robert when he was working at Coty. It was released as a fragrance in 1941 under the same name but repurposed later as a base. It is a sweet and very natural green muguet base replicating the scent of wild lily of the valley flowers. Edmond Roudnitska considering it the finest muguet ever made (despite making his own incredible Coroliane base ) used it as the foundation of his Diorissimo fragrance for Dior in 1956. In a coincidental turn of events, Henri Robert admired Roudnitska's Coroliane base so much that he used it as the foundation of No 19 for Chanel in 1970. We also sell the wonderful Coroliane base. Muguet Des Bois was the key lily in Poison by Dior. Reminder: This is not a perfume.

missing_other.title: Muguet Fleurs
missing_other.description: Safe for use up to 15% of the finished product for IFRA 51, this is a radiant and modern lily of the valley taking as its starting point a scientific headspace reconstruction. Use it as a complete muguet fragrance or as a luscious floral canvas. Fraterworks Muguet Fleurs' fresh green character is boosted with incredible radiant molecules and luscious absolutes and essential oils.

missing_other.title: Muguet Invar
missing_other.description: From 1914 to the 1930s, Roure made a series of bases they called referred to as invariable, or invar, meaning that they maintained the same odour profile from start to finish. They were effectively linear bases. These bases were enormously popular with Muguet Invar and Jasmine Invar being two of the most used. Muguet Invar presents a fresh and soft muguet with no rough edges. It is a perfect all-round floralising base. This is simply muguet. Useable at up to 8.4% of your finished product.

missing_other.title: Muguet Royale
missing_other.description: If you only have one muguet, Muguet Royale is it. Wtih an astonishing pedigree, Muguet Royale made famous many great scents, among them Arpège and Miss Dior. Beloved of Jean Carles, this base is floral to the max and accented with many delightful naturals. With an IFRA 51 max-use of 7.29% of the finished product, you can use Muguet Royale almost indiscriminately. In small amounts it adds richness and interest, while in overdose it adds a glorious lily of the valley note immediately recognisable to all.

missing_other.title: Muguet Weriguine
missing_other.description: Constanin Wereguine (1899–1982) was a master perfumer who was assistant and second perfumer to Ernest Beaux at both Chanel and Bourjois and Henri Robert at the Former. A Russian aristocrat educated in Yalta, Wereguin eventually went on to work at Rhône-Poulenc. Muguet Weriguine is the personal creation of this great perfumer and was used in place of other classic muguet bases that were fading from use in the 1970s and 1980s, notably Muguet 16 and Ernest Beaux's own Muguet de Grasse . Weriguine cleverly enriched his muguet with natural citrus (including a rather large dose of neroli oil) which gives it a lovely unique character that blends exceedingly well with the likes of Bouvardia De Laire , Floranol , Fleur D'Oranger and Jasmine 1109 which has its own orange blossom nuance.

missing_other.title: Musc Doré
missing_other.description: Musc Doré (Golden Musk) is the first in a new Bertrand Duchaufour x Fraterworks trilogy, Les Trois Voiles . In French, voile holds three meanings at once — veil, sheer fabric, and sail — and each musk takes one: Musc Doré — the veil: a sheer golden veil of warmth drawn over the skin. Musc de Lin — the fabric: voile is the gauze-fine cloth woven from flax, clean air made textile. Musc d'Embruns — the sail: canvas wet with sea spray, carrying the skin into open air. Musc Doré is a warm golden skin musk with powdered facets. It bears an almost fougère-like structure which hints at Duchaufour's masterpiece Sartorial (2010) for Penhaligons. This is the scent of the golden hours at the close of day, the scent of warm skin, the scent of nostalgia. While Musk Doré, and indeed the other two members of the trilogy, can be used as the foundation upon which to construct a fragrance, it is, in itself, so elegant and complete that it can be simply overdosed and worn as-is.

missing_other.title: Mushroom Abs, Deco
missing_other.description: Decolourised mushroom absolute opens with the unmistakable scent of autumn forests after rain. Damp earth mingles with fungal sweetness, creating an immediate sense of place. This pale version retains all the olfactory power of traditional mushroom absolute while offering formulation flexibility for delicate compositions. Bear in mind, however, that while paler than standard absolute, this is still brown in colour. This material works magic at trace levels, transforming simple accords into complex experiences. In chypres, it grounds mossy notes with authentic forest floor depth. Modern perfumers exploit its savory-sweet duality to create unexpected gourmand effects—think dark chocolate with mysterious umami undertones that intrigue rather than overwhelm. Deploy this treasure sparingly—its potency demands respect. At 0.01-0.1%, it adds subliminal earthiness that makes compositions feel grounded and natural. Combine with oakmoss for ultimate chypre depth, or pair with cocoa and coffee for avant-garde gourmands that challenge conventional sweetness. Owing to the high cost we are also offering this at 10% in natural odourless Triethyl Citrate.

missing_other.title: Myrrh Absolute 50% TEC
missing_other.description: One of the oldest resins used in perfumery, Myrrh is the bitter sweet gum which was offered as a gift by St. Balthasar to Christ at His birth. It was used by the Ancient Egyptians as a beautifying skin treatment and by the Ancient Greeks as a food additive. In the fragrance industry, Myrrh often forms part of a classic Opoponax base which should not to be confused with Opoponax resinoid sometimes called “sweet myrrh” adding further confusion. It should be noted that this product is technically a “resin-absolute” because it is cold extracted directly from the raw gum with ethanol. This is the preferred method for better odour properties as no damage is done to the product in manufacturing. Origin: Somalia Part: Raw Exudate Method: Solvent (ethanol) extraction

missing_other.title: Myrrh Oil
missing_other.description: Myrrh Oil is an ancient wonder of perfumery that still captivates the senses today. Sourced from the resin of the Commiphora myrrha tree, this rich oil has been celebrated for its warmth and mystery since the days of pharaohs and emperors. Its aroma is a beguiling blend of balsamic sweetness and earthy richness, with a smoky edge that evokes flickering incense in far distant sacred temples. In perfumery, Myrrh is nothing short of a cornerstone. Its resinous profile gives fragrances a grounding quality, pairing effortlessly with Frankincense, Patchouli, and Sandalwood. Whether you’re wanting a brooding oriental or a bright citrus-floral with character in the dry down, Myrrh is a powerhouse amongst base notes. This wonderful material features in Amouage’s Opus VI (2012), Tom Ford’s Sahara Noir (2013), and the iconic Shalimar (1925) by Jacques Guerlain. It is also a discreet but key material in Dior's original Homme (2005).

missing_other.title: Myrrh Wildii Oil, Namibia
missing_other.description: In the boiling heat of the Namibian desert comes a special type of myrrh oil: wildii ( Commiphora wildii) . The chief olfactory difference between this and traditional resinous myrrh ( Commiphora myrrha ) is that wildii is fresh, invigorating and diffusive. In other words, classic myrrh is rich, deep and dark while Namibian myrrh is an explosion of top notes. Use the two together to create a top to bottom myrrh accord. Further anchor it with myrrh resinoid. Myrrh Wildii oil blends extremely well with all amber bases, but particularly those of the opoponax variety: Opoponax Doux and Black Opoponax especially.

missing_other.title: Myrtle Oil, Rectified
missing_other.description: Myrtle Oil, Rectified opens cool and green, a fresh herbal top note carrying clean camphor and eucalyptus brightness. Underneath sits a soft, almost floral sweetness and a whisper of spice. Rectifying strips out the harsh, bitter edges, leaving a clearer, rounder oil. Myrtle is not a note often discussed amongst perfume aficionados but it appears in surprisingly many popular scents such as Neroli Portofino by Tom Ford, Invictus from Paco Rabanne, Ambre Sultan of Serge Lutens, the much-lauded Tam Dao from Diptique and Amouage Epic Man. Our Tunisian oil is from LMR so you can be certain you are getting the very best on the market.

missing_other.title: Mysoralex™
missing_other.description: Mysoral means two things in perfumery today. The first is the classic base by Synarome (Mysoral Base 601651) built around an overdose of sandela , amyris wood oil and spices. The second is a Firmenich captive molecule 2-methyl-4-(2,2,3-trimethylcyclopent-3-en-1-yl)pent-4-enal (CAS 166432-53-7). Mysoral is the aldehyde counterpart of Firsantol but unlike the alcohol, Mysoral has a brighter and shaprer quality, pushing higher into the top notes. Mysoral also has pine, cedar and frankincense nuances lacking in Firsantol. Mysoral has gained attention of late due to its inclusion (in relatively high doses) in a number of Louis Vuitton fragrances, however it should be noted that it forms part of the popular Firmenich Dreamwood base (at around 0.5%) so traces may appear in GCMS analyses of fragrances incorporating that (alongside considerably larger quantities of santalols). Our Mysoralex base is intended as a direct 1 for 1 replacement for captive Mysoral in modern formulas, however it is a beautiful and radiant sandalwood base in its own right also. Mysoralex is particularly great at bridging sandalwood notes with cedar, pine, fir, frankincence, and pink pepper . It has a synergy with Firsantol and blends of the two are a real delight. Add a touch to your existing blends and watch the sandalwood dance!

missing_other.title: Narcisse Base 184092D
missing_other.description: Narcisse Base 184092D opens with sharp green freshness carrying mentholic and herbaceous facets that evoke snapped flower stems. This legendary Firmenich base transforms into a narcotic white floral heart where narcissus mingles with jasmine and tuberose. The sophisticated blend captures the living flower's intoxicating presence more faithfully than natural absolute, though we highly recommend naturalising the base with the natural material. You'll find this base superior to natural narcissus absolute for most applications - it's brighter, more consistent, and vastly more affordable. Use it as the floral heart of your composition where it provides both character and exceptional tenacity. Its subtle animalic-honey drydown with chypre-like mossy undertones adds vintage elegance without overwhelming. The base contains approximately phenylethyl alcohol providing rosy sweetness, Veloutone for fruity-lactonic creaminess, ionones for powdery violet depth, and Evernyl for mossy sophistication. Build classic narcissus soliflores or use it to add narcotic floralcy to orientals. Combine with coumarin in fougères where its hay-like facets create perfect synergy. But be wary: you'll be surprised just how powerful this base can be so start off slowly.

missing_other.title: Natural Perfume Oil Kit
missing_other.description: Mandy Aftel is a highly regarded name in the field of natural perfumery and we have many clients who have started on their perfumery journey with her help. In order to be of service to those who follow her methods, we have put together a replica of her kit of 18 essential natural materials that go with her Natural Perfume Workbook. The Fraterworks edition of the Mandy Aftel Natural Perfume Oil Kit uses the very best natural oils from the top suppliers in France; these are the oils we sell and use ourselves and most are used by top brands such as Chanel, Creed, Guerlain and others. As it says on the Aftelier website: “You are welcome to obtain essences from other sources[.]” At Fraterworks are able to offer this kit at a significantly lower price (60% lower in fact) and it also comes with free shipping (some conditions apply, see here ). The kit contains (in her words with links to our matching products): Top Notes: Bergamot essential oil [FCF], Black Pepper essential oil , Blood Orange essential oil , Geraniol natural isolate , Ho wood essential oil , Tarragon essential oil Middle Notes: Clary Sage essential oil , Coffee essential oil , Jasmine grandiflorum absolute , Lavender absolute [50%], Nutmeg absolute , Ylang Ylang extra essential oil Base Notes: Coumarin natural isolate [15%], Frankincense absolute , Labdanum absolute [50%], Oakmoss absolute [50%], Peru Balsam resin , Vetiver essential oil . All liquids come in our high quality German-made glass bottles containing 5ml (4 grams) of luxurious naturals. We pride ourselves on supplying only the most precious materials from the very best French suppliers like LMR, V. Mane Fils, Payan Bertrand, Robertet, and more.

missing_other.title: Nearly Deer™ CMP
missing_other.description: Fraterworks' Nearly Deer ™ is a masterful recreation of Tonkin deer musk tincture. This can be used as a one-for-one replacement in vintage formulas for musk tincture or in modern perfumes to enrich and extend. Use in traces to boost performance and longevity or overdose it for a wonderfully natural animalic musk indistinguishable from the real thing. Tonkin deer musk is banned from international trade leaving a gap in the perfume industry in the range of animalics. Nearly Deer ™ fills that gap.

missing_other.title: Nebulux
missing_other.description: This blend exists to solve a specific problem: Nebulone is an IFF captive that independent perfumers cannot buy. Nebulux reconstructs its soft, powdery volume and woody-amber depth using commercially available materials and another IFF captive available no where else. Use it as a direct substitute wherever formulas call for Nebulone — typically at the same concentration. Nebulux opens with a soft woody radiance and a subtle pear-like fruitiness. As it develops, a warm amber backbone emerges — clean, textured, skin-like. The drydown is extraordinarily tenacious: a deep, velvety musk that clings to blotters for days. Combine Nebulux with Ambroxan and Hedione for the modern, diffusive skin-scent aesthetic found in fragrances like Le Labo Another 13. It also anchors woody and oriental accords superbly. Pair with Iso E Super and sandalwood for a warm, abstract, second-skin effect.

missing_other.title: Neroli Oil, Morocco
missing_other.description: From Fez and its surrounding areas, this opulent essential oil extracted from the blossoms of the bitter orange tree is a marvel. Compared to Tunisian neroli oil , the product from Morocco is more rounded, indolic and rich. It is a wonderful oil to add top note fresh floralcy to perfumes that link into a beautifully blended heart. Pair it with Orange Blossom absolute for a complete orange flower note. As usual, LMR one again tops the quality charts with this incredible oil. Due to cost and power, we offer this pure and diluted to 10% in natural TEC. For a breathtaking alternative, try our Neroli Supreme which is practically indistinguishable from natural neroli oil and significantly less expensive. Tunisia vs Morocco While both oils are from the same plant species, the terroir has much to play in the difference between the two for perfumery purposes. Tunisian oil is brighter, greener, fresher and more eau de cologne like. It is slightly zesty with petitgrain nuances. Moroccan oil is softer, rounder and more orange blossom like. It tends to be more linalool-rich and to have a creamy and honeyed side.

missing_other.title: Neroli Oil, Tunisia
missing_other.description: A wonderful pure neroli oil from Tunisia by master distillers LMR. Touches will add freshness and floralcy to a fragrance. Much admired by both ladies and gentlemen, neroli oil enhances almost all perfumes. For a breathtaking alternative, try our Neroli Supreme which is practically indistinguishable from natural neroli oil and significantly less expensive. Due to cost and power, we offer this pure and diluted to 10% in natural TEC. We also stock Neroli Oil from Morocco , also from LMR. Tunisia vs Morocco While both oils are from the same plant species, the terroir has much to play in the difference between the two for perfumery purposes. Tunisian oil is brighter, greener, fresher and more eau de cologne like. It is slightly zesty with petitgrain nuances. Moroccan oil is softer, rounder and more orange blossom like. It tends to be more linalool-rich and to have a creamy and honeyed side.

missing_other.title: Neroli Supreme
missing_other.description: With the rising cost of natural oils and absolutes, floral materials such as a rose and neroli are now priced far beyond the range of most perfumers. That is where Neroli Supreme comes in. Neroli Supreme is a complex blend of the same aroma chemicals found in neroli oil crowned by beautiful naturals from LMR. Dare we say it: Neroli Supreme is better than most commercial neroli oils on the market today. Once you try Neroli Supreme, you will be a convert for life.

missing_other.title: Night Queen
missing_other.description: NIGHT QUEEN is a rare fragrance base created by Master Perfumer Bertrand Duchaufour, exclusively for Fraterworks. Inspired by the elusive Queen of the Night flower ( Selenicereus grandiflorus )—a cactus that blooms for a single night each year—this composition captures the fleeting purity and nocturnal magic of this ghostly blossom. Its delicate floralcy is brightened by cool green facets and softened by creamy undertones, echoing the brief, beautiful life of a bloom that lives only in moonlight. Perfumery Usage NIGHT QUEEN brings a haunting elegance to compositions, with excellent lift and translucency. It pairs effortlessly with white florals such as Jasmine Sambac and Orange Blossom Absolute, as well as night-themed molecules like Helional, Melonal, and Methyl Dihydrojasmonate. It can be used as a central floral motif or layered for shimmer and mystery. Process Created through a blend of specialty aroma materials and carefully selected natural isolates, NIGHT QUEEN reflects Fraterworks’ commitment to olfactory innovation. Every element was guided by Duchaufour’s vision to reimagine a scent that lives in shadow—a floral portrait composed entirely in the dark. Background Despite its mystique and reputation among plant lovers, Queen of the Night has been largely absent from perfumery due to its unextractable nature. NIGHT QUEEN fills this gap, offering perfumers access to a completely original accord, conceptualised and brought to life through imagination, chemistry, and craftsmanship. NIGHT QUEEN is the Ghost Bloom of The Night Garden —silent, translucent, and gone before morning. Creative Director: Jamie Frater Master Perfumer: Bertrand Duchaufour Fragrance Composition House: Fraterworks®

missing_other.title: Nutmeg Absolute
missing_other.description: This product has seen a steep price increase from our suppliers and alas we must pass that on. We are monitoring the trends in pricing and will make reductions when possible. Nutmeg absolute is a softer and sweeter extract when compared to the essential oil. This lovely quality from Biolandes is very reminiscent of freshly grated nutmeg used in desserts and drinks such as eggnog and classic rice pudding. Nutmeg absolute is the perfect material to bridge the gap between spice materials and wood chemicals. Small amounts are all that are needed for a gentle heart to base note spice that blends particularly well with fruit, wood and other spice materials. This absolute is one of the materials in the Mandy Aftel Natural Perfume Oil Kit. Kiwi Rice Pudding Recipe While this Nutmeg Absolute must not be used in cooking, here is a fun and easy recipe for Rice Pudding, a classic New Zealand pudding from the national treasure known as the Edmonds Cookbook: 5 Tbsp short grain rice 2 Tbsp white sugar 3 cups Full-cream milk (alt: half and half) 2–3 drops of vanilla extract 1 Tbsp butter ¼ tsp nutmeg grated Combine first four ingredients in an oven dish and rest for thirty minutes. Dot with butter and grate nutmeg over the top. Bake for two or three hours at 150c (300f), stirring occasionally during the first hour. Origin: France Part: Seeds Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Nutmeg Oil, Aceh
missing_other.description: Nutmeg is a very versatile spice which blends extremely well with modern woody aroma chemicals imparting complexity and naturalness. It is a rather key material in Fahrenheit (1988) by Dior and Vetiver (1959) by Guerlain. Demo formulas for both can be found below. This Nutmeg oil is a speciality product of Payan Bertrand which is prized for having a particularly low methyl eugenol and safrole content, making it suitable for use at higher doses under IFRA 51 (up to 25% of your finished product). This is ethically sourced and is not molecular distilled, the low allergens are entirely a naturally occurring quality resulting from the selection of particularly fine nutmeg fruit.

missing_other.title: Oak Barrel CO2
tags: locale:pot for pure only. 10% needs no heat.
missing_other.description: This is the same material as Vigon's Oakwood CO2. It differs from our LMR Oakwood CO2, Extra which has a strongly smoked wood quality. When constructing a boozy spirit note, this Oak Barrel CO2 is our first choice. For a peaty whisky accord I'd recommend the LMR product, and for a decidedly sweet and sticky woody blend, Ventos' Oakwood Base is second to none. If you are looking for a powerfully intense smoked wood, I recommend our Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 which is modelled on a genuine 180 year old bottle of classic French perfumery birch tar.

missing_other.title: Oakmoss DEC Abs MD 55% TEC
missing_other.description: Note: This is IFRA compliant and our recommended go to oakmoss. One of the downsides to the restriction on oakmoss being coupled with the need to remove certain chemicals from it is that you can be left with a somewhat flaccid absolute. The great Laboratoire Monique Remy (LMR) has solved this problem with this molecular distilled IFRA compliant oakmoss absolute. The material is as colourless as oakmoss can get (being a very pale orange) but it punches well above its pay grade. It is pre-diluted by LMR at the laboratory in non-natural triethyl citrate so it is not suitable for natural perfumers. While we love pure unadulterated green Oakmoss for non-commercial use, this special molecular distilled product is our general oakmoss of choice. It is rich, intense, longer lastinging than all others (so much so it is almost hard to believe) and truest to the scent of the classic green Yugoslavian oakmoss used in the original Chypre by Coty. If you only buy one oakmoss, this is the one. We also stock original pure and natural non-IFRA compliant green oakmoss absolute from the former Yugoslovia, diluted to 50% in natural triethyl citrate for your convenience, making it suitable for natural fragrances.

missing_other.title: Oakmoss Green Absolute
tags: locale:Paste pot for pure only. High heat for pure.
missing_other.description: When Francois Coty created the great feminine masterpiece Chypre , there was only one oakmoss he would accept: pure and natural green Yugoslavian oakmoss. He adored it so much that he used a whopping 8% in that famous fragrance. Over the forthcoming decades all other perfumers used the same product - from Ernest Beaux with No 5 for Chanel, all the way up to the 21st century when tragically pure and natural oakmoss was restricted by IFRA and only permitted if it were chemically altered to remove atranol. Most suppliers today only stock the chemically altered brown IFRA compliant oakmoss which lacks a lot of the beauty of this product. But not all... we are absolutely thrilled to be able to offer pure and natural Yugoslavian green oakmoss absolute. This is not IFRA compliant. Despite that, it still finds many uses and is still permitted in numerous regions of the world. Needless to say, this incredibly rich and beautiful material is essential for recreating the classic scents of yesteryear. This is classic green oakmoss absolute sold pure (as a solid material) or in liquid form diluted to 50% in natural odourless triethyl citrate. We also offer an IFRA compliant oakmoss absolute (pure or at 50% dilution) from Laboratoire Monique Remy (LMR). Origin: Nations of the former Yugoslavia Part: Moss Method of production: Solvent extraction in Grasse

missing_other.title: Oakmoss “IFRA 43” Absolute
missing_other.description: One of the tragedies of modern perfume legislation is the ban on pure and natural oakmoss and the severe restriction on low-atranol versions of the same. Thankfully we have wonderful synthetics available to us such as evernyl, but those alone can not convey the true beauty of oakmoss. That's where this rich and intense IFRA compliant oakmoss absolute from LMR comes in. This is the ultimate IFRA-safe oakmoss absolute, tweaked to remove the banned material atranol. This oakmoss is earthy, green, sweet and the closest IFRA compliant material to the original product so beloved by Coty when he created Chypre. The original formula of that wonderful fragrance is below — simply replace the pure and natural green oakmoss with this product for a less allergenic version, but do bear in mind that this material is still restricted to a low 0.1% of your finished fine fragrance if you intend to commercialise it. Oakmoss absolute is extremely viscous so in addition to this 100% pure version, we are also offering it at a 10% and 50% dilution in natural triethyl citrate. We also stock original pure and natural non-IFRA compliant green oakmoss absolute from the former Yugoslavia and the most wonderful decolourised IFRA compliant oakmoss also from LMR. Origin: Macedonia Part: Moss Method of production: Extraction in Grasse

missing_other.title: Oakwood CO2 Extra
missing_other.description: This is the most perfect encapsulation of the scent of smoky and newly sawn oak. Oakwood CO2 from LMR is so good you'll want to build an entire fragrance around it! Blend it with a smoky base like Bouleau Pyrogene 1840 and an overdose of Orbitone® T for a modern scent. This is quite a dark viscous material at 60% (the default dilution from LMR) so we also offer it further diluted to 10%. Oakwood CO2 is an upcycled product because it is made from offcuts of oak used in the manufacture of superior aging barrels for the fine wine industry. In the words of LMR: “Creating unique, sustainably sourced natural extracts starts with the precise selection of the best trees. In the interests of protecting the environment and sustaining a quality resource, this sourcing of the best oakwoods by our partner has been awarded PEFC certification, as it meets very demanding specifications in compliance with the French National Forests Office. Together with IFF perfumers, LMR scientists have established a precise burning process for the discarded oakwood chips, to bring out the exact aromas desired by perfumers. The result: sustainable, unique, and memorable extracts that make waste beautiful.”

missing_other.title: Oeillet 208
missing_other.description: The great Oeillet 208 used in Chypre by Coty and the great L'Air du Temps . This is a wonderfully sweet carnation base which perfectly complements and extends the life of Dianthus . Thanks to a revolutionary Fraterworks® Isoeugenol replacer, we are able to offer this base for the first time in decades at an astonishing high safe usable level of 8.9% of the finished product. And just like the original, this base is richly floralised with natural absolutes and essential oils. A truly beautiful and realistic carnation. Used in Emir by Jean Carles for Dana, Fête (Molyneux), Fleurs de Roacaille (Caron), L'Air du Temps (Nina Ricci) and Cartier's Panthère .

missing_other.title: Olibanum Absolute
missing_other.description: Biolandes has a number of products in which they truly shine. When it comes to resins we have a range from a number of suppliers, but when it comes to a reference olibanum resinoid (via alcohol extraction) no one can beat this incredibly beautiful extract. Olibanum Absolute is a solid (fragrant dry pebbles in various sizes) so we offer it pure and in a 50% solution in TEC. If you are looking for other options we also have the highly popular Olibanol , Biolandes' Olibanum Coeur MD , Payan Bertrand's Frankincense Essential Oil and the historic Olibanum CNC base formerly of Chuit Naef and Cie.

missing_other.title: Olibanum CNC
missing_other.description: Olibanum CNC is one of the finest Chuit Naef bases from the early 20th century. It incorporates the noblest aspects of the frankincense tree (Omani Boswellia sacra ) — from the pure heart of the resin to the sacred essential oil. Olibanum CNC is richly floralised with pure and natural oils and absolutes and further enriched with the highest quality aroma chemicals. This base was so beloved that it extended past company boundaries and great perfumers with no connection to Chuit Naef & Cie (perfumers such as Jean Carles,) used it liberally in some of their greatest creations, for example Miss Dior . Olibanum CNC can be used in traces to impart a fine frankincense note through the entire life of a fragrance, or in overdose for a special cachet. Olibanum CNC is practically a perfume unto itself and it transports you to the wonderous ancient orient from whence came the Three Magi, golden pharaonic dynasties, and incense clouded sultanates.

missing_other.title: Olibanum CO2
missing_other.description: Olibanum CO₂ is the ultimate embodiment of frankincense resin, capturing its sacred essence in exquisite fullness. Unlike traditional distillations, this superior extraction retains both delicate, ethereal notes and deeper, resinous facets often lost in the process. Its profound, aroma evokes ancient rituals and spiritual serenity, unfolding with remarkable presence and longevity to lend depth and character to sophisticated fragrance compositions. Olibanum CO₂ shines at concentrations between 0.5–2%, anchoring fragrances with a compelling intensity. It blends beautifully with the dark sweetness of myrrh , the amber warmth of labdanum , and the structured elegance of cedar wood and vetiver extracts . Introduced into heart and base accords, it imparts a timeless, grounding dimension.

missing_other.title: Olibanum Resinoid Vulcain
missing_other.description: “ Introibo ad altare Dei ,” intones the priest as he ascends the steps to the altar amidst billowing clouds of frankincense and myrrh. Anyone who has attended a high mass knows well that fragrant scent of sacred smoke; but in fact its connection to religious places transcends faiths. Olibanum Resinoid Vulcain from Firmenich is that odour. Singularly, it encapsulates the fullness of the most common incense blends used in Church and it is most certainly the most important extract to use when replicating it. Vulcain is Firmenich's term for pyrogenation, the act of heating a raw material to create novel olfactory profiles. This process works well on all types of resins but its effect is particularly well observed with olibanum. The raw material is very viscous (albeit pourable at slightly higher than room temperature) so we also offer it diluted to 50% in odourless natural triethyl citrate for the benefit of natural perfumers and those who prefer working with mobile liquids.

missing_other.title: Olive Fruit Absolute
missing_other.description: What a rare treasure this one is! Olive fruit absolute has a rich, fruity-green aroma with distinctive fatty, oily notes and subtle nuances of freshly cut grass, green leaves, and ripe olives. It is an amazing and unusual material with the very distinctly unctuous lactonic character rarely seen in a natural. It has an amazing ability buff away all the sharpness of green chemicals which makes it suitable for all manner of natural replacers that rely heavily on synthetics. We highly recommend it.

missing_other.title: Ombre d’Iris
missing_other.description: Ombre d'Iris is a co-distillation — iris distilled directly onto cedarwood, producing aromatic compounds that neither material creates alone. This is not a blend. When two botanicals are distilled together, heat and steam generate new molecules at the interface, yielding a material with qualities impossible to achieve by simply mixing the finished oils. The result here is cedarwood transformed into something older, lonelier, and infinitely more complex — aged wood panels glowing with a century of shellac, and somewhere behind them, the powdery violet-root signature of iris drifting like a memory. The cedar announces itself first. But as the material develops on a blotter, the iris emerges — not as a dominant note but as a spectral presence woven through the wood. It does not compete with the cedar; it haunts it. There is a quality of dusty enclosed space, of books in rooms with closed doors, of fireplaces that haven't been lit in decades but whose stone still carries the memory. This is beautiful enough to wear undiluted as a skin scent. Combine it with Osmanthe sur Gurjun for a complete perfume — the sweet, physical osmanthus against this shadowy iris-cedar creates something extraordinary with nothing else needed. Alternatively, use it beneath any floral to add woody-powdery depth that reads as effortlessly expensive.

missing_other.title: Opoponax 216
missing_other.description: Created by a master perfumer at Chuit Naef & Cie in its earliest days, Opoponax 216 differs from Opoponax Doux in that it has a more intense vanilla note and subdued woods. It was favoured by the early Guerlain perfumers and featured in the original Jicky of 1889 with a wonderful overdose of Mysore sandalwood. It was also the key amber of Arpège by Lanvin. Usable at up to 16.6% for IFRA compliance, this is a very versatile and luscious base, rich with all the usual resins and luxurious naturals such as aged patchouli and Mysore sandalwood.

missing_other.title: Opoponax Doux
missing_other.description: This is the famous opoponax base beloved by Coty and used in L'Origan and Chypre . Additionally it was used in numerous perfumes by Guerlain, including an early formula of Jicky . Opoponax Doux is a wonderfully balanced and rich amber base loaded with all the finest resins balanced with the perfect dose of fresh citrus oils and sweet vanilla. The historic opoponax type base is a little confusing because "opoponax" is also the name of a resin used in perfume. However, opoponax bases are a type of ambreine base - artful blends of vanilla, citrus, resins and other luxurious naturals. The main difference is that opoponax bases are narcotic while ambreine bases are erogenous. This means they are synergistic. Combinations of Opoponax Doux and Ambreine are found through many historic perfumes and were particular favourites of Coty and Guerlain. This opoponax base is very similar to the other historic base Balsamol .

missing_other.title: Opoponax Doux, Natural
missing_other.description: This is a 100% natural edition of the famous opoponax base beloved by Coty and used in L'Origan and Chypre . It was also used in numerous perfumes by Guerlain, including an early formula of Jicky . Opoponax Doux is a wonderfully balanced and rich amber base loaded with all the finest resins balanced with the perfect dose of fresh citrus oils and sweet vanilla. The historic opoponax type base is a little confusing because "opoponax" is also the name of a resin used in perfume. However, opoponax bases are a type of ambreine base - artful blends of vanilla, citrus, resins and other luxurious naturals. The main difference is that opoponax bases are narcotic while ambreine bases are erogenous. This means they are synergistic. Combinations of Opoponax Doux and Ambreine Samuelson are found through many historic perfumes and were particular favourites of Coty and Guerlain. This opoponax base is very similar to the other historic base Balsamol . For a great blend, try 2% Opoponax Doux Natural with 0.8% Ambreine Natural .

missing_other.title: Opoponax Oil
missing_other.description: Opoponax Oil is resinous, spicy, and immediately evocative of ancient incense rituals. The distinctive mushroom-earthy undertones emerge quickly, adding savoury complexity that sets this material apart from simpler balsams. Subtle animalic facets provide depth, while a curious broth-like richness (somewhat like vegetable soup or lovage) makes this one of the more characterful naturals in our arsenals. Often called "sweet myrrh," opoponax belongs to the same Burseraceae family as myrrh and frankincense but offers a distinctly sweeter, less medicinal profile. Where myrrh is sharp and slightly bitter, opoponax is warm and effervescent. Use it in oriental compositions where its sweet-spicy balsamic character anchors heavier notes, or in chypres where it adds unexpected sweet lift. The mushroom-earthy facet works beautifully in leather accords and dark florals. Blend with labdanum, benzoin, myrrh, frankincense, sandalwood, and patchouli for classic resinous effects. The animalic depth makes it valuable in natural perfumery seeking complexity without synthetic musks. Opoponax Oil vs Myrrh Oil These two Commiphora oils share family character but differ meaningfully. Myrrh (Commiphora myrrha) is sharper, more medicinal, with bitter-aromatic facets and a drier, more austere profile. Opoponax is sweeter, warmer, more balsamic, with that distinctive mushroom-broth richness and subtle animalic depth. Use myrrh when you want incense severity and bitter complexity; reach for opoponax when you need sweet balsamic warmth with savoury intrigue. They layer beautifully together, with opoponax softening myrrh's medicinal edge while myrrh adds structure to opoponax's sweetness.

missing_other.title: Opoponax Resinoid 50% TEC
missing_other.description: Opoponax resinoid is not as common today as it should be, perhaps due to its hardness (hence being offered here at 50% in natural odourless triethyl citrate). It is also known as sweet myrrh which is understandable as it has a delightfully sweet caramel note making it especially valuable nowadays due to the popularity of gourmand scents. Unsurprisingly it blends well with other gourmand notes and with the other perfumery resins. Opoponax resinoid is not to be confused with the unrelated amber bases sold under the same name. In the words of the great Steffen Arctander, " Opoponax is a natural oleo-gum-resin, formed as a physiological product in natural cavities or tubular vessels in the parenchym (where most of the tree’s activity takes place,) between the bark and the wood. Harvesters make incisions in the trunks, but some opoponax flows out by itself. The crude botanical product is dark reddish, rarely dark yellow or brownish, and it occurs in comparatively regular lumps, tear shaped or bean shaped, of nut size to walnut size. Its odor is sweet-aromatic, reminiscent of spicy soups (a faint resemblance to celery or lovage,) a sweet-woody undertone, and a peculiar, animal-like, also sweet and root-like note. Although to a certain degree reminiscent of myrrh, the typical difference is that opoponax has a spicy, and an animal, root-like note, neither of which is hardly, if at all, distinguishable in myrrh. The difference in odor is wide." Origin: Ethiopia Variety: Commiphora erythraea glabrescens Part: Exudate Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Orange Blossom Supreme
missing_other.description: Orange Blossom Supreme is so realistic you can't tell it apart from natural orange blossom absolute from Morocco. Rich with natural oils and true to the spirit of the genuine material, you can entirely eliminate the need to purchase orange blossom absolute once you switch to this product. Luxury companies like Creed and Amouage use identical products in their fragrances to keep costs low despite their reputation as haute perfume houses. Try our proof of concept demonstration formula for Green Irish Tweed below to see why. We also stock the famous Fleur D'Oranger historic fantasy base that was used in L'Origan by Coty and Tabu by Jean Carles for Dana.

missing_other.title: Orange Flower Absolute, Egypt
missing_other.description: The molten sun surrenders to the horizon as jackals bay into the vast indifferent night. Linen-clad priests murmur prayers to long-forgotten gods and golden braziers cast tendrils of acrid smoke amongst baskets of ripe figs burst open in the dying heat. The thick air is filled with the scent of orange blossoms and lotus flowers. This is ancient Egypt; mysterious, opulent and eternal. This is the imagery evoked when smelling this stunning and rare orange blossom absolute from LMR. Whilst most suppliers offer Moroccan and Tunisian varieties of orange blossom absolute, LMR products this little-known radiant treasure of the old orient. While this has less of the rich honeyed notes of other varieties, it has a complex profile that embodies more of the entire tree and environment. This is dirtier, but in the direction of earthy rather than indolic. If we were to sum up the key differences between the three origins, we would say the following: Egypt : Fresh, luminous, airy, radiant, aldehydic, exotic, refined, transparent, elegant, complex. Tunisia : Rich, warm, floral, opulent, honeyed, deep, creamy, smooth, full-bodied, inviting. Morocco : Intense, balsamic, deep, narcotic, animalic, sultry, luxurious, smoky, heady, seductive. As with all high-cost naturals, we offer this diluted in natural TEC or pure.

missing_other.title: Orange Flower Absolute, Tunisia
missing_other.description: This is the orange blossom the world means when it says orange blossom. The bitter orange has been grown around Nabeul for centuries, and its flowers, gathered by hand in a few short weeks of spring and extracted at the peak of their freshness, yield the absolute against which every other origin is measured. This absolute is rich, honeyed and warm, a creamy white-floral heart that opens into a sweet, faintly waxy depth without ever tipping into the animalic. Where the Egyptian material is luminous and airy and the Moroccan dark and narcotic, the Tunisian sits in the golden middle: full-bodied, smooth and inviting, the very picture of the flower on the branch. It is the most familiar of the three and the most dependable, which is why it is so often the first one reached for. If there is to be only one orange flower absolute on your bench, this is the one it ought to be. If we were to sum up the key differences between the three origins, we would say the following: Egypt : Fresh, luminous, airy, radiant, aldehydic, exotic, refined, transparent, elegant, complex. Tunisia : Rich, warm, floral, opulent, honeyed, deep, creamy, smooth, full-bodied, inviting. Morocco : Intense, balsamic, deep, narcotic, animalic, sultry, luxurious, smoky, heady, seductive. As with all high-cost naturals, we offer this diluted in natural TEC or pure.

missing_other.title: Orange Flower Water
missing_other.description: Vallebona, a town in the Province of Imperia in the Italian region of Liguria has been home for seven generations to the family of Pietro Guglielmi. La Vecchia Distilleria, the family distillery, has been lovingly restored by Guglielmi under the watchful eye of his 97 year old grandmother who helps pick and sort the blossoms from their many bitter orange trees. La Vecchia Distilleria makes neroli oil, but the item of especial interest for us is the left over water from that process. We wanted only the very best orange flower water (hydrosol) for our colognes and our search ended here. The Guglielmi family puts as much love and care into the production of their flower water as they do their neroli oil. And for that reason we had to have it. Below is a demonstration formula for Eau de Coty which demonstrates the use of floral waters in fragrance making. NOTE: Adding water to a fragrance is always a risky undertaking that can lead to clouding. Always chill and filter fragrances before bottling.

missing_other.title: Orange Flower Water Absolute
missing_other.description: Orange Flower Water Absolute is a byproduct of the manufacture of neroli oil. It is made by solvent washing the water and materials remaining after the distillation of orange flowers for other purposes. The material is wonderfully rich despite being secondary product and has an intensely earthy quality absent from the oil and absolute of orange blossoms making it ideal as a nuancer and enricher of those products. Orange Flower Water Absolute is harsher but less indolic than Orange Blossom Absolute or Neroli Oil.

missing_other.title: Orange Heart
missing_other.description: Orange Heart is the warmest of the LMR citrus hearts. Where Lime and Lemon Hearts push zesty brightness, this one pushes richness — a deep, juicy, almost candied orange-peel sweetness that sits in the heart of a composition like sunlight through amber glass. It is unmistakably orange but with a depth that standard sweet orange oil never achieves. This is an LMR speciality — a concentrated citrus fraction developed to boost the citrus profile at very low dosage. Standard sweet orange oil is beautiful but notoriously fleeting — it can vanish from a composition within the first hour. Orange Heart anchors that warmth. Use it when you need the golden sweetness of orange to carry through into the drydown alongside woods, vanillas, and ambers. A natural partner for oriental and gourmand compositions. Try a touch in tonka-vanilla bases for a luminous citrus lift, or blend with our Bergamot Oil FCF (Côte d'Ivoire) and Cinnamon Absolute for a sun-drenched hesperidic accord with unusual warmth and gentle spice.

missing_other.title: Orchidée № 2
missing_other.description: De Laire produced two orchid bases, Orchidée №s 1 & 2. Fraterworks Orchidée № 2 is a restoration of the latter — the more floral and historically more popular and widely used base. Orchids are generally odourless and in perfumery circles the term is commonly used to refer to clover ( treflé ) or salicylate based fantasy aromas. Orchidée is no exception. Rich with natural floral absolutes, aldehydes and luxurious musks, this is a top to bottom base that can be used alone as a wonderful fragrance, or as part of a new fragrance. Usable in large quantities (up to 29% of your finished product), Orchidée is a perfect alternative to the far more common heart note synthetics (hedione and the like) around which most modern fragrances tend to be built. For a touch of je ne sais quoi , look no further than Fraterworks Orchidée .

missing_other.title: Orris Absolute, France
tags: locale:CHECK DILUTION! This is 160 thousand dollars a kilo
missing_other.description: Iris is perhaps the most esteemed natural in perfumery. It comes in multiple forms depending on use and Fraterworks stocks all of them! Orris is a complex material so here is a little primer on the types. Orris Tincture (variable Irones): Clear liquid. Alcohol extract from powdered iris roots. Orris Resinoid (1 – 10% Irones): Dark brown thick paste. Alcohol extracted. Orris Butter (10 – 20% Irones): Solid white wax. Also sometimes called orris concrete or orris essential oil. Steam distillation. Orris Absolute (80% Irones): Clear liquid. Almost never available for retail sale. Orris absolute is rarely seen in modern fragrances; the most notable recent exception was the masterpiece Dior Homme (2005 edition) with 0.25% and 0.3% in Iris Ganache (Guerlain, 2007). Of all the orris materials, the absolute has the most profoundly strong scent of orris root and a little goes a long way which is fortunate because the price is eye watering. This orris absolute is from orris Pallida.

missing_other.title: Orris Germanica Butter
missing_other.description: Orris Butter is renowned in perfumery for its luxurious aroma and this Germanica concrete is the finest example of the material. While Orris Pallida is the most common source of iris butter, the Germanica product has nuances it lacks. Germanica iris is creamier, more balanced and a little less powdery. Obtaining orris butter is a years-long process that involves digging up and curing the rhizomes, followed by a highly specialised distillation. The final product is a solid material with a butterscotch colour that melts to the touch. Sourced from the top supplier in Grasse, our Orris Germanica Butter is the most perfect quality, surpassing all other online offerings. Additionally, because our supplier is the world leader, a constant supply is assured. This is the gold standard with Chinese origin rhizomes far surpassing the cheaper Moroccan variety in beauty.

missing_other.title: Orris Germanica Resinoid
missing_other.description: With the highest fixative power of all the iris products, orris resinoid is a hidden gem that far too few perfumers take advantage of. This should not be confused with orris butter which is actually a true essential oil; orris resinoid is deep brown in colour while orris butter (also known as orris concrete) is a white waxy solid. In addition to being a great fixative, Orris Resinoid imparts a lovely sweet Iris root note quite similar to that of orris powder but more intense and certainly more compatible with perfumery. This is perhaps the truest scent of the rhizome as the concrete (essential oil) has a far lighter and less earthy scent. We are selling this resinoid pure and in a 50% dilution in natural (EU & US) Triethyl Citrate as it is difficult to work with pure as it is highly viscous. Please ensure you select the right dilution from the options. In addition to this well priced Germanica resinoid, we also stock the more expensive Orris Pallida Resinoid which is more floral and deep and less powdery. Origin: Morocco Part: Roots Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Orris Givco® 204/20
missing_other.description: Orris Givco is a modern Givaudan base for contributing orris notes to a fragrance. It was designed to mimic orris absolute and orris butter but in reality it is brighter and more radiant than both. The steady reduction in natural orris materials in the base over time (due to cost) means that it can benefit from the addition of small amounts of natural iris butter or resinoid ( Germanica or Pallida ) also. If you are looking for a richer and more luxurious alternative we recommend the great Orrisodore which featured in Jacques Fath's famous Iris Gris (1946, Vincent Roubert — download formula ) and Paco Rabanne's Calandre (1969, Michael Hy).

missing_other.title: Orris Imperial
missing_other.description: The price of orris butter has risen exponentially in recent years, placing it beyond the reach of most perfumers. Yet its role remains indispensable—it anchors floral hearts with sophisticated depth, bridges woody and powdery elements seamlessly, and acts as a fixative that amplifies surrounding notes while slowing their evaporation. The complex interplay of over 200 aromatic compounds, particularly the precious irones that develop during aging, creates effects no single synthetic can replicate. Orris Imperial answers this challenge with a replacer rich in irones that matches natural orris butter's character and radiating power. Use it one-for-one wherever orris butter appears in formulae, bringing the same violet-suede elegance and fixative strength without compromise. When replacing orris absolute, increase the quantity fourfold to achieve equivalent impact. This allows you to work with one of perfumery's most refined materials without the prohibitive cost that has made true orris butter practically vanish from perfumers' shelves.

missing_other.title: Orris Pallida Butter
tags: locale:do not melt - use a glass jar for pure and scrape material
missing_other.description: Orris Pallida Butter 15% Irones (sometimes called concrete) is a solid essential oil that strikes with its signature powdery violet character—soft yet penetrating, creamy yet dry. This waxy white material captures the essence of aged iris rhizomes from Italian Tuscany, rich in gamma-irone that develops only through years of patient maturation. Its scent hovers between floral delicacy and woody earthiness, with unexpected fruity facets that peek through like raspberry sherbet dusted with cocoa. Use this precious material primarily as a fixative where its tenacity amplifies and anchors surrounding notes without dominating them. Pair it with rose absolute and sandalwood to build elegant floral-woody structures, or combine it with vetiver and labdanum for sophisticated chypre bases. Its powdery character transforms aldehydic compositions, whilst its fatty richness smooths sharp citrus and adds creamy depth to berry accords. Apply it sparingly—even at high dilution, its strength emerges dramatically in the dry-down. We also stock Orris Germanica butter .

missing_other.title: Orris Pallida “Signature” Resinoid
missing_other.description: With the highest fixative power of all the orris products, this is a hidden gem that far too few perfumers take advantage of. This should not be confused with orris butter which is actually a true essential oil; orris resinoid is deep brown in colour while orris butter (also known as orris concrete) is a creamy white waxy solid. We are selling this resinoid at 50% dilution in natural odourless triethyl citrate as it is almost impossible to work with pure as it is so viscous that it borders on solid. We are, however, also supplying it pure so please check your selected dilution. This resinoid contains a maximum irone load of 1.7%. We also stock the lower cost more powdery Orris Germanica resinoid . Origin: Italy Part: Roots Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Orris Root CO2
missing_other.description: Orris Root CO2 (3% Irones) opens with a cool, powdery breath of violet that softens immediately into buttery cream and warm suede. Beneath that elegance sits a damp, earthy rootiness - almost carrot-like - that gives the material its grounding character. The overall impression is of vintage face powder resting on warm skin. The odour impression of the 10% variant (diluted in IPM which keeps it crystal clear and liquid even at very low temperatures) is that of orris absolute , making this an excellent way to naturalise irone alpha when cost is a consideration. This material functions as a powerful structural bridge between floral hearts and woody bases, smoothing harsh transitions and rounding sharp edges. Add it to rose accords for a couture finish or pair it with ionones and methylionones to build a convincing lipstick accord. Try it in trace amounts alongside sandalwood to amplify creaminess, or with vetiver to accentuate its suede-woody facets. Combine with aldehydes C-11 Undecylenic and C-12 Lauric (the classic French iris aldehyde) to soften their metallic bite into something polished. Keep your dosage restrained - too much orris will flatten a composition into dry, cosmetic monotony.

missing_other.title: Orris Root Tincture 10%
missing_other.description: Orris root tincture is a powdery soft iris product with a marvellous fixative property. It blends very well with fruit notes giving them grounding and naturalisation. It has a long history in perfumery where it joins the other plant based fixatives such as the popular tincture of benzoin and extracts of ambrette seed. Fraterworks produces this tincture in the classical French manner using nothing but rich and buttery dried and powdered iris roots and pure and natural ethanol produced using water from southern alpine glaciers. Orris root tincture is a dependable and trusted material that fits in to virtually any context. It can be used alongside or in place of Poudre à la Maréchale tincture . Also known as: orris rhizome tincture or iris root tincture.

missing_other.title: Orrisodore™
missing_other.description: Orrisodore™ is the supreme iris base. Rich with orris butter, iris resin, iris absolute, mysore sandalwood and so many other regal naturals, this base is the glory of the golden age encapsulated. One drop adds an indescribable iris beauty to your scent, while an overdose gives you a fragrance fit for a sultan. Just add peach and you have a perfume that makes Fath's Iris Gris seem mediocre.

missing_other.title: Osmanthe sur Gurjun
missing_other.description: Osmanthe sur Gurjun is a co-distillation — osmanthus flowers distilled directly onto gurjun balsam, producing aromatic compounds that neither material creates alone. This is not a blend. When two botanicals are distilled together, heat and steam generate new molecules at the interface, yielding a material with qualities impossible to achieve by simply mixing the finished oils. The result here is osmanthus at its most extravagant: sweet, sticky, overwhelmingly present, with the gurjun providing body and balsamic warmth without ever competing. The osmanthus dominates from the first moment — ripe apricot, suede, the full multifaceted complexity of the flower in unapologetic expression. Where Payan Bertrand's Fleur de Cuir co-distils osmanthus onto cedarwood for a drier, more restrained effect, our version on gurjun is sweeter, thicker, more lush. The balsamic base acts as a warm platform that amplifies the osmanthus rather than constraining it. The fruit and the leather and the floral facets all come through at once. Add Ombre d'Iris and you have a complete perfume — practically nothing else needed. The sweet, physical osmanthus against that spectral iris-cedar creates a dialogue between substance and shadow, fruit and ghost. Alternatively, use Osmanthe sur Gurjun beneath tuberose or jasmine to add sticky, apricot-skin warmth that no synthetic can replicate.

missing_other.title: Osmanthus Flowers
missing_other.description: Fraterworks Osmanthus Flowers (formerly just called Osmanthus) is an elegant and rich base featuring large amounts of the finest osmanthus oil. With its notes of leather and apricots, this base is a perfect unifier for modern gourmand types. Or simply overdose it for a luxurious and unusual floral fragrance. Osmanthus was a key note in 1,000 by Jean Patou and it is often used as a sweetener or complexing agent. This Fraterworks base is an excellent way to incorporate genuine osmanthus absolute at an unbeatable price.

missing_other.title: Osmanthus Heart
missing_other.description: Apricot, suede, warm milk, and flowers — all from a single natural material. Osmanthus Heart concentrates the most compelling fractions of this famously expensive absolute. The ripe fruit quality is immediate and unmistakable, unlike any synthetic peach or apricot note. Beneath the fruit sits a soft leather character that gives the material its extraordinary complexity. This is one of the rare naturals that provides a genuinely fruity note — most apricot and peach effects in perfumery rely on gamma-decalactone and similar synthetics. Osmanthus Heart delivers that fruit with a floral-animalic depth that no single molecule can match. Use it as the centrepiece of luxury floral compositions where the apricot-suede character becomes the signature. The leather facet makes it a natural bridge between floral hearts and animalic bases without needing a separate leather accord. It enriches rose and jasmine compositions with a fruity warmth. In oud-based compositions, the milky softness tempers harshness. Try it alongside iris butter and sandalwood for the quietest, most refined luxury accord imaginable.

missing_other.title: Osmanthus “Gold” Absolute
missing_other.description: Given it's rarity and price, Osmanthus Absolute is only produced by a few companies at present. There are, of course, the "supreme five": LMR (IFF), Floral Concept, V. MANE Fils, Payan Bertrand and Robertet, and then the mid-range Givaudan (Albert Vielle), and Firmenich. As with all our naturals, we don't seek the lowest prices, we seek the finest products and so we tested all the offerings of the aforementioned (even those at the lower end of the scale). The choice was an easy one: LMR. Rcently LMR has been producing an Osmanthus that simply astonishes. From the succulent scent of ripe apricots to the aristocratic leather scent of a royal stable, this Osmanthus absolute is the reference for this remarkable and exotic oriental flower extract. Smelling this absolute is like smelling Osmanthus all over again for the first time. It is, simply put, breathtaking. Note: this replaces the absolute we were previously selling by V. MANE Fils as it took the crown in our 2025 internal product competition in which we test naturals from a variety of sources. We are selling this at 10% in natural triethyl citrate and pure. If you are looking for something a little lower cost, try our Osmanthus Flowers speciality base or the wonderful Fleur de Cuir , a co-distillation of Osmanthus with Cedarwood by Payan Bertrand.

missing_other.title: Oud Assafi®
missing_other.description: East truly does meet West in this most famous of all wild harvested oud oils. Oud Assafi is the result of a collaboration of Bangladeshi master distillers Jalali Agarwood and Swiss fragrance giant Firmenich. Oud Assafi is intensely animalic and woody with a sweet undertone. It is perceptible in traces (which is fortunate given its high price). For a surprising good (and very cost-effective) extender to this treasured essential oil, blend it with a generous amount of Laine de Mouton absolute . The two are extremely synergistic and the combination allows a perfumer to mimic the effect of an Oud Assafi overdose. Owing to the intensity of this pure oil and the extremely high price, we are also offering it diluted to 1%, 5% and 10% in natural triethyl citrate, a marvellous odourless diluent produced from citrus. If you are purchasing for trade you may need a CITES export certificate (check your nation's regulations). We can assist you with that process which is relatively easy. Contact us for more details and costings.

missing_other.title: Oud Firbest®
missing_other.description: Oud Firbest is Firmenich's general Oud base, balancing woods, florals and animalic notes in such a way as to not focus on a specific terroir or variety of Oud. It was designed to give a consistent and cost-effective realistic oud note in perfumes as natural ouds can vary wildly in odour from batch to batch. It is a versatile base but is particularly well suited to oriental and woody fragrances. Firmenich's Firbest® range contains bases made of both synthetic and natural elements which replicate the scent of a natural extract without containing that extract itself. These bases solve problems often associated with naturals such as extremely high cost or, as mentioned, variability in batch quality. If you are looking for a 5-star alternative to the Firbest range, we also produce our own Oud Intense ™ base which is, in the words of one reviewer: “one of the best oud bases I've tried.” We also offer Oud Laos Firbest —a lighter and more fruity-floral oud base, Pretty Oud , a rich animalic but extremely easy to use Oud base, Oud Synth 184007 a lower cost Firmenich base and Black Agar Givco from Givaudan which is really more fantasy than reality. And for those with the budget for it, we offer Oud Assafi ® a glorious (but eye-wateringly expensive) natural Oud Assam wild harvested in Bangladesh. Alternatively you may like the much more frugal Aetoxylon or White Oud oil from V MANE Fils.

missing_other.title: Oud Intense™
missing_other.description: Wild, radiant and complex Fraterworks® Oud Intense™ is a powerful base offering the full spectrum of notes found in natural oud oil. Oud Intense is built around a fond of rich wood extracts — including, at its heart, 1.2% pure wild Oud Assafi from Bangladesh. The finest synthetic and natural musks add longevity while powerful contemporary molecules add an almost-impossible diffusion and radiance to the whole. Perceptible in traces, dazzling in overdose, Oud Intense is the holy grail of oud bases.

missing_other.title: Oud Laos Firbest®
missing_other.description: Oud Laos Firbest® is the second of Firmenich's Firbest bases to focus on the wonderful world of Ouds. Compared to the more general purpose Oud Firbest, this Laos version aims to replicate the oils from the territory of Laos—oils known to have a lighter, fruitier and more floral character. Both Firbest bases are very similar to one another but if you are seeking a more modern or broadly appealing type, the Oud Laos Firbest option is for you. It is less animalic, greener and certainly more approachable. It also serves as a good starting point for an accord in the direction of Yellow Kynam. Natural Laotian Oud is unique among agarwood varieties. The top notes often present an initial smoky, fruity and balsamic intensity, followed by a heart of leathery spice, musky citrus, and warm florals. The dry-down is notable for its smooth, slightly creamy woodiness, which enhances the overall balance and longevity of the fragrance. Firmenich's Firbest® range contains bases made of both synthetic and natural elements which replicate the scent of a natural extract without containing that extract itself. These bases solve problems often associated with naturals such as extremely high cost or, as mentioned, variability in batch quality. If you are looking for a 5-star alternative to the Firbest range, we also produce our own Oud Intense ™ base which is, in the words of one reviewer: “one of the best oud bases I've tried.” We also offer Oud Firbest —a more general purpose base, Pretty Oud , a rich animalic but extremely easy to use Oud base, Oud Synth 184007 a lower cost Firmenich base and Black Agar Givco from Givaudan which is really more fantasy than reality. And for those with the budget for it, we offer Oud Assafi ® a glorious (but eye-wateringly expensive) natural Oud Assam wild harvested in Bangladesh. Alternatively you may like the much more frugal Aetoxylon or White Oud oil from V MANE Fils.

missing_other.title: Oud Malacca
missing_other.description: Fraterworks Oud Malacca opens with a dank, almost murky hit that immediately signals authentic Malaysian oud character. Rich woody complexity unfolds quickly — resinous depth shot through with a hint of cinnamon warmth and a surprising suggestion of ocean air. A green, almost minty quality rounds out the profile with camphoraceous freshness. Use Oud Malacca base as the foundation of a luxurious oriental — usable at 0.92% of your finished product, it carries the weight. It works equally well as a subtle nuancer where you want oud presence without animalic dominance. Its versatility mirrors the natural oil: equally at home in fresh compositions and deep, resinous accords. Pair with Moroccan rose absolute and Saffron Attar for a classic Middle Eastern accord, or with marine and citrus notes to exploit that oceanic facet. Malaysian oud is the most versatile origin in perfumery — this base belongs in every perfumer's organ. Note: this base contains no natural oud oil and thus is not subject to any CITES restrictions.

missing_other.title: Oud Oil, Vietnam
missing_other.description: LMR's Oud Oil from Vietnam is sweeter and less intensely animal than the better known Oud Assafi from Firmenich. This will sit more politely in your blend, though make no mistakes about it, this is unmistakably oud: dark, foreboding and rich. It also has a price point that is less jaw-dropping. This particular oud comes from a single family-owned Vietnamese distillery that manages four forests of Aquilaria crassna. The trees produce two grades of resinous wood: white wood is distilled into Agarwood Boya Oil, while the higher-resin grey wood becomes this oil — the darker, more animalic of the two. The benefit of buying Oud from LMR or Firmenich is that the sheer size of these companies means the supply is consistent and ongoing. These are oud oils you can trust from batch to batch. If you are purchasing for trade you may need a CITES export certificate (check your nation's regulations). We can assist you with that process which is relatively easy. Contact us for more details and costings.

missing_other.title: Oud Synth 184007
missing_other.description: Firmenich's classic Oud Synth 10760 base has undergone a facelift in order to remove phthalates and furfural for better compliance with customer demands and updated IFRA standards. The odour profile of this new Oud Synth 184007 is very little changed from its predecessor and this is now the only version available from Firmenich. In Firmenich's own words: “A reconstitution of agarwood oil. Intensely woody, animalic and reminiscent of vetiver, with sweet balsamic undertones.” This is one of those oud bases built around a common blend of natural woods with Ambrinol supplying the animalic element. It is a lovely material that blends well with other Oud products. It can be used to add depth and richness to Givaudan's Black Agar Givco.

missing_other.title: Palisandrol 17979F
missing_other.description: Built around a wonderfully high dose of Norlimbanol, Palisandrol is a radiant wood base from Firmenich featured in such fragrances as YSL's M7 (0.5%) and Dolce and Gabanna Light Blue (2007) at 1.5%. With trace captives and a delicate fruity nuance, this is an excellent product to add high impact materials in easier to manage doses. Palisandrol is radiant and extremely diffusive. Palisandrol blends extremely well with Fauxmoss ®, Kephalis , Benzyl Acetone , and wood materials in general.

missing_other.title: Palmarosa Oil
missing_other.description: Palmarosa Oil opens sweet, rosy, and unmistakably floral. A fresh grassy-citrus quality lifts the opening, while gentle metallic and herbaceous undertones add dry complexity. The overall effect is warm, soft, and remarkably close to geranium oil. Use Palmarosa as your workhorse rosy-floral heart. It builds convincing rose, geranium, and carnation accords at a fraction of what rose absolute costs, blending beautifully with bergamot, jasmine, and cedarwood. In lily of the valley and apple blossom compositions, it provides the soft floral body that ties everything together. Don't overlook Palmarosa where you'd never expect a rose note — a trace softens and rounds woody accords beautifully. It adds an almost tea-like freshness to citrus blends. Pair it with oakmoss for an unexpectedly gorgeous chypre foundation.

missing_other.title: Paradise Molecule®
missing_other.description: The most desired material in perfumery today is the captive Paradisone® of Firmenich. Paradisone is the very heart of Hedione®. It offers room filling diffusion and a radiance unequalled… until now. Fraterworks' Paradise Molecule is a blend that mimics the power and beauty of the Firmenich masterpiece and offers an alternative to Hedione and the members of its family. Hedione® can be imagined as putting space between each molecule in a blend, thus causing diffusion (and the corollary of diminishing richness). On the other hand Paradise Molecule has the apparent effect of charging particles, thereby adding an almost impossible cloud of diffusion with no correlated loss of intensity. Use the Paradise Molecule as a one for one replacer for Hedione® and Hedione® High Cis, or in blends with both. Effective from traces to overdose. Keep in a cool dark place place when not in use to maintain its full two year shelf life.

missing_other.title: Patchouli Dark PA30
missing_other.description: This dark patchouli is a full-bodied oil with all the good and none of the bad that can be associated with patchouli oils. It has the most refined and sheer dry down we have ever experienced in an iron distilled patchouli. It is consistently good from top to bottom and for that reason it is our own go-to patchouli oil. Despite patchouli being an earthy material, the less dirty the dry down the higher the prestige. This dark oil has a wonderfully smooth quality that lasts. We tested dark patchouli oils from all the major suppliers in France and Indonesia and even many artisanal manufacturers to offer you the very best dark patchouli. And every year we re-test to ensure we are keeping up with the latest qualities coming from those suppliers. Patchouli is steam distilled using stainless steel or iron distilling units. Oil produced in a stainless steel vat is called “light” and it is the colour of pale straw. The classic iron distilled oil is dark (deep gold through orange to dark brown). The odour profile between the products is similar but the dark oil has a more complex and rich dry down. Origin: Aceh, Indonesia Part: Leaves

missing_other.title: Patchouli Heart MD PA50
missing_other.description: The most sublime part of patchouli oil is the patchouli alcohol (patchoulol). A typical high quality patchouli will have at least 30% with some natural oils going considerably higher, such as our Patchouli Light Aceh with a whopping 38%. Our Patchouli Heart from Floral Concept, one of the finest suppliers of luxury niche naturals in France, is the result of molecular distillation in which some of the unappealing side-notes are removed from the oil giving a significant boost to the patchoulol — fully half in fact. Patchouli Heart MD PA50 is the scent of spring rains falling on freshly furrowed earth. It is the scent of winding rivers through dank woodlands. This patchouli is nature at its best. NOTE: patchouli prices are currently on the rise due to political changes in Indonesia. We are doing our best to absorb some of that impact and there appear to be signs of stabilisation in the industry so we hope there will be no further increases. Origin: Indonesia, processing France Variety: Pogostemon cablin Benth. Part: Leaves

missing_other.title: Patchouli Heart N.3 PA60
missing_other.description: Patchouli Heart N.3 from LMR (Laboratoires Monique Remy) is a molecular distilled COSMOS certified patchouli oil and considered by many to the be the finest example of the type. The patchoulol content of Patchouli Heart N.3 is guaranteed by the LMR lab to be between 52% and 59%, the highest amount found in any of our patchouli collection . This is one of two molecular distilled patchouli oils we offer, the other being Patchouli Heart MD PA50 from Floral Concept. The Floral Concept product has a very soft and subtle opening with an earthy dry down, while this Patchouli Heart N.3 has a more characterful opening and a sweeter and creamier dry down. Both oils are wonderful and bring different nuances to a scent. We use and recommend both. Note: Fraterworks is not a registered COSMOS company so while this product is CSM certified when it reaches us, we cannot use that terminology when we resell.

missing_other.title: Patchouli Heart SFE
missing_other.description: Patchouli Heart SFE is a CO2 extract of dried patchouli leaves. Notably, it lacks sesquiterpenes— heavier, less fragrant molecules like caryophyllene or germacrene—which are typically present in steam-distilled oils. This removal enhances purity and creates a cleaner, more focused scent. Patchouli Heart SFE evolves into a softer, more harmonious note, sometimes with minty undertones. The absence of sesquiterpenes reduces the raw, heavy earthiness, making it more versatile and elegant for modern perfumery.

missing_other.title: Patchouli Light Aceh PA38
missing_other.description: This light patchouli oil from Aceh in Indonesia is so balanced that it's hard to believe it is not molecular distilled. Yet it is 100% pure and natural and still boasts a whopping 38% patchouli alcohol content (standard patchouli is usually 30% or lower). Since the ancient days of the sultanate of Aceh, patchouli from this region has been revered and it was an item of trade with the English East India Company (along with black pepper) in its heyday. Aceh is to patchouli as Île de Bourbon is to geranium and Comoros to ylang-ylang . Patchouli is steam distilled either using stainless steel or iron distilling units. Oil produced in a stainless steel vat is called “light” and it is the colour of pale straw. The classic iron distilled oil is dark (deep gold through orange to dark brown). The odour profile between the products is similar but in the long dry down the light oil is cleaner. Despite being an earthy oil, the less dirty the dry down the higher the prestige.
