This light oil is naturally high in patchouli alcohol, the heart of the oil with virtually no dirty qualities, and so the oil has one of the sweetest and softest dry downs possible in a pure and natural patchouli oil. For modern fragrances requiring a refined and regal patchouli note, this is the oil you need. Origin: Aceh, Indonesia Variety: Pogostemon cablin Benth. Part: Leaves

missing_other.title: Pear Belle
missing_other.description: Pear Belle is, as its name suggests, beautiful. It is the entire pear: flesh, skin and foliage. No pear base better represents the most beloved childhood fruit as this one from Fraterworks. Pear Belle blends beautifully with gourmand notes and citrus, as well as patchouli and vanilla. It is used to great effect in Infanta by Frater Perfumes and it adds an touch of elegance in all uses. “The pear tree was in full bloom, and its faint, sweet scent drifted through the open window, making her feel as if she were floating.” — Bliss (1918), Katherine Mansfield

missing_other.title: Peony Storm
missing_other.description: Peony (known as pivoine in French) is one of the most beautiful flowers to behold, from bud to blossom. The delicate odour is reminiscent of roses (indeed most classic peony bases rely on many of the same aroma chemicals) with the key difference being a lightly waxed quality and a faintly almond-like persistence to the peony blossom. As with all our luxurious classical perfumery bases, Peony Storm is loaded with opulent and expensive essential oils and absolutes giving it a truly marvellous natural quality. Peony flowers don't give up a natural essential oil, but with a base as rich and appealing as Peony Storm , it simply doesn't matter.

missing_other.title: Peppermint Oil “Black Mitcham”
missing_other.description: Peppermint oil is one of the most abused and adulterated oils in the fragrance industry, with large quantities of the most common oils (Indian and American) really being cornmint that has been stripped of menthol for the pharmaceutical industry. True French oil is the standard bearer of quality. But there is one other peppermint on the market that blows even the French out of the water: fine aged Peppermint Oil “Black Mitcham” indigenous to England and, after a period of extinction from those green isles, restored to its glory in recent years. Pining for the superior peppermint oil of his youth, Sir Michael Colman (of the Colman's Mustard family) sought out, discovered in far distant America, and restored this glorious plant to its native land where it has now thrived across generations. The black mitchan oil that we stock at Fraterworks is the very oil from Sir Michael's family estate in England. The Colman family produce the oil and age it for two years ensuring utter perfection. Dating back to the 1750s, Peppermint oil "Black Mitcham" is the supreme peppermint. It is the peppermint of candy canes, peppermint creams, and all things wonderfully Wonka. In a side by side comparison with finest French peppermint oil, Black Mitcham is distinctly gourmand. It has a sweetness and even a subtle floralcy that is lacking in the French. Additionally, due to the aging the oil undergoes, the penetrating top notes common to oils of the mentha piperita family are tempered, allowing the full harmony of the oil to be taken in at first sniff. Origin: England Variety: Mentha x piperita L. Part: Leaves Method: Steam distillation at source and aged 2 years

missing_other.title: Perfumer Consultancy
missing_other.description: Harness the mastery of Fraterworks’ founder and chief perfumer in a format that suits your goal—whether you require a swift course-correction or a deeper strategic partnership. Upon purchase you will receive an instant, secure online Non-Disclosure Agreement; once signed, we proceed without delay. Choose the right path Intro Consultation – 20 minutes A concise, outcome-focused session to resolve a specific question, identify the next step in a project, or assess a raw material shortlist. Perfect for first-time callers. Deep-Dive Consultation – 60 minutes A full hour to untangle complex formulation challenges, source hard-to-find ingredients, or map a brand-building strategy. Leave the call with a clear plan of action and written notes. Mentor Pack – 5 × 30-minute sessions Ongoing guidance spread over six months. Ideal for perfumers who wish to refine multiple releases, receive periodic formula reviews, or maintain steady strategic counsel. Formula Critique (off-line consultancy) Email your worksheet; receive an annotated analysis of structure, balance, and improvement opportunities—no live call required. What to expect Book your slot – choose a time in our calendar or purchase a critique. Sign the NDA – a simple digital signature protects your intellectual property. Prepare – send any formulas, briefs, or reference notes at least 24 hours in advance. Meet via video conference (live options) or await your written report (asynchronous critique). Actionable follow-up – receive Jamie’s notes, sourcing links, and next-step recommendations. Jamie Frater has launched multiple million-dollar ventures and guided scores of perfumers from first trials to market release. His counsel unites technical rigour, classical aesthetics, and sound business sense—delivered with warmth, clarity, and respect for your vision. Reserve your consultation today and advance your craft with confidence.

missing_other.title: Periploca Root Oil 10% TEC
missing_other.description: Periploca opens with an unexpected flash of green cucumber before settling into warm, vanillic-almond territory. Think rice milk, toasted marzipan, and cream soda — not straight vanilla but something more complex and interesting. Soft floral facets of heliotrope and mimosa hover in the background. This oil is solid at room temperature, so it comes diluted to ten percent in triethyl citrate. Even diluted, it quietly takes over blends during maceration — dose with real restraint and revisit after several weeks. Use it to add natural vanillic depth to gourmand and oriental accords. Blend with tonka bean and benzoin to amplify the gourmand warmth, or layer beneath white florals for an almond-blossom effect. It also pairs unexpectedly well with vetiver and tobacco. This is not a vanilla substitute — it is something richer and stranger.

missing_other.title: Permawood™
missing_other.description: Permawood™ is a high-performance wood base which is effective from traces but is perfectly suitable for uses up to five percent. It is a top to bottom blend which adds body and strength to the heart of a scent, a luxurious ambery dry down, and a softening and rounding polish to top notes. Permawood™ is composed of extremely modern aroma molcules with a very delicate odour which belies its astonishing power. Permawood™ is all about radiance, rounding and fixing. This is a base which will improve any fragrance to which it is added. Permawood™ can be used as a one-for-one replacer for Fixobois® which has undergone reformulation in recent times. Ambrox DL (EC 942-754-1) and Cetalox (EC 701-326-2) Update: This product contains Ambrox DL or Cetalox. As a result of recent testing, Firmenich has updated the hazards of those two materials to a new hazard category − Reproductive Toxicant Category 2 - H361d: Suspected of damaging the unborn child. Permawood™ is the perfect fixative for Lorysia ®, and Iso E Super ™, and has a synergy with Miraclewood ™, Thujopsene , Ambrexol ™, Ambergris , Saxon Moss , Suralette™ Extra , Verdantol ™ and woody, herbal or green notes in general.

missing_other.title: Persian Lime Oil, FCF
missing_other.description: While the most common lime oil in perfumery is distilled Mexican lime, this Persian Lime (ex Mexico) is expressed (cold pressed), giving a truer and more complex lime impression. Additionally, this LMR speciality is rectified to reduce the harmful furoucoumarins making it a really great alternative to the safe distilled oil without losing parts of the lime profile. Cold pressed lime retains the most natural, zesty, and vibrant aroma of the lime peel. Due to the risk of oxidation over the long term, a touch of BHT or Tocopherol (less than 0.1%) is recommended if you plan to store this oil. Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. This is a lovely and rare lime oil and one that all perfumers should try, even if you already have the distilled oil. Note: this contains 0.1% tocopherol as a preservative, added by LMR at the source.

missing_other.title: Persicol
missing_other.description: Persicol is one of the most famous classical bases, being first used in Nuit de Chine (1913—formula below) by Maurice Schaller for Paul Poiret's Les Parfums de Rosine, but most famously ten years later as the key peach note at 0.4% pure in Mitsouko (1919) by Jacques Guerlain. It also featured in Bois des Îles by Ernest Beaux for Chanel with 4% Ambre Solide . Contrary to popular belief, Persicol (created by Chuit Naef & Cie) is not a synonym for the chemical undecalactone gamma (so-called Aldehyde C-14) which was patented in 1908 but an achingly sweet peach base featuring that chemical to exploit and demonstrate its commercial uses to perfumers of the day, just as De Laire created Mousse de Saxe to market the then recently discovered chemical isobutyl quinoline. Persicol is used in the same way as undecalactone gamma and can be used as a one for one replacer.

missing_other.title: Peru Balsam Essential Oil
tags: Locale:Thin oil not resin or absolute
missing_other.description: Peru Balsam Essential Oil opens with a remarkably different character than its resinoid sibling—where the resinoid overwhelms with dense vanilla sweetness, the steam-distilled oil whispers amber sophistication. This clear, pale gold liquid captures the ethereal aspects of the crude balsam while leaving behind the heavier, potentially problematic components. The result is a more transparent balsamic note that allows perfumers to build nuanced amber accords without the overwhelming darkness and viscosity of traditional extracts. Use this essential oil at 0.4-2% when you need the characteristic Peru Balsam warmth but require regulatory compliance and formulation flexibility. Unlike the banned crude balsam or rich resinoid, the essential oil offers greater freedom while maintaining exceptional fixative properties. Its lighter character makes it invaluable for modern transparent formulations where the resinoid's dark colour would be problematic—think clear serums, light-coloured creams, or minimalist alcoholic fragrances demanding visual clarity. The practical advantages of Peru Balsam Essential Oil extend beyond compliance into creative territory previously inaccessible with traditional forms. Its reduced vanillin content allows you to control sweetness precisely by adding vanillin or ethyl vanillin to taste, while its cleaner profile integrates seamlessly with delicate florals that might be overwhelmed by the resinoid's intensity. Combine it with benzoin and labdanum for classic amber structures or explore contemporary applications in clean musks and molecular fragrances where its subtle warmth adds natural depth without vintage heaviness.

missing_other.title: Peru Balsam “Signature” Resinoid
missing_other.description: Peru balsam resinoid is a wonderfully sweet and complex exudate from myroxylon balsamum trees which have been intentionally scarred with cuts and burns to promote the outpouring of the healing raw gum. This exudate, or drug, is collected via cotton cloths which are pressed to the weeping trunk of the tree. Once removed from the clothes, the balsam is washed and made into a resinoid via ethanol or other solvent extractions to produce the IFRA safe product we stock. Peru balsam has a strongly vanilla quality and could be said to have the odiferous properties of a blend of vanilla absolute, benzoin resinoid and styrax resinoid . It is sweet, resinous, leathery, cinnamyl and powdery. Peru balsam resinoid is of a viscous but pourable consistency so we sell it pure. Note that this is the rare deep brown resinoid and not the clear essential oil, an entirely different product. Origin: El Salvador Variety: Myroxylon Balsamum L. var pereirae Klotzsch Part: Exudate from tree bark Method of production: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Petalux
missing_other.description: Petalux, a replacer for Givaudan's captive Petalia, opens with an airy burst of rose petals dusted with lychee sweetness. The peony character emerges soft and dewy, rounded by delicate muguet transparency. This is modern florality at its most radiant—fresh, clean, and effortlessly pretty. Build your floral hearts around this material for immediate lift and diffusion. It brings a contemporary, juicy quality to classic rose accords without heaviness. Pair it with citrus top notes to amplify freshness, or layer with musks to extend its soft glow into the drydown. Use Petalux at twice the dosage of Givaudan's Petalia when reformulating. Combine with hedione for enhanced radiance or phenylethyl alcohol for richer rose depth. Try it alongside fruity notes like cassis or raspberry to exploit its lychee facet.

missing_other.title: Petitgrain Bergamotier Oil
missing_other.description: Petitgrain bergamotier is produced by steam distilling the foliage from bergamot trees. This is a wonderful material to add interest and lift to a fragrance. It blends exceedingly well with other members of the citrus family which it modifies and extends, most especially bergamot , lemon and sweet orange . Try it with our Lemon Verbena and Suralette Extra . Petitgrain bergamotier was a part of the petitgrain fond in the original Green Irish Tweed by Creed (see our demo formula Tartan Dream below) where it was blended with petitgrain paraguay and petitgrain citronnier (from the lemon tree). Origin: Italy Variety: Citrus bergamia risso Part: Leaves and branches Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Petitgrain Bigarade Oil
missing_other.description: Petitgrain Bigarade is the extraction of the foliage from bitter orange trees (the fruit of which is used for classic Seville orange marmalade). Of all the petitgrain oils, this is probably the most widely used for fine fragrance. This oil is extracted exclusively from the bitter orange tree making it the finest type, different from the lower quality so-called “Bigarade (Paraguay)” variants that flood the market. Petitgrain Paraguay is extracted from hybrid trees which cross the bitter orange with sweet (or other) varieties. Pure Petitgrain Bigarade is much more rare and considerably more beautiful. Origin: Italy Part: Foliage Method: Steam distilled at source

missing_other.title: Petitgrain Citronnier Oil
missing_other.description: Petitgrain oil citronnier is produced by steam distilling the foliage from lemon trees. Less common than bigarade petitigrain (from bitter orange), this is a wonderful material to add interest and lift to a fragrance. It blends exceedingly well with other members of the citrus family which it modifies and extends, most especially lemon, lime and cedrat. Try it with our Lemon Verbena and Verdantol . Petitgrain citronnier was a vital part of the petitgrain fond in the original Green Irish Tweed by Creed (see our demo formula Tartan Dream below) where it was blended with petitgrain paraguay and petitgrain bergamotier (from the bergamot tree). Origin: Italy Part: Leaves and branches Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Petitgrain Mandarinier Oil
missing_other.description: The most unusual and intense of the petitgrain oils, Mandarin petitgrain is green, dusty and incredibly complex. It can be a great asset when wanting to add natural earthiness to a melange of citrus notes or to help soften the chemical nature of loved top notes like Dihydromyrcenol . Of interest is the fact the Petitgrain Mandarinier can contain up to 50% natural dimethyl anthranilate which is restricted by the DEA in the US so this oil is one way to incorporate that material without having to worry about problems with customs. Origin: Italy Part: Foliage Method: Steam Distilled at source

missing_other.title: Petitgrain Oil Terpeneless
missing_other.description: This LMR produced petitgrain oil terpeneless (Petitgrain Oil Tpls.) is hands-down the finest example of the material we have ever experienced. It isn't just slightly better — it is leaps and bounds ahead of the competition. This is so good it could pass for neroli oil with just a few small tweaks. W. A. Poucher uses this formula to convert Petitgrain Oil Tpls. into a neroli substitute with just four materials: 800g Petitgrain Oil Tpls. 100 Nerol Extra 90 Neroli Oil Tunisia 10 Aldehyde C-10, 10% in Petitgrain Oil Tpls. This deterpinated oil consists mainly of linalool, alpha-terpineol, linalyl acetate, geraniol, nerol and their esters. Petitgrain oil terpeneless finds use in all manner of fragrances but it is especially useful in heavy oriental types where it can convey a wonderful freshness in the midst of rich resins and sweet materials. Origin: Paraguay Variety: Citrus aurantium L. Part: Leaves and branches Method: Hydro distillation followed by rectification

missing_other.title: Petitgrain Paraguay
missing_other.description: Petitgrain Paraguay is the most common and, in the words of Steffen Arctander, the "most important by far of all the petitgrain oils." It is distilled exclusively from the bitter-sour variety of the orange tree (Citrus Aurantium), while Petitgrain Bigarade is made from the true Bitter orange tree (Citus Aurantium, Amara). In terms of the difference in odour and use, Petitgrain Paraguay is more fleeting and fresh while Petitgrain Bigarade has a slightly waxier and more woody quality. For slightly superior solubility and a longer lasting dry down we also have LMR's marvellous Petitgrain Paraguay Terpeneless . Petitgrain Paraguay blends well with orange bases such as Orange Blossom Supreme , Neroli Supreme , Floranol , Fleur d'Oranger and aroma chemicals such as Theaspirane, Nerolin ( Yara Yara and Bromelia), Oranger Crystals and Coumarone . Origin: Paraguay Part: Foliage Method: Steam distilled at source

missing_other.title: Pimento Berry Oil
missing_other.description: Sweeter than Clovebud oil and considerably longer lasting, Pimento (also known as Allspice) is a lovely spice oil that blends beautifully with rose materials and, of course, with other spices. Due to a high methyl eugenol content, it has a very strict IFRA restriction on use of up to 0.22% of the finished product but, frankly, it's worth using anyway. Origin: Jamaica Part: Dried Berries Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Pine Needle Oil, Sylvestris
missing_other.description: This is the reference standard for dry, airy coniferous freshness—distinct from the jammy sweetness of firs or the camphoraceous weight of spruces. The opening hits with a sharp terpenic bite that quickly softens into something sparkling and almost citrus-like. You'll find none of the cloying balsamic density that makes cheaper pine materials smell like floor cleaner. What makes Pinus sylvestris so valuable is its remarkably low bornyl acetate content compared to other conifers. This gives you a transparent, austere character that lifts rather than smothers your compositions. Pair it with bergamot or grapefruit to extend citrus longevity; the shared bitter-fresh quality creates a seamless bridge. In fougères, it acts as a vertical pillar connecting lavender's herbal top with oakmoss's earthy base. Use this oil sparingly in your heart notes—its medium diffusion power punches above its weight. Blend with frankincense to create modern incense accords stripped of musty church associations. Combine with labdanum for a "sun-baked forest" effect, or with juniper berry for ultra-dry gin-like freshness in masculine colognes.

missing_other.title: Pine Oil, Cembra
missing_other.description: Pine oil cembra is unlike any other pine oil you have encountered. Where Scots pine is sharp and turpentine-like, this Alpine species opens soft, sweet, and balsamic with a gentle coniferous freshness. A velvety warmth sets it apart — refined where other pines are rough. Use it to build forest accords, Alpine compositions, and coniferous elements in fougères and colognes. Its sweetness makes it more versatile in fine fragrance than harsher pine oils — it sits comfortably alongside bergamot, lavender, and cedarwood. The balsamic undertone blends naturally with labdanum, frankincense, and oakmoss. Longevity is the trade-off — like most pine oils, the coniferous top fades within hours. Extend it with isobornyl acetate, Iso E Super, or ambroxan to anchor the pine character into the drydown. Pinus cembra is the Zirbe of Austrian tradition, distilled from trees that grow above the Alpine timberline.

missing_other.title: Pineapple Natpop™
missing_other.description: V. MANE Fils is one of our favourite suppliers of naturals, but they are also (like Fraterworks) makers of some truly wonderful bases. Pineapple Natpop™ is one. In MANE's own words, Natpops are 100% "olfactory reconstitutions of fresh fruit notes." Pineapple Natpop™ is a marvel. Unlike our highly popular top note Pineapple Supreme base, Pineapple Natpop™ is a top to bottom blend which is not just pineapple, but tropical fruit, sweetness and wonderful richness. This base is absolutely essential for all perfumers. When you smell it you won't know how you lived without it. We have never been more passionate about a natural fruit base and honesty this surpasses many times over the more well-known Robertet natural fruit accords. Use Pineapple Natpop™ in a large amount for a rich pineapple note that lasts the life of your scent, or use traces to sweeten and add a fruity je ne sais quoi .

missing_other.title: Pineapple Supreme
missing_other.description: Have you wondered how Creed gets that incredible pineapple top note into Aventus? Wonder no more! This is it: the Aventus Pineapple. Incredibly powerful and intensely sweet, this base is impactful at mere traces. From DK Donna Karan , one of the most incredible men's scents of the '90s to Aventus — the modern blockbuster, pineapple is a note beloved by everyone. This powerful base is the only pineapple top note you will want. Nothing else comes close.

missing_other.title: Pink Acacia
missing_other.description: Pink Acacia (black locust or faux acacia) differs from the unrelated cassie and mimosa (members of the true acacia family) in that it has an intense note of orange blossom mixed with hawthorne. It is a very elegant floral note seldom seen in modern perfumes which is a shame as it has such a universally appreciated scent. Pink Acacia conveys the scent of warm summer breeze; it creates a sense of happy nostalgia. It is perfectly suited as the main floral heart of a contemporary fragrance. Fraterworks Pink Acacia is loaded with natural floral oils and it can be safely used in small amounts (for adding nuance and richness) or in overdose as is evidenced in the demo formula below.

missing_other.title: Pink Carnation, Natural
missing_other.description: With an overload of French iris extracts, spices, floral oils and absolutes and the ultimate natural isolates, Pink Carnation is a 100% natural base that brings not just a wonderfully natural carnation note to your fragrances but contributes a number of high class materials seldom affordable for hobbyist and artisanal perfumers. Combine Pink Carnation with natural Ionones and orange blossom for the beginnings of a luxurious natural take on Coty's great masterpiece L'Origan . This base is also able to be used as a one for one replacer for our classic non-natural Dianthus and Dianthine Extra bases, the use of which are demonstrated in our formulas below.

missing_other.title: Pink Lotus Absolute
missing_other.description: Pink lotus absolute bears no resemblance to the sheer aquatic lotus of mainstream perfumery. The living flower is light and sweet, but extraction concentrates it into something dense, dark, and honeyed. Expect spicy green top notes, a waxy floral heart, then leather, tonka-like warmth, and unmistakable animalic depth. Use pink lotus absolute as an exotic heart in your oriental and oud-based compositions, where its honeyed animalic character creates instant opulence. It transforms white floral blends, adding a dark richness that jasmine and tuberose alone cannot achieve. A little goes a very long way. Pair it with sandalwood and oud for a meditative, incense-like accord. Try it alongside mimosa or beeswax absolute to amplify its honey facets. Dose carefully from a dilution — the raw absolute is intensely concentrated, and even a trace rewrites your entire composition. Pink and white lotus are both colour forms of Nelumbo nucifera, the sacred lotus. They are the same species but produce noticeably different absolutes. The pink form is sweeter, more honeyed, and more complex. The white is bolder, less fruity, and more aquatic. Always check which you are buying. Blue lotus — Nymphaea caerulea — the sacred flower of ancient Egypt, is not a lotus at all. It is a water lily from an entirely different plant family. Its absolute is sheer, waxy, and fruity-sweet where pink lotus is dense and animalic. They share almost nothing in common despite the confusingly similar name.

missing_other.title: Pink Pepper CO2
missing_other.description: Pink Pepper (unrelated to Piper Nigrum or black pepper ) comes in two varieties: Schinus Molle (Peru) and Schinus Terebinthifolius (Brazil). They are closely related and quite similar in scent but the Brazilian extracts are brighter and fresher and, generally speaking, preferred. This CO2 extraction from LMR is the finest version of Schinus Terebinthifolius on the market today. It is supremely beautiful and a must-have for all perfumers. It is extracted from the berries of the tree. We also stock the essential oil of Peruvian pink pepper ( Schinus Molle) also from LMR.

missing_other.title: Pink Pepper Oil, Molle
missing_other.description: Pink peppercorn is not really from the pepper family ( Piper nigrum ). Schinus molle (false pepper tree, Peruvian pepper) is an evergreen tree native to Peru with a wonderfully piquant and fresh top note and resinous balsamic dry down that is universally loved. This prestige essential oil from LMR is extracted from the berries of the tree and is extremely versatile. Not to be confused with the close relative Schinus terebinthifolius (Brazilian Pepper and a native of that place) which, although also very beautiful, has a more astringent top note quality. We also stock Pink Peppercorn “Terebinthifolius” CO2 extract from LMR.

missing_other.title: Pink Pepper Oil, Terebinthifolius
missing_other.description: Pink pepper oil opens with a bright, sparkling burst of spice — peppery but lighter and more radiant than black pepper. There is a distinctive rosy-floral quality underneath, with green, citrusy freshness and a warm woody drydown. It reads as luminous and uplifting rather than heavy. Pink pepper is not a true pepper — it belongs to the cashew and mango family, which explains its fruity, rosy warmth. It became a modern perfumery staple after Estée Lauder Pleasures in 1995. Use it to add sparkling lift to florals, fresh masculines, and unisex compositions. Pair pink pepper with rose for an effect that is almost magical — the rosy facets in both materials amplify each other. It also works beautifully with bergamot, neroli, geranium, vetiver, and cedarwood. A little goes a long way; overdose and it turns harsh. Different species, different characters This oil — from Schinus terebinthifolius, the Brazilian pepper tree — is the brighter, fresher, more modern of the two varieties, with distinctive rosy-green nuances. Pink Pepper Oil, Molle (Schinus molle, the Peruvian pepper tree) is more balsamic, smoky, and woody — closer to juniper berry or angelica in character. We also stock LMR's Pink Pepper CO2 , a supercritical extract of terebinthifolius that captures even more of the fresh berry — brighter top notes and a fuller, more rounded body than this steam-distilled oil.

missing_other.title: Poivre Fort
missing_other.description: Poivre Fort is a classic spice base which, characteristically of products of this type, includes sympathetic woody and floral notes. The base has a wonderfully warming black pepper top note on a creamy and soft heart of Bulgarian rose, ylang-ylang and its related salicylates giving it a solar quality. This base works as a wonderful blender while imparting an elegant spice note. Poivre Fort is an ideal base to add freshness and lightness to heavy compositions. It can be used in high doses without dominating at up to 2.19% for IFRA 51 compliance.

missing_other.title: Pomelo Grandis
missing_other.description: Natural grapefruit and pomelo oils are the most easily degraded in perfumery and as a result synthetics like Methyl Pamplemousse are used liberally. However sometimes we need a genuinely realistic note of Pomelo or grapefruit that can be used in the same way as any other regular citrus oil with little to no risk of degradation. That's where Fraterworks Pomelo Grandis comes in. Pomelo Grandis has the power and longevity of true Pomelo oil as well as the wonderfully sulphurous and bitter top note quality. This base is almost entirely natural and blends with all the members of our Citrus Suite. This can be used as a one-for-one replacement for Grapefruit oil or Pomelo oil in a formula.

missing_other.title: Poplar Bud Absolute 50% TEC
missing_other.description: This product has seen a steep price increase from our suppliers and alas we must pass that on. We are monitoring the trends in pricing and will make reductions when possible. With no restriction in use, Poplar Buds absolute can be used in a similar way to styrax but in far greater amounts. It is a wonderful fixative and has the most alluring and unusual scent of honey, fruit and resin making it perfect for adding body and longevity to fruit bases and accords; indeed Edmond Roudnitska used this in his most famous Prunol SP ﻿ base. Poplar Bud Absolute is diluted to 50% in natural triethyl citrate (an odourless isolate from citrus) at the source by Biolandes. Origin: Eastern Europe Manufactured: France Part: Buds Method: Solvent Extraction

missing_other.title: Poudre à la Maréchale Tincture 20%
missing_other.description: The scent of powdered wigs. This is an 18th century tincture of dried flowers, spices, roots and seeds. Use it as a fixative or the foundation of an entire scent. A very precious and little-known ingredient of many French fragrances from the golden age of perfumery was Infusion Poudre à la Maréchale (tincture of marechale powder). Poudre à la Maréchale was a scented powder that had risen to popularity during the era of powdered wigs (perukes) in which horse-hair wigs (which were seldom if ever washed) would be dusted to mask malodours. The original marechale powder was created in the late 1600s for the wife of the Maréchal d'Aumont. The materials used varied from perfumer to perfumer though there were some fundamentals that were common to most: ambrette seeds, sandalwood, orris root, cloves and a variety of other spices, herbs and usually one or both of rose petals and orange blossoms. So popular was Poudre à la Maréchale that even as perukes fell into disuse, the great perfume houses that were beginning to emerge across Europe continued to supply the scent as cosmetic powders but also as an infusion (or tincture). Initially it was sold as an article for wear on its own like a cologne, but it also came to be added to other fragrances as a fixative base. Most of the early Guerlain fragrances incorporate this infusion, and Coty's L'Origan (formula below) owes much of its powderiness and complex dry down to it. Fraterworks is the only company in the world that is currently making and supplying Poudre à la Maréchale tincture. We manufacture this product using materials and methods that are completely traditional. Despite its age, this is a product which modern perfumers can use to impart a je ne sais quoi to their fragrances. It is a very powerful fixative and adds complexity, richness and interest to any scent. We supply this as a completely natural 20% tincture which is not vegan as it contains ambergris. Like all tinctures, this product will improve, strengthen and d

missing_other.title: Pralinol™
missing_other.description: Praline: roasted hazelnuts, toffee and chocolate. This is an outstanding and powerful base that lets you add a praline note to your perfumes with the minimum off fuss. It contains extremely powerful and rare materials for a truly unique blend. Pralinol can be used in overdose when mixed with the right accessories, but a trace is all you need (0.1% or lower) to add a decidedly edible note. It is particularly nice with vanillin and veratraldehyde .

missing_other.title: Pretty Oud
missing_other.description: This is an extremely attractive and easy to dose oud base by Firmenich which could almost be a fragrance in its own right. Pretty Oud offers a sensual woody profile with smoky and leathery facets, providing a direct and elegant interpretation of ambery fragrances. I would be surprised if this doesn't form an important unlisted component in Gucci's rather interesting 2017 Gucci Guilty Absolut e for men (and perhaps the feminine version also with blackcurrant and rose materials added).

missing_other.title: Prunella®
missing_other.description: For most, Prunella needs no introduction. It is the industry standard dried plum base from Firmemich which has most certainly withstood the test of time, being featured in such classics as the original Dior Poison and Chanel's Égoïste. Built around an overdose of phenoxyethyl isobutyrate, this is a very easy base to dose and while small amounts contribute a gentle sweetness, overdoses also work very well in a modern gourmand context. Prunella® blends very well with the Rose Ketones and other fruit bases and it makes beautiful accords with patchouli .

missing_other.title: Prunol SP
missing_other.description: After Mousse de Saxe perhaps no other classical base is as well known as Prunol SP by De Laire. Prunol is a wonderful floral and fantasy fruit base with a stronger emphasis on the floral than fruit. Nevertheless it imparts a luscious sweet plummy note to fragrances. Edmond Roudnitska created the base after his wartime discovery of casks of a rare type of methyl ionone discarded in the De Laire yard. To this he added many other products including luxurious naturals of Poplar bud, Helichrysum absolute, precious Boronia absolute and more. Blended with spices, lactones and a fond of De Laire bases, Prunol SP was born. Our base is 100% faithful to that formula by Roudnitska and so, in consquence, it contains Poplar bud absolute - a natural plant extract rich in salicin which may need to be avoided by people with allergies to aspirin or salicylic acid. Prunol is fruity, spicy, aldehydic, and floral. It is a powerful base and has a usability level up to 7.8% for IFRA 49 compliance, it can be used in an overdose for a novel effect. It featured heavily in the 1943 perfume Femme for Rochas. In the 21st century in which we find gourmand fragrances all the rage, Prunol SP deserves a renaissance.

missing_other.title: Raspberry Leaf Absolute
missing_other.description: Raspberry Leaf Absolute opens with complex green-leafy character—with a jammy nuance, and layered with unexpected depth. Delicate fruit facets mingle with musky tea notes, while balsamic-resinous undertones evoke mulled wine and dried fruits. The leathery warmth adds sophistication, creating a profile that transcends simple berry sweetness. This is a forest floor, not candy. This French absolute comes from the leaves of Rubus idaeus, extracted via solvent to capture the full aromatic complexity of the plant material. The resulting substance is extremely thick and sticky—practically solid at room temperature—requiring patience and warmth to work with. For that reason we offer it pre-diluted in natural triethyl citrate for practical use. Despite coming from raspberry, the leaf absolute smells nothing like the bright fruit; instead it offers deep green character with davana-like jamminess and amber-tobacco warmth. Work with Raspberry Leaf Absolute as a base note modifier where its green-jammy character adds sophisticated depth. Use it in berry accords seeking complexity beyond simple raspberry ketone sweetness, or in chypre compositions where fruity-green notes complement oakmoss and bergamot. It blends beautifully with rose, agarwood, patchouli, and vanilla. Try it in tea, tobacco, and cognac accords where its musky-resinous facets add naturalistic warmth. The balsamic depth makes it valuable in precious wood and amber compositions.

missing_other.title: Raspberry Ripple
missing_other.description: This is an intensely sweet raspberry base which can be used in traces for subtle fruity sweetness or in overdose for a fun modern gourmand. It blends incredibly well with other gourmand notes such as coconut and amaretto and it can be used in place of materials like ethyl maltol or maltol when a more interesting sugar note is wanted. Make Raspberry Ripple the centrepiece of a wild fruity chypre or simply add it to a monolithic base like the Grojsman Plus and leave it at that! For a luxury touch, add a little Ambrette Seed oil from LMR and sticky sweet Rose Ultimate Extract (boosted with some Rose Essence).

missing_other.title: Reaumur
missing_other.description: Reaumur is our internal formula for Angels' Share by Kilian. Launched in 2020 as part of The Liquors collection and created by Benoist Lapouza, this is a sweet gourmand fragrance built around cognac and oak barrel, with praline, vanilla and warm spice. This compound features a rich cognac accord laid over oak, giving the unmistakable impression of spirit ageing in a barrel. The opening is boozy and immediate, with cinnamon and tonka bean absolute warming the heart and hedione lending lift to what would otherwise be a very dense composition. The base delivers praline, vanilla, candied almond and creamy sandalwood for a finish that reads as stewed apples and Christmas baking. The result is a thick, enveloping gourmand with above-average projection and excellent longevity – indulgent and unmistakably festive. It is easy to see why this is one of the most popular gourmand perfumes. This compound is IFRA compliant and ready to dilute and bottle. Just add alcohol. We recommend a 22% concentration (Parfum). Top Notes: Cognac Heart Notes: Cinnamon, Tonka Bean, Oak Barrel, Hedione Base Notes: Vanilla, Praline, Sandalwood, Candied Almond

missing_other.title: Red Champaca Absolute
missing_other.description: Red champaca absolute is the deeper, more intense cousin of golden champaca. Where the yellow form is delicate and tea-like, this is heavy and sultry — rich dried apricot and raisin sweetness layered over warm clove-spice. Hay, tobacco, and vanilla emerge in a lingering drydown. Use red champaca as an opulent floral heart in your oriental compositions. It adds a spiced, fruity richness that jasmine and ylang alone cannot deliver. Blend it with sandalwood to highlight its tea-like warmth, or pair with patchouli for a darker, more brooding accord. Try red champaca alongside rose and tuberose for a layered floral of extraordinary complexity. A trace in amber accords contributes a fruity-spicy dimension you won't get from any other material. This is one of perfumery's rarest and most rewarding naturals to work with. This is a very expensive material and so we also sell our five start 100% natural replacer base, Red Champaca TruAbs .

missing_other.title: Red Champaca TruAbs
missing_other.description: Red Champaca TruAbs® is a scientifically crafted base designed to provide the full olfactory impact of precious Red Champaca Absolute. This 100% natural TruAbs® blend replicates the absolute's narcotic sweetness and complex dry down with astonishing accuracy. Perfumers can use this cost-effective material to achieve opulent, oriental accords and add unique depth to floral compositions. Incorporate Red Champaca TruAbs® at 0.1-5% to recreate a luxurious and exotic floral heart note. Blend with sandalwood and amber to enhance its warm, resinous qualities. TruAbs® bases, created in Grasse exclusively for Fraterworks, offer a consistent and readily available alternative to often unobtainable absolutes.

missing_other.title: Red Ginger Oil
missing_other.description: Red ginger (halia bara) is related to regular ginger but is smaller and red with a pink to yellow interior. This red ginger essential oil (steam extracted from the roots) is spicier and more pungent than ginger. This is a wonderful and unique oil that can add a really interesting and unusual character to your fragrances. Blends well with: other spice oils, sandalwood, resins and balsams. This product is certified halal and kosher. Synonyms: Halia Bara Origin: Indonesia Variety: ZIngiber officinale Linn Var. rubrum (Zingiberaceae) Part: Fresh Roots Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Red Seaweed CO2
missing_other.description: Trembling beneath the saliferous waters of the Breton coast can be glimpsed long reddish fingers of Palmaria palmata, a precious red seaweed. In Ireland, Palmaria palmata (also known as dulse) has been a staple food for centuries and now, thanks to MANE (the premium supplier of oils and absolutes from Grasse) it finds a new home in the world of fragrance. Red Seaweed Pure Jungle Essence™ is a jewel in the crown of MANE. While most seaweed materials come with unpleasant top notes, Red Seaweed has an almost gourmand quality, with nuances of fresh barnyard blended with the wild scent of the ancient Celtic Sea. Jungle essences are MANE's special CO2 products (watch the video clip below for a fascinating look at how these materials are made). This Red Seaweed is a pure jungle essence™ meaning it has nothing added in the making and is the pure essence extracted from the raw material. Due to its intensity and very high cost, Fraterworks offers this pure jungle essence pure and in a more affordable and usable 10% in natural Triethyl Citrate , making it a product that can be used by natural (EU and US) perfumers. Origin: Brittany, France

missing_other.title: Red Thyme Oil
missing_other.description: Red Thyme Oil Extra has a powerful and complex aromatic profile, characterised by intense warmth and a potent, spicy-herbal quality . This primary impression is often described as medicinal or phenolic, a direct result of its high concentration of constituents like thymol and carvacrol . Supporting these dominant notes are earthy, loamy undertones, a dry woody character, and subtle sweet, balsamic overtones that add richness . The "red" designation indicates this is the unadulterated, initial distillate, which provides a more tenacious, potent, and raw aromatic experience compared to its rectified counterpart, White Thyme Oil . As a perfumery ingredient, Red Thyme Oil Extra is a versatile and impactful tool used to add distinctive character to many fragrance types . It is a classic component in fougère compositions, where its herbaceous strength complements notes of lavender and oakmoss . Its aromatic quality also adds a "sunny touch" to woody and chypre fragrances, and its inherent spiciness makes it valuable in oriental blends . The dry, phenolic facets of the oil can even contribute to the creation of sophisticated leather accords . Beyond its primary scent, the oil's less volatile phenolic compounds allow it to act as a natural fixative, helping to anchor lighter notes and prolong a fragrance's longevity .
