missing_other.title: Roasted Barley Extract 40% ETH
missing_other.description: Roasted Barley Extract opens with the intoxicating richness of freshly brewed espresso, immediately complemented by the warm sweetness of toffee and toasted hazelnuts. This is no simple cereal note—it's an "accord in a bottle" that captures the entire sensory experience of a cosy bakery or whisky distillery. The Maillard reaction during roasting creates hundreds of aromatic compounds, particularly potent pyrazines that deliver those deeply satisfying nutty, coffee, and cocoa nuances. This material has a remarkable ability to add instant sophistication to gourmand compositions. Its complex evolution from sweet caramel top notes through bready, malty hearts to smoky, tobacco-laden bases provides extraordinary depth that synthetic materials struggle to match. The boozy facets make it essential for whisky and cognac accords, whilst its dark chocolate and coffee characters elevate simple vanilla compositions into compelling, textured experiences.

missing_other.title: Roman Chamomile Oil
missing_other.description: Roman chamomile (also known as English Chamomile) possesses a distinct aroma that is sweet, fruity, and herbaceous. It is characterised by its warm, floral aroma with subtle hints of apple and honey. The fragrance is often considered soft and comforting, with gentle notes that evoke a sense of relaxation and tranquility. Use this wonderful oil as a middle note or a supporting ingredient in floral, herbal, or aromatic fragrances where it adds a touch of warmth and complexity. The difference between German and Roman chamomile plants is that German chamomile flowers grow in clusters, while Roman chamomile flowers grow singularly atop a hairy stem. We also stock the finest rare single estate German (or blue) chamomile from England. Origin: Italy Part: Flower heads Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Rooibos “Red Tea” Resinoid
missing_other.description: Rooibos resinoid smells of warm honey, sun-dried hay, and soft caramel, with a fruity-apricot sweetness and a gentle woody depth. It is softer and sweeter than black tea, warmer and rounder than green tea. There is a faint bitterness in the drydown that keeps it from ever becoming cloying. Rooibos is not actually tea — it comes from Aspalathus linearis, a legume found only in the Cederberg Mountains of South Africa's Cape fynbos. That unique origin gives it a character no true tea can replicate: honeyed warmth with a red, almost wine-like quality. Use it in gourmand and oriental compositions where you want natural sweetness and depth. Pair it with vanilla and tonka for rich gourmand warmth, with immortelle and honey absolute for a golden, honeyed heart, or with cedarwood and vetiver for a darker, woodier direction. It also works beautifully with bergamot, black pepper, and orris for a sophisticated tea-inspired composition. The Payan Bertrand quality we stock is from their precious Signature range.

missing_other.title: Rose Absolute “Signature” Bulgaria
missing_other.description: If you possess only one rose for perfumery purposes, this absolute is it. Its versatility is unparalleled and even mere traces can have a wonderful enriching and exalting impact on a fragrance. We obtain this signature product from one of the finest suppliers of oils and absolutes in the world and the quality shows. With a full body and a long rich dry down, this is rose absolute perfection. Because of the high price of rose products, we also offer this diluted to 10% in odourless Triethyl Citrate which is a completely natural isolate, making it suitable for natural perfumers. We also stock Rose Bulgarian oil (otto).

missing_other.title: Rose Absolute, Isparta
missing_other.description: Isparta in Turkey has a long history of rose production; in fact it is called The City of Roses. The most common variety is Rosa Damascena, the same type that is used for the classic Bulgarian Rose Oil (otto) and Absolute . The other most used type of rose in perfumery is Rose Centifolia, a French variant. We stock the famous Rose de Mai from Grasse and the luscious Rose Centifolia Absolute, Tunisia. In the words of LMR: “ This unique petal rose note has a pronounced fruity top, green and spicy facets, and a touch of honey.” Rose extracts from Isparta are slightly more costly than standard Turkish products as the climate and soil produces richer and more balanced results. In Isparta, roses are still often farmed and harvested in the traditional way on multi-generational farms. LMR certifies this product as part of their “For Life” range which seeks to support these family-owned suppliers which tend to be highly sustainable due to their adherence to heritage methods. We also stock numerous other natural roses which can found in our rose collection . Fun fact: the waste produced in the extraction of this beautiful Turkish rose absolute is the starting material for the modern marvel of upcycled perfumery: LMR's Rose Ultimate Extract which we also stock. Origin: Isparta, Turkey Part: Flower petals only Process: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Rose Absolute, Morocco
missing_other.description: The main rose used in perfumes today is from Rosa Damascena. It typically goes by the name of just Rose Absolute (or oil) and the Bulgarian variety is the most common. However, it's lesser-used cousin, Rosa Damascena from Morocco is a somewhat different beast, with a lovely tea rose quality that is lacking in the slightly lower-cost Bulgarian absolute. The best Bulgarian roses tend to be used for the essential oil which is the most costly of the rose extracts, whereas in Morocco the best roses go to making the absolute. The soil of Morocco produces roses that give a lighter, more nuanced absolute with hints of herbal green and an almost peppery undertone. Moroccan Rose Absolute is definitely something to have even if you already use the Bulgarian absolute. The differences make both extremely useful for different ends. Because of the high price of rose products, we also offer this diluted to 10% in odourless Triethyl Citrate which is a completely natural isolate from citrus, making it suitable for natural perfumers. We also stock Rose Bulgarian oil (otto) and Rose “Signature” Absolute from Bulgaria. Origin: Morocco Part: Flowers only Process: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Rose Absolute, Select
missing_other.description: Fraterworks' Bulgarian rose absolute select is the cornerstone material for any perfumer's palette at an accessible price point. This product captures the rich, deep character that makes Bulgarian rose absolute indispensable in perfumery: its velvety texture, complex floral heart, and remarkable ability to enhance and elevate compositions even in trace amounts. While our signature Payan Bertrand rose absolute represents the pinnacle of luxury with its exceptional depth and longevity, this Fraterworks® Select rose absolute delivers the true essence of Bulgarian rose in a format that makes it practical for regular use, experimentation, and learning. It maintains the characteristic full-bodied profile and the transformative quality that rose absolute brings to fragrances - from simple soliflores to complex oriental compositions. This is an ideal choice for perfumery students developing their skills, enthusiasts building their organ, and professional perfumers who need a reliable, quality rose absolute for trials and formulation work where cost efficiency matters. Like all Fraterworks® Select products, it's been chosen to ensure authentic quality at an exceptional price. Available pure and in 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate. We also stock value Rose Bulgarian oil (otto).

missing_other.title: Rose Blanche
missing_other.description: Rose Blanche is the white rose base featured prominently in the stunning Detchéma fragrance by Révillon (1953). It is a luxurious and rich blend of the finest rose synthetics available and loaded with natural absolutes. Rose Blanche, in traces, imparts sweetness and sophistication but in larger amounts modifies a modern rose and adds a precious and noticeably expensive quality. This base is a top to bottom accord, so it can also stand alone as an entire fragrance unto itself. Rose Blanche has a synergy with Rose D'Orient and the two blend seamlessly together.

missing_other.title: Rose Centifolia Absolute, Tunisia
missing_other.description: The two main roses in perfumery are Rose Damascena and Rose Centifolia. Rose Damascena is rich, warm, and slightly spicy while Rose Centifolia is soft, fresh, and powdery. The latter is great for adding a soft rosy floralcy while the Damascena gives a bolder and more intense rose heart note. The finest extracts of Rose Centifolia are from Grasse ( Rose de Mai ) but due to the extremely high cost, most harvests now come from Tunisia. Rose de Mai comes from roses harvested during the month of May only, while Tunisian Rose centifolia is harvested at different times through the year; due to the hotter climate, the Tunisian absolute has a lighter, fresher, and slightly more citrusy profile with a delicate floral character.

missing_other.title: Rose D'Orient
missing_other.description: Rose D'Orient is one of the two great classic rose bases from the golden age of perfumery. It is a rose otto type base with a honeyed nuance. A large number of naturals (including orris materials) mean that this base, even in small amounts, exalts and enhances every perfume in which it is used. Famous uses: L'Origan , Chypre , Nuit de Chine , Miss Dior , Mitsouko , and many more. Between the absolute type of Rose Imperiale and the otto type of Rose D'Orient , we have all your bases covered.

missing_other.title: Rose de Mai Absolute, France
missing_other.description: Rose de Mai is the name given to the absolute produced from the rosa centifolia flowers picked only during the month of May. Traditionally this was produced in Grasse but limited supply and cost meant that most of the world's supply was moved to Morocco and Egypt. Fraterworks is, as far as we know, the only supplier to the artisan market of the true Grasse grown and produced May rose absolute. This is 100% pure and natural Rose de Mai absolute made in France. Almost all of the annual production of this absolute is taken by Dior and Chanel so we are very fortunate to be able to offer it. This masterpiece has an indulgence that defies belief. From the naturally sweet opening notes to the astonishingly balanced spice of the dry-down accented with hints of farmyard smoke and spring rains, it evokes every aspect of the Provence countryside. Use this oil for very special personal projects or simply as a historic treasure of indescribable beauty. Because of the high cost of this rose de mai absolute we are also offering it in one and ten percent dilutions in natural triethyl citrate (an all-natural odourless isolate from citrus which works particularly well with rose). We also stock LMR's Rose Centifolia Absolute from Tunisia which is a much lower cost alternative to French grown Rose de Mai. Certified: IG Absolue Pays de Grasse . Origin: Grasse, France Variety: Rosa Centifolia Part: Flowers only, May harvest only

missing_other.title: Rose de Mai Supreme TruAbs
missing_other.description: Exhibiting a rich yellow colour and a viscosity matching pure and natural French Rose de Mai absolute, this is the finest replica on the market and because it is all natural it is compliant with ISO 9235. This exclusive Fraterworks product is made in France to our very exacting specifications in order to replicate a particularly fine historic rose absolute extracted in Grasse from May blooming Centifolia roses only. Even more marvellous is the fact that it is priced at a fraction of the cost of Rose de Mai absolute. French Rose de Mai absolute is virtually impossible to obtain outside of France as the entire annual production is locked away for the exclusive use of one or two multinational fragrance houses. If you are looking for other options, we offer Rose Imperiale , the once captive version of the acclaimed Rose Wardia® from the early 20th century (a masterpiece in classical perfumery,) and we also stock pure and natural Bulgarian Rose Otto and Bulgarian Rose Absolute . Check out our entire Rose Collection .

missing_other.title: Rose Essence
missing_other.description: Rose Essence is a replacer base for Bulgarian rose oil. Built upon a foundation of a scientific reconstruction of the natural oil, this Fraterworks® base is unbeatable in quality, elegance and price. Loaded with natural extracts from Bulgarian rose, this is a must-have base as rose oil gets more expensive year after year. Rose Essence is so good you can't tell it isn't pure and natural. This formula has been slightly updated (reference 655235A) to increase the total content of natural rose extracts.

missing_other.title: Rose Imperiale
missing_other.description: Rose Imperiale is our reconstruction ( developed from our own analysis and research) of a very well-known classical rose base representing the whole French rose de mai. The original was a key base in many historic fragrances but fits perfectly well in a modern context. Fraterworks brings you the scent of glorious rose de mai in a product we consider as elegant as the pure absolute itself. This base is rich with natural materials and high class oils and absolutes found only in the finest fragrances. This is what Wardia was meant to be. Even traces of Rose Imperiale can enhance a fragrance with its complex yet beautifully balanced formula.

missing_other.title: Rose Maréchal Niel
missing_other.description: Soft and woody with a soft purr of floralcy, Rose Maréchal Niel was a much appreciated early 20th century base mimicking the scent of the beloved rose of the same name that appeared a century earlier. Forming part of the complex and sweet floral heart of Arpège, this rose base has all but dissapeared in the 21st century. If you are looking for a rose with that special je ne sais quoi, look no further. Rose Maréchal Niel is loaded with rich and costly floral and wood oils and absolutes making it an expensive base to produce, however it is effective in traces and makes for a wonderful addition to a general floral bouquet.

missing_other.title: Rose Oil “Superior” Bulgaria
missing_other.description: Rose oil (also known as rose otto) from Bulgaria is the premiere rose product. It is effective in traces but can be overdosed in the most luxurious floral fragrances. Rose otto is the classic pairing with jasmine absolute and blends beautifully with our signature Rose Bulgarian Absolute . We are offering this wonderful oil pure and in a 5% and 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate, an odourless isolate from citrus which is a particularly good diluent for rose materials. Our rose is produced by LMR and is COSMOS certified. LMR produces the highest quality Bulgarian Oil on the market bar none. Note: Fraterworks is not a registered COSMOS company so while this product is CSM certified when it reaches us, we cannot use that terminology when we resell.

missing_other.title: Rose Oil, Isparta
missing_other.description: We've made no secret of the fact that we love LMR when it comes to rose essential oil and so it should come as no surprise that they are also our go-to for Turkish oil. In perfumery rose oil usually comes in two varieties: Bulgarian and Turkish. But what a lot of people don't know is that Turkish oil also comes in two varieties: regular (mostly from Afyon, Denizli, and Burdur) and deluxe (Isparta region). The Isparta oil is the finest of the Turkish rose oils and even has a special designation much in the same way that Champagne has in France. When selecting between Bulgarian oil and Turkish oil, the differences to consider are: Bulgarian oil is sweeter and more intense, while Turkish oils are fruitier, fresher and spicier. We are offering this wonderful oil pure and in a 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate, an odourless isolate from citrus which is a particularly good diluent for rose materials.

missing_other.title: Rose Oil, Select
missing_other.description: Introducing Fraterworks® Select products, our new range designed to make exceptional perfumery materials accessible without compromising on quality. Our Bulgarian rose oil maintains the characteristic beauty of this precious material - the same origin, the same steam distillation process, the same captivating floral essence that has made Bulgarian rose the gold standard in perfumery. This product provides an excellent entry point for perfumers, students, and enthusiasts who want to work with authentic Bulgarian rose oil at a more accessible price point. While our signature LMR rose otto remains the ultimate luxury choice, this Fraterworks® rose oil delivers the true character of Bulgarian rose - its honeyed, fresh petal notes and subtle spicy undertones - making it perfect for study, experimentation, and formulation where budget considerations matter. Like all Fraterworks® products, this rose oil is carefully selected to ensure it meets our quality standards while offering exceptional value. It blends beautifully with jasmine, other florals, and can be used effectively in both simple and complex compositions. Available pure and in 10% dilution in natural Triethyl Citrate.

missing_other.title: Rose Orientale
missing_other.description: Oriental rose bases represent or replace natural rose oil (usually of Rosa x damascena ) in a fragrance. The term "oriental" or "d'Orient" referred to such places as Persia from whence the Damascus rose originated. Two oriental rose bases dominated the 20th century; the first was Rose D'Orient (enriched with Orris concrete and used in L'Origan, Chypre, Miss Dior, and many more) and the second was this Rose Orientale (originally from Roure where its internal name was simply "No 6"). Rose Orientale found its way into some great fragrances, such as Tabu by Jean Carles, but its most famous outing was in the Ernest Beaux masterpiece Chanel No 5.

missing_other.title: Rose Queen Marie
missing_other.description: Rose Queen Marie (formerly Rose Parisienne) represents the scent of roseraies (rose gardens) blooming in the French royal gardens as Spring arrives. It is a modern rose base of the essential oil type (Rose D'Orient) and has been used in a number of Guerlain fragrances since the 1980s. The base is named after Queen Marie Antoinette. This base has all the typical components of a rose oil base but in true French royal style it has a more refined and genteel character. Used in traces it imparts a subtle Rose Otto, or in overdose to create a delicate rosy canvas upon which to built an elegant multi-floral fragrance. Rose Queen Marie suits both masculine and feminine fragrances due to its subtle freshness and it is enriched with oils and absolutes from our premium selection of finest naturals.

missing_other.title: Rose Rouge
missing_other.description: Rose Rouge is a sweet classical rose base that layers French geranium with rose absolute and rose otto with other rich naturals to create an incredibly luscious and impactful rose note. Use it in traces to add natural rose to your fragrance, or in overdose for a spectacular and luxurious fragrance. This is a classical base from the early 20th century but there is nothing old fashioned about this wonderful deep red rose.

missing_other.title: Rose St. Columba
missing_other.description: Rose St. Columba is an incredibly natural sweet rose exhibiting all of the qualities of the living flower. This is our most modern rose base and it can be used alone or in combination with our other rose bases or natural rose materials. Inspired by an analysis of the flowers from an old rose bush planted in Ponsonby, Auckland in colonial times, Rose St. Columba is a dream rose.

missing_other.title: Rose Taïf Base
missing_other.description: Rose of Taïf (also known as Taïfi Rose or Wardh Taif) is the most precious rose on earth (even surpassing French grown Rose de Mai in cost). It grows only in the cool mountain air of the Taïf region of Saudi Arabia and is the variety Rosa damascena trigintipetala . Because of the difficulty in obtaining the rose oil we have crafted this ultra-luxurious replica base which is modelled on the real oil. Our Rose Taïf base is enriched with more than 30% pure rose damascena extracts and is the closest thing you will find to the scent of true Taif rose. Use it just like you would any rose essential oil. Due to the high cost of this base, we also offer it diluted to 10% in natural triethyl citrate which is the ideal diluent for rose products.

missing_other.title: Rose Ultimate Extract
missing_other.description: This rose extract is supremely rich and sticky sweet. It is almost impossible to believe it is taken from the materials that were formerly discarded in the process of making rose oil. And the price is simply outstanding. Now any perfumer can have genuine intense natural rose in their fragrances at prices nearly matching those of quality bases. Every perfumer needs this material. Even if you can afford lashings of Bulgarian Rose Absolute and finest Bulgarian Rose Essential Oil , there is room in your perfumer's organ for this astonishing product. LMR has outdone itself in the making of what we agree is the ultimate extract. We also stock Rose Absolute Isparta, the elegant Turkish Rose Absolute, the production of which is the source of the waste materials upcycled in this ultimate extract. Owing to the density of Rose Ultimate (0.96 g/mL) you get more mL than grams in each size. For example 5g gives you 5.2mL. This means that when you buy in mL you are buying less than when you buy in grams. See our FAQ below for more handy conversions and an explanation for this. Origin: Turkey (Isparta) Part: Upcycled Distillate Process: Molecular Distillation

missing_other.title: Rosemary Oil, Tunisia
missing_other.description: A luxurious and complex aromatic oil that has diverse uses in perfumery. This variety from Tunisia is rich in cineole (eucalyptol) which gives it a particularly vibrant top note. This type is often preferred in nature by bees for the production of a particularly delicate and fragrant honey. Rosemary blends incredibly well with lavenders , cedarwood, petitgrain , coumarin and the fresher resins such as labdanum , olibanum and elemi. Origin: Tunisia Part: Flowering tops Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Rosewood Cayenne
missing_other.description: Fraterworks Rosewood Cayenne is a high quality replica of natural bois de rose (rosewood) oil from Cayenne ( French Guiana) . At more than 90% natural oils it fits beautifully into any composition needing fresh top notes with a touch of elegance. Use as a one for one replacer for linalool or rosewood oil. Historically Brazilian rosewood oil was the most common, being both elegant and plentiful. More rare and supremely beautiful was Cayenne rosewood used by only the very best fragrances houses. Fraterworks Rosewood Cayenne is a scentific reconstruction of this supreme oil. This is the pinnacle of elegance in rosewood replacers.

missing_other.title: Rosewood Oil
missing_other.description: This is one of the great historic wood oils of perfumery. The warm rosy heart running through the golden age of French fragrance — through Guerlain, Caron, and Chanel — came from this tree. Every synthetic alternative, every reconstruction on the market exists because this material became almost impossible to source. You are looking at the original. Open the bottle and you understand why nothing replaced it. A sweet, rosy, woody warmth that seems to glow from within — no harshness, no rough edges, just serene floral-wood radiance. The peppery-spicy opening lasts only moments before the oil settles into its true character: luminous, sweet, deeply tenacious. It sits at the exact intersection of wood and flower, belonging fully to neither, and that is precisely what made it irreplaceable. Use it where nothing else will do. It brings a sweetness to woody compositions that cedarwood and sandalwood cannot, and a woody depth to florals that no flower oil can provide. Pair it with ylang-ylang, bergamot, oakmoss, vetiver, or sandalwood — it makes everything around it more refined. Most perfumers alive today have never worked with the real oil. This is your chance. CITES This oil is derived from Aniba rosaeodora, listed under CITES. If you are purchasing for trade you may need a CITES export certificate (check your nation's regulations). We can assist you with that process which is relatively easy. Contact us for more details and costings. For those who prefer not to use a CITES-listed material, we offer Rosewood Cayenne — our own 90%+ natural reconstruction of Cayenne bois de rose, designed as a one-for-one replacer. We also have Linalool ex Bois de Rose .

missing_other.title: Royal Leather
missing_other.description: While Cuir de Russie is wild, smoky and floral, Royal Leather is sophisticated, prim and proper. Royal Leather is the scent of gracefully aged bridle leather, nubuck shoes and peccary gloves. It is the scent of heritage, wealth and class. In traces Royal Leather adds a soft purr to your scent, while an overdose makes a bold statement. Enriched with the finest animalics, resins and sandalwood, this is a must-have modern base that is extraoardinarily easy to use at up to 49% of your perfume formula! So good you can just dilute and go. Royal Leather blends beautifully with Ambre Royale and Sandexol ®. Fraterworks® Royal Leather is a modern leather base. If you are looking for a more intense classical styled leather, see Cuir De Russie 394013 .

missing_other.title: Ruh Khus
missing_other.description: Ruh khus means "soul of khus" — and khus is what India calls vetiver. This is not the tidy, linear vetiver most Western perfumers know from Haiti or Madagascar . This is the wild oil, distilled from roots dug out of the alluvial soils of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, then processed in traditional copper degs in Kannauj using methods that have barely changed in centuries. Our supplier is the premiere traditional maker of this oil in India. The oil is thick, dark brown, almost syrupy. It will keep improving with age — growing rounder, more velvety, more complex over months and years of storage. Its chemical complexity is staggering: over 150 identified sesquiterpene constituents, many still not fully characterised, with an olfactory signature that distinguishes it sharply from all cultivated vetivers. Wild North Indian khus is consumed almost entirely within India, where it commands prices several times higher than the cultivated oil. There is a tonal quality in it — a sweetness woven through the earthiness — that cultivated vetivers simply do not possess. Use it with restraint. Unlike sandalwood, which recedes politely into support, ruh khus insists on being noticed. Build chypre and oriental accords around it with patchouli, cinnamon bark absolute, and oakmoss. Layer it beneath sandalwood for a devastating wood foundation. In fougère structures, it provides a dark, rooted gravity that nothing synthetic can replicate.

missing_other.title: Rum CO2
missing_other.description: This speciality Pure Jungle Essence (CO2 extraction) from V. MANE Fils is a true revelation. It encapsulates the purest aspects of an entire cask of rum from the most volatile alcoholic top notes to the nuanced drydown of scorched sugar. This is a must have natural ingredient for a Piña Colada type base (see our free demonstration formula below) or any scent needing a novel liquor character. “Rum is an alcoholic beverage obtained from sugarcanes and developed in the 17th century on the Caribbean plantations. The distillate is usually aged in barrels and coloured with burnt sugar. Rum became so popular that it was an accepted currency in Europe in the 18th century and George Washington ordered 700 litres of the finest Barbados rum for his pre-election celebration.” — V. MANE Fils. As evidenced by our Golden Seraglio formula (also below), this blends extremely well with MANE's other incredible product: Coffee Arabica Pure Jungle Essence and the magnificent Davana Essential oil from LMR. This material is extremely strong so we also offer it diluted to 10% in natural Triethyl Citrate. Origin: Martinique Method: CO2 Extraction

missing_other.title: Saffron Attar Base
missing_other.description: Attars are beautiful extractions of precious materials, particularly rose and sandalwood. Given the high cost of the raw materials it is not surprising that these can be some of the most expensive products in the naturals trade. Fraterworks' Saffron Attar Base (formerly known as Saffron Attar FW) is a blend which replicates the most sought after and precious extract of crocus stamens. Built around a heart of more than 30% natural Mysore Sandalwood, this base is further enriched with the most delicate trace of fine Omani Frankincense. It's worth every penny. If you are looking for genuine distilled Saffron Attar, we also stock Zafran Attar from the esteemed M. L. Ramnarain. Saffron Attar Base blends well with Osmanthus Flowers , Osmanthus Gold Absolute , Fleur de Cuir , Royal Leather , Olibanum CNC and LMR's Rose Ultimate Extract .

missing_other.title: Saffron Hamra Attar Type Formula
missing_other.description: By far this 2021 Attar from Amouage is the richest and most luxurious of the entire range. Crafted by Cécile Zarokian, it is a beautifully concise 25-line formula, with virtually every ingredient available right here at Fraterworks. Because the naturals in this attar—Bulgarian rose oil, genuine saffron, and a whisper of cade smoke—are so precious, the supporting aroma chemicals must be impeccably pure. Fortunately, Fraterworks offers only the highest-quality aroma chemicals, ensuring a result that rivals the original. Although some enthusiasts feel Amouage scents have lost a bit of their brilliance since Christopher Chong’s departure, the Attars remain a standout series—compact, sophisticated, and reliably elegant. Notes: Saffron, Rose, Cade Difficulty Level: Easy Total Lines: 25 Naturals: 11

missing_other.title: Saffron Oleoresin 5% PG
missing_other.description: Saffron oleoresin performs great in modern compositions. It combines spicy warmth with hay-like and leathery facets while maintaining blend compatibility. It shows versatility across fragrance families and maintains its signature from opening to dry down. Saffron works well with animalic accords, woody bases, and sweet orientals as both key ingredient and modifier. The material transforms compositions into multidimensional creations that project character without overwhelming neighboring notes in complex accords. Blends with R ose Taïf are masterful and, as you would expect, it is wonderful with classic Oud and Attar materials and spices . While we tend to use DPG and TEC as our main solvents for perfumery raw materials, Saffron Oleoresin benefits from dilution with PG (propylene glycol) as it blends well with Saffron's polar and aromatic mix. For that reason Biolandes uses PG (referred to as MPG in their literature) and we purchase this material pre-diluted. PG blends just as well in ethanol based scents as DPG.

missing_other.title: Sage Officinalis Oil
missing_other.description: Sage Essential Oil opens with an immediately recognisable blast of camphoraceous intensity that announces its presence with unwavering authority. This is not a gentle herb but a forceful aromatic statement—the characteristic thujone content (think absinthe) creates a sharp, almost medicinal edge that cuts through any composition with surgical precision. Behind this assertive opening lies warming spice from camphor and subtle pine-like freshness from cineole, creating a complex aromatic architecture that defines classic masculine perfumery. Sage Essential Oil's power lies not in volume but in impact—tiny amounts provide the authentic herbal lift that transforms pedestrian fougères into classics. Use it to sharpen lavender accords, add bite to citrus colognes, or create that distinctive masculine edge in traditional compositions. Its natural complexity provides what no synthetic can—the full-bodied herbal character that reads as authentically aromatic rather than merely fresh. Understanding the crucial differences between Sage and Clary Sage prevents formulation disasters. Where Sage shouts with sharp camphoraceous-thujone intensity, Clary Sage whispers sweet herbaceous-tea sophistication. Sage functions as a restricted top note modifier (thujone limits: 0.11% in lip products, 1.4% in fine fragrance), while Clary Sage serves as unrestricted middle-base fixative rich in linalyl acetate. Sage's medicinal sharpness suits masculine fougères and colognes, whereas Clary Sage's hay-tobacco sweetness enhances everything from florals to ambers. Most critically, Sage oil is IFRA restricted for neurotoxic thujone content, while Clary Sage contains virtually none, making it the safer choice for generous use. Choose Sage for authentic herbal punch in traces; choose Clary Sage for versatile blending and fixation without restriction.

missing_other.title: Sampafleur™
missing_other.description: Sampafleur™ is a beautiful modern base which can be used as a replacer for Jasmine Sambac absolute but in much higher doses. Sampafleur™ is enriched with natural Jasmine Sambac absolute and other luxurious florals. This means that the base alone is sufficient to add richness and classical refinement without the addition of other expensive oils and absolutes. Sampafleur™ blends with all our muguet and rose bases and can extend or replace Jasmine Sambac “Signature” Absolute .

missing_other.title: Sandalwood By-Absolute
missing_other.description: When Biolandes first sent me a sample of this material I was completely unfamiliar with it. By-Absolutes (absolutes produced from the by-products or waste materials of essential oil or absolute manufacturing) are relatively new and it was one I had never sampled. On the first sniff I was in love. This was the truest encapsulation of the soul of historic long-aged sandalwood This is pure nostalgia; secret rooms, vintage perfumes discovered in the back of a medicine cupboard, polished floors in now-vacant European palaces. No Sandalwood material has so excited me in many years. Once a regular part of the Biolandes offering but discontinued, it is now back and we are thrilled to be offering it. Blend this with our marvellous Sandalwood Mysore Oil to give it an instantly aged quality—the perfect blend of luxurious modern sandalwood with the rich complex heart of 100 year old vintage oil. Or simply use it in a scent with such modern wonders as Javanol and Polysantol to naturalise and add complexity to your sandalwood notes. Because it is highly viscous, we sell this at 50% in TEC natural.

missing_other.title: Sandalwood Imperial
missing_other.description: With the skyrocketing costs of genuine Sandalwood Mysore there is a real need for a well priced alternative. Fortunately there are a plethora of incredible sandalwood aroma chemicals out there. Anyone having spent time with those aroma chemicals knows that no single material can really stand in for the natural oil. That's where Sandalwood Imperial comes in. Sandalwood Imperial is a beautifully balanced blend of the best sandalwood chemicals enhanced with large quantities of natural wood materials to replicate that perfect balance of wood and creaminess. Sandalwood Imperiale is a one for one Sandalwood oil replacer. It bears the same strength, longevity and richness of the natural material and blends just as easily. This product blends with virtually all wood chemicals and has a synergy with our highly popular Sandexol ®, a powerful sandalwood base built around the most radiant and powerful aroma chemicals in the santal family. Sandalwood Imperial also works exceedingly well with Firmenich's Dreamwood ® which, while very beautiful, lacks a core of natural wood materials.

missing_other.title: Sandalwood Mysore “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: Distilled from wild and plantation sandalwood trees (including the esteemed heartwood) in Mysore (Mysuru), Karnataka with a minimum age of 25 years, this is the finest quality sandalwood essential oil (मैसूर चंदन तेल). This is the authentic sandalwood of bygone days, sourced from the region formerly known as the Kingdom of Mysore (encompassing a greater area than the present day Mysore city). This essential oil is so vibrant and alive that it dances. Packed with creamy goodness that typifies the highest quality sandalwood, this product also has a classic almost musky animal intensity in the dry down. This is not a linear B-grade sandalwood extraction, this is a rich and complex classic sandalwood oil. Wear it straight on the skin, add it to a perfume, or put it down to age for a decade. This is the gold standard of sandalwood which is why it carries our “signature” mark. Authenticity Our oil has a verified (Z)-α-santalol content of 47.5% and a (Z)-β-santalol content of 20.4% confirming its authenticity via ISO 3518:2022 (the international standard for verifying Sandalwood oil). Kingdom of Mysore Mysore sandalwood oil is extracted from trees that come from the southern parts of the Western Ghats, basically encompassing present day Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and the Konkan region of Maharashtra. The finest quality is from the forest regions of Marayoor in Kerala and present day Mysore city in Karnataka (formerly the capital of the greater Mysore kingdom). Much confusion exists today as trees from areas outside Mysore city are correctly (but confusingly) a source of traditional Mysore sandalwood oil. Legal Information As of 2022, the government of Karnataka removed all restrictions on the private growing and selling of sandalwood on the open market. Origin: Southern India (regions of the former Kingdom of Mysore); मैसूर कर्नाटक Part: Heartwood Method: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Sandalwood Oil “Indian”, Australia
missing_other.description: Unfortunately the demand for sustainable Indian sandalwood has been so low that the grower and supplier (Quintis) has fallen into receivership - the Australian equivalent of Chapter 7 Bankruptcy. Consequently once our supply of this oil runs out, we will be unable to replenish stocks. If the notion of terroir is less important to you than the sustainability and ethics of your raw materials, this is the sandalwood for you. Not only is our Australian Santalum Album environmentally friendly, it also has the beauty and regal quality of classical Mysore sandalwood - the sandalwood of epic poems and history. Australia is now a source of both Santalum Album (“Indian” Sandalwood) and Santalum Spicatum (an Australian native). This product is the Indian variety. Environmental Data We can trace each batch of our Australian sandalwood oil down to the hectare of trees from which it was extracted. Using continuous distillation, our supplier is able to lower their energy needs by 75% compared to regular distillation, and of the remaining energy used over 80% is from renewable sources. The entire plantation absorbs 195,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere each year. Carbon Zero Transport Because we are right next door to Australia we don't need to ship our sandalwood oil half way across the planet before we offer it to you; the trip from “farm” to Fraterworks is a short carbon zero flight. Origin: Australian Variety: Santalum Album (Indian sandalwood) Part: Heartwood Method: Continuous steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Sandalwood Oil, Australia
missing_other.description: Australian Sandalwood Oil opens with surprisingly fresh, green-terpenic character—drier and sharper than you might expect from sandalwood. The signature creamy-milky notes emerge quickly but remain lighter, more yoghurt-like than the thick buttery richness of Indian sandalwood. Warm peppery spice adds complexity, while cedary-woody undertones provide the familiar sandalwood base. This essential oil comes from Santalum spicatum, a small evergreen tree native to arid southwestern Australia. The lower santalol content (20–40% versus Indian's 70–90%) creates a distinctly different olfactory profile: fresher, woodier, and more terpenic. Crucially, S. spicatum presents earlier in a formula than other sandalwood species, projecting its character during the dry-down rather than lurking purely at the base. This makes it effective at surprisingly low concentrations (0.1–2%). Australian Sandalwood vs Indian Sandalwood These two sandalwood oils offer fundamentally different characters despite sharing the Santalum genus. Indian Sandalwood (Santalum album) is the richer, creamier option—soft, buttery, sensual, with thick lactonic sweetness and clove-like spice. It's intimate and enveloping, the classic sandalwood of fine perfumery. Australian Sandalwood (Santalum spicatum) is drier, greener, and more terpenic—fresh woodshop sawdust rather than warm butter, with sharper spicy facets and cedary depth. It projects more readily and presents earlier in the dry-down. Use Indian when you want luxurious creamy warmth; Australian when you need woody projection and accessible naturalism. Most commercial sandalwood fragrances actually rely on Australian oil combined with synthetics rather than prohibitively expensive Indian.

missing_other.title: Sandalwood Oil, New Caledonia
missing_other.description: You will find it hard to beat our price on this sublime New Caledonian essential oil from LMR, the top supplier in the world with decades of experiencing in the sandalwood field. Despite being a different species to the Indian oil, New Caledonian sandalwood is not an inferior product but must be taken on its own merits. The oil is highly sustainable and has an odour profile very similar to the Indian oil. In fact it is so good that Chanel used it to replace the 10% Mysore Sandalwood in their famous Égoïste when cost and scarcity became problems. LMR has partnered with a 100% kanak company located on Lifou Island in New Caledonia, in the Xepenehe village, for responsibly sourced sandalwood. LMR pre-financed all the equipment needed by our partner to build a new facility. Their Sandalwood Oil New Caledonia is "For Life" certified, showing their commitment to transparency and sustainability. For a tiny boost and to tweak the oil in the direction of Mysore Sandalwood try this little accord: 900 Sandalwood Oil, New Caledonia 60 Amyris Oil 25 Cedarwood Virginia Oil 8.5 Firsantol 5 Guaiac Wood Oil 1.5 Polysantol

missing_other.title: Sandexol®
missing_other.description: Fraterworks Sandexol ® is a powerful and radiant sandalwood base which can be used standalone as a one for one replacement for natural sandalwood oil. Sandexol is also perfect for extending sandalwood notes in a fragrance or adding a nuance to a multi-wood fond. Sandexol ® is constructed around natural absolutes and oils in addition to the very latest radiant sandalwood molecules. This is an essential tool for all perfumers, adding beauty and exaltation to your creations. Sandexol ® i s perfect for creating a luxurious woody foundation for modern gourmand fragrances.

missing_other.title: Saxon Moss (Mousse de Saxe)
missing_other.description: The famed Mousse de Saxe base has been, until now, long gone — although modernised bases have appeared in recent years as historic perfumery becomes popular once again. Fraterworks recreation of the original, which we call Saxon Moss, is true to the original Mousse de Saxe as we can make it. Rich with naturals, including a megadose of Mysore sandalwood, this wonderful mossy leathery base can be felt at less than 1% of a fragrance yet it can still be used in large amounts (as the original was) in such fragrances as Nuit de Noel by Caron (formula below) and Chanel No 19 . The original Mousse de Saxe contained musk xylene which we have judiciously replaced in our Saxon Moss base for IFRA compliance.

missing_other.title: Scent Strips, 100 Pack
missing_other.description: Scent strips are an essential tool for perfumers. Our high quality strips (also known as mouillettes) are made from luxurious acid free card stock 400 microns thick. This stock is environmentally friendly and contains no glues or resins — just pure and natural paper. Each white strip (sold in sets of 100) measures 20mm by 160mm and has a crease down the centre to allow you to fold the strip when dipping into bottles with small mouths. The crease runs end to end. These strips are designed with the perfumer in mind and can be used for soaking (via dipping) or spraying (hold the wide end and spray the pointed end). Our scent strips are made in New Zealand. NOTE: The stand pictured here does not come with the scent strips.

missing_other.title: Schisandra Fruit CO2
missing_other.description: Schisandra does not smell like a bright berry. The first impression is warm, woody, and softly balsamic — dried plums and goji berries layered over a peppery, lightly smoky base. It reads as comforting and rooty, more forest floor than fruit bowl. Use it as a blender to add quiet complexity to orientals, spiced compositions, and woody-fruity accords. It fills gaps between notes rather than standing alone. Pair with ylang ylang, patchouli, and frankincense for a dark, contemplative base with an unusual fruity undertow. This is Schisandra chinensis — the legendary "five-flavour berry" of Chinese medicine, named for possessing all five basic tastes simultaneously. It grows wild in the forests of Manchuria and the Russian Far East. The CO2 extract is still uncommon in perfumery — an explorer's material.

missing_other.title: Seaweed Fucus Absolute
missing_other.description: Fucus absolute hits you with raw, salty iodine and an immediate phenolic dryness — seaweed drying on rocks after a storm, with smoke and leather underneath. It is far rougher and more confrontational than Laminaria absolute. Where Laminaria is refined, Fucus is feral. It is extraordinarily powerful. Use it when you want marine character with real bite — in dark chypres, leather accords, and compositions that need an animalic, oceanic edge. It reads more like wet harbour rope and weathered wood than clean seaside air. On dilution it becomes greener and more aquatic, with mineral-oyster facets emerging in the drydown. Always work from heavy dilution. Three seaweeds, three tools. We carry three seaweed materials — they are not interchangeable. Seaweed Fucus Absolute (bladderwrack) is the roughest and most animalic — salty, phenolic, with harbour-side leather. That's this product. Laminaria absolute is the most refined: iodine into mushroom and cocoa, with mossy depth. Red Seaweed CO₂ (Palmaria palmata) from V. MANE Fils is almost gourmand: umami richness and savoury briny depth with none of the harshness. Layer all three for the most complete natural marine accord you can build.

missing_other.title: Seaweed Laminaria Absolute
missing_other.description: Briny iodine, wet rocks, seaweed drying in the sun — laminaria absolute is the genuine smell of the Atlantic coast. It has nothing in common with synthetic aquatic notes. The drydown shifts into dark mushroom, walnut, and cocoa, finishing mossy and woody. Use laminaria wherever you want marine character that smells like a real coastline. In chypres, it fills the dark, grounding role of oakmoss but with an oceanic identity. A trace in green or woody compositions adds mystery and a convincing sense of place. Pair it with oakmoss and vetiver for a full coastal chypre, or with labdanum and cypriol for dark marine depth. The cocoa-mushroom drydown works surprisingly well alongside tobacco and leather notes. Work from a dilution — it is extremely powerful. This is a Payan Bertrand Signature material. Three seaweeds, three tools. We carry three seaweed materials — they are not interchangeable. Laminaria absolute (this one) is the most refined: iodine into mushroom and cocoa, with mossy depth. Seaweed Fucus Absolute (bladderwrack) is rawer — saltier, greener, overtly phenolic, with harbour-side roughness that reads more animalic than marine. Red Seaweed CO₂ (Palmaria palmata) from V. MANE Fils is almost gourmand: umami richness and savoury briny depth with none of the harshness. Layer all three for the most complete natural marine accord you can build.

missing_other.title: Sesame SFE Absolute
missing_other.description: Sesame SFE Absolute opens with unmistakable roasted warmth — toasted bread, caramelised hazelnuts, and a coffee-like richness that signals gourmand territory immediately. A balsamic woody undertone sits beneath the nuttiness. The effect is deeply comforting and remarkably true to freshly toasted sesame seeds. Use Sesame SFE to boost and enrich gourmand accords — it adds volume and naturalistic warmth that synthetic alternatives struggle to match. This Firmenich CO2 extract pairs brilliantly with vanilla, tonka, and amber bases. Even small additions transform a composition's gourmand credibility. Blend with coffee absolute and vanillin for a rich café accord, or layer beneath sandalwood and benzoin for an oriental with toasted depth. Supercritical CO2 extraction captures the complete aromatic profile of the seed without heat damage. Sesame remains rare in perfumery — your compositions will stand apart. A costly material, we dilute this to 10% in natural triethyl citrate. Note that the 10% solution also includes 10% food grade ethanol. There are no denaturants or non-natural additions to this product.

missing_other.title: Shamama
missing_other.description: Shamama is one of the great traditional Indian attars: warm, spicy, herbal, woody, resinous, and long-lasting. It may be worn directly as a perfume oil, but it is also widely used as a compounding base in mukhallat, bakhoor, incense, tobacco, and oriental-style perfume blends. Shamama opens with a warm spice-smoke accord — clove, cinnamon, cardamom and nutmeg over roasted cypriol, spikenard and valerian roots. The sandalwood base sits underneath, threaded with charila lichen and choya smoke. A faint floral lift from rose, jasmine and saffron lights up the heart. Use Shamama as the anchor of orientals, mukhallats and bakhoor compositions where you want dense Indian complexity in one material. A few drops bind disparate notes into a unified whole, scaffolding rose, oud, ambergris and saffron. In tobacco and incense bases it adds heating animalic depth lighter florals cannot reach. This Shamama is from M.L. Ramnarain Perfumers, one of the oldest continuously operating distilleries in Kannauj. The Kapoor family has been distilling for five generations using the traditional deg-bhapka method. Their Shamama is widely considered among the finest examples of the form. For more information on how Shamama are made, read our article Oils and Attars of Indian and Oriental Perfumery .

missing_other.title: Siberian Castoreum Tincture 3%
missing_other.description: Siberian castoreum has historically been considered inferior to the Canadian variety, but upon smelling this beautiful tincture one can't help but wonder if cold-war politics may have had a part to play in that judgement. This tincture is, in our opinion, finer than Canadian and more nuanced. While both varieties have a soft smokiness the main difference is that the Siberian product has a more profoundly natural leather note with fewer fruity aspects making it drier. This is our favourite castoreum tincture, a tincture which transports you to the wintery woodlands of ancient Russia so beloved by Chanel perfumer Ernest Beaux. Our Siberian castoreum tincture is made in exactly the same way as all of our tinctures, using finest pure and natural alcohol. ‘Castoreum [tincture's] warm, animal, leather-like sweet odour makes it an interesting item in “men's perfumes”, fougeres, chypres, Oriental bases, leather notes, Tabac bases, etc. [It blends] particularly well with ambra notes, calamus, cananga, cedarwood Atlas, chamomile moroccan, creosol, labdanum products, isoeugenol, oakmoss products, sandalwood oil, […] etc.’ — S. Arctander. Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin, Carol Stream: Allured Publishing Corporation, 2008, pp. 136–137. French Name: Infusion de Castoréum

missing_other.title: Solafleur™
missing_other.description: Solafleur is a modern multifloral base of great softness and finesse. It blends together delicate materials with natural oils to make a high-use base that sits perfectly at the heart of a modern fragrance. Solafleur smells like a tranquil summer day at the beachside: suntan lotion, warm sand and the scent of light florals floating on a gentle breeze. In the scent of Solafleur you can almost hear the distant laughter of children at play and seabirds crooning from above frothy waves. Solafleur's blends with Gardenia J. Ellis , Neroli Supreme , Tuberose Supreme and Rose Blanche (white rose) are sublime, but it also creates beautiful accords with Pink Acacia , Bouvardia DL , Amarante , Muguet 16 , Mellitis , Lilac A07 , Lyfral ®, Dianthine Extra , Prunol SP , and Saxon Moss .

missing_other.title: Solgard®
missing_other.description: Solgard ® is a proprietary blend of virtually odourless industry standard UV blockers, conditioners and preservatives for fine fragrances. Now your products can benefit from the very same protection used by all the major fragrance producers. Solgard offers protection from UVA and UVB rays, potentially reducing discolouration and changes to the odour profile due to exposure to light. To support long-term stability, Solgard contains Tocopherol (Vitamin E) as its antioxidant preservative system. This natural antioxidant helps extend shelf life without the labelling and perception issues sometimes associated with synthetic stabilisers. The previous Solgard® B variant, which contained BHT, has been discontinued and is no longer supplied. Solgard also contains octyl salicylate, parsol ( Neo Heliopan® ) and avobenzone. Typical use is to pre-fix your perfumers alcohol with 1% Solgard (10 grams of Solgard per kg of ethanol). Alternatively, Solgard can be safely added directly to your fragrance juice, with typical use from 0.5% – 4%. British, New Zealand and European destined fragrances should not contain more than 15% Solgard. You can boost the effects of Solgard® with Oxynex® ST . Solgard® is a registered trademark [1229641] of Frater Perfumes Ltd. Because this product is designed to be added to blends in quantities over which Frater Perfumes has no control we make no warranty or guarantees as to its suitability for your fragrances. Solgard® is for commercial use only and is not a sunblock or sun tan lotion. Solgard® should not be applied directly to the skin but used only as an additive in the manufacture of fine fragrances.

missing_other.title: Sophira
missing_other.description: Sophira is the restoration of the classical base Sophora , an artistic copy (created by Marius Reboul of Roure) of the competing Cedarome base by Chuit Naef & Cie. In S ophira , Reboul focussed on the intense vetiver quality of the original base which was a balance of vetiver and cedarwood. Sophira formed the core of Un Air Embaumé by Rigaud in 1912 combined with a healthy dose of Jasmin Blanc and it was key to Tabac Blond by Caron in 1919. It was also used in the magnificent Nuit de Chine (1911, Rosine) in harmony with Rose D'Orient and sandalwood. Like most bases of the era, Sophira is built around a delicate balance of other bases, resulting in a very complex and rich foundation for your fragrances. NOTE: This product may crystallise slightly in cold environments. Apply gentle heat to dissolve.

missing_other.title: Southernwood Oil
missing_other.description: Opening with a light tangerine note mixed with camphor, pine and wormwood, this rare oil was called both Lad's Love and maiden's ruin in the 18th and 19th centuries because of its alleged aphrodisiacal properties and the promise to cure baldness and grow beards in men. It was frequently used as part of a church nosegay (a small bouquet of flowers) sniffed during long church sermons to keep the holder awake and to mask the malodours of large gatherings of people. The French called it "garderobe" for its reputation protecting clothes from moths. The pine-woody undertones add structure, while bitter wormwood character (for it is a member of the artemesia genus along with Armoise ) provides the distinctive signature of that genus. Green herbaceous depth emerges as the oil develops, creating a profile that feels simultaneously medicinal and refreshing. Work with Southernwood Oil sparingly—its intensity requires respect. Use it in fougère and chypre compositions where bitter herbal notes provide complexity, or in masculine aromatics seeking green freshness with character. The camphoraceous lift works beautifully alongside lavender, rosemary, and other aromatic herbs. Blend with oakmoss, coumarin, and citrus oils for novel aromatic effects. Its wormwood-like bitterness adds sophisticated depth to otherwise sweet compositions. All in all, this is an unusual and interesting oil that deserves a wider use in modern perfumery.

missing_other.title: Spearmint “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: This is the most refined spearmint oil we have ever experienced! From a single estate in England, this oil has perfectly balanced top notes which bear the signature spearmint scent from the very first sniff. Use small amounts to add vibrance and freshness to top notes, both masculine and feminine, or overdose it for a characterful minty scent. You will never want another spearmint oil after trying our Signature product. Origin: England Variety: Mentha spicata L. Part: Leaves Method: Steam distillation at source and aged 2 years

missing_other.title: Spicyrup™
missing_other.description: There is no denying it: we love the naturals from V. MANE Fils , but we also love their bases, an area in which we ourselves are specialists. Spicyrup™ is one such base. Built around an overdose of the MANE captive Presantone H™, this base opens with dank earthiness and dries down into a rich gourmand accord reminiscent of carrot cake, caramel, liquorice, and spices. An incredibly unique and unusual base, the possibilities are endless. The loamy opening is crying out for a rich patchouli pairing, while the exceptionally balanced, vanilla-leaning dry down would work beautifully with a classic Tabu-like blend, albeit in a highly modernised context.

missing_other.title: Spiked Ginger Lily Oil
missing_other.description: Do not expect ginger — this is something else entirely. The oil opens fresh and camphoraceous, almost eucalyptus-like, then unfolds into a rich, warm cinnamon-spice body of extraordinary depth. The drydown is woody and balsamic, less sweet but still warmly spiced. Use it in balsamic, woody, and heavy-floral bases where you want warm cinnamon-spice without using actual cinnamon oil. It works beautifully in lavender and lavandin compositions, adding spicy richness and remarkable tenacity. Blends well with styrax, benzoin, sandalwood, and ionones. This is Hedychium spicatum — a Himalayan ginger lily distilled from its rhizomes, known in India as kapur kachri and in Japanese perfumery as sanna. Arctander considered it exceptionally versatile but noted it was never regularly available outside Asia. That scarcity persists today (unless you are a Fraterworks customer!)

missing_other.title: Spikenard Oil
missing_other.description: Spikenard (Jatamansi) hits the nose with deep, sweet earth — damp forest floor, rooty warmth, and a musky-animalic depth that is entirely its own. There are facets of chocolate, ginger, cardamom, and Atlas cedarwood, but the overall impression is darker and more primordial than any of those. It smells ancient. Use it as a base note in orientals, heavy florals, and woody-animalic compositions. It blends naturally with patchouli, vetiver, labdanum, and oakmoss — anywhere you want earthy depth and fixation. A single drop anchors a formula and extends the life of everything above it. This is one of the oldest perfume materials on earth — the nard of the Bible, burned by Nero and used by St Mary Magdalene to anoint the feet of Christ. It grows wild above 3,000 metres in the Himalayas and is still harvested by hand from remote slopes. Scarce, irreplaceable, and profoundly beautiful. Spikenard essential oil is derived from a species listed in CITES Appendix II. However, the essential oil itself is generally excluded from CITES controls under the annotation that applies to this species. For that reason, a CITES export, re-export, or certificate of origin is not usually required for normal trade in the oil. Import requirements can still vary by country, and some jurisdictions may have their own customs or wildlife rules. We recommend checking with your local authorities before ordering if you are unsure.

missing_other.title: Star Anise Oil
missing_other.description: Leverage Star Anise for its remarkable ability to impart immediate character and warmth, bridging top and middle phases effectively. Its complex undertones offer versatility beyond the expected liquorice facet, adding depth to aromatic Fougères and even floral compositions. This is a cornerstone spice material. While both Star Anise oil ( Illicium verum ) and Anise oil ( Pimpinella anisum ) share a dominant sweet, liquorice-like aroma from trans -anethole, Star Anise is botanically distinct, often stronger, woodier, and contains IFRA regulated estragole (also found in tarragon oil), unlike Anise. At low temperatures this oil may crystallise. In that case, simply warm to melt.

missing_other.title: Styrax Oil, Honduras
missing_other.description: Styrax (or more correctly storax) is a sweet and delicate material which blends well with the other classic perfumery resins; it works well as a fixative (especially for iris notes). Styrax is most commonly found as a resinoid or absolute, but this more rare hexane free essential oil is a beautiful material for florals, particularly delicates ones such as muguet. Felt more in the top notes but still a classic resinous dry down, this is really quite a valuable material at a very good price. The proper naming conventions for all balsams is: Crude Balsam → Steam Distillation → Essential Oil [this product] Crude Balsam → Non-Ethanol Solvent Extraction → Resin oid Crude Balsam → Ethanol Extraction → Resin Absolute [and sometimes resinoid] While a resin absolute is often wrongly referred to simply as an "absolute", the correct use of that term within the balsams category is for an alcohol extraction of a previously extracted resinoid (usually produced with hexane or other non-alcohol solvent). Resin oid → Alcohol Extraction → Absolute NOTE: This is IFRA compliant styrax oil Country of Origin: Honduras Part: Tree exudate Method of production: Steam distillation at source

missing_other.title: Styrax Resinoid EAL, Wild
missing_other.description: Styrax (or more correctly storax) resinoid is a sweet and delicate material which blends wonderfully with the other classic perfumery resins; it works well as a fixative (especially for iris notes). These days most extracts on the market suffer from a pronounced styrene note (the plastic smell of polystyrene) which, being far from the genuine odour of styrax, more closely resembles the smell of an old mechanic's shop. As pleasant an odour as that may be for some, it has no place in the scent profile of styrax. This styrax resinoid is sweet, cinnamic, vanilla, subtly spicy and enticing. It is extracted from the raw balsam of wild Liquidambar styraciflua trees (commonly known as American sweetgum or hazel pine) using just-warm alcohol (hence the EAL designation in the name). This produces a “resin absolute” as opposed to a true resinoid or absolute. However, the market has generally taken to referring to these styrax materials as resinoids and so we are using the name of the manufacturer. The proper naming conventions for all balsams is: Crude Balsam → Steam Distillation → Essential Oil Crude Balsam → Non-Ethanol Solvent Extraction → Resin oid Crude Balsam → Ethanol Extraction → Resin Absolute [and sometimes resinoid] While a resin absolute is often wrongly referred to simply as an "absolute", the correct use of that term within the balsams category is for an alcohol extraction of a previously extracted resinoid (usually produced with hexane or other non-alcohol solvent). Resin oid → Alcohol Extraction → Absolute Our wild harvested styrax resin absolute is the finest extraction on the market. Nothing else comes close. This is so good you will start looking for opportunities to feature it in a fragrance. NOTE: This is IFRA compliant styrax resin due to the absence of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons: None detected [limit of detection: benzopyrene Country of Origin: Honduras Country of Manufacture: France Variety: Liquidambar styraciflu

missing_other.title: Suederal® LT 0710
missing_other.description: Suederal® is one of the most well-known leather bases and while we love and use Royal Leather far more, this IFF product is a wonderful addition to the perfumer's toolkit and one we highly recommend. Small amounts can be used as a fixative while large amounts give a very distinctive suede character. Compared to Royal Leather, Suederal is drier and more chemical smelling, so it works particularly well when combined with other materials. Suederal® blends marvellously with Royal Leather , Cuir de Russie , Fleur de Cuir , Verdantol ™, Neobutenone® Alpha , Permawood ™, and Saxon Moss .

missing_other.title: Sugandh Kokila Oil
missing_other.description: Sugandh Kokila Oil smells warmly spicy and camphoraceous, with a fresh herbal-minty top and a resinous, slightly fruity base. It is steam-distilled from the dried berries of Cinnamomum glaucescens, a wild tree in the cinnamon family native to the mid-hills of Nepal. The oil runs pale yellow. In fine fragrance it brings natural spice and warmth to masculine colognes, fougères and modern orientals. The camphor edge sharpens cedar, patchouli and vetiver, while the fresh top lifts heavier spicy materials like clove and cinnamon. It also ties citrus and green notes to a warm woody base. Pair with bergamot, lavender and coumarin for a modern fougère, or use against benzoin, labdanum and amber for a spicy oriental. A touch alongside tobacco absolute adds smoky warmth. Use sparingly — the camphor side can push through and dominate if overdosed.

missing_other.title: Sugandh Mantri Oil
missing_other.description: Sugandh mantri opens with a sweet, floral-woody freshness that immediately recalls rosewood — but give it a minute. Underneath sits a deep, damp, earthy rootiness like nothing else in the palette. The combination of floral top and earthy base makes it genuinely unusual. Use it as an earthy base note in orientals, woody compositions, and Indian-inspired attars. It adds a damp, rooty depth that rosewood and ho wood cannot — they give you the floral sweetness but not the earth. Blend with sandalwood, patchouli, vetiver, and frankincense for warm, contemplative bases. The name means "Minister of Fragrance" in Sanskrit — this root has been a cornerstone of Indian attar-making for centuries. Arctander judged it as just another linalool source, redundant alongside rosewood and ho wood — but he was evaluating supply, not character. Today's interest is in provenance and personality, and this root has both.

missing_other.title: Suralette™ Extra
missing_other.description: Suralette™ Extra is a complex herbal base containing over 40 natural oils and absolutes. It is a key base in the original Aventus (formula below). Suralette Extra is green, herbal, anisic and woody and is a wonderful addition to the perfumer's library. In small amounts it adds complexity and radiance, while in large amounts it provides a unique alternative to anise naturals such as star anise, mugwort and tarragon. Suralette Extra blends beautifully with green notes and particularly with narcissus, jonquil, muguet and tropical fruit. Also synergistic with Verdantol ™, Jonquil , and Pineapple Supreme .

missing_other.title: Sweet Clover Absolute
missing_other.description: Opening with a profoundly coumarinic and edible tonka note with a curious seminal nuance, the herbaceous nature of this absolute becomes more obvious as it dries down. Known as Melilot in classical perfumery, this is a new offering from Biolandes and at a massive 15% allowance under IFRA 51 it clearly positions itself as a great alternative to tonka bean absolute. Sweet Clover Absolute is extremely refined, offering not just the gourmand and agrestic qualities you'd expect for a coumarin rich grass, but it evokes warm days lying in green fields as clouds float lazily above. This is a dream in a bottle, a hint at summers to come and a distant memory of summers past. A true delight that belongs on every perfumer's shelf. Sweet Clover holds a distinguished place in perfumery history as nature's coumarin source before synthetic alternatives emerged. Classic fougères relied on melilot's hay-like sweetness to create their characteristic aromatic warmth. Today's perfumers value this absolute for its complex natural profile that synthetic coumarin cannot replicate—those subtle tobacco, almond, and caramel undertones that develop during proper extraction make all the difference in sophisticated compositions. Owing to the thickness and difficulty of working with this material, it is sold exclusively at 40% dilution in DPG so it is pourable.

missing_other.title: Sweet Marjoram Oil
missing_other.description: Sweet marjoram opens with warm spice — nutmeg and cardamom, not the green herbs you expect. A gentle woody undertone and faint medicinal sweetness sit underneath, but the dominant impression is soft, inviting warmth. It is one of the most underused naturals in fine fragrance. Use it in fougères to add warm depth between lavender top notes and oakmoss-coumarin bases. It gives colognes an unexpected richness — just enough exotic warmth to lift a simple citrus structure into something considered. A natural companion for nutmeg, bergamot, and clary sage. Fraterworks also stocks Wild Marjoram Oil ( Thymus mastichina ), which despite the name is a thyme — eucalyptus-forward, camphoraceous, and bracing. Sweet marjoram shares no common ground with it. They are named the same but smell nothing alike, and are never interchangeable.

missing_other.title: Sweet Orange Oil 10 Fold
missing_other.description: Folded citrus oils are highly concentrated, having been fractionated to remove many of the terpenes and leaving behind the heart of the oil (in this case limonene — up to 85% — and a considerable amount of aldehyde C-10). Our orange oil (taken from the peels of sweet and blood oranges) is ten times folded, making it very similar to terpeneless orange oil but retaining the natural colour of the oil. Folded orange is a little softer and easier to work with, and has the same benefit of terpeneless oil in being longer lasting than regular citrus. Additionally this has a better blended aldehydic character. Mere touches contribute a wonderful character to colognes or use it to blend with linalool and linalyl acetate to create your own unique citrus oil. Origin: Calabria, Italy Variety: Citrus sinensis Part: Peel Method: Cold pressed at source and fractionated

missing_other.title: Sweet Orange Oil, Decolourised
missing_other.description: Sometimes you need a hit of citrus without the extreme colour. This sweet orange oil is a wonderfully natural and fine Tarocco blood orange oil (a type of sweet orange with a particularly good character) that has the benefit of being completely devoid of all colour. It is as clear as water without sacrificing any odour. Also known as Sweet Orange Oil Decolorized.

missing_other.title: Sweet Orange Oil, Terpeneless
missing_other.description: Terpeneless oils can help to reduce the risks of clouding in fragrances and also pack a greater punch than the standard oils. In fact, this sweet orange terpeneless is about the most powerful orange note you can find in a non-single chemical form. In a Chypre a trace of this will leave a lasting orange note right through the dry down and can certainly hold its own against overdoses of Oakmoss, Labdanum and other rich base materials. Or use a touch to boost and support a lovely blended citrus top note. If you want something that is also very strong but retaining more of the terpenes and nuance of fresh orange, we also stock Sweet Orange Oil 10 Fold . Origin: Calabria, Italy Part: Peel Method: Cold pressed at source and deterpinated

missing_other.title: Sweet Orange “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: Our sweet orange signature oil is extracted from blood oranges, resulting in a slightly sweeter, richer and more elegant oil. Being more than 99% Limonene, this beautiful natural can be used with no limitations at all though we recommend the addition of Solgard ® or Butylated Hydroxytoluene to any fragrances in which you use this in order to prevent oxidation products from forming. Origin: Italy Part: Peel Method: Cold pressed at source

missing_other.title: Sweet Pea
missing_other.description: Sweet Pea has a bluish scent and it is the key note in Jour d'Hermes , the highly popular sweet floral from 2013. In recent years sweet pea has enjoyed a rebirth in fragrance circles and when you smell Fraterworks Sweet Pea you will understand why. This base is not an abstraction of the flower, it is a full bodied rich and luxurious base loaded with rare and precious absolutes and oils. All you need is a trace, but overdoses are welcome too.

missing_other.title: Tagetes Oil
missing_other.description: Tagetes (Marigold) oil hits your nose with an almost aggressive burst of green — crushed leaves, bitter herbs, and a sharp vegetal pungency. Give it a few moments and a sweet, fruity character emerges underneath. Dilute it further and you find a beautiful apple-like softness that explains everything. This oil earns its place through transformation — in trace amounts it becomes an extraordinary green-fruity modifier. Add it to florals for an airy, naturalistic lift that nothing synthetic can replicate. Pair it with clary sage, bergamot, or jasmine for complex herbaceous-fruity accords. Handle tagetes oil with respect — it resinifies on exposure to air and light, so keep it sealed and dark. No substitute exists for its unique character; once you build it into a formula, you will always need it. It helped define Calyx by Prescriptives and remains irreplaceable in modern perfumery.

missing_other.title: Tangerine Heart
missing_other.description: Tangerine Heart is the most generous member of the LMR citrus heart range. Where Lemon Heart is sharp and sparkling, Lime Heart is zesty and green, and Orange Heart is warm and marmalade-rich, Tangerine Heart brings something none of them offer: sweetness with genuine floral depth. It opens juicy and bright — ripe tangerine peel, immediately mouthwatering — but underneath there is a soft floralcy, almost neroli-like, that gives it a complexity the other citrus hearts lack. This is an LMR speciality developed in partnership with IFF Citrasource in Florida. Like all the citrus hearts, it is a concentrated fraction produced by molecular distillation — the terpenic bulk removed, the character amplified, the tenacity extended far beyond what standard tangerine oil can achieve. A few drops in your formula will push that juicy, sparkling citrus character well into the heart of a composition. Standard tangerine oil shares a species with mandarin — both are Citrus reticulata — but the tangerine cultivar runs sweeter, stronger, and more overtly fruity. The Heart version concentrates those differences further. Use it in fruity florals, gourmand compositions, and summer colognes where you want citrus sweetness rather than citrus sharpness. Pair it with Orange Heart for a rich, layered citrus accord, or combine with neroli and petitgrain for a tangerine blossom effect.

missing_other.title: Tarragon “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: Tarragon oil is a wonderful herb with a distinctive anise note. It is indispensible in Chypre fragrances and was found in the original (formula below). Our signature Hungarian tarragon is lively and fresh; a must have oil. According to Steffen Arctander: “Tarragon (estragon) is a colorless, or very pale yellow to greenish-yellow liquid, with a sweet-anisic, green-spicy, slightly celery-like odor, very similar to that of the fresh herb. Tarragon (Estragon) is used in perfumery, usually in trace amounts, in Chypre, l’Origan types, Fougères, lilac bases, green floral bases, etc. Blends well with galbanum , lavender , vanilla, cardamom , clovebud, oakmoss .” Origin: Hungary Part: Leaves Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Taste of Rose Sample Kit
missing_other.description: This deluxe sample kit gives you a broad overview of our most beloved rose bases, naturals and aroma chemicals.
