missing_other.title: Tea Black SFE
missing_other.description: Open the tin, not the teapot. Tea Black SFE smells of the dry leaf itself: leafy and hay-like, with tobacco and a gentle smokiness, an astringent, tannic edge and a fresh, spicy lift running through it. Extracted with carbon dioxide rather than hot solvent, it stays true to the leaf. Use it to bring a smoky, woody dimension to compositions. It anchors tea accords with the realism of the leaf, deepens leather and tobacco themes, and gives chypres and orientals a dry, tannic backbone. A little in a rose or osmanthus heart lends the thorny, bitter darkness of tea rose. Bergamot on top gives you Earl Grey; cardamom, cinnamon and a touch of vanilla turn it toward chai. For a smokier direction add a trace of birch tar or guaiacwood. With osmanthus and violet leaf it slips into a floral-leather, and beside oud or labdanum it turns dark and contemplative. Tea CO2 extracts are famously difficult to work with, so Firmenich supplies these ready-diluted and fully mobile in ethanol. We stock the full tea SFE range: Jasmine Tea SFE, Tea White SFE, Tea Green SFE, and Tea Keemun SFE.

missing_other.title: Tea Green SFE
missing_other.description: This is green tea as dried leaf rather than brewed cup: fresh, aromatic and green, with a hay-like herbal character, an oily, woody body and a faint seaweed nuance at the edges. The leaves come from China, oven-warmed straight after picking, and the extract smells more matcha tin than teahouse. Use it to bring a fresh, aromatic green effect to aromatic and gourmand compositions, to lend leafy realism to a green tea accord, or to sharpen a citrus cologne with a herbal, slightly bitter greenness. Start small: a little gives a herbal accent, more gives a distinct tea signature. Hedione opens it into the airy, transparent tea heart of modern fresh florals. With bergamot, petitgrain and a trace of mint it becomes a green tea cologne; with violet leaf and cucumber notes it turns watery and cool; over rice and milky notes it suggests a bowl of matcha. Tea CO2 extracts are famously difficult to work with, so Firmenich supplies these ready-diluted and fully mobile in ethanol. We stock the full tea SFE range: Tea Black SFE, Tea White SFE, Jasmine Tea SFE, and Tea Keemun SFE.

missing_other.title: Tea Keemun SFE
missing_other.description: Keemun is the black tea of Qimen county in Anhui, grown between the Yellow Mountains and the Yangtze, and this extract captures what sets it apart: a dark, plummy fruitiness, an unsweetened cocoa undertone and a soft tobacco smokiness, with a delicate floral facet and toasted grain beneath. It reads darker and fruitier than a straightforward black tea note, so use it where a plain tea accord feels thin. It deepens tobacco and dried-fruit themes, lends cocoa-tinged warmth to gourmands without sweetening them, and gives woody autumnal compositions a brewed, leafy heart. It suits noir directions. Pair it with tobacco absolute, davana and a dry amber for a fruity-tobacco accord, or with cocoa absolute and a whisper of birch tar for a smoky, bittersweet gourmand. Bergamot lifts it toward a Chinese-leaf Earl Grey, and osmanthus draws out its fruit. This one is, in my opinion, the most beautiful and interesting of the tea extracts. Tea CO2 extracts are famously difficult to work with, so Firmenich supplies these ready-diluted and fully mobile in ethanol. We stock the full tea SFE range: Tea Black SFE, Tea White SFE, Tea Green SFE, and Tea Jasmine SFE.

missing_other.title: Tea White SFE
missing_other.description: White tea is the least handled of all teas, just young leaves and buds withered and dried, and the extract is correspondingly gentle: delicately aromatic, green and fruity, with fresh floral facets and sweet hay. Underneath sits a soft, mossy, tobacco-like dryness, with hints of osmanthus and peach leaf. Its lightness is the point. Use it to give white florals a fresh, leafy tea nuance, to add volume and realism to a tea accord without darkening it, or to lend a green, faintly fruity softness to fresh florals and light gourmands. Jasmine, freesia and gardenia all take to it. Osmanthus absolute draws out its fruit; violet leaf and a trace of melon note make it cooler and greener. In a tea-rose theme, set it against a dewy petal material such as Rosaphen for a soft, powdery effect, or build a Chinese white-tea accord with hay absolute and clary sage. Tea CO2 extracts are famously difficult to work with, so Firmenich supplies these ready-diluted and fully mobile in ethanol. We stock the full tea SFE range: Tea Black SFE, Jasmine White SFE, Tea Green SFE, and Tea Keemun SFE.

missing_other.title: Thioxane Base 38375 D
missing_other.description: Thioxane Base opens with a vivid blast of fresh green citrus — grapefruit peel, lemon zest — that quickly reveals a juicy tropical dimension underneath: ripe mango, passion fruit, a hint of something bitter and almost savoury. The overall impression is strikingly natural, far more realistic than most synthetic citrus or tropical reconstructions. It smells like actual fruit rather than a fragrance interpretation of fruit. That realism comes from the same family of naturally occurring sulphur compounds found in yellow passion fruit and grapefruit peel. Firmenich has balanced these potent materials with supporting green and citrus ingredients to make the base usable without careful micro-dosing. Even so, it is powerful and best used from a dilution — it projects with unusual reach. Use Thioxane Base to add a natural, peely freshness to citrus accords, or to introduce tropical fruit facets into floral compositions. It gives a lovely petal-like freshness to floral-citrus blends and adds convincing lemon-peel character to clean accords. Pair it with Hedione for a bright, diffusive citrus-floral effect, or with green materials for a naturalistic leafy opening.

missing_other.title: Thyme Oil ct Borneol
missing_other.description: Thyme ct borneol opens warm and herbaceous, then reveals a dry, woody-camphoraceous depth that neither red thyme nor thyme ct linalool can give you. The camphor sits behind the herbs rather than dominating — it reads as pine forest and balsamic warmth, not medicine cabinet. Earthy and grounding, with quiet persistence. Use it in fougères and colognes where you want authentic herbal backbone with woody structure. It bridges top-note herbs and base-note woods in a way that feels natural and seamless. It also enriches incense and oriental accords, where its dry camphoraceous quality amplifies frankincense and labdanum. Three thymes, three characters This oil comes from Thymus satureioides, a Moroccan species entirely different from the Spanish thymes. Red Thyme Oil (ct thymol) is sharp, phenolic, intensely medicinal — the apothecary thyme. Thyme Oil ct Linalool is soft, sweet, almost lavender-like — the gentlest of the three. Thyme ct Borneol occupies the middle ground: warm and herbaceous like both, but with a dry, woody-camphoraceous depth completely absent from the others.

missing_other.title: Tilleul (Linden Blossom)
missing_other.description: The scent of tilleul blossoms (also known as tilia, linden blossom and lime tree) floating on the air in summertime is one of the most beautiful. Fraterworks® Tilleul captures the very essence of this wonderful tree. With doses possible at up to 49% of your finished product, this can be used as the central core of a modern multiflor fragrance by simply adding accents of other flowers and woods. Forget muguet, try Tilleul for a head-turning difference.

missing_other.title: Timut Pepper Oil
missing_other.description: Made in collaboration with Jean Claude Ellena when he was head of perfumes at Hermes, this wonderfully rare pepper oil is quite a surprise. With hints of styrax (and other balsamic notes on account of the material containing cinnamates), a coriander seed quality and a touch of grapefruit, this is a versatile and useful product and extremely beautiful. Recently discovered by perfumers and gastronomes alike, the French eat the Nepalese spice with Foie Gras where its pomelo and candied lemon nuances complement the unctuous texture of the goose liver. And being a close relative of the Sichuan pepper makes it a suitable alternative to that popular spice also. Blends with Styrax Oil, Styrax Resinoid, Coriander Seed, and Citrus Oils.

missing_other.title: Tobacco Absolute MD
tags: locale:this is MD - do not confuse with tobacco absolute.
missing_other.description: Tobacco absolute (nicotine content You'll find this absolute invaluable for creating authentic tabac accords where colour removal prevents staining in finished products. It excels at adding masculine sophistication to oriental bases and unexpected depth to aldehydic compositions. Use it sparingly at 0.1-1% where its concentrated power adds warmth without overwhelming delicate florals. Combine tobacco absolute with vanilla and tonka for gourmand tobacco sweetness or blend with castoreum and leather for animalic depth. Pair with amber accords where honey facets enhance balsamic warmth. This material bridges woody bases with sweet top notes beautifully, particularly with bergamot and clary sage. Molecular Distillation This molecular distilled variety from Payan Bertrand undergoes vacuum distillation to remove colour whilst preserving aromatic integrity. The process eliminates a lot of the typical red-brown pigmentation that causes staining, creating a clearer (albeit not water-white) product ideal for light-coloured formulations. Where standard tobacco absolute limits usage due to colour concerns, Payan Bertrand's molecular distillation allows broader application whilst maintaining the full aromatic complexity of traditional extraction.

missing_other.title: Tobacco “Signature” Absolute
missing_other.description: Over the years we have sampled many Tobacco absolutes, being ever on the lookout for that singular one which encapsulates every wonderful aspect of the plant in its most distinguished forms: snuff, pipes and cigars. This is it. Upon first sniff of this marvellous absolute one smells antique wood and hay notes. Payan Bertrand's recent harvests have achieved an exceptional level of refinement, surpassing even our former offering. Their latest production attains such quality that one would be forgiven for believing oneself to be smelling a hand of aged tobacco leaves. Following the typical masculine opening is a distinctly honey and dried fruit nuance. Rounding it all out is a sweet vanilla-tonka complex that confirms the versatile role that tobacco extracts play in our art form. We have made the decision to switch from our previous MANE tobacco absolute to this superior Payan Bertrand product for two compelling reasons: the recent harvests demonstrate notably finer aromatic qualities, and crucially, this absolute carries no IFRA restrictions whatsoever. Unfortunately, changes in MANE's processing methods resulted in their product becoming IFRA prohibited, making it unsuitable for our purposes. We call this our "Signature" absolute because it is the first tobacco product we turn to in virtually every instance. It is used in a number of our products and we have yet to sample finer. This product blends exceedingly well with the sticky dried plum note of Firmenich's Prunella, Cocoa Resinoid , Oud Intense , and Vanilla Supreme . For a 1700s Fribourg & Treyer snuff accord of the Bordeaux variety, try it with a trace of fine Bourbon Geranium , Rose Ultimate Extract and the merest suggestion of Egyptian Violet Leaves . Tobacco "Signature" Absolute from Payan Bertrand is nicotine reduced (to a level that it is usually classified as nicotine free); the total nicotine content is 0.09%. It is not IFRA restricted and, as such, will be limited only by the laws of the country in whi

missing_other.title: Tocopherol (Vitamin E)
missing_other.description: Tocopherol is an anti-oxidant which can be useful in materials such as linalool to prevent dangerous oxidation from occurring. While it doesn't entirely replace BHT (a synthetic preservative and antioxidant) it is a viable replacer for it and for natural perfumers this is a must. Tocopherol is Vitamin E and it does have a slight odour (somewhat unpleasant) however it is usually used under 0.5% of your finished product so it is seldom and issue.

missing_other.title: Tolu Absolute Replacer 50%
tags: locale:BASE not the usual resinoid or absolute
missing_other.description: One of the annoyances of Tolu Balsam is the intensely dark brown colour. Payan Bertrand has solved that problem by producing this marvel of blending, a synthetic Tolu Balsam Absolute Replacer which is both pale in colour and utterly sublime in scent (nicer, perhaps, than natural tolu!) Our love of this material is so great that we employ it in a number of products for its odour value alone. And best of all it is extremely cost effective and there are no supply chain risks around obtaining the raw material. Tolu Balsam Resinoid and Absolutes are both permitted at fairly high amounts under IFRA, and this replacer is likewise allowed at 16% (in its diluted state), but even if you routinely use the natural products or don't need to worry about the dark colour of them, we still strongly recommend you purchase this replacer. For the sake of ease of use, we sell this at 50% diluted in triethyl citrate which makes it pourable and allows the beautiful scent of the base to open up its beautiful cinnamic heart.

missing_other.title: Tolu Balsam Absolute 50% TEC
tags: locale:Tolu ABSOLUTE not resinoid. Always double check.
missing_other.description: Tolu Balsam Absolute delivers exceptional fixation while imparting refined sweetness without Peru's medicinal edge or benzoin's cloying tendency. This material excels in hyacinth and tuberose compositions where its complex profile enhances white florals. Use 0.5-3% in alcoholic formulations for optimal impact. Apply this material sparingly—overdosing dampens other materials more aggressively than benzoin. Create powdery effects by combining with hydroxycitronellal and linalool. Build sophisticated oriental bases by blending with labdanum and patchouli. This pre-diluted format ensures immediate workability without heating requirements. Difference Between Tolu Balsam Resinoid and Absolute: Tolu Balsam Resinoid results from benzene or similar non-polar solvent extraction of crude balsam, yielding 60-70% of viscous, dark material containing waxes and heavier compounds. The absolute undergoes further alcohol washing to remove these components, producing a more refined, concentrated aromatic extract. Commercial "absolutes" sometimes bypass the resinoid stage through direct ethanol extraction, technically creating "resin absolutes." True absolutes exhibit cleaner profiles with enhanced solubility in perfume compounds, though both forms require heating for handling. The absolute's superior refinement justifies its use in fine fragrance, while resinoids suit soap perfumery where their retained acids pose no alkalinity concerns. We also stock Tolu Balsam Resinoid at 50% in natural TEC.

missing_other.title: Tolu Balsam Resinoid 50% TEC
tags: locale:Bottle may say Tolu Res or Tolu Balsam Res. NOT ABS or REPL.
missing_other.description: Tolu balsam is a wonderful fixative and adds a valuable richness and complexity to tuberose and hyacinth bases (amongst others). It was far more frequently used in the golden age than today though some wonderful modern fragrances fully exploit the beautiful resin, particularly Chypre Palatin by Bertrand Duchafour for MDCI Parfums. Tolu balsam has a sweet fruity and cinnamic profile, quite similar to peru balsam which comes from the same tree (though a different variety, namely Myroxylon balsamum pereirae) . Crude tolu balsam (exuded from cuts made in the bark of the Myroxylon balsamum var. balsamum tree) is washed in solvent to produce a resinoid free of much of the non-odiferous matter. This practically rock hard resinoid is then blended by us with natural triethyl citrate (an odourless isolate of citrus oil) to produce an easy to use solution — classically this would be referred to as dissolution de tolu . Because we employ natural TEC, this can be used freely in fragrances or products needing to meet the ISO standards for natural products. Tolu balsam products can be very confusing in name, largely because there are multiple products sharing common names. Benzene (or other non-alcoholic solvent) extractions of the crude tolu produce tolu balsam resinoid (or just tolu resinoid) - this product. Further alcohol extraction would then produce tolu absolute. However, some companies produce a so-called "absolute" by direct ethanol extraction of the crude balsam rather than the resinoid which should be called "resin absolute". Here is a clearer description — square brackets indicate optional terms: Crude Balsam → Steam Distillation → Tolu [Balsam] Essential Oil Crude Balsam → Non-Ethanol Natural Solvent Extraction → Tolu [Balsam] Resinoid (this product) Crude Balsam → Hot Ethanol Extraction → Tolu Resin Absolute, or sometimes (wrongly) Tolu [Balsam] Absolute Tolu Balsam Resinoid → Alcohol Extraction → Tolu [Balsam] Absolute French Name: Dissolution de Tolu We also stock

missing_other.title: Tonka Bean CO2 Abs
tags: locale:pot for pure only. 10% needs no heat.
missing_other.description: Tonka Bean CO2 opens with the familiar coumarinic warmth of tonka — but this version leans unmistakably cherry. A roasted almond-marzipan richness sits alongside that cherry note, creating something genuinely edible. The drydown is creamy vanilla-praline with the hay-sweet depth you expect from the bean. Beyond a doubt this is now our favourite Tonka Bean extract. The CO2 process captures lighter aromatic facets that traditional solvent extraction misses — those cherry and almond nuances that make this version special. Use it anywhere you want tonka's warmth with a gourmand edge: amber bases, tobacco accords, oriental hearts. It anchors blends with exceptional tenacity. Pair it with cocoa absolute for a dark chocolate-cherry accord, or blend with vanilla and benzoin for gourmand decadence. It lifts rose and jasmine with confectionery sweetness that smells effortlessly luxurious. Compare it with Fraterworks' Tonka Bean "Luxe" Absolute — each captures a different facet of the same bean. Note that this is a superior CO2 Absolute in which an initial CO2 extraction is followed by an additional purifying alcohol extraction.

missing_other.title: Tonka Bean Tincture 20%
missing_other.description: Coumarin is the usual method of adding tonka bean nuances to a perfume today, but nothing beats the full complexity of the natural bean. Cold tincturing is the best way to extract this beautiful scent. By combining coumarin, tonka bean absolute and tonka bean tincture you can create fragrances that are out of this world. Our tincturing process uses the finest odourless food grade alcohol only. Absolutely no synthetic plasticisers, denaturants or diluents are used, resulting in a totally natural product by ISO 9235 standards. This is the gold standard of tonka bean tinctures and every care has been taken to ensure consistent excellence in every drop. NOTE: this tincture is not made in a food safe environment. This product is for perfume and cosmetic use only. This is not a food product. Origin: Peru Variety: Dipteryx Odorata Part: Beans Method: Cold ethanol tincture

missing_other.title: Tonka Bean “Luxe” Absolute
tags: locale:pot for pure only. 10% needs no heat.
missing_other.description: Up until recently, we offered a single tonka bean absolute—the wonderfully gourmand creation from V MANE Fils, known as our Tonka Bean “Signature” Absolute . However, as we embarked on our 2025 evaluations to ensure we continue providing only the finest materials, we made an extraordinary find: this Tonka Bean Absolute from LMR. This deluxe, meticulously crafted extract was too exceptional to overlook, compelling us to add it to our collection. While the MANE Signature absolute captivates with its sticky-sweet, gourmand charm, the LMR Luxe absolute offers a refined, drier profile, perfectly balancing elegant agrestic notes with gourmand delight. Its distinct sophistication justifies offering both side by side and the title Tonka Bean “Luxe” Absolute. We offer both our tonka absolutes at 10% dilution in pure and natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless isolate from citrus) or pure. In pure form tonka bean is a solid paste. In describing tonka absolute, Arctander says: ‘Tonka absolute is a semi solid or crystalline mass of pale amber or pale brownish-yellow color Its odor is very rich, sweet and warm, distinctly coumarinic / herbaceous, with a prune-like, or caramelic-sweet undertone. The odor description “tobacco-like” is somewhat confusing since Tonka tincture has been used quite extensively in the flavoring of cured tobacco leaves. The absolute consists of 20-45% coumarin, but the effect of a true Tonka absolute goes far beyond that of the coumarin contained in the absolute. Tonka is a fixative and non-floral sweetener which introduces warm notes in chypres, fougères, new mown hay bases, lavender bouquets, Oriental bases, etc. It blends well with: Lavender , lavandin , clary sage , bergamot , oakmoss .’ Origin: Brazil Part: Beans Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Tonka Bean “Signature" Absolute
tags: locale:pot for pure only. 10% needs no heat.
missing_other.description: If you have been searching for the holy grail of tonka, you have found it. Intensely edible, warm, spicy and sweet, this absolute is the profound expression of the full aroma of the beans. In this incredibly complex scent is the gourmand odour of delicious French patisserie, the vanilla sweetness of puddings, and a warm fond of subtle spices centred around a delicate cinnamon note. We offer this incredible product 10% dilution in pure and natural Triethyl Citrate (an odourless isolate from citrus) or pure. In pure form tonka bean is a solid paste. In describing tonka absolute, Arctander says: ‘Tonka absolute is a semi solid or crystalline mass of pale amber or pale brownish-yellow color Its odor is very rich, sweet and warm, distinctly coumarinic / herbaceous, with a prune-like, or caramelic-sweet undertone. The odor description “tobacco-like” is somewhat confusing since Tonka tincture has been used quite extensively in the flavoring of cured tobacco leaves. The absolute consists of 20-45% coumarin, but the effect of a true Tonka absolute goes far beyond that of the coumarin contained in the absolute. Tonka is a fixative and non-floral sweetener which introduces warm notes in chypres, fougères, new mown hay bases, lavender bouquets, Oriental bases, etc. It blends well with: Lavender , lavandin , clary sage , bergamot , oakmoss .’ Note: due to scarcity of supply, the price of tonka bean absolute has increased significantly in 2026.

missing_other.title: Tonka Torréfiée, Esprit d'Odeur
missing_other.description: Tonka Torréfiée Esprit d'Odeur is a luxurious combination of roasted tonka beans with fifteen year aged small batch rum, distilled with perfumer's alcohol into a light and ethereal perfumery spirit. With subtle nuances of cherry, bitter almonds and caramel, this is a truly unique and precious material and one almost never seen on the stock books of modern perfumery raw materials suppliers. First we roast fresh tonka beans which intensifies the ripe cherry and marzipan notes. These are then crushed and tinctured for a period of months in dark rum, triple aged for 15 years in oak casks. The final stage is to then distil the rich tincture resulting in a delicately scented colourless nearly pure perfumer's alcohol. This can be used as a tincture or the foundation of additional tinctures. Tonka Torréfiée presents with a bouquet of sandalwood, freshly baked pastries, marzipan, black cherries, and the merest suggestion of musk. To smell this infusion is to smell happiness. IMPORTANT : this product must not be consumed . It is for perfume manufacture only. It is not safe for human consumption. This should be treated as any other denatured alcohol product.

missing_other.title: Tonkin Intense
missing_other.description: For those seeking an animalic note equalling the strength and ferocity of pure wild animal extracts, our Tonkin Intense and Ambergris Intense fit the bill. Forget Tonquitone , Shangralide and Muscarome … Tonkin Intense is the most profoundly luxurious deer musk you will ever experience. Tonkin Intense is built using the most radiant and powerful synthetic musks with accents matching the full spectrum of molecules in natural deer musk. This is pure animal. We recommend diluting to 1% or less for modern fragrances and up to 10% for floral rich or classical styled perfumes.

missing_other.title: Treemoss “Non-IFRA” Absolute
missing_other.description: What made fragrances like First (1976) by Van Cleef and Arpels, Coco (1984) by Chanel, Polo Green (1978) by Ralph Lauren the masterpieces they were? Perhaps not exclusively but most certainly significantly: pure treemoss absolute. Often looked down upon as the dull younger brother of Oakmoss, this Robertet extraction absolutely proves the contrary; this is every bit as wonderful as the nicest green Oakmoss (which we also stock). This is so thick and deeply green that we offer it in a more mobile 50% solution with natural TEC so it remains viable for natural perfumers also. But, because of the rarity of supply of this product we are offering it pure despite the challenges that go along with melting such a tar-like material. This is NOT IFRA compliant and, as such, should not be used in any perfumes or cosmetics requiring adherence to those standards. Origin: France Part: Moss Method of production: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Tubereuse 184108
missing_other.description: Tubereuse demonstrates how popular bases are in both classical and modern perfumery and illustrates their ongoing use as key components of masterful fragrances. Tubereuse is used in Anais-Anais, Fidji, Cartier's Must, Hermes Amazone, and a multitude more. It is one of the most popular tuberose bases. Tubereuse is effective from 0.1% and is usually used to a maximum amount of around 2%. We highly recommend using it to add captive warmth to our Tuberose Supreme base which is loaded with natural tuberose absolute from LMR.

missing_other.title: Tuberose Supreme
missing_other.description: An incredibly rich and oppulent tuberose base loaded with natural tuberose absolute and other complementary naturals. Orinally a Chuit Naef and Cie base replicating the popular Roure Tuberose (as found in Poison , Tendre Poison , O scar de la Renta , Fracas and many more). Gently and sympathetically updated with modern molecules which provide radiance to this perfectly blended luxury floral. Traces add richesse and depth, while larger amounts contribute a powerful and distinct tuberose note.

missing_other.title: Tuberose TruAbs
missing_other.description: Tuberose TruAbs captures every facet of genuine tuberose absolute with astonishing accuracy. You get the full narcotic white floral intensity — creamy, honeyed, almost dangerously sweet — with the signature green, slightly medicinal opening and the buttery, animalic depth that makes tuberose unforgettable. This 100% natural base is crafted in Grasse exclusively for Fraterworks. Use it anywhere you would use genuine tuberose absolute — narcotic white florals, heavy orientals, gardenia and frangipani accords. Incorporate at 0.1–5% for a luxurious floral heart that reads as completely authentic. Blend with jasmine and ylang-ylang for a classic white floral bouquet, or pair with sandalwood and benzoin to bring out the warm balsamic drydown. TruAbs bases offer a consistent, readily available alternative to one of perfumery's rarest and most expensive absolutes.

missing_other.title: Tuberose “Signature” Absolute
missing_other.description: Tuberose — a flower so intensely erogenous that in Victorian times an English lady would avoid the scent for fear of an sudden lapse of self-control. Meanwhile, in France, the extrait from pomade was liberally doused upon the décolletages of upper crust women who, with gay abandon, revelled in its scent. No flower in the history of fragrance has so titillated, so intoxicated and so enthralled perfume wearers. Its high cost and powerful scent make it a very rare treasure today compared to what it once was but fortunately even trace amounts can have a profound effect on a scent. The merest soupçon can naturalise and enrich a simple classic floral accord of Jasmine and Rose or add a sultry je ne sais quoi appreciated by all. Our signature Tuberose Absolute from LMR was selected from the offerings of all the top suppliers in Grasse. It stood out for its clarity of scent and the diaphanous quality of its dry down — rather unique for such a rich floral material. We are certain you will find this as sublime as we do.

missing_other.title: Ultramber® Xtreme
missing_other.description: Super ambers are wildly popular today and they are now found in almost every new fragrance. For a novice perfumer they can be the hardest materials to dose right, and often for experienced perfumers there can be a tendency to simply add a touch of their favourite one or two to each blend keeping within safe margins. That is where Ultramber® Xtreme comes to the fore. This product is a sophisticated blend of the very best of super ambers, adding harmony, diffusion and radiance to any fragrance while being easier to dose. If super ambers are the stars in the glistering firmament, Ultramber® Xtreme is a supernova. This is where super ambers begin and end. You don't need anything else. Just add this from trace to overdose. Ultramber® Xtreme contains the perfect dose of Ambrocenide, Amberketal, Dextro Norlimbanol (35%), and many other enhancing and boosting materials. Love Ultramber®.

missing_other.title: Vanellia™
missing_other.description: A wonderful Tahitian vanilla fantasy base at a fraction of the cost of natural absolute, Vanellia™ contains luxurious vanilla extracts in combination with revolutionary modern synthetics. Achieve all the radiance and gourmand elegance available to perfumes of yesteryear. Usable at up to 5.2% of the finished product for full IFRA 50 compliance (and 35% for IFRA 51) this is an essential toolkit material for all perfumers.

missing_other.title: Vanilla Barka Attar Type Formula
missing_other.description: By far this 2021 Attar from Amouage is the most popular of the range. Crafted by Dominique Ropion it is a simple 24 line formula with virtually all ingredients available here at Fraterworks. Because the naturals in this attar are scarce, the quality of the aroma chemicals must be absolutely supreme. Fortunately Fraterworks sells only the best aroma chemicals so you get a wonderful result from this formula. The quality of Amouage scents has been a little in decline since Christopher Chong left the company but the Attars remain a relatively quality little side-line for the brand. Notes: Vanilla, Olibanum, Tonka Bean Difficulty Level: Easy Total Lines: 24 Naturals: 6

missing_other.title: Vanilla Bean CO2
tags: locale:pot for pure only. 10% needs no heat.
missing_other.description: Vanilla (planifolia) CO2 is the most recent addition to the natural extracts derived from this most important perfumery material. Vanilla is considered the salt of perfumery and it is found in almost every perfume to some extent. This CO2 is an LMR speciality and the quality and luxury is immediately obvious. While the natural absolute is dark brown, this CO2 is pale straw in colour. It is organic at source, and uses no petrochemicals. All the CO2 in the process is recycled by LMR. Starting with the creamy balsamic facets we all love in high quality natural vanilla, this extract contains the lovely phenolic and powdery drydown of the absolute at a much lower price point.

missing_other.title: Vanilla Bourbon Absolute
missing_other.description: Vanilla Absolute is pure indulgence, and Vanilla Bourbon Absolute from V MANE Fils is the height of said indulgence. This deep brown absolute is pourable with a little gentle heat and soluble at 10% in natural Triethyl Citrate (albeit with a touch of cloudiness which is to be expected with vanilla). At a whopping 30% vanillin, this Vanilla Absolute has to be smelled to be truly believed and appreciated. It is so rich it verges on being chocolatey. We can say with absolutely no hesitation, that you will never want to use vanilla absolute from another supplier once you experience the beauty of this product. A very interesting and unique powdery combination can be had blending Vanilla Absolute with Olibanum Coeur . Use a trace to naturalise our beautiful signature Vanillin ex Guaiacol, or simply indulge in an overdose. We sell this at 10% in completely natural odourless Triethyl Citrate (an isolate from citrus) or pure. Our demonstration "smells-like" formula below for Chanel's Gabrielle (2017) demonstrates how beautifully well Vanilla Absolute blends into floral fragrances to add subtle and rich sweetness without the sometimes cloying solidity that can come from synthetic sweeteners. Origin: Madagascar Part: Pods

missing_other.title: Vanilla Intense, Esprit d'Odeur
missing_other.description: Vanilla Intense Esprit d'Odeur 20% is a vanilla lover's dream and rarely available in the perfume raw materials market these days. We start by tincturing finest Madagascan vanilla pods in French Cognac in perfumer's ethanol and after a long maceration period we perform a co-distillation over fresh vanilla pods. The result is a double-vanilla "spirit of odour" that is simply a revelation. This product is colourless and ethereal in scent. It is traditionally used in the same manner as a tincture of vanilla. IMPORTANT : this product must not be consumed . It is for perfume manufacture only and is not safe for human consumption. This should be treated as any other denatured alcohol product.

missing_other.title: Vanilla Pod Tincture 20%
missing_other.description: This is the finest vanilla tincture on the market today. Every care and the characteristic Fraterworks attention to detail has been engaged at every step of the way. Our intensely rich, dark and luxurious tincture of vanilla is a unique way to add the full complexity of vanilla to your scent. We use specially harvested whole vanilla pods which are given extra drying time in the Madagascan sun to intensify their aroma for an especially dark and surprisingly powerful vanilla tincture. We use only the purest food grade alcohol made with remote New Zealand glacial water so nothing stands in the way of a perfect cold process vanilla extraction. Because our tincture is made at such a high concentration, the alcohol can absorb quite a lot of water naturally from the pods. As Steffen Arctander says: “Certain perfume houses still use the old fashioned “infusion” method of extraction. […] The resulting infusion may be filtered immediately or after cooling. […] It will become cloudy and show additional precipitate on standing.” All fragrances created with naturals or tinctures must be chilled overnight after maceration (typically a period of one month) and fine filtered to remove any cloudiness that may remain. Use the tincture directly in your perfume formulas or pre-blend it with perfumer's alcohol for a natural vanilla touch impossible to obtain any other way. NOTE: this tincture is not made in a food safe environment. This product is for perfume and cosmetic use only. This is not a food product. Origin: Madagascar Variety: Vanilla planifolia Part: Sun-dried Pods Method: Cold ethanol tincture

missing_other.title: Vanilla Supreme
missing_other.description: Madagascan vanilla absolute is one of the most luxurious materials available to perfumers but its price is far out of budget for most uses. Vanilla Supreme by Fraterworks is the cost-effective solution: a one-for-one replacer. Despite its amazing price, Vanilla Supreme is enriched with luscious — and dare we say superior — naturals (including a judicious amount of finest Vanilla Bourbon absolute). Vanilla Supreme has a wonderfully creamy scent and unctuous texture and is safe for use at a whopping 10% of your finished product. Use it in traces to impart a naturalistic vanilla nuance to your scent or in overdose for pure decadence (as in our "Ravishing" demonstration formula below which replicates Musc Ravageur from Frederic Malle). Try a marvellous accord by combining Black Opoponax To Vanilla Supreme in a 1:5 ratio. Vanilla Supreme also synergises with Coconut Delight , and all the lactones. We also offer Vanellia ™, our popular Tahitian vanilla fantasy base if you are looking for something different.

missing_other.title: Verbena Absolute
missing_other.description: Verbena essential oil is banned by the EU and IFRA but fortunately that is not true of the absolute. Verbena Absolute opens with an effervescent lemon-sherbet luminosity that feels candied yet distinctly green. Crush a fresh leaf between your fingers and you'll recognise that unmistakable snap—bright aldehydic citrus married to an herbaceous coolness. The heart reveals a soft, neroli-adjacent floralcy and dried chamomile tea character that sets this absolute apart from crude citral reconstructions. This material transforms standard citrus openings into something sophisticated and alive. Use it to naturalise synthetic lemon accords built on Litsea cubeba or geranyl nitrile (Citralva)—even trace amounts will contribute the waxy, tea-like nuances that reconstructions lack. Verbena bridges the Hesperidic top and aromatic heart beautifully, making it essential for authentic Eau de Cologne compositions and green-floral hearts. Build verbena accords with petitgrain to extend its leafy woody facets, or pair with neroli for a seamless orange blossom continuum. The hay-like dry-down bonds naturally with oakmoss in chypre structures. Fix this volatile material with frankincense or elemi rather than heavy musks—these resins share its lemony-peppery character and extend longevity without suffocating its brightness.

missing_other.title: Verdantol™
missing_other.description: Fraterworks® Verdantol™ is a penetrating and diffusive green herbal base built around powerful aromatic molcules and rounded out with luxurious extracts of natural foliage, galbanum and grapefruit. Verdantol™ provides a sophisticated note perfect for modern fine fragrances, imparting complex layered tones of fresh herbs, cut grass and greenery. Its superior power makes it an ideal choice for novel and long-lasting effects. Recommended use at a 10% dilution is from traces to a few percent of your finished formula. However novel effects may be achieved at higher amounts. Blends beautifully with fruity, citrus, agrestic and floral compositions.

missing_other.title: Veticoeur™
missing_other.description: A classical cedar base with delicate nuances of violet and leather, Veticoeur™ is a wonderful canvas type material that can be used up to a whopping 5% of your finished product. Veticoeur™ was used in No 19 by Chanel and numerous other great fragrances of the 20th century (see our demonstration formulas below). Veticoeur™ (classic Vetyrisia) is a perfect starting point for a modern woody fragrance that can be twisted in many different directions, from dry and green with Galbanum oil , to gourmand with Ethyl Maltol . It suits feminine and masculine scents and blends extraordinarily well with Miraclewood™ , Vetiveryl Acetate , Aetoxylon Oil , Orrisodore and Cedarome .

missing_other.title: Vetiver Bourbon Absolute
missing_other.description: Vetiver Bourbon Absolute is a rather rare gem in the vetiver world, particularly an elegant extraction from the “Bourbon” starting material. It has a bright (but rounded) top note similar to a fine lavender absolute but its heart and dry down are pure unadulterated vetiver; loamy, dank and rich. Very small amounts are all you need but interesting effects could certainly be had in overdose. We offer this pure and diluted to 50% in TEC for ease of use. Origin: Madagascar Part: Roots Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Vetiver Bourbon “Signature” Oil
missing_other.description: A good perfumer needs one great vetiver oil. This is it; this is the vetiver of renown. From the very first sniff you will recognise this oil from such masterpieces as Guerlain's Vetiver (2000) and Jean Claude Ellena's Terre D'Hermes (2007) for Hermes. We refer to this oil as “Bourbon” oil as it is the closest product to the near-mythical vetiver of the golden age, now no longer produced in La Reunion (formerly Île Bourbon) but sourced on the neighbouring island of Madagascar. This is not a blend or derivative product — it is 100% pure and natural vetiver goodness from Biolandes. Wonderful effects can be achieved with this oil by blending it with our incredible Vetiverol ex Vetiver Haiti . Origin: Madagascar and Mauritius Part: Roots Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Vetiver Haiti SFE
missing_other.description: This SFE extract captures Haitian vetiver at its most natural. The low-temperature CO2 process preserves delicate green top notes that steam distillation destroys, delivering a woody-earthy character that is cleaner, rounder, and truer to the freshly unearthed root. No burnt artefacts, no harshness. Where standard Haitian vetiver oil can have unwanted asparagus-like or potato-peel top notes from thermal degradation, the SFE avoids these entirely. You get the full woody-smoky-earthy vetiver signature — the refined smokiness, the dry mineral bite, the sweet precious-wood drydown — but in a smoother, more user-friendly form. Use this in fougère and chypre accords where you want vetiver depth without roughness. It blends seamlessly with bergamot, oakmoss, and sandalwood. Layer it with your steam-distilled Haitian vetiver for a complex, multi-dimensional vetiver accord.

missing_other.title: Vetiver Oil, Haiti
missing_other.description: Historically Haitian origin vetiver played second fiddle to the Bourbon type (now from Madagascar) but in more recent times tastes have shifted and the Haiti type is now preferred. LMR produced the finest qualities and so it is their stock we have. The price on this material is as good as we can get it but due to unrest in Haiti (as of writing in 2024) supplies are becoming scarce and costs will increase so get it while you can! We will continue to supply it as long as we can get it and LMR will be resuming production once peace returns to Haiti. This Vetiver oil is COSMOS certified and holds the LMR “For Life” Certification which “recognizes an organization’s compliance with specific sustainability criteria, including transparency, environmental responsibility, fair working conditions and positive relations with producers and local communities.” Note: Fraterworks is not a registered COSMOS company so while this product is CSM certified when it reaches us, we cannot use that terminology when we resell. Origin: Haiti Part: Roots Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Vetiver Oil, Java
missing_other.description: Due to the scarcity of Vetiver oil from Haiti, LMR has just launched a high quality Vetiver Oil from Java. This is an astonishingly unique type of vetiver, being considerably more fluid, and decidedly more flinty and smoky. Owing to the great care exercised by LMR in its manufacture, this vetiver oil is vastly better than most Java types, revealing sweet, vanilla, and butterscotch undertones while cheaper oils are often little more than smoke and peanuts. It has a distinctive odour of spent matches and would work incredibly well alongside such oils as Cypriol and Guiacwood Oil . Use it as you would any vetiver oil as a long lasting and woody, earthy and vaguely gourmand base note. This is definitely different enough to the Vetiver sourced in other parts of the world to justify every perfumer having some.

missing_other.title: Vetiver Oil, South India
missing_other.description: When people talk of vetiver they usually think of Madagascar (the source of the near mythical Bourbon type ), Indonesia (Java usually), and Haiti. But perhaps the best kept secret for speciality vetiver oils is South India (pictured). On the sandy coast of South India, Vetiver has long been grown not just for its treasured scent but also for religious and medicinal uses. One of the leading suppliers from the region is TMV Aromas, established in 1958 and holding many prestigious awards for the quality of their natural Indian origin extracts. TMV is our supplier of choice for this material. Vetiver Oil, South India smells as all vetiver oils should, but with the added richness of baked earth and saltiness from the myriad sandy beaches facing distant Ceylon. You may also like our Vetiveryl Acetate (V. MANE Fils), Vetiver Oil Bourbon (Biolandes) and, coming soon, Vetiver Haiti Oil CMS (LMR). Origin: South India Part: Roots Method: Steam distillation

missing_other.title: Violet Leaf Absolute, France
tags: locale:trace of heat for 30 seconds for pure only.
missing_other.description: Violet leaf absolute is one of the most useful in perfumery, lending naturalness and freshness to virtually all types of fragrances. As a modifier to the ionone family they are unsurpassed by synthetics. From traces (in fragrances such as L'Origan by Coty) to overdoses of nearly 1% pure in 1000 by Jean Patou (formula below), violet leaves contribute a magical quality that simply can't be replicated. When comparing French violet leaves with the more common Egyptian type (which we also stock ), the main thing you will immediately notice is that the French material is cleaner, smoother and greener (in the direction of grass alcohol). The Egyptian leaves are a little more intense and have a distinct leather nuance. Intensely green, oily, earthy and floral, violet leaf absolute is best appreciated in dilution where its myriad complex layers reveal themselves fully. We offer it in 10% and 1% solutions in natural triethyl citrate also. Certified: IG Absolue Pays de Grasse .

missing_other.title: Violet Leaf ”Signature“ Absolute
tags: locale:trace of heat for 30 seconds for pure only
missing_other.description: Violet leaf absolute is one of the most useful in perfumery, lending naturalness and freshness to virtually all types of fragrances. As a modifier to the ionone family they are unsurpassed by synthetics. From traces (in fragrances such as L'Origan by Coty) to overdoses of nearly 1% pure in 1000 by Jean Patou, violet leaves contribute a magical quality that simply can't be replicated. Our violet leaf “signature” absolute comes from Floral Concept, a renowned specialist supplier in Grasse. It is a signature product because it is the finest extraction of Egyptian violet leaves we have come across, with the perfect balance of floralcy and earthiness. Intensely green, oily, earthy and floral, violet leaf “signature” absolute is best appreciated in dilution where its myriad complex layers reveal themselves fully. Violet Leaf 10% Superessence (Natural) In dilution, violet leaf absolute contains a lot of non-soluble low (or no) odour matter. Our violet leaf 10% Superessence is a deep green crystal clear 10% dilution. To achieve this, we dilute the pure violet leaf absolute in a blend of natural Benzyl Benzoate (approximately 20%) and natural Triethyl Citrate (approximately 70%). We then perform a special filtration which removes any remaining insoluble product. This results in a purer and more concentrated product that can be used one for one in place of regular 10% dilution of violet leaf. This is a 100% natural product. Origin: Egypt Part: Leaves Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Violette Bleue
missing_other.description: A wonderfully complex modern base replicating the whole scent of parma violets. Using classical building blocks combined with modern discoveries from headspace analyses of actual violets, we are able to produce an inimitable product. Overdose it for a true violet note, or use small amounts to add a natural and luxurious green note to your fragrances. Safe at up to 30% under the new IFRA 51 guidelines. This base is loaded with many rich floral oils and absolutes.

missing_other.title: Whisky CO2
missing_other.description: This speciality CO2 extraction from V. MANE Fils is a marvel. The company has positioned itself as one of the finest producers of modern SFE extracts and this whisky essence is no exception. It is very costly but very powerful so there is considerable value for money. We recommend using it as an ethereal top note natural. It opens with a strong scent of fermented beer which gives way to the classic whisky notes that separate the two alcohols in their final form (whisky and beer are made from similar starting materials). Whisky P. Jungle Essence blends very well (as you might expect) with Whiskey Lactone to which it contributes a naturalising and radiant power. Try it with a touch of LMR's incredible smoky and woody Oakwood CO2 Extra , an extract of pyrogenated aged fine wine barrels. Or overdose it in a luxe gourmand with our hugely popular Coconut Delight and Raspberry Ripple bases. This material is extremely strong so we also offer it diluted to 10% in natural Triethyl Citrate. We also offer Rum Pure Jungle Essence . Origin: Scotland Method: CO2 Extraction

missing_other.title: White Amber
missing_other.description: One of the areas of expertise at Fraterworks is animalics — natural and synthetic; we even have a whole category dedicated to them. White Amber joins that collection as a magnificent and regal ambergris base rich with natural animal musk. This is not for the faint of heart and certainly not for the vegan perfumers out there. If you need a vegan option, our Ambergris Intense and Absolute Ambergris are the products for you. White Amber is loaded with incredibly rare naturals that are almost never seen in modern perfumery due to their high cost. With White Amber you can incorporate genuine Boronia absolute into your products, noble labdanum fractions, and more. From traces to overdose, White Amber is a powerful natural fixative and naturaliser that brings together the very best elements of nature and aroma science.

missing_other.title: White Paris Mushroom Extract
missing_other.description: White Paris Mushroom Extract offers something rare in perfumery—the genuine scent of mushrooms as they release their aroma in the pan. This extract from Agaricus bisporus presents soft, rounded earthiness without the aggressive savoury punch that plagues many fungal materials . Its delicate nature makes it approachable where other mushroom products feel too culinary or confrontational. You'll find this material invaluable for building forest floor compositions where authenticity matters more than amplification. Layer it with oakmoss, patchouli and vetiver to construct complex woodland bases that feel genuinely wild rather than synthetic. Its gentle character allows higher dosing than typical mushroom absolutes—the 10% MCT dilution gives you control whilst maintaining olfactory precision. Combine it with damp earth accords, mossy notes and cool green materials to evoke morning walks through deciduous forests. Use this extract when reconstructing truffle effects alongside leather and tobacco, or pair it with wet stone accords and metallic florals for modern compositions that reference natural decay without repulsion. Its softness works beautifully beneath violet leaf and iris where it adds humus-like depth. Consider it for chypre structures where you need earthy authenticity without the regulatory concerns of traditional oakmoss.

missing_other.title: White Rose Absolute, Moldova
missing_other.description: This is one of the rarest rose absolutes available. It is produced in Moldova from the white Rose Alba type. This is a rose of extraordinary beauty; while Bulgarian ottos pounce at you with brightness and vigour, Rose Alba imparts a warm ribbon of rich cooked plums with a clove bud spiciness. A drop on the hand is so addictive that it is impossible to stop sniffing. Because of the high price of rose products, we also offer this diluted to 10% in odourless Triethyl Citrate which is a completely natural isolate from citrus, making it suitable for natural perfumers. Origin: Moldova Part: Flowers only Process: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Wild Cherry
missing_other.description: Wild Cherry represents the natural fruity sweetness of cherries in their fresh state. This is not an intensely almond glace cherry but rather a natural and extremely complex scent of freshly picked fruit. Fraterworks Wild Cherry can be used in small amounts to add a sparkling fruit top note, or in larger doses for a decisively cherry note. Modify with benzaldehyde and ethyl maltol to create a classic glacé cherry.

missing_other.title: Wild Civet Tincture 2% (13 Yrs Aged)
missing_other.description: This is a one-off chance to purchase the rarest and most wonderful of all civet products: 13 year aged 2% tincture of wild Abyssinian civet. Most civet today is farmed as it is now under CITES protection, but this Fraterworks tincture was created prior to that. As a consequence this is one of the finest forms of Civet tincture you will ever experience. Compounded with the fact that it was made with food-grade alcohol batch made in New Zealand and you have a treasure of perfumery past. Our wild civet tincture has the typical characteristics of civet but due to age it is mellow and rich. Additionally, because this is a wild harvest, it is imbued with the incredibly profound scent of the wild glory of Africa herself. NOTE: there are some ambiguities around the US customs position on the import of civet to the US. We are happy to take the advice of our clients so if you add this to your cart we presume you are aware and are giving us the green light. We ship civet and other high-odour products in sealed unmarked silver foil bags to prevent cross-contamination in the event of leaks or parcel damage. French Name: Infusion de civette

missing_other.title: Wild Marjoram Oil
missing_other.description: First sniff is pure eucalyptus — sharp, clearing, bracing. Underneath sits a quiet sweet-spicy warmth and herbaceous softness that eucalyptus itself never delivers. This is Thymus mastichina , a Spanish thyme carrying the name "marjoram" for centuries despite sharing nothing with it. Use it sparingly where you need bracing herbal freshness without eucalyptus oil's one-dimensional quality. A few drops lift a fougère or cologne, adding sun-baked Mediterranean garrigue character. Pair with lavender, rosemary, and cypress for scrubland accords — but measure in drops, not millilitres. Fraterworks also stocks Sweet Marjoram Oil ( Origanum majorana ), which is a completely different plant — warm, nutmeg-scented, and gently spicy where this oil is clearing and camphoraceous. Despite the shared name, they are never interchangeable. Treat them as entirely unrelated materials.

missing_other.title: Wild Strawberry
missing_other.description: While most strawberry bases are achingly gourmand, Wild Strawberry represents sun-ripened berries, complete with seeds and greenery. It is still ideal for gourmand fragrances but it won't introduce overwhelming amounts of ethyl maltol or other highly-sticky aromatics. Use it as a decisive strawberry note in a high dose, or as a novel alternative to the more common peach notes found in perfumes through the use of gamma undecalactone. Use it with Raspberry Ripple, Passionfruit Base 109223, Pineapple Supreme, and IFF's Tropicalia for a full bodied tropical fruit salad accord. A strange, yet delightful, synergy occurs when pairing Wild Strawberry with Black Musk.

missing_other.title: Wool Absolute
missing_other.description: An incredibly low-cost animalic that comes from a highly sustainable industry, Wool Absolute is upcycled by Biolandes in France from wool shorn from 100% pasture reared New Zealand sheep. In an age where classic animalics such as civet and deer musk are becoming difficult to obtain, novel products are needed to get the same blending and luxuriating fixative effects. Wool Absolute is a perfect addition to the perfumer's palette as it is the byproduct of an enormous existing industry and is extracted from the animal's wool after shearing. No sheep or lambs are harmed in the process however this would still be considered non-vegan as it is produced by an animal. The scent of this musk is pure rich lanolin with nuances of booze and fruit. For those who have worked on farms or seek a farmyard scent without fecal notes, this is ideal. In terms of animalics it is softer and more genteel than most (in fact it is rather nice to apply a little neat to the skin for its soothing and natural moisturising properties). Excellent for Oud fragrances. Wool Absolute has excellent 10% solubility in ETH, DPG, IPM, DEP, BB and TEC. Starting in 2024, all Fraterworks orders ship using green eco-fuel. Origin: France (from New Zealand grass fed sheep) Part: Wool

missing_other.title: Ylang Heart
missing_other.description: Ylang Heart captures the creamy, exotic centre of the ylang flower: radiant and floral, warmed by soft spice and a whisper of fruit. A bright, almost wintergreen freshness lifts the top. It smells lush and rounded, without the sharp or fatty edges of the whole oil. This is the ylang to use when you want richness without harshness. It slots into the heart of white florals, deepening jasmine, tuberose and gardenia, and lends a creamy, solar glow to rose. Its rounded spice also warms orientals and softens chypres, blending seamlessly with sandalwood and soft musks.

missing_other.title: Ylang Impériale
missing_other.description: Ylang Impériale is a rich and powerful replacer for ylang ylang extra oil. This base can replace the finest ylang ylang at a 1:1 ratio and can be used at a huge 7.3% of the finished product for IFRA compliance — many times the amount permissable with natural ylang ylang products. This scientific reconstruction is enriched with natural cananga odorata extracts. It can be used in small amounts for floralcy or in overdose for a Chanel No 5 or Patou Sublime type fragrance.

missing_other.title: Ylang-Ylang Absolute
missing_other.description: Ylang-ylang absolute is luxury to the max. Intensely sweet and so balanced it is almost hard to believe. Take the very best aspects of all the ylang-ylang essential oils and then add volume, richness and a smouldering radiance and you have this product. Origin: Madagascar Grown, France processed Variety: Cananga odorata Part: Flowers only Method: Solvent extraction

missing_other.title: Ylang-Ylang Complete Oil
missing_other.description: Our Ylang-ylang complete is a magnificent oil 100% processed in Comoros, the home of the finest ylang oils. Ylang-ylang complete is a cost effective way to get the ethereal beauty of the more expensive extra oil with the full bodied creaminess of the lower-cost fractions. This is a superior alternative to ylang-ylang III and can be used as a one for one replacer. This oil, being sourced directly from Comoros, is the most luxurious of all complete products. In side by side tests with products from other high-end suppliers, our ylang-ylang complete has the longest lasting and creamiest dry down, lacking the sharp unpleasant cresylic notes apparent in most other extractions. We also stock the sublime ylang-ylang extra "superior" oil as used in Chanel No 5 and the very finest French fragrances. Additionally, if you are looking for a synthetic replacer for ylang-ylang oil that can be used at much higher quantities under IFRA guidelines, you may prefer our wonderfully realistic Ylang Impérial base. Origin: The Union Of Comoros Variety: Cananga odorata var. genuina Part: Flowers only

missing_other.title: Ylang-Ylang Extra Oil, Comoros
missing_other.description: While most Ylang-ylang extra is from flowers grown in Madagascar, this beautiful Robertet extraction is from Ylang-ylang trees grown on Comoros just as it was when Ernest Beaux created Chanel No 5. It was formerly considered the premiere origin until low harvests and economics nearly shut down the Comoros trade. Thankfully it is now back and running full steam so you can have access to this nearly lost treasure. In addition to this Robertet product we also offer a beautiful organic version from Biolandes. The chief difference between them is that the Robertet Comoros oil is sweeter and richer with a creamier and more balanced top note and a fruitier and spicer cinnamic dry down. This Robertet Comoros oil is the Fraterworks default Ylang-ylang and we use it in all of our products. In ylang-ylang production terms, the “superior” oil is taken during the first few minutes of steam distilled extraction, giving the fruitiest and most ethereal top notes. Following that is this more balanced ( and most beautiful representation of the flower in nature) “extra” grade which can comprise up to 40 or 50% of the total remaining oil. The functional remnants are sold as grade I, grade II and grade III or taken on the whole as “complete” oil . Of those remnants, only complete and grade III are of value to modern perfumers with grade III being a cheap oil for soaps and “complete oil” being useful as a general mid-range ylang ylang which blends very well with most other florals. If you are looking for a synthetic replacer for ylang-ylang oil that can be used at much higher quantities, you may prefer our wonderfully realistic Ylang Impérial base. Grown: The Union Of Comoros Extracted: The Union Of Comoros Variety: Cananga odorata Part: Flowers only

missing_other.title: Ylang-Ylang Extra Oil, Org
missing_other.description: While some fragrances such as Chanel's original No 5 required a special penetrating variety of ylang-ylang (our “ Extra Superior ” product), the finest and most balanced all round ylang-ylang is the “Extra” quality distilled in Comoros on the same day as harvesting. This oil has the perfect balance of sweet top notes with a rich creamy floral heart and luscious dry down. If you only have one ylang-ylang, this is the one to have. In ylang-ylang production terms, the “superior” oil is taken during the first few minutes of steam distilled extraction, giving the fruitiest and most ethereal top notes. Following that is this more balanced ( and most beautiful representation of the flower in nature) “extra” grade which can comprise up to 40 or 50% of the total remaining oil. The functional remnants are sold as grade I, grade II and grade III or taken on the whole as “complete” oil . Of those remnants, only complete and grade III are of value to modern perfumers with grade III being a cheap oil for soaps and “complete oil” being useful as a general mid-range ylang ylang which blends very well with most other florals. If you are looking for a synthetic replacer for ylang-ylang oil that can be used at much higher quantities, you may prefer our wonderfully realistic Ylang Impérial base. Note: Fraterworks is not a registered organic company so while this product is organic when it reaches us from Biolandes, we cannot use that terminology when we resell. Extracted: The Union Of Comoros (same day) Variety: Cananga odorata Part: Flowers only

missing_other.title: Ylang-Ylang Extra Superior Oil, Org
missing_other.description: This is the famed ylang-ylang extra "superior" oil from Comoros (organic edition), the brightest ylang-ylang quality there is. This is the oil that Ernest Beaux demanded for Chanel No 5 because nothing else had top notes penetrating enough to handle the aldehyde overload. Most vendors settle for Madagascan processed extracts as they are less costly, but the Comoros oils remain to this day the peak of cananga perfection. From the ethereal fruity top notes to the intensely sweet and lasting dry down, you will be absolutely converted to this quality of ylang ylang. This is the stuff of legends. In ylang-ylang production terms, the "superior" oil is taken during the first few minutes of steam distilled extraction, giving the truest and most beautiful representation of the flower in nature. Following that is the more heart balanced “extra” grade (organic) which can comprise up to 40 or 50% of the total remaining oil. The more functional remnants are sold as grade I ,grade II and grade III or taken on the whole as “complete” oil . Only complete and grade III are of value to modern perfumers with grade III being a cheap oil for soaps and "complete" oil being useful as a general low-cost all-purpose ylang ylang which blends very well with most other florals. If you are looking for a synthetic replacer for ylang-ylang oil that can be used at much higher quantities, you may prefer our wonderfully realistic Ylang Impérial base. Note: Fraterworks is not a registered organic company so while this product is organic when it reaches us, we cannot use that terminology when we resell. Processed: The Union Of Comoros, same day Variety: Cananga odorata Part: Flowers only

missing_other.title: Yuzu Oil
missing_other.description: This cold-pressed Yuzu Oil bursts open with a sparkling, bitter-sweet citrus tang, somewhere between tart grapefruit and juicy mandarin. Behind the zesty brightness sits a dry, green, almost tea-like nuance. Yuzu has a luminous quality that feels fresher and more three-dimensional than lemon or bergamot. Pair Yuzu oil with ginger (it is especially good with our Ginger Oil, Cote d'Ivoire ), Timut pepper and cedarwood virginia for a vivid modern signature, or with our Lemon Verbena base and Provençal clary sage oil to play up its herbal, tea-like side. A touch with jasmine or neroli add a dewy, translucent lift. It works equally in unisex, sporty and quiet-luxury styles.

missing_other.title: Zafran Attar
missing_other.description: Zafran Attar is the classical Indian saffron perfume — Kashmiri saffron stigmas (Crocus sativus) hand-collected from the Pampore valley in autumn, then co-distilled by deg-bhapka into Mysore sandalwood oil over multiple rounds until the wood is fully saturated. Saffron remains the most costly spice on earth, which puts this attar among the more rarefied Indian co-distillates. Zafran Attar opens with the warm, honeyed character of dried saffron over soft, creamy sandalwood. Classic saffron notes of earthy hay and a faint leathery edge threads through the heart. Use Zafran Attar in classical oriental-rose accords, mukhallats, leather chypres and Mughal-style attar reconstructions. It pairs naturally with rose otto and oud — the three-way saffron-rose-oud accord is a backbone of Middle Eastern perfumery. A small dose adds golden warmth to amber bases without competing with the resinous notes. This Zafran is from M.L. Ramnarain Perfumers, a Kannauj distillery run by five generations of the Kapoor family using copper degs and the traditional water-distillation method.

missing_other.title: Zambezi
missing_other.description: Zambezi is our internal formula for the original Safari for men by Annie Buzantian (Firmenich) for Ralph Lauren. Launched in 1992. The scent built upon some of the earlier foundations of masterpieces like Polo Green (also for Lauren) in its artful use of the quite potent artemesia oil in concert with fir balsam. As Buzantian was with Firmenich, she did not have access to the great base at the heart of Polo, Artemal , and instead built a cut down fond that mimicked and modernised that base. When comparing this compound (and please note that this is not compliant for IFRA or the EU as it contains atranol-rich green Yugoslavian oakmoss ) to the formula in bottles today, the main thing you will notice is the richness from all the trace naturals. The scent was rather cutting edge for its time, having not just large doses of rich Firmenich bases, but layers of herbs and layers of spices. Its overdose of neroli oil is rather out of place today, but certainly still acceptable in a mass market scent of the 1990s. A smidgen of aldehydes adds a vaguely soapy note which reads "clean" rather than "bath time". This compound is not IFRA compliant but if you wish to dilute it to sample on spray cards, it should be kept to a light 8 – 12%. If you need an IFRA or EU compliant version, we can, for a 5 kilogram MOQ, produce it to order. IFRA compliance is possible to around 16% with minimal changes. Top Notes: Lavender, Bergamot, Aldehydes, Coriander, Artemisia, Green Notes, Neroli, Lemon Heart Notes: Tarragon, Carnation, Cinnamon, Rose, Jasmine, Cyclamen Base Notes: Leather, Oakmoss, Sandalwood, Cedar, Patchouli, Musk, Amber
